# Section I. Portion IV. Part I. Book II.

...invisible, in the regions of water and earth, as if it were a legate or messenger sent from the higher realms to the lower world, foretelling accidents that must occur on the land, in the water, and to their creatures. It is like a highly polished tablet or table upon which the planets and stars, as if with a painter's brush, have depicted with their rays—as if with living colors—rains, snows, hails, thunders, winds, storms, and the like. It also displays the most evident signs of drought, cold, earthquakes, fertility, sterility, and other things pertaining both to the ruin and the health of men. In the air, therefore, through the mediation of God’s celestial creatures, is shaped the reading and knowledge of future things, which is given only to men of true science and those fortified with wisdom to read and understand. 

For example, <term>Comets</term><note>In early modern science, "meteors" and "comets" referred to any atmospheric phenomena, not just astronomical ones.</note> do not appear in the air for nothing or in a vain manner, nor do the infinite other particular meteors and wonders. From these, we are clearly taught (by the testimony of the ancients) that the air, with the help of the heavens, indicates to us like a mirror or a pointing finger the beginnings of common calamities, the deaths of illustrious persons, the cruelties of wars, the changes of seasons, famine, plague, and all kinds of diseases and such things. Hence, Robert Grosseteste, the Bishop of Lincoln, says: 

> The air is the matrix of all impressions, for by grace of its moisture, it acts as a spiritual mirror. It most easily receives or emulates the forms and natures of all things placed or cast against it, and it readily represents and receives the likenesses of all shapes and colors. 

Thus he concludes that the air is the womb of all impressions, since it is the medium whether in its own region or in the bowels and depths of water and earth; it is also the very matter of meteors, both healthy and unhealthy. Indeed, and what is more, it retains within itself invisible and imperceptible impressions, which are the images of manifest and visible things. For this reason, if someone passes through a place where a man was killed, or where a fresh corpse is hidden, he is immediately shaken by fear and stupor. This is because the air in that place is filled with the specters of the killing—the horrible images of the homicide and its "seeds," as it were—and these affect the spirit of the man passing through as he breathes that air, disturbing him with those similar images and striking him with great terror. 

Similarly, through these kinds of hidden impressions in the air, various dreams and multiform impressions are produced in the human spirit through the icons of "idols" (images), likenesses, or species. These arise from things originating from words or actions whose forms have multiplied in the air. Therefore, this species of invisible or hidden "meteors" is the reason why such miraculous cures are brought to a happy conclusion by the <term>Weapon Salve</term><note>original: "Unguento Armario" — a controversial medicinal ointment believed to heal a wound by being applied to the weapon that caused it, rather than the body.</note>, as has been more than sufficiently explained in our treatise on *Mystical Anatomy*. 

Furthermore, these types of "meteors" reigning hidden and invisibly in the air are the origins of epidemic or popularly spreading diseases—namely the plague and pestilential illnesses. These diseases are the effects of either a Comet or some other meteor (whether fiery, watery, windy, or mixed) which was visible in times past but has now been dissipated everywhere through the air into invisible parts. Because the human spirit, as well as the terrestrial spirit, enters with the air through breathing, it pollutes them from every side just like the external air, as will be demonstrated more broadly below.

Regarding the disposition or "complexion" of this spirit, <margin>(Galen, *On the Powers of Simple Medicines*, Book 2, ch. 20)</margin> a massive difference seems to arise among the princes of Philosophy (who are observed to be at odds with one another in their writings). For Aristotle and those who follow his opinion think the air is hot, while the Stoics, opposing them, confidently say it is cold. But if we explore the matter a little more accurately, we will perceive that it is neither hot nor cold, nor moist nor dry by itself, but consists in a middle state between these qualities. Hence, it is judged fit and suitable to receive any of these accidental impressions, although the air itself exists with no certain or manifest quality of its own. 

For this reason, it is observed to be sometimes hot, sometimes cold, sometimes moist, and not rarely dry. Therefore, it is not improperly compared to the celestial Mercury, the messenger of Jupiter (as was said above), who usually takes on the nature of the quality of whichever planet he is joined with. Thus, it is noticed that he is cold and dry with Saturn, more hot and less moist with Jupiter, hot and dry with Mars, but with the Sun in a more moderate degree, more moist and less hot with Venus, and cold and moist with the Moon. The air is observed to do the same, receiving various temperatures according to the variety of celestial influences and the difference of the blowing winds. 

Therefore, we say that the air, considered simply and in its own nature, is neither hot, nor cold, nor moist, nor dry. However, insofar as it withdrew from the abyss of dark <term>hyle</term><note>The "hyle" refers to the primordial, unformed matter of the universe.</note> in the first creation under the name of "waters," it is more fit to participate in the quality of darkness—namely coldness—which reigns mostly in the absence of light. But insofar as it participates in the form of light, it is rendered ready to receive hot and fiery influences. From this it is clear that in its own nature, without respect to other influences, its aptitude for coldness is removed by its inclination toward the heat of the informing light; therefore, it cannot be called hot or cold originally and in its essence. Since moisture and dryness are simple qualities arising from the "simples" (that is, from heat and cold), it follows that the air by its nature is neither cold nor hot, and consequently neither moist nor dry. # On the Material Cause of Meteors.
### 23

Its potential existence in the <term>hyle</term><note>original: "hyla"; referring to the Greek concept of "hyle," the raw, unformed matter of the universe.</note> or dark chaos was naturally a companion to potential coldness. Later, when the water actually flowed out from the darkness at the creation of the world, the air retained a greater inclination toward a certain hidden humidity. This humidity, however, is not essential to the air’s existence, since the air can be converted into an extremely dry state or condition, as is seen during the summer season. We conclude, therefore, that the air is capable of receiving any of the four aforementioned qualities <note>The four primary qualities of Aristotelian physics: hot, cold, moist, and dry.</note>. It habitually brings this capability into action according to the nature and condition of the wind that happens to blow. For example: the **Northern winds** <note>original: "Aquilonares"</note> make it cold and dry; the **Southern winds** <note>original: "Australes"</note> make it hot and moist; the **East wind** <note>original: "Eurus"</note> makes it hot and dry; and the **Western winds** make it cold and moist. Thus, the quality of the air can change at any moment according to the ordinance of GOD, who disposes it according to His will; indeed, the air itself receives whatever is poured into it, yet it nevertheless retains and preserves its spiritual and uniform essence.

### CHAPTER V.

->*Where the active reason for changing air from one quality to another is explained.*<-
->*Here also is described how the air itself is accustomed to be altered*<-

Although the air (as has already been said) is single and simple in its nature and existence, it nevertheless—through the mediation of the Word and the angelic ministers who blow and move it with various winds—is accustomed to migrate from one quality to another. Consequently, it moves from a dense substance to a thin or moderate one, or conversely from thin to dense, and this happens daily. For who, having even common experience, does not see that clouds are composed of thickened air? And who does not see that the substance of the air itself is condensed into hail, frost, and hoar-frost by the cold of the north? Sacred Scripture teaches us that this cold flows from the divine breath.
> For (as Job says, chapter 37:9-10), "The mighty GOD brings forth ice by His breath; by the breath of GOD the frost is increased." And it is said elsewhere: "He sends His word to the earth; His word runs very swiftly. He gives snow like wool, and scatters the hoar-frost like ashes; He casts forth His ice like morsels; who can stand before His cold?" (Psalm 147:16-17).

From this, it is clear that the thin and invisible air thickens into dense and hard matter through the mediation of the Word of GOD, which commands the cold. This Word (witnessed by the fountain of truth in Psalm 104) is carried out by angels of greatest strength. Again, when heat is sent forth through the Word and the administration of angels, the air is reduced by contrary winds into vapors and watery clouds. Having been changed from a cold breath into snow, hail, frost, and hoar-frost, it is again dissolved into drops of water, as is evident from the conclusion of the testimony cited from the Psalmist:
> For there follows in verse 18: "He sends out His word and melts them; as soon as He blows His word, the waters flow."

From this we argue that by the sending of the Word—that is, the divine light—and by the Southern wind blowing by His power through the ministry of Angels, those things which the cold Northern wind froze are dissolved by the Southern wind back into what they were before. No one familiar with common boiling can deny that watery vapor is dissolved by the action of heat into air, as if into the "prime matter" from which it first arose. Therefore, cold condenses the air, while heat makes it thin and subtle. 

However, the cause of this condensation and thinning always occurs with the assistance of the winds and their qualities. By the opposition of these winds, the air between them is compressed; it is first reduced into the form of vapor, and then into a watery smoke or cloudy substance. This happens especially if a hot and moist (Southern) wind contends against a cold and dry (Northern) wind. For it is necessary that a mass of air—either watery and moist, from which rains are generated, or dry, bringing forth hail and snow—be procreated in the aerial space or medium between these opposing blasts, depending on which wind dominates. 

But where the North wind <note>original: "Aquilo"</note> blows and the South wind <note>original: "Auster"</note> offers little or no opposition, there ice, frost, and hoar-frost are produced from the condensation and constriction of the air and waters. Likewise, when the South wind blows, if the North wind does not oppose it, we see that the sky is not so full of clouds, nor is the air so damp; but since the northern wind rarely rests, there are also rarely southern winds that are not associated with clouds and rain. 

We say, therefore, that the uniform nature of the air is accidentally suited to take on any disposition of the winds. Thus, when the North wind blows from the Arctic, it freezes and thickens the air itself; by its dryness, it gathers and glues together the dispersed parts of the air, and by its coldness, it coagulates and thickens them, converting them (as is seen in snow, hoar-frost, and hail) into an earthy condition. But when the South wind blows from the Meridian, that wind conversely turns that portion of the air which the North wind made "earthy" back into water, since the works of cold are destroyed and dissolved by heat. Again, the hot and dry spirits of the East wind <note>original: "Euri"</note> convert that water into an aerial or fiery disposition, which the West wind nourishes and refreshes with its breath. Are we not taught by the testimony of all truth that winds of this kind have power over the air? For it is left written for us that by the power of the Word; which (as is witnessed...

(as David states in many places) the winds or the angels of GOD bring it about—by making a sound and commotion in the air—that the very dry bones of the field should come together, each bone to its joint, and that nerves and flesh should grow upon them, and skin be stretched over them? *Ezekiel 37*. This air is the simple beginning or end of those very meteors, or imperfect mixtures, from which they first departed. O our salt-nitre dwelling in the sea of the world! O our Vegetable! O our fixed and volatile Sulphur! Water not wetting the hand, without which no one can live,”* etc. And indeed, he rightly calls the air the "Mercury of the Philosophers," since it seems to alter its own nature according to the nature of the influence of any planet or the wind blowing upon it.

Do we not also see, as confirmation of this matter, that common **Mercury** (which for this reason the common Alchemists called "Quicksilver" <note>original: "Argentum vivum"</note>) when joined or **Amalgamated** with any of the other fusible metals, converts its own nature into the nature of the metal with which it is joined? This is just like the celestial Mercury, which is convertible into the nature of any planet to which it is applied. And yet this quicksilver is nothing other than mere air, changed by the mediation of cold into a visible, heavy water; this is shown by its effect, for by the violence of fire it vanishes and is transmuted back into the air from which it primordially arose. Furthermore, that this air, so condensed into water, is "earth in potential" is proved by the fact that through the industry of Chemistry, we have observed it to be precipitated into earth by itself, and without the help of another.

And again, the wise have noticed that a "living fire" leaps out from the center of quicksilver. By this, it is indicated that the air, thus reduced into a Mercurial cloud, possesses within itself the nature of every wind and, consequently, every element. For we see this same thing in a cloud formed from the air in its own bosom or womb; experience teaches that fire, water, earth, and smoke (or wind) are within it. Whence the philosopher says: *“I pray you, consider the simple water of a cloud. Who would ever believe that it contains within itself all that the world has—hard stones, salts, air, earth, fire—and yet by itself it appears as simple water?”*

It has also been proven by us through experience that a portion of air enclosed in a large round glass vessel and sealed by fire <note>referring to a "hermetically sealed" glass flask.</note>, if exposed to the celestial sun or a slow heat, will be converted into water. The reason is that it is the nature of heat to refine <note>original: "subtiliare"</note> air that was previously imbued with a moderate coldness. But because refined air requires a wider place for its expanded existence, it is necessary either that the glass be broken, or that as much of the air be condensed into water as the dimension of the positioned and now-refined air exceeds the space it would take if it were all refined—which is clearly demonstrated in our experimental instrument. It follows, therefore, that the same water, which was previously air, returns again into air in the absence of heat and the presence of cold, lest a vacuum should occur; for cold requires its portion in thickness, just as heat requires its own in thinness. By these things, it is aptly declared that air (which is nothing other than **subtle water**) can very easily be converted into the coarse disposition of visible and thick water.

But since it is certain that every visible thing comes first from an invisible thing, according to that saying of St. Paul alleged above: namely, that *“through faith we understand that the worlds were framed by the word of God, so that things which are seen were not made of things which do appear,”* *Hebrews 11*. Therefore, it must be held as an infallible axiom that visible water was primordially made from air, or from invisible water or spirit. Whence, when it was said that the "Spirit of the Lord moved over the waters," Moses wished to imply (as Augustine interprets) a fiery love over the spiritual—and not visible—waters; from which was created the substance of the Empyrean heaven and that angelic substance, which is the more sublime portion of the air or universal spirit.

We conclude, therefore, that coarse things were made primordially and *a priori* <note>from the cause to the effect; from the preceding.</note> from subtle things, and not the other way around. Similarly, subtle things are made from coarser things by a final resolution and *a posteriori* <note>from the effect to the cause; from the following.</note>, which is also confirmed by the testimony of the sacred scriptures: *“Who has numbered the heavens in wisdom, and made the things that descend from the heavens to rest? When the dust descended into that hardness, and the clods cleaved fast together?”* *Job 38:37*. By these words, it is indicated that the earth first descended from the heavens—namely from the air or the mundane spirit. This is also clearly declared by the generation of a "thunderstone" <note>original: "lapidis ceraunij"; a stone believed to fall from the sky during a lightning strike.</note> or lightning bolt.

What then is the **Universal Air**, and of what consistency? Certainly, it is an intermediate spirit between darkness and light, produced by mutual action and passion at the instant of creation by the operation of the wind. When the one and supreme Divinity had thought within Himself concerning creation, He reflected into Himself and contracted His heat, so that it did not yet shine upon the world. The difference, however, that is created in this simple and uniform universal aerial sea—both in heaven and in the sublunary place—does not arise from the nature of the air itself, but from the disposition of the Sphere or Orb. Finally, the place that Philosophers attribute to the air is that middle substance of the world-spirit that lies between earth and fire. Therefore, if the air suffers the action of extreme heat, it will have the least sign of coldness and, consequently, of moisture, but a greater sign of dryness, and thus it approaches the nature of fire, which is also called the fiery element. Sect. I. Port. IV. Part I. Book II.

...we are taught by **Holy Testimony**: And this is the reason why we said the air is by itself neither hot nor cold, nor moist nor dry, but sometimes hot, sometimes cold, and sometimes moist and dry. But indeed, we said that at the very instant of its creation, it tasted especially of moisture, in a way, and by a sort of adventitious <note>original: "adventitio"; meaning something added from the outside rather than inherent to its basic essence.</note> custom, because of the reasons we alleged above. Indeed, even Aristotle himself, and **Robert of Lincoln** <note>Robert Grosseteste (c. 1175–1253), a famous English statesman, scientist, and philosopher who wrote extensively on light and the liberal arts.</note>, his commentator, seem to hint at this same thing when they maintain that a certain vapor is hot and moist, another hot and cold, and another hot and dry (which others call an "exhalation"). However, they assertively claim that no vapor is cold and dry, even though we see the **Thunderstone** <note>original: "lapidem Ceraunium"; these were stones or fossils traditionally believed to fall from the sky during a lightning strike.</note> (or lightning stone) has a terrestrial constitution. Consequently, its nearest cause must have been the air, or water, or a thick vapor that was cold and dry; for that which creates such a thing must itself be more like that thing. But those Philosophers say that hot and dry vapor comes partly from water and partly from earth; they want the hot and dry part to come from the earth, while they say the cold and moist part is exhaled from water.

As if indeed water itself, and consequently the earth, were not made of air, rather than air being made of water or earth! For in Genesis, mention is made of the **Heavens** (by which name "Air" is understood) before mention is made of either the visible waters or the earth; for the Heavens were the work of the second day, while the visible water and earth were of the third. Nor indeed is it just in the course of Nature that the thing which is begun <note>principiatum</note> should be the cause of its own beginning; rather, it is the other way around. The Heavens and the earth were made from these kinds of invisible waters, as St. Peter witnesses in *2 Peter 3:5*, and St. Paul says in the place cited before, *that visible things were preceded by those which are not seen. Heb. 11.*

But in **Occult Philosophy** and **Theosophy**, those who are more skilled acknowledge (as seen in Reuchlin's *Cabala* <note>Johannes Reuchlin (1455–1522) was a German humanist and scholar of Hebrew who introduced Jewish Mysticism/Cabala into Renaissance philosophy.</note>) that all lower things are representative of higher things. From this, they say that as it is below, so it is also enacted above. All the Doctors of the Hebrews and those more skilled in the **Cabala** approve of this. From this it follows that the figure and image of the earth and waters existed first in the air, just as the impressions of the air descended first from the **Aether**; in the same way, no true Christian will deny that the image of the heavens and the pattern of the world descended from the **Archetypal Throne**.

Therefore, we conclude that **Air** is the first material origin of every kind of meteor. According to the disposition of the angels who rule over it and breathe into it, the air is altered from one constitution to another by the divine will. We say that when the **fiery winds** blow (for angels *are winds and the flaming ministers of God*), the substance of the highest region of the air—which is nothing other than invisibly expanded fire—is contracted into the visible form of a **Comet** or another meteor of that same kind, according to the nature of the acting angel. Similarly, according to the nature of the wind, when fiery angels breathe against watery ones, and the watery ones also equally predominate, they produce thunder and lightning, or "mixed meteors," by the compression of the air.

But if cold winds especially prevail, or moist ones with a very small portion of heat, we say that snow, hail, or rain are produced there, without lightning or flashing, in the middle region of the air. Finally, if the dominion of hot winds is in the middle region of the air, then **fiery meteors** are usually generated in the lowest region of the air—measuring from the place of the clouds down to the earth—by the compression of the parts of the fiery air expanded everywhere in this region. If it abounds in cold and dryness, it brings on frost and ice into the middle region of the air. In this generation, the **material cause** is the Air; the **near efficient cause** is the wind (or air moved centrally by angels performing the Word of God); and the **remote or primary cause** is God the Father, who ordains all things that are done in the world.

And yet, in truth, the **Angels** are only the organs in which and through which He alone acts immediately in the created spirit. Therefore, the opinions of those who posited that vapors rising from the earth or water are the material causes of meteors in the air are empty. **Aristotle** was blind, and blind (I say) are the **Peripatetics** <note>Followers of Aristotle's philosophy.</note> and all the Philosophers who have dared to write about the natures of meteors while being ignorant of their causes, both material and efficient. These secular "wise men" or Philosophers did not understand that at the point of creation, God simultaneously created by His Word the air and the angels and spirits. Look at where they think clouds, rain, hail, snow, frost, heat, cold, lightning, thunder, the thunderbolt, the thunderstone, floods of water, and good and bad storms arise; you will perceive their errors with your own eyes wide open. # On the Material Cause of Meteors.

Indeed, it is not in the manner that those Pagans <note>original: "Ethnici"; referring to pre-Christian Greek and Roman philosophers whose natural philosophy the author is contrasting with Christian doctrine.</note> wrote in their spurious books, but rather that GOD has His own peculiar treasuries for these previously mentioned types, from which He produces winds and storms, as in Jeremiah 10 and 51, and that He makes His angels spirits and His ministers flaming fires, as in Psalm 134 <note>This refers to Psalm 104:4 in modern Bibles: "Who maketh his angels spirits; his ministers a flaming fire."</note>. GOD, I say, to bring about a variety of storms, has His own peculiar treasuries and angels, as well as spirits, through whose mediation He brings about all those things we see: namely, how wonderfully storms arise, how miraculously the <term>thunderstone</term> <note>original: "lapis ceraunius"; a stone or fossil traditionally believed to fall from the sky during a lightning strike.</note> (or lightning stone) solidifies, and by what reason heat and cold generate thunder so that it reaches even houses, citadels, and trees, etc. And although our effort might perhaps seem of very little importance to the foolish, yet if they consider the matter a little more accurately, they will indeed perceive that it concerns the divine honor. It is vital that the children of GOD truly and fundamentally know and understand that storms and other related operations do not occur by their own motion, or by chance, or by such foolish ways as the erroneous books of the Pagans imagine. Rather, they are brought in and proceed from divine providence and the treasuries of the divine vaults, and are sent down from above into this lower world. Thus, when dangerous storms arise, or morbid and pestilential <term>meteors</term> <note>In this period, "meteor" referred to any atmospheric phenomenon, including rain, wind, and plague-bearing vapors, not just falling stars.</note> are scattered through the air, we may call upon GOD, that He might mercifully turn away that danger of meteors, storms, and contagious air from us, and in their place grant us benign and healthy meteors, while simultaneously defending, protecting, and preserving the fruits of the earth, along with humans and livestock, from all evil.

We conclude, therefore, that since all things were created through the Word of GOD, and by that same Word are directed, governed, moved, and led in the course originally implanted in them at creation, it is also necessary that the Air (which is <term>Pan</term> <note>A reference to the Greek god Pan, used here as a personification of "Universal Nature" or the "All."</note> or Universal Nature) remains in the Word of GOD. It must be led by the angels of GOD appointed for this purpose, whenever, wherever, and however GOD wills. Thus also, by divine command through Moses, the powerful meteors were moved—for instance, the winds, clouds, hail, the pillar of cloud and fire, thunders, and other things of this sort—according to the divine will. Finally, this must be especially observed: that air is the material origin of any thing, as it is that which contains all the elements within itself. Consequently, it is the mother of all things, just as the Word of God is their father. For **Thin air** is the element of fire, which by condensation produces fiery meteors subject to our sight, such as Comets, Spears <note>A term for a specific type of linear aurora or atmospheric light phenomenon.</note>, lightning flashes, etc. Furthermore, **moderate air** is the intermediate spirit between the fiery element and that of visible water. **Thick air** is mist, cloud, and rain, and consequently water. However, the **Earth** is the thickness of water or the "dregs" of water, as can be seen in the thunderstone or lightning stone. From this it happens that earth, through thinning, can become thick air or water; and water, through rarefaction, becomes moderate air; and that air is again sublimated into thin and rare air, or fire, by further attenuation. And this is the **circle in nature**, which the Word of God, through the mediation of angels, revolves according to the divine will. Therefore you see that all things, as far as their matter is concerned, are made of air through the operation of the Word.

## CAP. VI.

### *How meteors are also generated in the earth and waters, and concerning their nature.*

In the preceding sections, we have declared that all things, as far as their substance is concerned, are originally forged from air, and nothing exists without its benevolent breath, since nothing can live without it. For thin air nourishes the spirit of things; in its moderate substance, it feeds the humors; and it daily refreshes thick, solid bodies. By these differences of air, those things remain as they were created. Air therefore abounds, and that most fluently, in every thing: namely in the earth, in the water, in crags, in stones, in man and other animals, and also in every plant. Just as we see that every animal is filled with air and spirit and daily breathes in air for the sustenance of its life, so also the life of the earth, the sea, and the waters consists in air, through which they subsist and are perpetually refreshed. Nor indeed is air present only in the empty places of the earth itself—just as it is in the spaces and hollows of the human body—but it is certain that it penetrates the pores of the earth, stones, and metals everywhere, filling them spiritually. Furthermore, the substances of the waters are also full of air, seeing as they originally proceeded from air, no differently than we have our blood (both arterial and venous) filled everywhere with aerial spirit. Just as we said that in the space between the sphere of the Moon and the earth, the air is uniform in itself but ordered into parts of different quality, so also the air contained in water or earth observes a similar order. Namely, it is thicker and denser near the center of the earth, from which minerals forged from thick and heavy water are generated; but in the heart of the earth, the air is thinned and congeals into stones; a little higher it turns into spring water and is condensed, upon which vegetables chiefly depend; and joining itself at the surface of the earth with the open aerial sea of the world, it is converted into vapor useful for the generation of animals. And the earth claimed this proportion of air for its own existence at the primordial moment of its creation. But truly, this air in the earth and

## CHAPTER VII.

### On the material cause of meteors in Man.

We have said that Man is composed of spirit and body—just as the world is made of heaven and earth—in no other way than the world itself. Because of this, philosophers have not unwisely called him the "Minor World" <note>original: "Mundus Minor" or Microcosm.</note>. Indeed, as Hermes Trismegistus testifies in *Pymander* 8, *man is the image of the world,* and in another place he called him *the son of the world.* Therefore, it is necessary that his dark body be derived from the world’s earth, and his airy spirit from the world’s heaven, and that both be sustained and nourished in succession through terrestrial foods and the perpetual drinking of the "airy cup." This is why Moses testifies that *GOD created Adam from the mud of the earth, and breathed into his face the breath of life.* From this it is clear that whatever the state of the external air may be, the human spirit must have the closest relationship to it, since the <term>Macrocosmic spirit</term> <note>The spirit of the great universe.</note> constantly mixes with the spirit of the <term>Microcosm</term> <note>The spirit of the individual human.</note> through various breaths. Thus, it is inevitable that air infects air, just as water colored with blood, snow, or saffron converts other water into its own condition. So too, the foul air of one place makes the sweet and fragrant air of another smell terrible; consequently, air defiled by rot and pestilent "seeds" converts healthy and clean air into its own nature.

This is exactly what Hippocrates and Galen proclaimed in various parts of their writings. For Galen recognized that our bodies are necessarily altered by the surrounding air. Elsewhere he says: *Hotter states of the surrounding air, such as those occurring especially around the rising of the Dog Star, clearly heat the heart through breathing; and being poured around the body from the outside, they make the whole body hotter. But this is especially true of the arteries, as they draw in something of the substance of the surrounding air itself, from which the heart must necessarily be affected.* Similarly, Hippocrates teaches us that through the surrounding air we can reach a knowledge of diseases. Elsewhere he says that *at the beginning of winter, bile decreases because it is now cooling, and <term>phlegm</term> <note>original: "pituita"; one of the four traditional humors believed to regulate health.</note> increases anew, both from the following rains and from the length of the nights.* Hippocrates himself seems to acknowledge this same thing in his book *On Nature* and throughout the first book of *On Epidemics*, where he appears to declare and predict the effects of epidemic diseases based on the rising of winds and the rising and setting of stars. Galen, his commentator, also acknowledges that animal bodies are altered by the air, so that they become wetter through rains and drier through heat or summer glow. He says that *when heat prevails, the head will be firm; when cold is abundant, the head will be very light, but the chest and lungs will suffer.* Furthermore, elsewhere he speaks in these words: *Of those things which happen to bodies from the outside, one is certainly inseparable from it, adhering to it like a perpetual kinsman: namely, the surrounding air, which harms us by making us excessively hot, or cold, or wet, or dry.* There are infinite other passages in both Hippocrates and Galen by which we are warned that the internal air has an inseparable union with the spirit of animals. Moreover, the method by which air is drawn into the lungs and "cooked" by them is demonstrated by Galen. Similarly, he explains how the air drawn in by breathing is carried in two directions: partly to the heart via the lungs, and partly to the brain with the help of the nostrils. Finally, in his famous booklet *Whether Blood is Naturally Contained in the Arteries*, he admits that inspired air is spread through every single member of the whole body by means of the lungs, heart, arteries, and nostrils.

But now we shall make a brief discourse concerning the air or spirit contained within man, and concerning its origin, seat, and motion in the human body. We have declared elsewhere that the living soul inhabits the center of this body, just as the bright influences of life sent down from the sun into these lower regions inhabit the innermost parts of the worldly...

### On the Material Cause of Meteors.

...hidden in the bowels of the world, as we have said. Hermes Trismegistus <note>original: "Mercur. Trismegistus"; a legendary Hellenistic figure regarded as the author of the Hermetic Corpus</note> says in *Pimander*, Book 10: *The human soul is carried in this manner: the mind in reason, reason in the soul, the soul in the spirit, and the spirit in the body. This spirit, diffused through the veins, arteries, and blood, stirs the living creature on all sides and supports and carries the suspended mass of the body. Because of this, some were deceived into thinking the moisture of the blood was the soul; it clearly escaped their notice that it is necessary for the spirit first to flow into the soul, then for the blood to thicken, and the hollow veins and arteries to be stretched out, and finally for the animal to be dissolved—which dissolution is the death of the body.* In these words, he denotes the dominion of the spirit or air in the body, since he makes it the vehicle of the soul. Indeed, he seems to suggest how, by the mediation of the spirit with its ethereal form, the blood originally flowed forth. It is as if he said: through the "airy meteor" <note>In this period, "meteor" referred to any phenomenon of vapors, fluids, or spirits, whether in the sky or the body</note>, agitated by its own internal form, the internal part of man and even his humors are procreated. This is according to that saying of Hippocrates mentioned above: "At the beginning of winter, bile grows cold and decreases, and phlegm <note>original: "pituita"</note> increases anew." From this it is clear that air, with its internal essence, is the cause of the variety of humors, or the change of one humor into another. These humors take on the appearance of meteors; indeed, upon the dissolution of the living creature, the blood is accustomed to migrate back into its internal spirit, just as the meteors of the sky vanish into the air. Whence Trismegistus also says: *As the soul returns into itself, the spirit is contracted into the blood, and the soul into the spirit, etc.*

Do not the Holy Scriptures also confirm that the seat of the soul is the blood? From which it follows that blood is nothing other than tempered air of a "second mixture," reduced into that bloody mass by thickening, like a natural meteor. Therefore, this air—dispersed everywhere through the body and carrying the soul through every small part of the body (just as it is said by the Philosophers to be "in the whole and in any part")—is that "sublime place" in which meteors or "imperfectly mixed" things are procreated. It is also the place from which, by thickening caused by "Microcosmic winds" (made in imitation of those in the Macrocosm), various meteors—both healthy and unhealthy—are produced in man. Those which are more spiritual and invisible assert good or evil passions of the soul, according to the favorable or unlucky nature of the meteor created in and from that airy medium. Therefore, we must sincerely say the same thing regarding the *internal efficient cause* of these meteors as we said of the meteors of the great world: namely, that the primary cause is the essence-making property of the ineffable Name of GOD, turning either toward mercy or toward punishment. These things are ordained, and then afterward commanded to be executed by His angelic ministers who "do His word," by the mediation of the air. They change and convert the air into this or that nature and constitution according to the will of the Divine Creator, which we propose to demonstrate more openly and copiously elsewhere.

And in this way, you have before your eyes an anatomy of the human spirit, and at the same time its necessary relationship with that of the Macrocosm. Now, let me speak—and indeed briefly—concerning the comparison between the human body and spirit (the "lesser world") and the spirit of the earth in the "greater world." Between these most noble creatures of the sublunary world, a very great and necessary commerce and reciprocity takes place at every moment of time.

Thus, as we drink from the sacred fountain that God established man in His own image, so also we read abundantly that He created and ordained all His creatures for the use of man. Whence Pico della Mirandola and other experts in divine philosophy quite aptly call **Man "every creature."** Following him in nobility and excellence among the lower bodies is this immense Earth. By its nod and administration, all lower bodies that are perfectly mixed are nourished and refreshed daily, after they have first received the foundation of their mass and structure from it. And yet, this huge and giant creature was created for human use, according to that of the royal Psalmist: *GOD made the earth and gave it to the sons of men.* From which it is right to gather that man himself is the end <note>The final purpose or goal</note> of all creatures, and consequently a creature of extraordinary height. The Earth is next to him in dignity, for it is not only the base of the external man, but it also produces, contains, and nourishes all creatures required for human life and sustenance. Certainly, if we explore the matter a little more curiously, there is the greatest relationship between these two creatures in their composition. For just as we observe man to be composed of body and spirit, in which spirit a certain divine soul or internal active principle holds its habitation, so the matter stands with the mass of the Macrocosmic Earth. It was composed and formed by the Creator from an external body and an internal spirit, in which spirit a certain "Solar soul" dwells, which the wise have—not without reason—called the **Central Sun.** Both of these extraordinary creatures are therefore "animals" (if I may say so) endowed with the same functions and offices of life. Both bodies are vehicles, receptacles, and matrices of influences—both from the super-celestial and celestial regions and from the sublunary air. These bodies contain similar spirits "cut out" from the universal sublunary air as if from a great cliff or spiritual sea, just as we see the lunar circle or sphere embrace the entire mass of sublunary air. This kind of air or spirit, enclosed in man as much as in the earth, has as much fellowship and commerce with the universal worldly air as a single drop of water has to its whole; for they are joined by an inseparable "glue" to the air or Great Spirit of the World, just as a drop of seawater, when joined to the whole, is united with that entire body of water by an inseparable union. ...homogeneous and of the same nature as that of the **greater world** <note>The Macrocosm, or the universe at large</note>; therefore, the human spirit lives and is sustained by the breathing in of external air. By this means, it is refreshed, preserved, and nourished, receiving both celestial and earthly gifts. In the same reciprocal way, the spirit of the Earth also lives; it draws the liquid of its life from the same fountain, and without the breathing in of the infinite air, it could not endure for even a moment of time. 

It is for this reason that we have it confirmed by the fathers of **Astrology** and the more **abstruse Philosophy**, that not only the Earth, but indeed all bodies—even the celestial ones—are to be regarded as certain **giant animals**. Within them exists a spirit of life breathed from the universal **World Soul** <note>original: "vniuersa mundi anima"</note>, by which they are daily refreshed and live through a continuous administration of spirits. For this reason, a vast distance of airy spirit is placed between each of these huge bodily animals, so that enough vital spirit might be supplied to each for its own existence and for the life and breathing of the creatures living upon and within it. This occurs without the ambitious intrusion or incursion of one into the portion of another. Thus, the **Greatest and Best Creator** fixed a constant place in the world for each, lest one, like a predator wandering beyond its proper limits, should rashly or unjustly invade the territory granted to another by the Creator, and thereby ignite war and discord in the bowels of a peaceful world. This is why the stars and the Earth always claim the same stations for themselves. 

Therefore, the entire space of the airy region between the Moon and the Earth is appropriated to both the Moon and the Earth, but especially to the Earth. Without the breath of its spirit, it is impossible for the Earth or any of its creatures to endure. From this, it follows beyond all doubt that the Earth breathes in and breathes out this airy spirit (which is filled with the grace of divine life) no differently than a human, any other animal, or even a plant. 

In man, we see that the **heart** is that noble organ whose duty is to purify the spirit drawn in centrally by breathing, and then to expel the superfluous and smoky air through exhalation. Does the Earth not also have its own heart? It has the **central sun** <note>This refers to a hidden, spiritual, or central fire within the Earth, a common concept in Hermetic and alchemical philosophy</note>. Through its operation, celestial benefits of life are attracted by a certain **magnetic virtue** through the pores, carried by the airy spirit. Then, through a contraction or narrowing, that which is superfluous is emitted in the form of vapors. Along the way, those vapors are frozen in the veins and changed into water, from which springs arise. However, that which is useful is reserved in the Earth's belly and is abundantly shared with the creatures she nourishes like a **bountiful mother**. 

By the same logic, the human heart offers and scatters a portion of its *Manna* <note>original: "Manna"; here used to mean a celestial, life-giving dew or essence</note> or **celestial honey**—newly collected or drawn from the air—through the arteries to all the members of the whole body, and especially to its spirits. That which is superfluous, it sends outside. If the place into which that vapor is exhaled is smoky, narrow, and cold, it condenses into drops of water. For example, if someone breathes into a vial, a mirror, or onto marble, we perceive that spirit coagulating first into a mist, then into dew, and finally into drops.

But someone will object (I know) that "breathing in and out" is not proper to the Earth, or at least is entirely hidden from men. To this we reply: if we consider the **ebb and flow of the sea** <note>The tides</note> with diligent intuition, we will perceive that it was not made in vain by "Nature Naturing" <note>original: "natura naturante"; a philosophical term referring to God or the creative force of nature as an active agent</note>. Rather, it was ordained for the **inspiration and expiration** of the giant Earth itself. Thus, in the *Diastole* <note>The phase of the heartbeat when the heart muscle relaxes and allows the chambers to fill with blood</note>, the Earth seems to dilate as if by the retreating tide, and in that time it absorbs subtle water and even air into its bowels. But in the *Systole* <note>The phase of the heartbeat when the heart muscle contracts and pumps blood from the chambers into the arteries</note>, by contracting itself in a certain way—or by the hidden virtue of nature—it expels superfluities through its "marine mouth" as well as through its pores, creating the incoming tide. 

It is not enough for those who will argue that the ebb and flow are not universal; for by the same logic, it is well known that the lungs in a man are not in the whole body, but in a single place most convenient for respiration and expiration. We see a similar motion in the gills of recently caught fish, which they now contract and now dilate, just like the ebb and flow of the sea. 

But now I know it will be objected against us: if this is probable and consistent with reason, let the reason be shown why there is not as much time between the *Systole and Diastole* of a human as there is between the ebb and flow of the sea? We answer that the larger the animals are, the slower is their motion in breathing in and out. The Earth is an animal of immense magnitude, so that a long time is required for the complete inspiration of its spirit, its dilation through all its inner limbs and members, and likewise for its expiration. 

Salomon <note>King Solomon, traditionally the author of Ecclesiastes</note> seems to prove this same thing by its effect, asserting that: "All the rivers enter into the sea, yet the sea does not overflow; to the place from whence the rivers come, thither they return, to flow again" <note>original: "Eccl. c. 1"; referring to Ecclesiastes 1:7</note>. From this, he seems to argue that the thinner part of the sea, free from all saltiness, is drawn into the bowels of the earth by inspiration along with the air dispersed everywhere in those waters. There, what is pure and suitable for the sustenance of earthly creatures is reserved by the **Archeus** <note><term>Archeus</term>: In Paracelsian philosophy, the "inner alchemist" or vital force located in an organ that separates the useful from the waste</note>, the servant of nature. The rest is converted into vapor, which, as it moves through the veins and pores, is condensed into drops. From a multitude of these drops joined together, springs are created for the benefit of creatures, and especially for man, who is the end of all creatures. From the union of springs and rivulets, rivers result, which hasten their way back to the sea from whence they originated. 

In this sense, there will be an agreement (though it might not appear so at first glance to all philosophers) between the opinion of **Aristotle**—which is that the origin of springs is from terrestrial vapor frozen into water—and that of **Salomon**—which is that springs arise from the sea and tend toward the sea from which they were derived. <meta>This page continues the author’s argument that the Earth is a living organism mirroring the human body. Having previously discussed the Earth's "breathing," the author now explores the specific layers or "regions" of the air and how atmospheric phenomena—which he calls "meteors"—affect both the health of the world and the human spirit.</meta>

-># On the Material Cause of Atmospheric Phenomena #<-

Neither Aristotle nor anyone else could fully perceive the origin of those vapors as Solomon did; nor would I wish the readers of our writings to think that my opinion regarding the **breathing in and breathing out** of the earth is vain, simply because, as far as I know, it has been devised by no one before this time. This theory consists in the mystery of the flow and ebb of the sea, since it is certain beyond doubt that more things still lie hidden from men than have been revealed to them. We shall declare the difference between the **Peripatetics** <note>Followers of Aristotle's philosophy</note> and the Holy Scriptures more than sufficiently in the following sections.

But let us proceed in this comparison of ours between the external aspect of man and the earth. We find in the spiritual or airy—that is, the **internal man**—three regions of air varying from one another in purity, thinness, and composition. For the **animal spirits** <term>spiritus animales: the "spirits" of the mind and senses, thought to reside in the brain</term> are composed of the purer air; the **vital spirits** <term>spiritus vitales: spirits responsible for heat and life, centered in the heart</term> from the medium air; and the **natural spirits** <term>spiritus naturales: spirits responsible for nutrition and growth, centered in the liver</term> from the denser air. In respect to these, the air expanded universally through the vast cavity of the world reflects this: the first or "animal" air is likened to the substance of the **Empyrean** <note>The highest, most refined part of the heavens</note> world, whence it is the vehicle of reason and sense. The middle or "vital" air is likened to the **ethereal spirit**, which is midway between the highest and the middle. The lowest or "natural" air is likened to the **sublunary spirit**, which is commonly called "air." Furthermore, regarding the air below the moon, the animal spirits relate to the highest region of that air, the vital to the middle, and the natural to the lowest. For it is the lowest region of air that contributes to the nutrition of the body; the middle region regards life and the procreation of arterial blood; and the highest contributes to the senses and the inner faculties of the soul.

Does the earth not also have within itself as many grades or regions of its own internal air or spirit, in imitation of the mundane and human air? Since in its supreme region is found the **animal kingdom**, which is of a more fiery and Empyrean nature, according to the intentions of all Philosophers; then the **vegetable power** occupies its middle region, which participates in the nature of air and ether, or of thinner water; and its lowest region is the **mineral and metallic**, which consists of thick water from which metals are procreated—just as in man the natural power procreates the solid parts. Moreover, these spirits, or "double air"—namely, both the human and the earthly—were infused into them by the Creator from the universal bosom of the sublunary air at their creation. Thus, there is no difference between this particular enclosed air and that universal air expanded everywhere in the elementary region, except in its location. They agree, I say, in nature, and they cohere together in an inviolable bond, not unlike how terrestrial water has an inseparable union with the sea through the rivers. Hence, the parts of the one and the other are most fit to be bound and mixed together in inseparable conjunction, no differently than water with water. 

From this it happens that the disposition of a smaller portion is easily changed into that of a larger one. For we observe that fresh rivers poured into the salt sea migrate and are transformed into its salty nature. In exactly the same way, air that is infected universally is noticed to pollute not only the earth but also its creatures, both animal and vegetable, with its breath. From these things it is right to conclude that **meteors** <note>original: "meteora" - In this era, "meteors" referred to all atmospheric phenomena, including rain, wind, lightning, and comets</note>, whether fiery, airy, or watery, scattered in the vast air, infect the air of both man and the earth. Indeed, if the meteors are from the higher region of the open air, they tend to penetrate the internal spirit of man because of the thinness of their "seeds." 

Hence it happens that **comets** and other such fiery meteors of the highest air region are also said to excite the rational spirits of men toward passions—namely, anger, war, and dangerous imbalances <note>original: "dyscrasias"</note>—and to procreate plagues in the very marrow of the spirits. So also, pestiferous vapors in the bowels of the earth are stirred up by the entrapment of air full of meteorological "seeds," which the earth draws in through inspiration; it even infects fruits and animals with its breath, so that the food of man becomes more deadly than the corrupted air drawn to his heart through breathing. And from this, for the most part, we see **epidemic diseases** arise, which tend to proceed and happen more from the corrupted nature of nourishment than from an evil alignment of the heavens—though the heavens also contribute primarily to the corruption of food. 

Man, therefore, has his own "meteors" which are procreated in imitation of those in the world's air in every region. These arise from invisible seeds dispersed in the world's air, introduced with the air through breathing (both by the movement of the lungs and the attraction of the pores) and mixed with the human spirit. From this, both diseases (which we call "malignant meteors") and health are procreated by either harmful or beneficial meteors, as will be explained more copiously in its proper place. The earth also has its own proper meteors, which very easily mix their own "sperms"—whether healthy or poisonous—with the human spirit by means of human drink and food.

That the earth suffers from contagious diseases and various passions, we gather from these facts: for in an **earthquake**, she herself is heard to groan, and to bellow as if with the voice of thunder, as if she were seen to be afflicted by some contagious and painful disease. From this it happens that, besides her horror and trembling (by which she suddenly raises peaceful seas on high and destroys towers and palaces), she also infects nations and the people of cities with a lamentable plague and devastates them with contagion. We also see her sometimes sterile, and languishing as if with **alopecia** <note>A medical term for hair loss, here used metaphorically for a landscape stripped of vegetation</note>; sometimes suffering from sulfurous inflammations and reduced to lime and ashes by burning; sometimes corrupted by poisonous waters and turned into a filthy and diseased swamp; sometimes submerged by a flood of waters and as if suffocated and made slimy and putrid; sometimes dried into dust and wounded with cracks and gashes; sometimes even seething with foggy sweats and exhaling the vapors of sighs, and infinite...

...preternaturally affected by passions of this kind. All these "accidents" <note>In philosophy, "accidents" are non-essential properties or events that happen to a substance</note> are received from the meteorological passions of the external air, which infect its internal spirit (which is itself derived from the external air). This is testified by philosophers and astrologers, as well as those more skilled in **theosophy** <note>original: "theolosophia" — divine wisdom or mystical philosophy</note>. *By all these languors (I say) the earth is affected; for although it was first ordained for the benefit of man—healthy and free from passions—it is now rendered cursed and morbid because of the sin of Adam. Thus, it afflicts man with diseases, painful languors, and a lack of harvest, punishing him for his disobedience; according to that saying of the Wise Man: For God is not the author of death, nor does He delight in the destruction of the living; for He created all things that they might exist, and the origins of the world were healthful, in which there is no poison of destruction, nor is the kingdom of the underworld upon the earth. But through the envy of the Devil, death entered into the world: Wisdom of Solomon 1:13 and 2:24.* 

But there are some who will undoubtedly rise up against this opinion of mine, asserting that no sensation exists within the earth, and consequently, that it can neither suffer nor be affected by pain. To these we shall likewise respond that they are very little practiced in the Sacred Scriptures, or have entirely forgotten their teaching. For we are taught by them (*as is held in the song of Ananias, Azarias, and Misael uttered in the fiery furnace* <note>Referring to the "Song of the Three Holy Children" found in the Greek additions to the Book of Daniel</note>) that it is for the Earth to bless the Lord, and to extol Him with praises forever above all things. We are instructed by that very passage that not only the earth, but also the Sun, Moon, stars, heaven, waters, and fire—indeed, even all other meteorological creatures—possess a sense and a certain instinct of reason to bless God and to magnify Him above all with praises. 

Furthermore, the Royal Psalmist says, *The Earth praises Jehovah, Psalm 69:34,* and elsewhere, *that the Earth trembled when God looked upon it, Psalm 104:32,* and that *the Earth, opening itself at the divine command, swallowed Dathan and his companions, Psalm 106:17.* We could review many other places establishing this same point, which might perhaps be tedious for the reader to review now—such as how we read that the Sun stood still in the heaven at the command of Joshua and prolonged the day, and so on in other instances. From this it is certain that the earth possesses not only life, but also sensation and a certain hidden reason. 

Those most skilled in the **mystery of the Magnet** <note>A reference to early geomagnetic science, likely influenced by William Gilbert's "De Magnete" (1600), which argued the Earth is a giant magnet</note> have also discovered that the earth has its own poles, its own circles, a **Zodiac**, an **Equinoctial**, **Solstitial**, and **Polar** lines. From this it follows that winds blow in its internal spirit from their own quarters no differently than those blow from the quarters of the world or the open air; but indeed, we recognize that such particular winds depend on those universal ones, as we shall show more clearly in what follows.

We conclude, therefore, that there is a universal **aerial sea** in the world, vivifying all the bodies of the world by its presence, permeating all beings, providing them with an internal spirit, and courteously imparting to them something of its own aerial nature. From this it happens that, according to the "temperament" or "intemperament" <note>The balance or imbalance of qualities like heat and moisture</note> of the universal air, any particular air—whether included within a body or otherwise—is very easily altered. Consequently, the bodies which are (so to speak) promiscuously bathed by these particular airs follow the conditions of those "included" spirits; they are altered by their temperament or lack thereof. And from here, philosophers and physicians concluded (and quite maturely so) that the **temperament of the body follows the temperament of the soul**. Hence it happens that when the internal spirit is disturbed by the external—whether by heat, cold, moisture, or dryness—the body in which it resides is also disturbed by the same afflictions. 

From these things, therefore, it is clearly declared that since the entire mass of **sublunary air** <term>sublunaris: the region of the atmosphere below the moon, subject to change and decay</term> is affected by a manifold kind of "meteors" (whether healthy or unhealthy), it is also necessary that the particular air of both the giant creature (the Earth) and the tiny creature (Man) be affected in the same way. Indeed, when the terrestrial spirit is infected by that worldly spirit, we see that the spirit of man also participates in those same passions. 

And this is why **famine**, **pestilence**, and **pestiferous fevers** are, for the most part, inseparable companions. Hence it is said that when a **comet** reigns, famine and plague are foretold; for famine argues for the sterility of the earth and the impurity and poisonous nature of the fruits nourished by that same spirit, as well as a corruption of the universal spirit. Thus it happens that the human spirit also suffers from the corrupted universal spirit (drawn in through breathing) and also from the terrestrial spirit (by way of nutrition). Indeed, sometimes the particular air is infected by the diseased condition of the earth, as sometimes appears in an earthquake, which a plague follows. And what is more, we say reciprocally that the human spirit by its own error corrupted that terrestrial spirit; whence it happened that because of Adam's sin, not only man but also the earth itself (which God originally ordained for the sons of men) was cursed and became deadly to man himself—but concerning these things, we shall speak more abundantly in the following pages.

## CHAPTER VIII.

### *On the three stages in the movement of growth and increase between simple air and meteorological bodies (or "imperfectly mixed" bodies), and on their mathematical reasoning.*

In the final chapter of the previous booklet, it was explained to you how a progression was made from nothing—or from the "bosom of matter" <note>original: *hylae gremio* — 'Hyle' is a Greek term for the fundamental, unformed "stuff" of the universe</note>—through the emanation of light toward unity. By the revelation of this light, another potential unity was produced, opposite in its disposition: namely, darkness. Thus, the progression moved from the **monad** <note>The number one; representing absolute unity or God</note> to the **dyad** <note>The number two; representing duality or the introduction of "the other"</note>, and from the **dyad** to the **triad** <note>The number three</note> through the introduction and production of the **moist spirit**. This spirit acts as a **glue** <note>original: *gluten*</note>, joining both extremes together just as the soul is joined to the body. Finally, all these things progress to the **quaternary** <note>The number four</note>, which completes the "simple world" by bringing the four distinct elements into active existence. These elements are the immediate starting points for all mixed things, just as in geometry, square surfaces are the immediate principles of a cubic body. We have depicted this order arithmetically as follows:

## CHAPTER VIII.

### *Concerning the three stages in the movement of expansion and growth between simple air and meteorological bodies (or "imperfect mixtures"), and concerning their mathematical ratio.*

In the final chapter of the preceding booklet, you have seen it declared that progression was made from nothing, or from the womb of primordial matter <note>original: *hylæ* — the Greek term *hyle* refers to the raw, unformed substance of the universe</note>, through the emanation of light toward unity. By the revelation of this light, another "potential unity" was produced, opposite in its nature—namely, darkness. Hence, there was a progression from the monad <note>The number one, representing unity or God</note> to the dyad <note>The number two, representing duality or opposition</note>, and from the dyad to the triad <note>The number three</note>, through the introduction and production of the moist spirit from these two. This spirit acts as a "glue," joining both extremes together like a soul joined with a body. Finally, all these progress to the quaternary number <note>The number four</note>, which brings the simple world to completion. This produces the four elements, differing from one another in their action; these are the immediate beginnings of all mixtures, just as in geometry square surfaces are the immediate principles of a cubic body. We have depicted this order arithmetically as follows:

<meta>This page continues the mathematical and metaphysical explanation of how the physical world is constructed. While the previous page established the "simple" world (the four elements), this page explains the "mixed" world—specifically "meteors"—using the same ratios of progression. It bridges the gap between the invisible elements and visible, complex life forms.</meta>

Sect. I. Port. IV. Part I. Book II.

<image-desc>A geometric diagram showing a triangular arrangement of dots. The dots are organized into five vertical columns of increasing height from left to right: the first column (labeled h. 4) has 1 dot, the second (i. 5) has 2, the third (k. 6) has 3, the fourth (l. 7) has 4, and the fifth (m. 8) has 5. Dashed horizontal and diagonal lines connect the dots, forming a triangular grid structure representing the progression of complexity.</image-desc>

In this order, **h. 4** relates to a perfectly mixed body just as **1. a** (or the light of simple progression) relates to **e. 4** (the four elements). Furthermore, just as **b. 2** signifies prime matter and form from which the four elements have progressed through multiplication, so indeed **e. 4** (or the four elements) denotes matter and form in the simplicity of the elements. From these, by further multiplication, mixed bodies proceed—becoming more numerous and more perfect the more deeply unity immerses itself into the multitude of matter. Therefore, just as the shining unity **1. a** is the simplest source of all simple things, so also **e. 4** (or the four elements) are the simplest origin of mixed bodies. In the progression of mixtures, the 5th order (the quintenary) relates to the others just as 2 relates to nothing (or darkness) among simple things. Similarly, the 6th order relates to the 5th as 2 relates to 1; the 7th to the 6th as 3 relates to 2; and finally, the 8th to the 7th as 4 relates to 3. 

As we see in the first progression—where, as light dawned, the number 2 was made—so also as the four elements gather themselves together in the "womb of the air" <note>original: *ventre vnius aeris*</note> (which is their parent, the universal spirit of the world), the first species of mixture is produced. From these come the winds and invisible "meteors" <note>In the 17th century, "meteor" referred to any atmospheric phenomenon, including rain, wind, or rainbows, not just falling stars.</note>, both fiery and watery. These gradually thicken by the force of the winds and visibly take on a fiery nature, which is indicated by the 6th order. This 6th order has a relationship to the number 3 of the simple progression, in which either the water is abundantly illuminated by light (denoting "fiery meteors" in the second degree of mixtures), or the water prevails over the light (indicating "thunderous meteors"). 

Finally, the 7th degree shows more dense and dark meteors, such as clouds of hail and snow, as well as rain and other things of that kind. If these proceed even further into composition, they coalesce into perfectly mixed bodies. For this must be known for certain: all bodies—animal, vegetable, and mineral—are nothing other than clouds or meteors produced unto a state of perfect mixture. For who can doubt that anything perfectly mixed was once imperfectly mixed? It is necessary that imperfection stands between the simple elements and the completely composed ones, since it is impossible to find two extremes where a middle ground between the "point of departure" and the "point of arrival" is missing. Thus, we observe in the movement toward birth <note>original: *generationem*</note> that the seed is a kind of imperfect mixture, like a cloud or "little mist" of generation, which proceeds steadily by natural motion until it reaches the complete production of a fetus or a perfect mixture.

We say, therefore, that a meteor is called an "imperfect mixture" because it is "on the way" <note>original: *in via*</note>, or in natural motion, having arisen among the simple elements in the womb of the air, and moving toward the goal of perfection for the species it intends to become. But if, due to some obstacle in the way, it fails in its motion so that it cannot progress further on the path of perfection, it gradually retreats back into its simple nature from which it was first derived. If it is procreated by "poisonous winds" <note>original: *ventis venenosis*</note> or malevolent spirits blowing together, it then infects the air for the most part and brings a bad omen. But if it is procreated from benevolent breaths by the divine power, it sometimes purges and cleanses the air, bringing a good and propitious omen to the earth and its fruits; it is even proven to be healthy for the lives of animals, God willing. Nor should it be doubted that meteors contribute to the production of perfectly mixed things, since we are taught by experience that frogs, worms, and monstrous animals—likewise flesh, blood, grain and other fruits, and even stones, sand, and dust, and other such wonders—have fallen from the clouds and the air by the blowing of the winds. It must be known, therefore, that there are meteors of both generation and corruption.

# BOOK THREE.

## Member I.

### Concerning the formal cause of Meteors.

### Chapter I of Member I.

->*He treats precisely the formal cause of the Meteors of both worlds, as well as their differences.*<-

Since in the preceding book we have discussed the material origin of the meteors <note>In this period, "meteor" referred to any atmospheric phenomenon, including rain, wind, clouds, and lightning, not just falling stars.</note> of both worlds enough and more (as it seems to us), I now intend to discourse upon their **formal cause** <term>formal cause: the internal essence or "blueprint" that gives a thing its specific shape and identity</term>, though in few and succinct words, for the sake of a more certain method. Just as we declared in the previous sections that the material cause of meteors is the substance from which they are all composed—namely, a thinner portion of air, more or less compressed according to the nature of the meteor—so we also affirm that their formal cause is that by which those meteors are "carved out" or sketched from the vast and invisible mass of the world’s air. It is this cause that brings them into visible reality and gives them their specific names and essences. 

This formal cause "dresses" or shapes various aerial vapors into different figures. This diversity of shapes or images arises from the hidden and internal form of the meteors, just as a human's external figure or "icon" proceeds from an internal essence unique to them. It is this internal essence that makes a human's structure different from that of animals or plants, allowing us to recognize from a distance that a specific person is neither a beast nor a plant. 

By this same reasoning, we distinguish a "dark" meteor from a "bright" one—that is, one species from another—and more specifically, we distinguish one bright thing from another, or one opaque thing from another. For example, we observe that a comet, a flash of lightning, or a "burning spear" <note>original: "lanceam... ardentem"; likely a reference to a linear atmospheric phenomenon like a meteor trail or a specific type of aurora</note> or column of fire differs from a cloud, a mist, a halo, or dew. Even within the same category, we see that a comet varies from a burning column or a lightning flash by this same formal difference. Similarly, in the "dark kingdom" of phenomena, even the common eye discerns that a cloud is distinct from a mist, a mist from dew, and rain from frost. 

Therefore, in this treatise, by means of these formal causes, we first distribute meteors into their **genera** (general groups), then into their **species**, and finally, through various subdivisions, into infinite individuals. We do this just as one sees the trunk of a tree divide into branches, then into smaller divided twigs, and finally into little shoots, so that you may reach the goal of our intent by an easier method.

And since our purpose in this present treatise leads us to compare the meteors of the **Macrocosm** (the great world) with those of the **Microcosm** <term>Microcosm: the human being, viewed as a miniature reflection of the entire universe</term>, we do so to more clearly demonstrate the reasons for health or sickness. We achieve this by looking at the effects of the "good" or "bad" meteors generated within a person. Therefore, throughout the thread of this progression, after every chapter on the meteors of the Macrocosm, we will apply a correlation and comparison between those chapters and the parts of the Microcosm (humanity)—applying the meteors, humors, and properties of one to the other, as the subject and occasion for discussion arise.

We find it written, quite wisely, by Hermes Trismegistus <note>original: "Mercurio Trismegisto"; a legendary Hellenistic figure viewed as the founder of Hermetic philosophy, which links man to the universe.</note>, a most profound priest of wisdom, that the world is God's, but man is the world's son and image. For just as God originally brought the substance of the world into being out of nothing, so also He fashioned man from the matter of the already created world—his external part from the mud of the earth, and his internal part from the worldly, divine spirit, which had been previously adorned with the breath of life as a most precious gift, shaped by the reason and intellect of God. 

From this we observe that just as the vast house or vessel of the **Macrocosmic spirit** <term>Macrocosmic spirit: the vitalizing "breath" or energy of the entire universe</term> is the opaque Earth (without which no perfectly mixed substance in the sublunary world can be brought to completion, for the Earth is the matrix <note>In early science, "matrix" refers to a womb-like environment where things are formed.</note> of the worldly elements as well as of celestial and even super-celestial influences), so also it can escape no one's notice that the human spirit claims for itself a similar receptacle. This human receptacle is no different a vehicle for celestial and super-celestial influxes than the elemental air is in the Great World. 

From this it is clear how great and how close and necessary the relationship is between these two spirits and both of these bodies—namely, those of the Macrocosm and the Microcosm <term>Microcosm: "The Lesser World," referring to a human being as a reflection of the universe</term>. Indeed, since both the spirit and the body of the "lesser world" are derived from those of the "greater," it must infallibly follow that both the airy and ethereal spirit in man, and his opaque body, are sustained and nourished by that of the world, and remain in their state and existence at every moment because of it. They adhere to the parts of the world, both spiritual and bodily, by an unbreakable bond, such that they cannot be separated from one another even by death or the dissolution of the composite being. This is why, from the beginning, it has happened that when the elements of the "greater world" are sickly, the airy and terrestrial parts of man are also very quickly infected, as will be described more accurately in the following pages.

At their prompting, the sublunary demons (whether good or evil) are most obedient to them. They act with the force of fate in the form of **winds** within the air, water, and earth, working either toward the destruction, sickness, and unhappiness of mortals, or toward their health and preservation, according to the good pleasure of the Creator and the specific nature of their primary leader. 

The earth, therefore, attracts the worldly spirit, whether it is infected with good or evil celestial "juice." Thus, the spirit attracted into the earth by "breathing" is fit to procreate similar meteors in its "belly," for within it are the seeds both of meteors that appear visibly in the world's air and those that remain hidden. The same can be said of the human body, which every moment necessarily draws in a portion of the surrounding air through breathing.
