# On the Formal Cause of Meteors.
<note>original: "De Causâ Meteororum Formali." In this period, a "meteor" referred to any atmospheric phenomenon, including rain, snow, and hail, not just falling stars.</note>

...that he was deceived in this way has been explained in the preceding pages. Therefore, since the origin of snow is unknown, it is extremely difficult—indeed, truly impossible—to judge it solely by its effect. Let us see, then, what truth can be drawn from the Holy Scriptures on this matter, so that we may better and more correctly judge the aforementioned description given by the **Peripatetics**. <note>The Peripatetics were followers of the philosopher Aristotle, whose natural science dominated universities at the time.</note>

We have it confirmed by the testimony of the royal Prophet <note>referring to King David</note> that when **GOD** sends His word to the earth, His command runs very swiftly; He who "scatters snow like wool, and frost like ashes, He casts down His ice like morsels; who can stand before His cold?" *Psalm 147:15-17*. From these words, we gather that snow and the other frozen <term>meteors</term> <gloss>atmospheric phenomena</gloss> are procreated from cold through the mediation of the Word of **GOD**, or His Wisdom. Hence it is said elsewhere that cold comes from the **North winds**, and elsewhere, "By the breath of God ice is given," and that the mighty God produces ice by His breath, *Job 37:10*. <note>The text cites Job 27, but the quote corresponds to Job 37.</note> That is to say, God, from the center or the internal realm, moves and stirs His angelic ministers of the winds, or those presiding over the winds, who mingle themselves at His will in the "aerial sea" to fulfill either the freezing or the dissolving of waters. For everything that is done in this world ought to be rightly attributed to God as the First Mover (following the manner of the Holy Scriptures) and not to the creature (after the manner of the **Pagan Philosophers**), since the creature is moved primarily by **GOD**. Thus it is said: *God breathing, God thundering, God striking, God being angry, God showing mercy, God leading, God inflicting a plague, God distilling the rains*, and so on.

But truly, how God sends forth His breaths, or by what method, or from what place the snow and other cold-constricted meteors come, is quite difficult—even impossible—for the human intellect to grasp, unless one is distinguished by the teachings of Divine Wisdom. Hence, Jehovah Himself, questioning Job on this matter, said: "Have you entered into the treasures of the snow? Or have you seen the treasures of the hail?" *Job 38:22*. By this He seems to hint at how secret and hidden their mystery is. For it is not sufficient to affirm with **Aristotle** that the cause of snow is "cold condensing vapor." Other matters of greater weight must concur in the investigation of such a mystery: namely, where do these cold effects come from? Even if they come from the winds, how are the winds themselves regulated by God? What kind of vapor is this? Is it from the thickened air above the earth, or does it leap up from the earth? And where is the seat of its generation?

In the preceding sections, therefore, it was said that by the breath of God and the most swift running of His Word, snow is procreated, *Psalm 147:16*. That the effect of that breath is cold is declared therein, for it concludes: "Who can stand before His cold?" From this it is clear that by the Word of God, the strong Northern blasts are stirred up along with the gentler Southern ones. From which it follows: "He sends out His word and melts them; He causes His wind to blow, and the waters flow," *Psalm 147:18*; that is, the snows are dissolved. That the substance of snow is drawn from the secret bosom of the air is noted in the question: "Have you entered into the treasures of the snow?" *Job 38:22*. Here, by "treasures," he means the heavens, according to the verse: "Jehovah shall open His good treasure, the heavens, to give the rain to your land in its season," *Deuteronomy 28:12*. In this context, by "heavens" He means the **air**, as it is the common treasury-chest of the meteors, as was said before.

Therefore, in the bosom of the air and from the consistency of the thickened air—as the material cause—all such meteors are formed, with the Divine Will acting as the first efficient cause. Therefore we say that the breath of the gentle **South wind** <note>original: "Australis"</note> applies the material by the positioning of the parts of the air for the snows (for it is the nature of that wind to thicken the air), while the coagulating disposition of the **North wind** <note>original: "septentrionalis"</note>, blowing more strongly and with greater dominance, freezes the air thus contracted in a moderate way. Thus snow is made, the substance of which is partly frozen and partly fit for dissolving—and it is more fit for dissolving the greater the force of the South wind. The internal act of these things is from the Word fulfilling the will of the Father.

From this it is clear that **Aristotle’s** reasoning is most false when he asserts that the matter of snow is "vapor exhaled from the earth and water," and likewise that the coldness of the middle region of the air is the cause of coagulation, and the heat of the stars the cause of its elevation. In truth, the matter is the air above the earth, thickened by the blasts of the winds; the first mover is the **Word**, present everywhere according to the will of the Creator, who by His occult power performs these wonders—not merely by cold or heat, though these may be external effects of His internal operation. Indeed, if this were not so, it would be impossible for snow and hail to remain in the same mixture with fire (whose nature is to dissolve frozen things and blunt cold effects) without the alteration or dissolution of both. Hence it is written: "Snow and hail endured the force of fire and did not melt, that they might know that the fire burning in the hail and flashing in the rain destroyed the fruits of the enemies," *Wisdom 16:22*.

From this it is evident that Snow is of a far higher intention and more mystical to the intellect than to be produced in the way proposed and marked out for us by **Aristotle**. For against his assertion—in which he says the substance of snow is vapor rising from the elements of water and earth, massed into the likeness of carded wool by the cold of the place in which it is generated—we are taught by the Holy Scriptures that the place from which its material is drawn is the "treasures," which He calls the heavens and the air, and not from water or earth. Furthermore, we say according to the testimony of the Holy Page that the cause reducing the substance of the air into the form of wool is the **breath of Jehovah**, the effect of which is cold. It is as if one were to say that by God breathing from the Northern region, the cloudy substance of the air (which the light and remiss breath of the South wind has thus formed) freezes into the shape of carded wool.

However, how the Divine Will (which Jehovah placed in the elements of the world) acts in the minds of the **angels**—who preside over both the constricting and loosening winds and who possess the four corners of the world—to make them obedient to His command in the blink of an eye, we shall explain clearly enough in our treatise on the *supernatural efficient cause of meteors*.

But to the description of snow according to the sense of the Holy Scriptures, which differs vastly and overtly from the opinions of the Pagans, we thus proceed.

<meta>This page continues the investigation into the nature of frozen atmospheric phenomena, transitioning from the general divine origin of cold to specific definitions and critiques of the "Peripatetic" (Aristotelian) theories of snow and hail. Sect. I. Port. IV. Part. II. Lib. III. Membr. II.

Snow is a <term>meteor</term> <gloss>atmospheric phenomenon</gloss> which **GOD**, bringing it forth from His hidden treasuries, sends upon the lands according to His will—just like wool—either for a blessing or to execute a scourge.

->Or thus:<-

Snow is a created thing, produced from the air or the heavens—which is **GOD'S** treasury-chest—by means of the divine breath and cold, appearing like carded wool to fulfill the divine will.

->Or thus:<-

Snow is an <term>imperfectly mixed creature</term> <note>original: "creatura imperfecte mixta." In early science, "meteors" like snow and rain were called "imperfectly mixed" because they were transient and did not form stable, permanent substances like stones or animals.</note> which the mighty **GOD** brings forth from His heavenly treasuries; He makes it congeal by His breath, so that whatever the Creator Himself has commanded it to do upon the surface of the earth—whether for a blessing or for punishment and a scourge—it may immediately perform and execute.

In these descriptions, it is primarily noted that Snow is a created thing, and consequently not eternal. Secondly, that the place from which it is drawn is the treasury of **GOD**, and that this treasury is the heaven or the air, and consequently it is neither water nor earth. Thirdly, that its material cause is the substance of the air or heaven from which it is originally drawn—not otherwise than the bones and flesh of a chick were potentially in the yolk of the egg before they were brought into reality. Fourthly, the efficient cause is explained: namely, that it is the divine breath or spirit. For **GOD** acts centrally by His will, ordering all things, and His Word or Wisdom carries out His will, just as a son does for a father; and the Angels, as ministers of the Word (since it is their role to make the Divine Word effective, as the royal Psalmist testifies), immediately execute what has been ordained by **GOD**. Therefore, it is not correctly said that angels, or cold, or any other created thing performs this or that; rather, it is **GOD** Himself, who is the primary actor or author. For that which belongs to **GOD** the Creator must not be attributed to a created thing. This was the error of the Heathens, the very source and origin of Idolatry, who for that reason used to worship the creature instead of the Creator in a false manner. Finally, in the last place, the final cause of this phenomenon is explained: namely, that it is ordained to execute either the Creator's blessing or His wrath upon the earth, just like other atmospheric phenomena.

The **Peripatetics** <note>Followers of Aristotle’s philosophy.</note> also place no small difference between the generation of Snow and Hail, as they fall into this opinion: namely, that hail arises from a warm vapor, which the surrounding cold in the middle region of the air first penetrates because of the vapor's thinness, condensing it into a cloud. They then claim that this cloud, having been broken up and falling drop by drop, is compressed into ice through <term>antiperistasis</term> <note>original: "antiperistasin." An old philosophical theory that a quality (like cold) becomes more intense when surrounded by its opposite (like heat).</note> by the penetrating cold, as well as by the heat of the lowest region of the air; thus, it falls in rounded and angular fragments of ice. This is their view, in which description they establish that hail is first procreated from warm vapor rising from the earth and water; then, that vapor is coagulated into a hailstorm cloud by the cold of the middle region of the air; and finally, that cloud, having dissolved into drops, is reduced during its fall from the middle region of the air into innumerable fragments by the cold of that place.

But **Aristotle** himself admits that hail is nothing other than the freezing of rain, caused by cold and wind in the air. And yet, elsewhere he seems to assert nonetheless that hail is generated in clouds very far distant from the earth, and he says the cause of the generation of hail is vapor received into the cavity of a cloud, which vapor he claims is thickened by the coldness of the air.

**Bede** <note>The Venerable Bede (c. 672–735 AD), an English monk and scholar.</note> maintains that, just as the North wind is cold and dry, so by its breath it freezes and constricts the dewy drops descending from heaven, converting them into hail.

And so we see that the **Peripatetics** themselves—both the Heathens and the Christians affected by them—are in every way confused and uncertain in their opinions. The reason for this is that they seem to be ignorant of the true internal agent (or central act) and the primordial material cause of meteorological things. They attribute the praises and the name of "creation" to created things or effects, and not to **GOD** the Creator, in the manner of fools who think in their hearts there is no **GOD**, since they understand all things only as they appear in external vision. But let us now gird our loins for the examination of the descriptions above; we shall attempt to complete this first with the **Lydian stone** <note>A touchstone used to test the purity of gold; here, a metaphor for a test of truth.</note> of true Philosophy, and then afterwards by the most penetrating fire and light of the Divine Page.

In their first description, they establish the primary matter of hail to be vapor; the second to be the cloud, which they therefore call "hail-bearing"; and the third to be the breaking up of the cloud into raindrops. They posit a twofold efficient cause: namely, the cold of the middle and even the lowest region of the air, which holds the power of constriction or freezing; and heat, to which they attribute the faculty of dissolution and division.

For the refutation of that **Peripatetic** opinion—where they claim that vapors rising from the element of water are the origins of clouds—we would refer you to our preceding chapter, where we treated the origin of mist and clouds in a more sincere manner. In that place, we left it proven by reasons established both by our own experience and the doctrine of the Holy Bible, that clouds were by no means composed of vapors ascending from the watery or earthy element, but were made by the condensation of air by winds blowing from opposite directions. Without a doubt, this same thing is the beginning of the substance and composition of the body of hail: namely, the hidden substance of the air or celestial matter, turned into the manifest and visible matter of hail at times, just as at other times it becomes snow, rain, or frost, according to the manner of the gaze of the Divine Will.

# On the Formal Cause of Meteors.

In the second part of their description, they seem to waver, in that they call a cloud "hail-bearing" even before it has taken on the nature or appearance of hail, any more than that cloud from which only rain is observed to gush and sift down; for they recognize the appearance and form of hail in drops falling after being released from the cloud, and especially following within the cloud itself. Furthermore, if the matter stood as they have dreamed, why by that same reasoning would the drops of rain not also be frozen? These are quite often observed to fall along with hail, and they undoubtedly feel and suffer the freezing cold of the place just as much as that substance of the hail does. But truly, if there be any difference between a hail-bearing cloud and a rain-bearing one, why is the entire substance of that cloud not converted into ice, since it is certain and approved by all philosophers that the middle region of the air abounds and is stiff with cold? Consequently, from where did such great heat arise in the cloud that it melts and flows in the middle region of the air (where the effects of a whirlwind are cold), yet conversely, the drops proceeding from it in the lowest region of the air (in which heat predominates due to the various reflections of the heavenly rays) are frozen again?

And again, we see that hailstorms are usually more frequent in the month of April, and indeed in summer, than in winter—times when the temperature of the air overflows with heat, and consequently, that region is less fit to freeze liquid drops falling from the clouds. How has it happened (<note>The author is addressing the "Peripatetics," the traditional followers of Aristotle's philosophy.</note> my Peripatetics) that the greatest error lies hidden in this description of yours? That is undoubtedly not the chest or dwelling-place of truth. But if you reply with your Master Aristotle that the hail-cloud is very far distant from the earth, and that the drops—while distilling from the cloud and passing through the space of the middle region—are frozen by the force of the cold of that place, which is increased more through <term>antiperistasin</term> <note>original: "antiperistasin." An ancient physical theory suggesting that a quality, like cold, intensifies when it is surrounded by its opposite, like the heat of summer.</note> in the times of summer and spring: I respond that by this very same reasoning, the substance of a cloud floating in the midst of such a region ought to be constricted and bound together into a glacial substance by such vigor of cold, so that it could not be reduced into the pre-supposed liquid droplets due to the lack of dissolving heat.

As for that second description brought forth by Aristotle, truth itself prohibits us from confessing or defending its integrity. For if hail (according to his opinion) were nothing other than the freezing of rain droplets, produced by cold and wind in the air, we can see no reason why the rain drops descending together with the hail are not, by the same reasoning, converted into hail, since the temperature of the air is equal in coldness. For he undoubtedly understands this to happen in the lowest region of the air, since he seems to recognize cold winds as the causes acting upon the freezing of the drops. But truly (as was demonstrated above), he seems to deny the entry of winds into the middle region of the air, as it is a place into which windy exhalations (as he thinks) are not permitted to penetrate. Is he not also observed to contradict himself in this: that he makes the cause of the generation of hail to be vapor received into the cavity of a cloud, in whose belly he does not blush to assert that it thickens and freezes because of the coldness of the place and the air?

But what else, I pray, is a cloud than thickened vapor? And if vapor be added to vapor, it must necessarily pass into the same nature of vapor—not otherwise than when water is added to water, it is accustomed to constitute a single water, not of different forms. Therefore, if the enclosed vapor is of the same nature as that which encloses it, there will be no reason why, upon the freezing of a part, the whole should not also gradually freeze. But we have the argument of his contradiction in this: that in his prior assertion, he calls hail nothing other than the condensation of rain droplets.

But truly, rain occurs after the resolution of a cloud; yet in the latter [assertion], he relates that hail is made not from rain droplets, but from the freezing of vapor received into the cavity of the cloud. How contrary these two things are, I commend to your judgments (readers, you guardians of the scales of justice).

We now approach that opinion of <note>Saint Bede the Venerable, an 8th-century English monk and scholar.</note> Bede, which we shall pass over lightly since it does not recede far from the truth. He makes the North wind the efficient cause of hail, and that not without consideration, since cold is derived from it. However (by his leave), he speaks more from the effect and about the effect than about the internal acting cause. This cause we make threefold, differing in dignity and rank: namely, the Creator breathing centrally according to His hidden will; His Word, which does His will; and the angels whose task it is to execute those things which are presented by the Word of **GOD**. Thus **GOD** ordains according to the property of His name; the Word of **GOD** disposes the things ordained in the manner of a royal prince; and the windy angels execute what was ordained by the Word or divine will. The effects of the execution are cold, heat, moisture, and dryness, and those things which follow secondarily from them, such as thickness, ice, snow, and thinness—from which rain, hail, comets, the <term>flying dragon</term> <note>original: "draco volans." A term used for a fireball or a specific type of streaking meteor.</note>, <term>will-o'-the-wisp</term> <note>original: "ignis fatuus." Literally "foolish fire," referring to phosphorescent lights seen over marshes, then classified as a type of meteor.</note>, and other such things arise by various and hidden operations.

But let us bring forth the aforementioned opinions and descriptions of the Peripatetics—whether Heathen or Christian—to the testimony of the Divine Scriptures, or to the Lydian stone <note>A touchstone used to test the purity of gold.</note>, as if to the examination of a most penetrating fire, so that we may better see whether there is truth in them or not.

Sect. I. Port. IV, Part. II. Lib. III. Membr. II.

Therefore, without controversy, Aristotle is mistaken, and the <term>Peripatetics</term> <note>Followers of Aristotle’s philosophy.</note> are mistaken, regarding both the "mine" of the hail-meteor and the consistency of its substance.

Furthermore, they ascribe the reason for the shaping and formation of these hailstones to the cold of the air itself, whereas the Scriptures of truth ascribe all these things to God and His word, which the angels are said to carry out; hence we find written:

> He sends His word to the earth, and it runs very swiftly; He gives snow like wool and scatters frost like ashes; He casts forth His ice like morsels; who can stand before His cold? Psalm 147:16.

From this it is clear that the agent for the procreation of such meteors is God Himself, by means of His word, from whose cold breaths or **Northern angels** <note>original: "angelis Borealibus"</note> the cold is produced as a proximate effect; wherefore it is said:

> Who can stand before *His* cold?

It does not say "before the cold," but "before *His* cold," that is, that which arises from His breath. Wherefore it is also said elsewhere:

> The mighty God produces ice by His breath; by the breathing of God the frost is congealed. Job 37:9.

Moreover, they are surrounded and mixed with lightning on all sides, for Jehovah produced sounds, and fire ran along the ground. Therefore, the **Air** is the "patient" <note>The passive element acted upon.</note> in the composition of meteors, but the "agent" is the constrictive and freezing disposition and property of the Divine Name. These are whirled around in the violent motion of the gusts by a spiral revolution of the windy air, just as is observed in the meeting of two opposing rivers, where we notice foamy waters rotating and being driven in a circle. Hence it is that before or during the fall of hail, very loud and sometimes terrible sounds are heard in the air; indeed, even a murmur and a crash, and sometimes a noise as if of armed men, are perceived from above. # On the Formal Cause of Meteors

...will be explained more fully in the treatise on the supernatural <term>efficient cause</term> <note>The "efficient cause" is the agent or force that brings something into being; in this context, the author argues it is God rather than natural laws.</note> of meteors. We conclude, therefore, gathering from the doctrine and testimony of Holy Scripture, that hail is to be described in this manner:

> ->**Hail** is a certain hard and icy phenomenon, the matter of which the mighty God Jehovah <note>original: "DEVS fortis Iehoua"</note> draws from His treasures or His treasury—namely, the hidden bosom of the air—shaping and gathering it in the heavens into infinite little stones of water by His cold spirit or breath, separately freezing and compressing them; these He finally rains down and casts upon the lands to fulfill His will, whether by itself or accompanied by lightning and rain.<-

In this definition, there is first presented the "mine" of its matter or substance, which, according to the testimony of Holy Scripture, is extracted from His treasures (which we explained above to be the heavens or the air); from this it is clear that the substance of the air is the matter not only of hail, but of all other <term>meteors</term> <note>In the 17th century, "meteor" referred to any atmospheric phenomenon, including rain, snow, and hail.</note>. Next, it is explained that its <term>formal cause</term> <note>The "formal cause" refers to the specific shape or essence that makes a thing what it is—in this case, the icy, stone-like form of hail.</note> is received from the divine breath or inspiration as the efficient cause; for it is said that *the mighty God brings forth ice by His breath, and by the breath of God the frost is frozen. Job 37:10.* <note>The text cites Job 27:9, but this verse corresponds to Job 37:10 in modern Bibles.</note> And elsewhere: *He casts forth His ice like morsels; who can stand before His cold? Psalm 147:17.* <note>Original: "Psal. 147. 16."</note> Here, "morsels of ice" can be understood as hailstones, and consequently, it is confirmed that such hailstones are formed from the cold of Jehovah’s breath in the shape of watery pebbles. This extraction of the matter of hail and ice from the dewy bosom of the air is verified elsewhere: *The ice comes forth from the womb of the dew, and like a stone the waters are hidden, and the face of the deep is frozen.* This can be understood as much regarding the ice in the clouds of the middle region of the air as the surface of terrestrial waters, since clouds are called "the deep" <note>original: "abyssi"</note> elsewhere in the Bible, *Job 38:28.* Finally, the <term>final cause</term> <note>The "final cause" is the ultimate purpose or goal for which something exists.</note> is explained there: namely, to fulfill the divine will. Hence it is said elsewhere: *Cold, ice, frost, clouds, lightning—whatever God has commanded them to do upon the face of the world, whether for a scourge or for mercy, they perform it instantly. Job 37.* Furthermore, God sent or brought forth hail from heaven to harm and destroy the men, cattle, herbs, and trees of the Egyptians. *Exodus 9.* <note>Original: "Exod. 19." This likely refers to the plague of hail in Exodus 9.</note> Likewise, Jehovah sent down great stones of hail from heaven, with which He slew the enemies of the Israelites, *Joshua 10:11.*

Therefore, we gather from our description that the <term>material cause</term> of hail is extracted from the air; for in its substance it is nothing other than air, thickened into a cloudy consistency by contrary winds. Next, we have the formal cause in that it is reduced into the shape of watery pebbles, either round or angular; hence Joshua says, "Jehovah sends great stones of hail from the heavens." From this it is also clear that the place where the dense air is reduced into such an image by means of the divine breath is the heaven or the air. Furthermore, the efficient cause is the cold, freezing, and hardening breath of God. Finally, the final cause is most often punishment, a scourge, or a penalty: for the earth is made far more fertile by rain than by hail, the nature of which is to harm fruits, trees, and crops rather than to bring them any benefit or profit.

But now we have reached the third species of such solid meteors: namely, **Hoarfrost** <note>original: "Pruina"</note>, which does not seem to differ much from the others regarding its efficient cause, as it is the cold breath or inspiration of Jehovah.

**Aristotle**, along with his sect, defines this for Christians as a certain phenomenon arising from a moist and cold vapor rising from the element of water, which is not gathered into the thickness of a cloud; this phenomenon is frozen in the middle region of the air by the coldness of the place (where no heat is present) and the season, and is thus reduced into the form of hoarfrost.

**Others** (among whom I name **Bede** <note>Bede the Venerable (c. 672–735), an English monk and scholar.</note>) maintain that this phenomenon is nothing other than frozen dew, which, in its descent toward the earth, drinks in and receives the nocturnal cold, by means of which it puts on that white, hard, and cold appearance that is hoarfrost.

We turn then to that Aristotelian description and say that if its first part were true—namely, that the matter of hoarfrost was such a cold and moist vapor gushing and exhaling from the nourishment of water and earth—it would follow that the frost would diminish and decrease more and more every day. This is because, during frosty weather, the pores of the earth are closed by the freezing cold, so that neither plowshares nor other iron instruments can penetrate it; furthermore, the waters are usually shut away by such tight ice that we see fish dying in great quantities for lack of penetrating air. Yet everyone will admit that air is thinner than vapor. Since this is proven false by its effects, we say that Aristotle’s opinion regarding the substance or matter of hoarfrost is erroneous, as we do not see the frost decreasing daily from its state; rather, we observe it mostly growing stronger from day to day, clothing the earth and trees more and more in a **swan-like beard** <note>A poetic description of thick rime frost on branches.</note>.

The same must also be said regarding the material cause of hoarfrost explained in the second description: namely, that it is not made of the substance of dew, if we assume it arose and was procreated in the Aristotelian way—that is, from vapor exhaled from water and earth. But that opinion of Bede will be probable if he confesses with us that the entire matter of meteors consists in the power of the air.

But we proceed to the efficient cause of both, which Aristotle believes to be the cold of the middle air (in which he recognizes no heat), while Bede says the cold of the night is the cause of both the freezing and its white form.

...will be explained more fully in the treatise on the supernatural efficient cause of meteors. We conclude, therefore, from the doctrine and testimony of the sacred pages, that hail is to be described in this manner:

**Hail** <note>original: "Grando"</note> is a certain hard and icy impression, the matter of which the strong God Jehovah—drawing from his treasures or his treasury, namely the hidden bosom of the air—shapes and conglomerates into infinite little stones of water in the heavens by his cold spirit or breath, separately freezing and constricting them; these he finally rains down and casts upon the earth to fulfill his will, whether by itself or accompanied by lightning and rain.

In this definition, the "mine" or source of its matter and substance first presents itself, which, according to the testimony of Holy Scripture, is drawn from His "treasures," which we have explained above to be the heavens or the air. From this it is clear that the substance of the air is the matter not only of hail, but of all other <term>meteors</term> <note>In this context, "meteors" refers to any atmospheric phenomena, including rain, snow, and wind.</note>. Next, it is explained that its <term>form</term> <note>The "formal cause" refers to the specific shape or internal nature that makes a thing what it is.</note> is received from the divine breath or respiration as the <term>efficient cause</term> <note>The agent or force that brings something into being.</note>; for it is said: *By the breath of God frost is given, and the broad waters are frozen, Job 37:10* <note>The original text cites Job 27:9, but the quote corresponds to Job 37:10.</note>. And elsewhere: *He casts forth his ice like morsels: who can stand before his cold? Psalm 147:17.* Where by "morsels of ice" hail can be understood; consequently, it is confirmed that such hail is formed by the cold of Jehovah's breath in the shape of little stones of water. This extraction of the matter of hail and ice from the dewy bosom of the air is verified elsewhere: *Out of whose womb came the ice? and the hoary frost of heaven, who hath gendered it? The waters are hid as with a stone, and the face of the deep is frozen. Job 38:28-30.* This can be understood as much concerning the ice in the clouds of the middle region of the air as the surface of terrestrial waters, since clouds are elsewhere called "the deep" in the Bible. Finally, the <term>final cause</term> <note>The ultimate purpose or goal for which something exists.</note> is explained there: namely, to fulfill the divine will. Hence it is said elsewhere: *Fire, and hail; snow, and vapors; stormy wind fulfilling his word... whether for correction, or for his land, or for mercy. Job 37.* Furthermore, God sent or brought forth hail from heaven to harm and destroy the men, cattle, herbs, and trees of the Egyptians. *Exodus 9.* Likewise, Jehovah cast down great stones of hail from heaven, with which he slew the enemies of the Israelites. *Joshua 10:11.* 

Therefore, we gather from our description that the <term>material cause</term> <note>The substance out of which something is made.</note> of hail is extracted from the air; for in its substance it is nothing other than air, thickened into a cloudy consistency by contrary winds. Next, we have the formal cause in that it is reduced into the shape of little stones of water, either round or angular in appearance; hence Joshua says, *Jehovah cast down great stones of hail from the heavens.* From this it is also clear that the place where dense air is reduced into such an image by means of the divine breath is the heaven or the air. Furthermore, the efficient cause is the cold, freezing, and hardening breath of God. Finally, the final cause is most often punishment and a scourge or penalty: for the earth is rendered far more fertile by rain than by hail, whose nature is rather to damage fruit, trees, and crops than to bring them any benefit or profit.

But now we touch upon the third species of such solid meteors, namely **Hoar-frost** <note>original: "Pruinam"</note>, which seems not to differ much from the others regarding its efficient cause, as it is the cold breath or respiration of Jehovah.

**Aristotle**, along with the Christians of his sect, defines this as a certain impression from a moist and cold vapor rising from the element of water, not gathered into the thickness of a cloud; this impression is frozen in the middle region of the air by the coldness of the place (where no heat is present) and the time, and is reduced into the form of hoar-frost.

Others (among whom I name **Bede**) <note>Referring to the Venerable Bede (672–735 AD), an English monk and scholar.</note> maintain that this kind of impression is nothing other than frozen dew, which in its descent toward the earth drinks in and receives into itself the nocturnal cold, by means of which it puts on that white, hard, and cold appearance that is hoar-frost.

We approach that Aristotelian description, and we say that if its first part were true—namely, that the matter of hoar-frost was such a cold and moist vapor springing and exhaling from the nourishment of water and earth—it would follow that the frost would diminish and decrease more and more every day. This is because in the weather of hoar-frost, the pores of the earth are closed by the freezing cold, so that neither plowshares nor other iron instruments can penetrate it; furthermore, the waters are for the most part shut up by such tight ice that we see fish dying in great quantities for lack of penetrating air. But truly, everyone will admit that air is thinner than vapor. Since this is proven false by its effect, we say that Aristotle's opinion concerning the substance or matter of hoar-frost is erroneous, as we do not see the frost decrease daily from its state, but rather we observe it for the most part growing stronger from day to day, and clothing the earth and the trees more and more in a **swan-like beard** <note>original: "barba cygnea"; a poetic description of thick, white frost covering branches.</note>.

The same must also be said concerning the material cause of hoar-frost explained in the second description: namely, that it is not of the substance of dew, if we conclude it to be arisen and procreated in the Aristotelian way—that is, from vapor expired from the waters and the earth. But that opinion of Bede will be probable if he agrees with us that the entire matter of meteors consists in the power of the air.

But we proceed to the efficient cause of both, which Aristotle believes to be the cold of the middle air, in which he recognizes no heat; Bede, however, says the coldness of the night is the cause, both of the freezing and of its white form.

### On the Formal Cause of Meteors.

...will be explained more abundantly in the treatise concerning the supernatural efficient cause of <term>meteors</term> <note>In this period, "meteors" referred to any atmospheric phenomena, including rain, hail, and wind.</note>. From this, it is clear that the substance of the air is the matter not only of hail, but of all other meteors. Next, it is explained that its form is received from the divine breath or breathing as the efficient cause; for it is said that *the mighty God brings forth ice by His breath, and by the breath of God the frost is produced* <note>original: "DEVS fortis edat glaciem flatu suo flante DEO concrefcat gelu." # Section I. Portion IV. Part II. Book III. Member II.

We, however, say that the primary, most principal, and internal cause is **God** alone, who through the **Word** <note>The "Word" here refers to the *Logos* or the second person of the Trinity as the creative force.</note> incites His angelic winds to fulfill His will, both in the heavens and on the earth. The actions of these winds are assigned to **GOD** as the central and primary operator, as they are the ministers of **GOD**, ready to execute those things ordained by **GOD** as the First Mover. Hence it is said that **GOD**, sending forth His word, *scatters the frost like ashes; who can stand before His cold?* <note>original: "pruinam quasi cineres dispergat, coram frigore eius quis consistat?" For just as in matter there is only a single material cause, which is the created universal spirit of the world; so also there is but one single efficient and acting cause upon that matter, which is the uncreated Form or Light. And although **GOD** the Father can be called one agent, and the Son or the Word another, and the Holy Spirit yet another, and consequently infinite creatures which have their powers of acting immediately from them; nevertheless, in the Divinity there is but one Deity and one Spirit, by whom all spirits are created and acquire life and actions. This is no different than how all other parts of the world are filled by the rays of a single sun, and yet none of those rays can be distinguished or separated from the unity of that one sun, as **Mercurius Trismegistus** <note>A legendary Hellenistic figure associated with hermetic philosophy.</note> testifies. For whatever is perfected in vegetation or in vivification from the lucid fountain of the sun, we attribute all of it to the sun, and not to any specific ray of it. Thus **Orpheus** and the other **Platonists** assigned a peculiar **GOD** to every creature of the world, and yet they referred all these particular **GODS** to a single **Jupiter**, just as all the rays of the sun expanded everywhere through the world are referred to one sun. Hence the Evangelist says: *All things were created by Him, and without Him was nothing created; in Him was life, etc.* (John 1). And Saint **Paul**: *From Him, in Him, and through Him are all things.* And elsewhere we find that the incorruptible spirit of **GOD** is in all things.

Therefore, it is not without consideration that the creation of every creature, whether perfectly or imperfectly composed, is attributed to the primary and unique cause, and not to its effects; thereby excluding the creature from the honor due to the Creator, so that no species of idolatry might follow. Hence **Job** said: *By His breath the mighty God produces ice, snow, and frost; when God breathes, the frost congeals* (Job 37:10; Job 27:9). We conclude, therefore, that snow and hail are impressions in the air, formed when opposing or transverse winds are applied and condensed into the form of a cloud. These are reduced into this or that shape by the divine breath producing cold, according to the stronger or weaker predominance of the blowing winds. For example, when the South Wind blows more weakly while the North Wind is still stronger, soft snows and such clouds are generated; but when the South Wind blows more strongly along with a stronger Northern wind, grainy or hailing clouds for the most part arise. Furthermore, a strong Northern wind, when an opposing wind blows only slightly or not at all (whereby the air is condensed into a cloud), is accustomed to bring forth frost and ice. I say "frost" because the Northern wind, blowing according to the divine will, constricts the moist and moderately dense nature of the air by its breath springing from the first act; from which the denser part, thus constricted, falls onto trees and herbs. Indeed, falling upon the waters, and with that breath now assisting and persevering, it immediately results in ice and unites itself with the surface of the water. Thus, the hard form of ice is established and shaped upon the waters because the warm vapors expiring from the waters and the bowels of the earth cause that frost or ice to appear on the surface of the waters, rather than within the sphere of the water itself. And this glacial crust is strengthened day by day through the addition of new air congealed by cold blasts on the upper part. That crust is hardened through <term>antiperistasis</term> <note>original: "antiperistasin." A physical theory where a quality is intensified by being surrounded by its opposite, such as cold becoming more intense when trapped by heat.</note>, as the cold acts on its exterior surface by constricting and hardening it, due to the access of warm vapors expiring from the earth and water, which resists from the upper surface. By resisting, it confirms the ice through the addition of congealed air gradually falling from the heavens. And this is the reason why they notice that warm water exposed under the open sky in a time of extreme cold freezes more quickly than cold water. We have here, therefore, the formula for the procreation of both frost and ice explained according to our opinion.

Job 38:28[-30].* <note>original: "Glacies egressa est è roris vtero, instar lapidis aquæ absconduntur, & superficies abyssi congelatur."</note> Where he denotes that the air, reduced into a moist and dewy substance by the light blowing of the winds, is the matrix <note>The "matrix" refers to a creative womb or source environment.</note> from which the substance of ice proceeds and comes forth, according to what we reported before. Then, its form or figure is explained in that it is reduced into the appearance of a "watery stone" or Crystal; then afterwards the agent or **efficient cause** is unfolded in another place of his, where it is found that *the mighty **God** produces ice by His breath; by the breath of **God** the frost is congealed. Job 37:9[-10].* <note>original: "DEVS fortis edat flatu suo flante DEO concrescat gelu."</note> Therefore it is clear that the breath of the mighty God **Jehovah** is the most ancient and primary cause of this birth; for the mighty **God** produces ice, and the instrument by which He produces it is explained in that He produces it by His breath, and also forms it and reduces it into its icy substance; for by the breath of **God** the frost congeals. That such a breath is mostly northern we gather from the same chapter 37, verse 9, where we have it manifested that *cold comes from the North winds.* Finally, the **final cause** is for the will of the creator, whether to execute punishment or benevolence. Furthermore, that it is accustomed to freeze on the surface of the waters is explained both in the place cited before and by common experience.

## Relating to the Microcosm, in which human meteors are discussed
### concerning very liquid ones.

We call these meteors "gross" <note>In early science, "gross" meant dense, thick, or material, as opposed to "subtle" or spiritual substances.</note> in comparison to the higher ones, which take the form of vapors—namely, those listed in the preceding section. Similarly, these types of meteors, which are still steeped in sensible moisture or humor, appear to differ in their liquidity and thinness, as well as in their thickness, condensation, viscosity, and freezing. Since some are from the more liquid part of a watery substance, like celestial dew, they are those which—immediately and according to the intention of nature—arise from vapor into "chylous" drops in the stomach, bloody drops in the liver and heart, and clear, limpid drops in the ventricles of the brain. 

By the same logic, we see that vapor in an <term>alembic</term> <note>A chemical apparatus used for distilling liquids.</note> is barely perceptible, much like a very thin smoke; as it ascends into the cap or head of the gourd-shaped vessel, it is converted into dewy drops. In the same way, the vapor arising from food and drink by the power of digestion is turned into dewy drops that temper the mass of the <term>chyle</term> <note>A milky fluid of fat and lymph formed during digestion.</note>. Then, by a second extraction in the cavity of the liver, that vapor is transformed again into reddish drops, much like the smoke of organic wheat, which we described in our *Anatomy of Bread and Wheat*. 

But the chemistry of nature spends its labors on the juice of nutrients; that which exercises its power in the brain and heart takes and chooses its subject from the clearly invisible air. For that external air, which is drawn into the brain through the <term>mammillary processes</term> <note>Early anatomists believed these structures (now associated with the sense of smell) drew "vital air" directly into the brain's ventricles.</note>, claims for itself the celestial "marrow" or <term>quintessence</term> <note>The "fifth element," a pure, heavenly substance thought to be the source of life and thought.</note> of the air, which is suitable for the faculties of the senses and reason. Whatever is superfluous it emits through a certain <term>systole and diastole</term> <note>Usually referring to the heartbeat, here it describes the rhythmic expansion and contraction (breathing) of the brain or its vessels.</note>. Then, it changes that useful air, thus retained and constantly replenished by more of its kind, into vapor, and from vapor into healthy "dews"—provided that the nature of the drawn-in air is familiar, benevolent, and healthy to the one breathing it. 

However, if the nature of that air is very damp and filled with "evil seeds," it induces diseases in the brain, vexes that whole region unnaturally, and loads it with "catarrhal clouds." Similarly, benevolent air drawn to the heart passes into benevolent vapors necessary for life; but if it is filled with unlucky seeds, it usually brings evil and discomfort to the heart and, consequently, to every member of the body. This tends to happen to people more or less according to their birth, their temperament, and the disposition of the place where the breather lives—it does not happen to everyone.

Furthermore, these dewy drops will be converted into rain or "catarrhal phlegm" in the brain (if the air introduced is affected by excessive moisture). We have this confirmed by <term>Galen</term> <note>A prominent Greek physician and philosopher in the Roman Empire whose theories dominated Western medicine for 1,500 years.</note> in *Aphorisms* 3.12: "Phlegm flowing from the head to the belly causes a flux." Elsewhere he says that phlegm flows down from the head, and that in those fluxes the excrements are foamy (*Aphorisms* 7.30). Finally, he admits that phlegm is primarily produced in the brain (*Aphorisms* 3.12). 

From this it is evident that it is the state of the air—either temperate or intemperate—that generates more or less phlegm in the brain. Hence it is declared elsewhere that phlegm is generated especially in the winter time (*Aphorisms* 3.20)—which is also when the rains of heaven are produced—whereas in the summer time it is weakened and diminished (*On the Nature of Man*, Commentary 1.33 and 35). It is as if he had said: when the air is "phlegmatic" (moist and cold), watery or rainy humor is produced in the "sky" of both the Macrocosm [the world] and the Microcosm [the human]. This is because in the air, spirits steeped in southern moisture are breathed everywhere; these convert the air (or the "Mercury of the world") into their own moist nature. Consequently, this air, which by necessity penetrates animals and plants, converts and changes them into its own nature by altering their spirits, which are of the same kind as its own, like a son from the same father. 

For this reason, fruits and animals nourished by air infected with long-lasting southern moisture are observed to lead more toward phlegm and a "rainy" nature than those refreshed by North or East winds. Consequently, in the stomachs of bodies fit to receive such effects, they produce specific results. As Galen says: "Cold phlegm causes lightness of the intestines" (*Aphorisms* 3.12). And elsewhere: "Phlegm in the stomach or intestines causes lightness of the intestines" (*Aphorisms* 6.1)—that is, it induces a <term>lienteric flux</term> <note>A form of diarrhea where food is discharged mostly undigested.</note>. 

It is as if he said: Phlegmatic air, swelling in the food and the surrounding air within the stomach, falls from the stomach into the intestines like rain. It creates a flux, like a rainstorm, from the stomach (acting as the "middle region of the air") to a greater or lesser degree, according to the greater or lesser malignancy of the universal air in that year. From this arise "fluid diseases" that spread among the population, and various kinds of abdominal fluxes [diarrhea]. But if this disease is more localized, it can happen because of food that leans toward a moist and fluid nature, or because of a particular body's imperfection, which makes it ready and prone to generate such phlegm and convert the inhaled air into this poisonous disposition.

As for the "frozen meteors" in the Microcosm, some are in its thinner air, and others in its thicker air—namely, in its "water," which was also once air. The freezing of air in a human usually produces many "frozen diseases," appearing both visibly in the flesh and hidden secretly within the body, known only by their effects. Galen himself testifies that air is as ready to freeze and receive the impressions of cold as it is of heat (*On the Powers of Simple Medicines*, Book 1, Ch. 18). And in the book *On the Differences of Diseases*, he recognizes that all "congealings" <note>original: "congelationes"</note> are called "passions" [afflictions] which come from cold causes...

If we consider frost and hoarfrost in the land of the Macrocosm <note>The "Great World" or the universe at large.</note>, we will perceive that they are nothing other than the freezing of the air as it penetrates everywhere through the pores of the earth. This process is a pattern of constriction and coagulation into the thinnest ice. By this means, both the air in its own nature and the visible water produced by the air are gathered together into a single earthy mass, clustering both heterogeneous and homogeneous parts together. 

In the same way, in the Microcosm <note>The "Little World"—the human being.</note> or man, the entire "fleshy earth" is affected by stupor, the loss of sensation and motion, and by chilling. This is seen in <term>Apoplexy</term> <note>A sudden loss of consciousness or voluntary motion, similar to a stroke.</note> (which Galen, in *On the Affected Parts* book 3, chapter 10, and *Aphorisms* book 2, aphorism 42, defines by its effect as the loss of sensation and motion in the whole body of the animal), in catalepsy, <term>Paraplegia</term> <note>Paralysis of the lower half of the body.</note>, and stupor (which is described as a notable chilling in the human spirit, bringing about difficulty in sensation and motion, *On the Affected Parts* book 2, chapter 2). Just as complete chilling entirely removes both sensation and motion, numbness also occurs due to the freezing and chilling of the body within the porous substance of a nerve. When this happens, according to Galen (in the book *On the Diagnosis of Renal Affections*, chapter 3), the nerve is so obstructed and constricted that the <term>animal spirits</term> <note>In early medicine, these were subtle fluids that carried "messages" of sensation and movement through the nerves.</note> cannot be transmitted to the limb that the nerve is meant to serve and manage. 

We discuss such diseases arising from the freezing of the "human air" more abundantly elsewhere; these types of diseases carry with them the evidence of the effects of freezing. However, those conditions which visibly appear with a snowy whiteness, due to the freezing of internal air or vapors (by which means the fleshy earth and the parts growing from it are altered), are graying hair and <term>leprosy</term> <note>In the 17th century, "leprosy" often referred to a wide variety of skin conditions characterized by whiteness or scaling.</note>. Regarding this, we find it said in Holy Scripture: *Her hand (namely Miriam’s) was white as snow, Leviticus 13:9.* And elsewhere: *there is a white swelling in the skin and it has turned the hair white.*

But truly, when freezing occurs in either a <term>pituitous</term> <note>Relating to phlegm, one of the four bodily humors.</note> or <term>sanguine</term> <note>Relating to blood.</note> humor, diseases are produced that are no less dangerous than the others we have reported. This is the sort of thing that usually happens in mortification <note>Gangrene or tissue death.</note>, where the blood is typically frozen by extreme cold, as is commonly found among those who live in regions stiffened by icy cold.

Furthermore, in the "falling sickness" <note>Epilepsy.</note>, cachexia <note>A "wasting" syndrome of weight loss and muscle atrophy.</note>, and similar conditions, we see a predominance of glassy and viscous phlegm, having the form of egg whites. This is more clearly revealed in those given emetic medicines <note>Medicines that induce vomiting.</note>, and we frequently notice that a glassy and viscous matter is produced in obstructions of the brain caused by cold. Moreover, a slimy, sluggish, and <term>melancholic</term> <note>Relating to black bile, the humor associated with the earth and coldness.</note> humor is seen to abound in those who suffer from natural and "earthy" melancholy. It is very easy to judge that this entire process of freezing proceeds from a "northern" or "splenic" cold <note>The spleen was believed to be the seat of melancholy, which was associated with the cold, dry North.</note>, because in that human region exists the earthy melancholy, which corresponds in its actions to the qualities of the North: consequently, it is congealing and constricting, being cold and dry in its state.

The author often pits Aristotle’s "pagan" logic against "divine" Biblical revelation.</note> are not ashamed to contradict this most wise man, even though they recognize that the doctrine of their own teacher [Aristotle] is entirely opposed to that of Solomon. Indeed, with unheard-of audacity, these same <term>Peripatetics</term> <note>Another name for Aristotelians, referring to Aristotle's habit of walking while teaching.</note> delight in publishing this pagan doctrine in the Academic Schools. Because of this, no certainty in natural philosophy can be found among common Christians, and consequently, the truth of science has been so shrouded from us Christians by the dark clouds of the pagans that shadows are grasped for substance and fantastic dreams for reality by those blinded by the world.

# On the Formal Cause of Meteors.

...can you rightly gather His will? *It is not possible (says Christ) to serve two masters sincerely.* Therefore, those who wish to follow Aristotle rather than the Holy Spirit (who, by the testimony of Holy Scripture, is the Teacher of Teachers) in assertions contrary to the sacred pages, are so inclined toward the Devil and immersed in darkness that it is impossible for them to comprehend God and His light. For when God is unknown, all things are unknown; for Christ is all that is, as the holy testimony affirms, and without Him, there is nothing. I therefore sincerely warn the Christians of following ages that they should by no means divert or distort the intention of their Philosophy from the sense of the Holy Scriptures (however much they may be seduced by the vain opinions of the Pagans, those rebels against the light). Thus, whatever appears to disagree with the holy context (however much it may be confirmed by the Pagans), let us reject it, unless we prefer to speak in an impious and detestable manner with the poet: *I see the better things and approve of them, but I follow the worse* <note>original: "Video meliora proboque, deteriora sequor" — a famous quote from Ovid’s Metamorphoses, often used to describe the conflict between conscience and action.</note>. Indeed, **Johann Velcurius** <note>Johann Velcurio (1490–1559) was a German philosopher whose commentaries on Aristotle’s physics were widely used in universities.</note>, a man quite famous in natural philosophy, speaks in these words in *Chapter 6, Book 3 of his Commentaries on Physics*: *The Sacred Scriptures do not plainly agree with the physicists regarding the origin of rivers and springs, which Ecclesiastes Chapter 1 testifies flow from the sea through various channels and passages, and flow back to their sources, saying: All rivers enter into the sea, and the sea does not overflow; to the place from which the rivers go out, they return, that they may flow again.* Furthermore (he says), the physicists claim the matter is vapor resolved into water, liquefied by cold and heat together within the earth. And so, having neglected the path of truth, he proceeds to publicly recount and teach false opinions of the Pagans on this matter against his own conscience, as if no true doctrine of physics were to be found in the Holy Bible.

But we, treating this matter with greater precision, will prove that the way expressed by **Solomon** concerning the origin of springs is the only true and authentic one, while that Aristotelian way is vain, fantastical, and bears only a resemblance to the truth. We shall show this by ocular demonstration <note>A "visual proof" or experiment intended to be seen with one's own eyes.</note>. Namely, that the matter of springs is real water, not changed in its aquatic form, penetrating from the sea through the hidden passages of the earth to its very bowels. This water—by the marvelous connection with the air, and by the divine Word operating centrally (by the power of cold contracting the whole air, or heat likewise dilating and thinning it)—is either exalted toward the surface or depressed toward the center from the heart of the earth. This has indeed been demonstrated most clearly by us in *Book 3, Chapter 3 of this part, concerning our universal experiment*, and shown as if with a finger by the reasoning of the ascent and descent of water in the neck of a **matrass** <term>matrass: a long-necked glass flask used in chemistry and alchemy to observe the expansion and contraction of fluids.</term>.

For when heat is present, the more it is intensified, the more the water is gradually pushed downward into the abyss of the sea or earth (that is, into the watery mass) by the rarefaction of the enclosed air. But, on the other hand, in the domain of cold, that water which was previously depressed by heat is raised up again into the neck of the flask because of the contraction and condensation of the air. This happens without any change of its form or the alteration of the water’s substance into vapor (according to the opinions of the Pagan philosophers) and then back into water again. For although I admit it is easier for a light thing to be lifted up than a heavier one, we nevertheless say it is not against the laws of nature for water itself to be raised on high by the marvelous contraction of the air caused by cold (since air is joined to water in an inseparable union), just as you have seen clearly demonstrated in the spiritual conclusions expressed previously.

We believe, therefore, that the essence of a spring, according to the intention of the Holy Bible, should be described in this manner:

**A spring is a flow or gushing of water, produced from the sea as the starting point, and through the bowels of the earth as the medium, to its upper surface, by the Divine Word operating through the effect of heat upon the World Spirit <note>original: "spiritum mundanum" — the vital, subtle substance that Fludd believed permeated the universe and mediated between the divine and the physical.</note>, either for the safety and preservation of man and the creatures destined for man's use, or for their punishment and destruction.**

In this description of ours, we establish that the primary efficient cause of the spring is the Divine Word, and the secondary cause is heat, produced by the power of the Divine Word and dispersed everywhere in the air or World Spirit. Finally, we have said the final cause is either for the preservation or the punishment of creatures, according to the divine will. In this description of springs, you also have the origin of that water duct, namely the sea—inasmuch as it is the primary source and fountainhead of springs and rivers—and the local motion, which occurs through the veins and pores of the earth itself, until it reaches the exit or the visible beginning of the spring. It is our task to prove all these parts or members of such a description and to establish them with the testimonies of Holy Scripture.

As for the material cause of the spring, which we said is water, we have it handed down in express words by the wise man (even if ocular experience had not indicated this): *All rivers enter into the sea, and the sea does not overflow; to the place from which they go out, they return, that they may flow again.* From these words, it appears clearly enough that the material cause of a spring is water and not vapor, because all rivers are perennial from their sources, the motion of the spring water from the sea to the sea is circular, and its middle motion is through the earth. Moreover, that God is the principal efficient cause of springs, we have from many other places in the Holy Scriptures. For there it is said: *Who sends out springs through the valleys, that they may walk among the mountains (Psalm 104)*; and elsewhere, *when Jehovah strengthened the fountains of the deep, wisdom was with Him (Proverbs 8:28)*; and in Job we find these things written: *He cuts out rivers among the rocks, and binds the floods from overflowing (Job 28:10)*. Here, he makes God not only the author of springs and streams (which have their origin from springs), but also His other...

# Section I. Portal IV. Part II, Book III. Member II.

...in His own property he depicts Him, while he says: *at His will He lifts them up and dries them out* <note>original: "pro velle suo eos tollit, ac dessiccat"</note>. This is as if one were to say that God, in His hot and boiling power, dilates the air and is the cause of the binding of springs—and consequently of rivers—by their "weeping," that is, by their liquidity and fluidity. Yet, in His cold property, He makes them rise on high and flow greedily. Finally, we gather that the final cause <note>The "final cause" is a philosophical term meaning the ultimate purpose for which something exists.</note> of springs and rivers is for both the comfort and the punishment of creatures. This is because we read in the royal Psalmist <note>King David, the traditional author of the Psalms.</note> in the place cited before: *You who send forth springs through the valleys, so they may walk between the mountains, and provide drink to all the beasts of the field; the wild asses <note>original: "Onagri" — Asiatic wild asses mentioned frequently in the Bible.</note> quench their thirst. Beside them the birds of the heaven dwell, giving forth their voice from the midst of the foliage. He waters the mountains from His upper chambers, and the earth is satisfied by the fruit of Your works, making the grass grow for the cattle, and plants for the service of man, that they may bring forth food from the earth.* **Psalm 104:10.**

Here, therefore, you see the final cause explained by the royal Prophet for the benefit of creatures. However, we read elsewhere that springs and rivers are sometimes ordained for the ruin of creatures and the destruction of men. For concerning the destruction of every creature, it is said *that the fountains of the great deep and the floodgates of heaven were opened, and there was rain for 40 days and 40 nights.* **Genesis 7:11.** And elsewhere it is said *that God, because of the malice of those dwelling on the earth, reduces the desert into a pool of waters, and the thirsty land into water-courses.* **Psalm 107:33.** Finally, it is right to gather from these words of the Holy Bible that the sea is the origin from which all springs and, consequently, all rivers are derived: *God said, let the waters which are under the heaven be gathered into one place so that the dry land may appear, and it was so; and God called the dry land Earth, but the gathering of the waters He called Seas.* **Genesis 1.** From this it is clear that the sea is the place originally ordained in creation for all waters in general; wherefore it is necessary, according to the opinion of Solomon, that all particular waters proceed from it. But this is the most valid argument of all, brought forth by the wise man himself, namely: *since all rivers enter the sea and the sea does not overflow,* it is therefore clearer than the midday light that all that water which enters the sea from springs and rivers has flowed out from the sea.

Regarding the generation of temporary springs, you have it indicated in a single word from its parts in the preceding division how they occur: namely, either from an excessive abundance of rain, or from the melting of snows.

Sect. I. Port. IV. Part. II. Lib. III. Membr. II.

...a bubbling spring is a source, or rather from many sources; just as a Stream commonly comes from one or a few. Briefly then, in this place, according to the doctrine of the Holy Bible, we shall declare in a few words what a river is, what a stream, and what a torrent.

A **River** <note>original: "Flumen"</note> is a gathering of many waters from the sea as the primordial source, flowing upward through the bowels of the earth from the caverns of springs, and flowing into a single channel by means of many rivulets through divine power. It is ordained to fulfill the will of the Creator on earth, whether for harm or for blessing, and once its business is finished, its waters return to their place—namely the sea—from whence they came.

In this description of a river, you see that its material cause is water, and in its form, it is fluid and contained within its channels. The efficient cause, however, is divine power—specifically Wisdom itself—by means of which it is said that *Jehovah strengthened the fountains, Proverbs 8:28,* from which rivers seem to gush. Furthermore, we find it written in Ecclesiasticus: *I, Wisdom, have poured forth rivers, Ecclesiasticus 24:40.* Finally, we have declared its final cause to be the fulfillment of the Creator's will, either in punishing or in doing good. We have also drawn this from the sacred source: for instance, by taking away the benefits of healthy rivers because of the impiety of those living there. Thus it was said by the Prophet: *The rivers shall fail, the streams of the embankments shall be diminished and dried up, the channels of the stream shall be laid bare from their source, Isaiah 19:6.* And elsewhere: *The Lord shall strike from the channel of the river even unto the torrent.* And elsewhere: *I have dried up all the streams of the embankments with the sole of my foot, Isaiah 37.* And elsewhere: *I will dry up thy rivers, Job 37.* <note>The author is likely paraphrasing Job 14 or 28, or perhaps referencing a specific commentary on Job regarding the control of water.</note> And in Ezekiel we find these words: *I will make the channels of the rivers dry and will deliver the land into the hands of the wicked, Ezekiel 30:12.* Or, contrary to the laws of nature, by multiplying its waters. Hence King David said: *He turned the rivers into a wilderness, and the water-springs into dry ground, for the wickedness of them that dwell therein, Psalm 107:33.* Finally, the Wise Man <note>referring to Solomon</note> testifies in *Ecclesiastes 1* that the universal source of rivers and streams is the sea, from which they come and to which they return; and the particular springs in the earth are the secondary origins, first of streams and then of rivers. For streams arise immediately from the springs of the earth, just as rivers arise from streams. Hence the Prophet says: *The channel of the stream shall be laid bare from its source, Isaiah 19:7.* Finally, we are taught by the experience of our own eyes that many small streams concur to form one river.

A **Stream** <note>original: "Riuus"</note> therefore we describe as a living and permanent flow of waters, leaping forth immediately from a single spring or from the bubbling sources of several small springs, which then descends into the channel of some river and is made one with it.

The members of this description are so linked with the parts of the preceding one that the logic of both is the same; for a stream is related to a river as a part is to the whole, or as the head is to the body.

Finally, as pertains to the nature of a **Torrent** <note>original: "torrens," referring to a seasonal or storm-driven rush of water, similar to a wadi.</note>, it differs from a river and a stream both in its origin and in its duration. For while those two arise from the sea and from waters bubbling up to springs from the depths of the earth—and consequently are for the most part perennial—the torrent receives the matter of its flow from the clouds, namely from rains and snows. The Holy Scriptures make mention of this type of flow in many places where they discuss the torrents of *Arnon, Zared, Kishon, Besor, Kidron, Gaash, Cherith, Mamre, etc.* <note>These are all Biblical wadis or seasonal streams that often dry up in summer.</note> That there is a great and distinct difference between these three is taught to us by these words: *Stretch out thy hand over the waters of Egypt, and over their rivers, and over their streams, and over their torrents, and over their pools, and over all their lakes of water.* <note>Exodus 7:19.</note>

To a river or stream, as they flow naturally and perpetually from their sources, we compare:
- The **Kidneys**, acting as sources, through the **ureters**, acting as streams or rivers, into the **bladder**, acting as the sea; the substance of this flow is serous <note>watery or whey-like fluid, i.e., urine</note>.
- The **Stomach**, acting as a source, through the **intestines and mesenteric veins**, performing the roles of rivers or small streams to the **Liver**; the substance of this is chylous <note>the milky fluid "chyle" extracted from digested food</note>.
- The **Liver**, acting as a bubbling source, through the **splenic branch** in the manner of a river into the **spleen**, and through the **vena cava** into the fleshy parts; the consistency of the flow to the spleen is muddy and earthy, while that passing through the trunk of the vena cava is bloody.
- The **Heart**, acting as a source, and through the trunk of the **aorta**, acting as a river channel; the substance of which is subtle blood and highly spiritual.

Sect. I. Port, IV. Part. II. Book III. Section II.

## On Manna.

Both the Pagans and those Christians well-versed in pagan philosophy have admitted that the substance of **Manna** is a certain honey-like dew descending from the sky. However, they also claim the origin of this same dew (vainly fostering their own imaginary fantasies) arises from the earth and water—specifically from a fatty and viscous vapor produced by the mixing of water and earth, exhaled from the inner elements along with air, which then falls back upon plants by freezing, resembling sugar or a very sweet flour. In this opinion, they always seem to establish the foundations and bases of their philosophy upon error, deriving visible things from visible things rather than from the invisible. Yet the matter stands quite differently according to the testimony of Holy Scripture, by which we are taught (as has been frequently alleged before) that it must be believed through faith that visible things were first created from those which are invisible. We say, therefore, that **Manna** is a dense type of <term>Meteor</term> <note>In early modern science, a "meteor" referred to any atmospheric phenomenon, such as rain, snow, or dew, rather than just a falling star.</note>, produced by the thickening of the celestial air when it is soaked with moisture. *Does not a certain distinguished Philosopher say: I pray you, consider a simple cloud of water; who would ever believe that it contains within itself everything the world possesses—hard stones, salts, air, earth, fire—and yet, by itself, it appears to be simple water?* Thus he spoke. Truly, in the places previously cited, we have proved clearly enough by reasons established in the Holy Bible that vapors, clouds, and their waters are formed from the condensation of simple air and brought forth into the world.

We, therefore, have deemed it fit to describe **Manna** according to the laws of holy testimony in this manner:

->Manna is a fatty substance of the air which, when the gates of heaven are opened and the divine treasury is revealed, descends from the clouds by divine command in the manner of dew or frost. It grows into a minute form, round like a white coriander seed, falling upon the lands to carry out the will of the Creator.<-

->Or thus,<-

->Manna is heavenly bread, the wheat of heaven, spiritual meat, the food of angels, and the very word proceeding from the mouth of **Jehovah** <note>original: "Iehouæ"</note>. It descends from the sky and the clouds in the manner of dewy rain—either together with the celestial dew or upon the dew—onto the surface of the earth by divine power. It appears in a minute and round form, like heaped frost or coriander seed, thickening there into hardness so that it might serve as food, nourishment, and even medicine for men.<-

In our first description, you have the **material cause** of Manna expressed, insofar as it is described there as a fatty substance of the air. Next, the **formal cause** is expressed in that it is said to grow into a minute species, round like coriander seed. Then, we declared its **efficient cause** to be the divine command—that is, the power and the Word. Finally, we affirm the **final cause** (the purpose) of its descent or generation to be the exercise of the Creator’s will. You have all these parts of our description confirmed specifically from the most holy page in this way: For as pertains to the material cause, **GOD** says to the Israelites, *Behold, I will rain bread from heaven for you* (Exodus 16:4). And elsewhere, *He gave them bread from heaven to eat* (John 6:31). And elsewhere, *He had commanded the clouds from above and opened the doors of heaven, and rained Manna upon them* (Psalm 78:23-24). By these it is clearly declared that the matter of Manna itself is of an aerial composition, since by the word "heaven" the air is understood, as it is the place of the clouds which Jehovah commanded. Hence the treasury-chest of Manna, in which it is reserved and from which it is fashioned as a substance, is the air itself. The **form** is also explained by these words: *In the morning, the dew lay round about the host, and when the dew that lay was gone up, behold, upon the face of the wilderness there lay a small round thing, as small as the hoar frost on the ground* (Exodus 16:13-14). And elsewhere: *The Manna was as coriander seed, white; and the taste of it was like wafers made with honey* (Exodus 16:31). And elsewhere: *Its taste was as the taste of fresh oil* (Numbers 11:8). Furthermore, its **efficient cause** is confirmed by these words: *I (says Jehovah) rain bread from heaven for you* (Exodus 16:4). And: *He commanded the clouds from above and opened the doors of heaven.* Finally, the **purpose** of this kind of meteor is explained where it is said: *He fed thee with Manna... that he might make thee know that man doth not live by bread only, but by every word, etc.* (Deuteronomy 8:3). And elsewhere: *Thou feddest thine own people with angels' food, and didst send them from heaven bread prepared without their labor, able to content every man's delight, and agreeing to every taste* (Wisdom 16:20). And: *He gave them bread from heaven to eat* (John 6:31).

We conclude, therefore, that in addition to all these things, you have the place of generation for this kind of divine nourishment in our said description: namely, that it descends from the clouds when the gates of heaven are opened and the divine treasury is unlocked. For it is written: *Behold, I rain bread from heaven for you* (Exodus 16). And: *He commanded the clouds from above, and opened the doors of heaven, and rained down Manna upon them* (Psalm 78:24).

In the second description, you also have the four causes of this kind of meteor exactly explained. But the **material cause** is explained in a more hidden manner: through the "bread" and "wheat of heaven," through "spiritual meat," "angels' food," and indeed through the "material word," the efficient cause of which we make Jehovah Himself. The place from which it is brought forth is the sky and the clouds; the manner of its emanation is indicated, along with the **formal cause**: namely, that it descends in the manner of dewy rain, or together with celestial dew, or upon the dew, onto the surface of the earth, hardening into a minute and round shape, like heaped frost or coriander seed. Finally, its **final cause** is explained therein, in that it serves men as food and nourishment as well as medicine.

But I know there will be many who will not hesitate to object that the Manna mentioned in the Holy Scriptures, by which the Israelites were nourished in the desert, was a certain miracle and not at all natural...
