# On the Formal Cause of Meteors.

...and consequently, they will assert that the aforementioned description in no way matches natural **Manna**, given that dew descends more or less every day. To these people, I truly respond that the substance and form of the one differs very little from the other, even though we see one ordered and prepared differently than the other (according to the Creator's pleasure). In this same way, the quails which **GOD** sent abundantly into the camps of the Israelites for their nourishment did not differ in substance or form from other quails, even though they were introduced into that place by divine power and ordained for the sustenance of the Israelites. And certainly, if anyone knew how to rightly collect the **Manna** falling from heaven commonly with the dew—especially in May and even in the summer—and how to prepare it by removing the husk, I believe he would acquire for himself a thing far more precious than gold and gems, and would possess a most excellent balsam of life; for I have been so instructed by men most skilled in the divine mystery <note>The "divine mystery" likely refers to alchemy or Hermetic philosophy, where Manna was often sought as a universal medicine or the "Manna of the Philosophers."</note>. And **Manna** of this kind, prepared in such a way and stripped of its external layers (making the hidden manifest, and the manifest hidden), is then called the "hidden Manna" <note>original: *Manna absconditum*</note> which is promised to the victor in the Book of Revelation, inasmuch as in it, heavenly grace and the **quintessence** <note>original: *vis quinta*; the "fifth element" or purest essence of matter</note> abound copiously, diffused everywhere by uncreated rays. Thus indeed we see that the external man has within himself his internal or spiritual man, which is the temple of the Holy Spirit. So also it is said: *The incorruptible Spirit is in every thing, Wisdom 12.* <note>The author quotes the Book of Wisdom, a deuterocanonical book of the Bible.</note> But it is further taught that it abounds more in one thing than in another; thus Christ is said to be *all and in all*. But because of our sins, He is crucified in His creatures—or rather, bound and imprisoned. But if we, like good Jews and true Israelites, could bind Barabbas and set Jesus free—contrary to the custom of the worst Jews who bound Jesus and freed Barabbas—then we would truly know Jesus in His essence: we would become one with Him and be numbered among the elect of **GOD**, according to that word of the Evangelist in *John 1*.

Regarding the proof of our final description, we have it thus written in the sacred pages: *He fed you with Manna, so that He might make known to you that man does not live by bread alone, but by everything that proceeds from the mouth of Jehovah, Deuteronomy 8:3.* From this it is clear that **Manna** proceeds immediately from the benevolent breath of Jehovah. So also it is said that the upper clouds drop down dew by wisdom (*Proverbs 3:20*), and that by His wisdom He gives weight to the air (*Job 28:25*). Likewise it is said: *By the breath of God frost is given (Job 37)*, and that *His word is fulfilled by the stormy wind (Psalm 148:8)*, etc. Furthermore, we read that *He gave them heavenly bread to eat (John 6:31)*. And elsewhere: *He had commanded the clouds from above, and opened the doors of heaven, and rained down Manna upon them to eat, and had given them the corn of heaven (Psalm 78:24–25)*. And elsewhere: *All ate the same spiritual meat (1 Corinthians 10)*. From these examples it is sufficiently clear that our final description of **Manna** is confirmed even by sacred testimony.

### On the Ceraunian Stone or Thunderbolt.

The **Thunderstone** <note>original: *Lapis fulminaris*</note>, also called the **Ceraunian stone** or the **thunderbolt**, is a thing worthy of admiration in nature. The ancients hesitated regarding its origin, nor did the **Peripatetics** <note>The followers of Aristotle, whose scientific theories dominated universities at the time.</note> write anything of great importance, having failed to consider the matter accurately enough. Indeed, philosophers of sounder mind—both several ancients and more recent ones—found this subject to be of such depth that (having considered their wonderful properties again and again) they believed the origin of such <term>meteors</term> <note>In this period, "meteor" referred to any atmospheric phenomenon, including lightning and stones believed to fall from the sky.</note> comes immediately from the Supreme **GOD** rather than from the artifice of Nature. Hence it is that Aristotle and his school (who strive to provide a natural explanation for this meteor established upon their own fabulous foundations) are observed to wander from the truth in their entire description of it. For it is their opinion that the thunderstone is a sulfurous exhalation mixed with some terrestrial and mineral or metallic matter, reduced into a single mass within a cloud (usually green and blackish). They claim it is clumped together by the surrounding moisture—like flour gathered into one with water—and then, by an approaching intense heat from the sun and stars (that is, by the power of their influences) and partly by **antiperistasis** <note>The supposed sharpening or intensification of a quality by being surrounded by its opposite, like heat intensifying when surrounded by cold.</note>, it is transformed from its muddy disposition into a hard and firm stone, just like bricks are made, and is then driven downward by the violent force of the fire trapped in the cloud.

In this description of theirs, they made the **material cause** of the stone a sulfurous exhalation, or sulfur mixed with certain terrestrial mineral or metallic matter, reduced into a single mass; it is as if they said that the matter of the thunderbolt is denser and more compact, being the terrestrial part of that exhalation which was elevated from the earth into the middle region of the air by the sun's power. Next, they explained its **form** by saying that this slimy mass was transmuted into the appearance of a hard stone by the power of heat, in the manner of bricks. Finally, they proposed that the **efficient cause** of this formation was the hidden influences of heaven, namely stellar heat.

As for the opinion of the Peripatetics regarding the matter of the thunderstone, it seems to be erroneous and poorly suited to the laws of Holy Scripture. For (as was explained abundantly in the preceding pages), God is accustomed to produce clouds—and consequently everything that comes from the substance of clouds—from the air or heaven, and not from the earth. Indeed, this great earth itself which we see is, as it were, the dregs of the waters or the drier part, according to that saying of Saint Peter (often cited before): *the heavens and the earth were of old from water and through water by means of the Word.*

Wherefore it is clear that both the clouds themselves and those things which, according to the Philosopher, are procre-

He did not say He would open the lands, but the heaven—that is, the air—as if He had said, Jehovah will open the vitals or the hidden <term>matrix</term> <note>A "matrix" in this context refers to a womb-like place of origin or a formative substance.</note> of the air, making the hidden part of the air manifest. The Apostle also teaches us in the passage cited above that all visible things were previously invisible. From this it is clear that not only visible water, but also earth, and consequently stone (which is a denser portion of water), comes from the invisible spirit, which is spiritual water. Concerning their <term>formal cause</term> <note>The "formal cause" is the internal design or essence that makes a thing what it is.</note>, I will say nothing in this place, as it is known to almost everyone through visual experience. 

However, we say that the <term>efficient cause</term> <note>The "efficient cause" is the primary agent or force that brings something into being.</note> claimed by others is erroneous and utterly false, as it is opposed to the holy scriptures. They claim that the heat of the Sun and the stars brought this "meteor" to perfection. But the Most Holy Bible assigns this work not to creatures, but immediately to the Creator, who—although He has placed His tabernacle in the sun—does not dwell there exclusively, insofar as He dwells everywhere by His presence, fills all things, and acts everywhere according to His will. For He who is the eternal fountain of light is, consequently, the origin of action, motion, and heat, both in the stars and in the entire universe. Hence St. John says in Chapter 1: *“By Him all things were made, and without Him nothing was made; in Him was life,”* and elsewhere: *“The incorruptible Spirit of GOD is in every thing”* (Wisdom 12:1). We say, therefore, that the God **JEHOVAH** is both the mediated and the immediate efficient cause of a matter of such great importance, inasmuch as He is the Alpha and Omega, between whose prior and posterior acts there is no distinction or separation in essence. For as He is permanent in Himself, so also His actions are permanent. 

But (my good <term>Peripatetics</term> <note>The "Peripatetics" were followers of Aristotle’s philosophy, which dominated universities at the time. Fludd frequently argues against their "naturalistic" explanations.</note>), if it were true that the influences of the heavens or stars were the authors of this kind of lightning-meteor, I would very much like to know whether there was thunder in the world before the creation of the heavenly hosts or not? And yet, we can very easily gather from the sense of the sacred scriptures that **GOD** spoke through thunder even at the beginning of the creation of the world, through passages to be cited by us a little further down where mention of thunder will be made. From this it follows that such an opinion is not well-founded. And although it has been proven by the experience of the more skilled **Astrologers** that thunder is heard after certain alignments of some planets, it does not follow that this happens by necessity. We observe that such effects by no means always follow such planetary alignments. For it is in **GOD’S** power—to whom alone it is given to act according to His will—to direct His face from His solar tabernacle toward this or that planet (or several at once) using them as His instruments; or sometimes by means of His winds, which must obey their Commander. We observe this happening very often with no evident heavenly cause preceding it—sometimes through fiery or watery spirits and <term>daemons</term> <note>In the 17th century, "daemons" or "spirits" were often viewed as neutral agents of nature or divine will, not necessarily "demons" in the modern evil sense.</note> carrying out the Creator's commands, and in infinite other hidden ways, which would be impossible for even the most skilled **Astrologer** to explore. However, in what way and by what means **GOD** works to produce meteors in the world, we have proposed to speak more clearly below, where the natural efficient cause is treated.

Also known as a Ceraunian stone, these were prehistoric stone tools (like axe heads) that people in the past believed fell from the sky during lightning strikes.</note> is according to the intention of the sacred scriptures.

The **lightning weapon** is a stony dart or arrow which, like a breath of burning coals from the mouth of **JEHOVAH**, is ignited like passing torches and is sent down from the clouds, either for the public punishment of the wicked or for the hidden benefit of those born of the earth.

That it is a stony dart, arrow, and weapon of **JEHOVAH**, we gather from these passages: *“Jehovah thundered from heaven, and the Most High gave His voice; He sent His arrows and scattered them; He lightened and consumed them”* (2 Samuel 22:14-15). Here it is manifest that he understood lightning weapons by "arrows," since he speaks of lightning afterward. Similarly elsewhere: *“Jehovah, bow your heavens and come down; touch the mountains so that they smoke; cast forth your lightnings and scatter them; shoot out your darts and destroy them”* (Psalm 144:5-6). Furthermore, it is said elsewhere: *“The bolts of lightnings go directly from the clouds as if from a well-curved bow”* (Wisdom 5:21). Moreover, elsewhere they are called the "little stones" of **JEHOVAH**. 

As for its form, where it is said that it is ignited like a breath of fiery coals from the mouth of **JEHOVAH**, like passing torches, it is confirmed by this testimony: *“By GOD’S sneezings,”* says Job, *“light shines, and His eyes are like the eyelids of the morning; out of His mouth go burning torches, and sparks of fire leap out; His breath kindles coals, and a flame goes out of His mouth”* (Job 41:18).

Furthermore, from these things already recited, it is clear what its efficient cause is: namely, **JEHOVAH** Himself through His scorching and flashing breath. Finally, its purpose is explained in this definition: namely, for the punishment of rebels. Hence it is said: *“Shoot out your darts and destroy them”* (Psalm 144), and elsewhere: *“He sent His arrows and scattered them”* (2 Samuel 22).

But lest anyone foolishly reply that these words previously cited concerning divine thunder were uttered by the sacred page as something non-natural, we respond that this can be understood of *all* thunder. Without this efficient cause, no meteor—indeed, nothing new in the nature of things—can be produced, whether according to the order of nature or against the laws of nature, just as we shall make fuller mention in the chapter on thunder and lightning.

### Concerning dust descending from heaven.

The matter of meteors of this kind differs very little from that of a thunderbolt; but they are truly different in form, inasmuch as the substance of the latter <note>Referring to the thunderbolt.</note> is solid and compact, while that of the former <note>Referring to the falling dust.</note> is dissipated into infinite parts. The <term>efficient cause</term> <note>The primary agent that brings something into being.</note> is indeed the same as the one previously mentioned, namely THE LORD Jehovah, and the purpose is also one of vengeance, namely for the sin of the rebellious. Hence Moses says: *The Lord shall make the rain of thy land powder and dust; from heaven shall it come down upon thee, until thou be destroyed.* <note>original: "Efficiet Iehoua ut terra tua sit puluisculus, seu puluis e coelo descender super te donec exscinderis." ### Concerning worms, lice, birds, and frogs.

These monstrous meteors, as well as blood, sometimes descend from the clouds because of the sins of men. You will find both the sacred scriptures and other authors full of accounts of the arrival of such meteors; indeed, you even have these things confirmed by experience, though it be rare. From these examples, we can understand clearly enough that the air (which is "invisible water") is fit to be converted into any nature according to the divine disposition—namely into worms, lice, birds, frogs, blood, and so on.

Meteors in the <term>microcosm</term> <note>The "microcosm" is the human body, viewed as a miniature reflection of the "macrocosm," or the universe.</note> that are clearly visible, simple, dark, and earthy are of two types, namely arising either from:

*   **The Heaven:** That is, springing forth from the air in a body disposed to this, of which some are:
    *   **Inanimate**
        *   Fatty and oily, like grease.
        *   Dry, and these are either:
            *   **Compact**, and gathered into one, such as <term>calculus</term> <note>Stones or mineral buildups.</note> of the kidneys, bladder, gall bladder, etc.

        *   Worms.

        *   Sometimes other monstrous animals.

## CHAPTER XII.

### The fourth part concerning the visible dark meteors of the Macrocosm arising from the earth.

Visible dark meteors of the Macrocosm <term>Meteors: In 17th-century science, "meteors" referred to any natural phenomena in the atmosphere or on the earth's surface, including clouds, vapors, and minerals.</term>, arising from the earth, are of two kinds, namely either:

## CHAPTER XIII.
### *Concerning the luminous Meteors of both Worlds.*

<note>In this context, "Meteors" refers to any phenomenon occurring in the atmosphere, including lightning, wind, and rainbows, as well as their equivalents within the human body. The "two worlds" are the Macrocosm (the universe) and the Microcosm (the human being).</note>

**The luminous Meteors of the Macrocosm are either:**

*   **Manifest and visible**, to whose composition two things concur, namely:
    *   **An animated ethereal body**, that is, one illuminated by light or fire, and is of the order:
        1.  **Not appearing**, but hidden in the air in an occult manner.
        2.  **An angelic spirit or animating fiery wind**, which is fiery and luminous, [which manifests as] **Apparently and visibly**, and is either: Coruscating, Flashing, Lightning, or Thundering.
        3.  **Of a superior and thinner substance**, and of this nature are: Comets of various forms (discussed below), Columns of fire, Beams, Spears, and Flying sparks.
        4.  **Of a middle nature**, such as thunder mixed with lightning, and chasms <note>original: "chasmata"; these were historical descriptions of "gaps" or "openings" appearing in the night sky.</note>.
        5.  **Airy, mixed with light or fire**, such as: Evening blueness, Radiation or *Assub* <note>original: "Assub"; an Arabic term used by medieval scholars to describe shooting stars</note> which quickly appear and disappear, Falling stars, Will-o'-the-wisps <note>original: "ignis fatuus"</note>, "Hair-licking fire" <note>original: "ignis crines lambens"; likely a reference to static electricity or St. Elmo's Fire appearing on the hair or skin</note>, Castor and Pollux <note>A term for the twin lights of St. Elmo's fire seen on ships</note>, etc.
        6.  **Of an inferior and thicker nature**, and are of a consistency either:
            *   **Terrestrial**, tending toward burnt Melancholy <note>The author is linking atmospheric fire to the "fire" of the black bile humor in the body</note>, which are: Grosser, or of the nature of Sulfur and Bitumen.
            *   **Thinner and moist**, such as the earth [which appears] Yellow or Red.
*   **Hidden** (See Section L).

## CHAPTER XIII.
### First Small Part.
### *Concerning the luminous angelic spirit, or animating fiery wind, both hidden and manifest.*

<margin>Virgil, Book 6 of the Aeneid.</margin>
That all creatures receive their soul from light and fire, I think is hidden from no one who is even moderately-versed in natural philosophy, or indeed in the sacred scriptures. Rather, even that uncreated light is recognized to animate the universal spirit of the world by its vivifying inspiration, as we may see from the words of the Poet:

Who, then, is that wisdom? Is it not that uncreated light, the Word or Christ, who is truly the light of the world, the life of creatures, and the soul of the world? 

Thus also it was said regarding the person of the great God Jehovah: *clouds were kindled by the brightness in his presence, 2 Samuel 22.* And certainly, if we contemplate the sacred writings with a little more curiosity, we shall perceive indeed that this universally animating spirit is a soul prone to both corruption and generation and preservation. Hence Jehovah said of the same angel or eternal wisdom: *Behold, I send an angel before you to lead you into that place which I have prepared; take heed of his face and listen to his voice, do not provoke him, for he will not bear your rebellion, because my name is in him, Exodus 23:20.*

# CHAPTER XIII.

## Second Section.

->*On the animated aerial body, that is, one illuminated by fire or light of a higher order.*<-

Now, indeed, we shall reveal what a comet is, as well as those other fiery portents observed to appear in the highest region of the air or above it. We will do this according to the opinion of both the Peripatetics <note>Followers of Aristotle’s philosophy</note> and the truthful Scriptures. At the same time, we shall briefly and yet clearly demonstrate how immense is the discrepancy regarding their origin between the Heathens and those who are truly enlightened and taught by the Holy Spirit.

The Peripatetics (among whom we acknowledge **Aristotle** as the leader) agree on this: namely, that the comet itself is a terrestrial exhalation—thick, hot and dry, fatty and viscous, with densely compacted parts—which is easily flammable. They believe it is raised little by little and part by part from the bowels of the earth into the highest region of the air by the power of the stars. There, because of the disposition and abundance of its matter, it is spread out near the element of fire and ignited. Taking on a "tailed" or "bearded" form, it moves circularly in a long and diffused path, following the motion of the star under which it is born, or the circular motion of the highest aerial region. 

Many have identified a variety of "formal causes" for such a meteor, since it usually brings about drought, sterility of the earth, and pestilence, and consequently, sometimes a change in political government and the region it overlooks. In their description, they first placed the "material cause" of the comet as a terrestrial and viscous exhalation, which others claim exists in great quantity and is clumped together in the form of very hard pitch. They wish to signify its "formal cause" by the fact that they make this mass either "illuminated" or "tailed" (having matter that is denser in one part and rarer as it stretches out), or "bearded" (when the extremities of such an exhalation appear rarer and more dispersed, for then it creates a "bearded star"). They made the "efficient cause" of such a meteor to be astral heat, and especially that of the sun; for by its power, that exhalation is not only raised little by little from the bowels of the earth to the middle region of the air, but it is also reduced into a mass in that region—as if in a womb—by the intense cold of the place, where it is immediately kindled and illuminated.

However, concerning the cause of the comet and other fiery impressions according to the aforementioned intention of the Peripatetics: we say that their substance or existence, before they were brought into the light, was hidden and lurking in the **air** as the primordial receptacle and womb of animating light, and **not in the earth**, as they have quite foolishly written, as [will be seen] in the follow-

### Section I. Portal IV. Part II. Book III. Member II.

<meta>catchword: suæ (of its own)</meta>

...discussed more extensively in what follows. Here, however, we shall show in a word that their opinion in this matter is foolish and vain. For first, if this were probable, then it would follow that their assertion is most stupid, by which they strive to infer that the material cause of wind is a hot and dry exhalation, light in consistency and not at all flammable. They claim that because of this disposition, it is denied passage through the middle consistency of the air due to the coldness of that place, which through **antiperistasis** <note>original: "antiperistafin"; a philosophical concept where a quality is intensified by being surrounded by its opposite, such as heat becoming more concentrated when surrounded by cold.</note> drives that hot exhalation downward. But truly, we do not see this reasoning as being sufficiently fit. For if this assertion of theirs were true, then the exhalation that constitutes **comets** and other meteorological impressions of both the middle and highest regions of the air would be denied passage through that medium even more than the exhalation of the wind. You have this proven elsewhere by many reasons, which I will briefly attempt to re-examine and repeat in this place.

The exhalation that creates wind (according to the statutes of *Aristotle*) is very light in its substance, and therefore it is more fit in its own measure to tend and ascend upward; for just as it is the natural inclination of all heavy things to tend downward, so conversely it is natural for light things to seek the heights. Therefore, such an exhalation is more prone, due to its lightness, to be sublimated higher than the material of ignited **meteors** (among which the **Comet** is the prince). The matter of these meteors is more compact, dense, and viscous, and consequently not as well-disposed to ascend as that of the winds.

Furthermore, he assigns to the windy exhalation a certain disposition—namely, subtlety and thinness—which makes it more inclined by its nature to penetrate through the middle region of the air than the material of a comet and other flowing or ignited impressions, which are given a thicker and more compact matter. Therefore, just as it is more difficult for such a thing to be carried upward due to its viscosity and compact disposition than the wind-exhalation (which is lighter), so also it is certain that it penetrates with more difficulty; for thinner things penetrate where access is denied to thicker ones.

Finally, he ascribes to the nature of the windy exhalation that it is not fit to be inflamed or set on fire. From this, it is manifest—by his own admission, as it were—that it is easier for this exhalation to penetrate through the middle region of the air without great impediment than for the material of ignited meteors. For something that is actually fiery, or closer to a fiery act, is more repelled and attacked by cold (which is the predominant quality in the middle region of the air) and consequently propelled downward, than something that has no potential for inflammation. Yet, by the testimony of the said *Aristotle*, windy exhalations are least fit for illuminating or catching fire, whereas those ignited impressions are most prone and suited to inflammation.

From these points, it is likely that those thick, hot, dry, and viscous terrestrial exhalations, being densely compact, are less fit to ascend into the highest region of the air than those thin and non-flammable ones. This is both because they are raised to the heights with greater difficulty due to their more compact consistency, and because they can penetrate with more difficulty due to their thicker and more obscured composition; and furthermore, because they are in the most immediate potential for inflammation—indeed, such matter is often seen to be inflamed even in the lowest and middle regions of the air, as daily experience teaches us. Therefore, without a doubt, either this matter does not ascend from the earth into the highest region of the air as *Aristotle* thought, or the material of the winds has its origin from elsewhere. Indeed, to use the very arguments of the **Aristotelians**, neither the one nor the other can spring from the earth because of the contrariety that exists between them and the cold middle region of the air, whose nature is to attack its opposites, to resist them with all its might, and to depress them downward toward the earth and the sea.

But without doubt, everyone will ask: if the material of such comets and ignited impressions does not flow out from the earth by exhalation, where then is its spring, or from what source does its consistency or essence come? To this question, we think we should respond not unadvisedly: the source of such impressions is the same as that of the winds and waters—namely, the heaven or the open air. This we shall proceed to prove by reasons leaning upon both **true Philosophy** and **holy theosophy** <note>Theosophy: here meaning divine wisdom or a mystical understanding of the natural world through God’s laws.</note>.

First, among philosophers both modern and ancient, it is a well-worn saying that just as fire is nothing other than very thin and dilated air, so also "thick fire" is air itself altered in dryness by divine motion. It is for this reason that they called the **Ether** <note>original: "ætherem"</note> as if it were *aithe-aer* <note>A Greek-derived etymology common in the Renaissance: *aithein* (to burn) + *aer* (air).</note>, that is, fiery air, or a spirit equally mixed with fire. This species of purest air, although it cannot be discerned by us with the eye in its dissipated and subtle nature, yet if it be gathered into a mass by the will and act of **Divine Wisdom**—through the mediation of its **angelic ministers**—it will appear in the likeness and form of a light-bringing star (such as a comet).

Will this seem arduous and difficult to the **Aristotelians**? Even their prince, *Aristotle* himself, supported our opinion when he stated that a star is a denser portion of its own orb—as if he had said: a luminous star is a contracted and condensed part of the ether, brought about by the operation of the world's **Lucid Spirit**, from which that star acquires its bright and fiery form. If this is conceded by *Aristotle* himself, what prevents the **aerial spirit**, moving in any region of its sphere, from acquiring a visible form by its own condensation? For the stars of the ethereal heaven, along with the consistency of the element of fire or the highest region of the air, are far greater in their simplicity...

# On the Formal Cause of Meteors.

<term>Meteors</term> <note>In the 17th century, "meteors" referred to any atmospheric phenomenon, including rain, wind, lightning, and rainbows, not just falling stars.</note> of its own nature are denser than that supernatural substance of the world, and consequently more adapted for condensation. Moreover, we have stated that the efficient causes of these compressions—which occur beyond the common laws of nature—are angelic spirits or <term>demons</term> <note>original: "dæmones"; here used in the classical sense of "spirits" or "intelligences," which could be good or evil, rather than strictly malevolent beings.</note> who move the winds in every region of the world. Do not both the Platonists and the Aristotelians acknowledge peculiar <term>Intelligences</term> <note>Spiritual beings believed to govern the movements of the celestial spheres.</note> of the stars, presiding over them, governing, and moving them? They believe many legions are subject to these spirits, and that they exercise the properties of the very star (whether wandering or fixed) to which they are assigned, within the ether and the elements. We read everywhere—both in the works of the most observant ancient philosophers and in the Holy Scriptures—that demons or angelic spirits mingle themselves with thunder and lightning.

But truly, we have declared elsewhere that there is one supreme Prince over these angelic spirits, whose commands they are accustomed to fulfill sincerely, and beyond which they cannot move even a foot. This prince is GOD, the Word, and Wisdom, whom angels of every kind are prepared to serve. *Angels (says the royal Psalmist) most powerful in strength, performing his word, hearkening to the voice of his speech; his ministers doing his pleasure. (Psalm 103:20).* Is it not also said elsewhere, *Who makest the spirits or winds thy angels, and thy ministers a burning fire? (Psalm 104:4).* And yet, nevertheless, just as we see the glory and the name of victory or a triumph in great military deeds attributed to the great leader and commander presiding at that time—namely Alexander, Caesar, etc.—so also every remarkable deed effected by the invisible army in the heavens and on the earth is mostly referred to GOD rather than to the ministers. Thus it is said, *O Jehovah, rebuke me not in thy anger (Psalm 6:2).* And elsewhere, *The spirit of the power of God fanning and of justice pursuing the unjust (Wisdom 11:21).* So the spirits of the wheels were moved by the presence of GOD, to fulfill his pleasure *(Ezekiel 1).* Thus it is said that GOD struck Job with an ulcer and a plague, and yet he performed that through the mediation of Satan. Furthermore, what the seven angels (to whom seven trumpets were given) standing before the face of Jehovah did by the mere sound of the trumpets is declared everywhere in the Apocalypse.

Furthermore, it is said, *Behold, I send my angel to keep thee in this way*, and yet it is said elsewhere: *GOD went before the Israelites in a pillar of cloud by day and by a fire shining through the whole night (Psalm 78:14).* And elsewhere: *Wisdom was a covering for the Israelites by day and the light of stars by night (Wisdom 10:17).* We see, therefore, that this same work is attributed to the Angel of Jehovah and to Wisdom, who were indeed the same in effect; for it is said: *Do not provoke him (that is, the angel), for he will not bear your rebellion, because my name is in him (Exodus 23:21).* So also it is said that when lightning appears, it is clear; and that very thing and the spirits are diffused through every region: and the clouds, which when they are commanded by Jehovah to travel through the entire world, perform what is commanded of them *(Baruch 6:60).* <note>The author cites Baruch 6, though in many Bibles this is the Letter of Jeremiah.</note> Even the fire sent from above to consume mountains and forests does what is commanded of it; and elsewhere it is said: *The creature of fire, serving GOD who made all things, is at one time intensified for the punishment of the unjust and at another time relaxed for doing good (Wisdom 16:24).* And elsewhere: *The whirlwind, the cold, the ice, the frost, the clouds, the rain, the lightning—whatever GOD commands these to do upon the surface of the orb in the earth, whether for a scourge or for doing kindness, they make it ready at hand (Job 37).*

And yet elsewhere it is said that *GOD makes a weight for the wind or the air (Job 28:25).* That *GOD makes the sapphire clouds of wisdom, and according to his will overturns the bottles of heaven.* He begets the drops of dew, and produces ice and frost; he gives *snow like wool, scatters his ice like morsels*, and binds the waters in thick clouds. It is said elsewhere that he effects all these things by his Word, whose role it is to do the will of the Father. Hence it is said in the place cited above: the clouds scatter their light, which surveys all things in a circuit wherever the will of the Governor drives them, for everything he had commanded them upon the face of the world, whether for a scourge or for doing mercy; and elsewhere, *When GOD shall drop the droplets of water, which shall pour down rain for his calamity (Job 36:27).* And elsewhere: *The spirit or breath of the nostrils of Jehovah works wonders*; and elsewhere: *By the sneezings of GOD light shines, and indeed his eyes are like the eyelids of the morning; out of his mouth go torches, and as if his breath kindled coals and a flame went out of his mouth (Job 41:18).* And elsewhere: *Jehovah, descend, bow thy heavens, and touch the mountains that they may smoke; cast forth thy lightning and scatter them (Psalm 144:5).* And elsewhere: *Jehovah shall thunder from heaven, and the Most High gives his voice; he sent his lightning and consumed them.* And elsewhere: *GOD makes the clouds his vehicle or his chariot, who walks upon the wings of the wind, who makes his angels winds and his ministers a burning fire (Psalm 104:3).*

From which words it is most evidently clear that GOD is the leader and ordainer: but truly, he works mostly through his ministers in the nature of things, and executes his will—both according to the laws of nature and extraordinarily and prodigiously (that is, beyond the custom of nature). He always acts primarily through his Word or his Wisdom, which fulfills his commands and takes the place of the divine will; and secondarily through angels of many orders differing in dignity. Whence it happened that this Wisdom (which the sacred page calls the first creature, *Ecclesiasticus 1:1*)—that is, the first emanation or outgoing from the Father—the <term>Cabalists</term> <note>Practitioners of Kabbalah, a school of Jewish mysticism that influenced many Renaissance and Early Modern Christian thinkers.</note> have identified as that great Angel <term>Metattron</term> <note>Metatron; in mystical tradition, the highest of the angels and the "lesser YHWH."</note> in whom the name of Jehovah is. The Platonists said this was the "Informing Soul of the World" (<term>Anima Mundi</term>), which St. John supports in Chapter 1, saying: *by it (namely the Word) all things were made, and without it nothing, in it was life, etc.*

The primary minister of this Wisdom is the Archangel Michael, who has the protection of souls in his guardianship; for it was he who waged war against the great angel of darkness with his followers, obtained the victory, and is said to always stand in a glorious manner before the face of Jehovah. Therefore, at his command, all other angels offer obedience, and they are said to receive life in no other way than the creatures of this world receive it from the Sun (over which this very angel also presides). Hence, the winds are called the "children of the Sun" (as was said before), by whose breath all other meteors in the world are procreated. Therefore, the actions of all things are subject to the command of Jehovah.

Section I. Part IV. Part II. Book III. Member II.

...dealing with these matters more broadly in the following sections. Here, however, we shall show in a word that their opinion in this matter is foolish and vain. For first, if this were probable, it would follow that their assertion is most dull, by which they strive to infer that the material cause of wind is a hot and dry <term>exhalation</term> <note>In ancient science, an "exhalation" was a dry, smoky vapor rising from the earth, distinct from moist "vapors" that formed rain.</note>, light in consistency, and not at all flammable. They claim that because of such a disposition, it is denied passage through the middle consistency of the air due to the coldness of that place, which—by <term>antiperistasin</term> <note>original: "antiperistasin"; a philosophical concept where one quality is intensified by being surrounded by its opposite, such as heat concentrating when surrounded by cold.</note>—drives that hot exhalation downward. But truly, we do not see this reasoning as being sufficiently fit. If their assertion were true, then comets and the other meteorological "impressions" of both the middle and highest regions of the air would be denied passage through that medium even more than the wind would be. This has been proven by many reasons elsewhere, which I will briefly attempt to measure and repeat in this place. The exhalation that produces wind (according to Aristotle’s decrees) is very light in its substance, and therefore it is more fit in its measure to strive and ascend upward; for just as it is the natural inclination of all heavy things to strive downward, so conversely it is the nature of light things to seek the heights. Therefore, such an exhalation is more prone, because of its lightness, to be sublimated higher than the matter of ignited meteors (among which the <term>Comet</term> is the chief). The matter of comets is more compact, dense, and viscous, and consequently not as disposed to ascend as the matter of the winds.

Furthermore, he assigns to the windy exhalation a disposition of subtlety and thinness, by which it happens that in its nature it is more inclined to penetrate through the middle region of the air than the comet and other <term>assub</term> <note>An Arabic-derived term used in medieval and Renaissance texts to refer to shooting stars or "falling" meteors.</note> or ignited impressions, which are given a thicker and more compact matter. Therefore, just as it is more difficult for such matter to be carried upward due to its viscosity and compact disposition compared to wind, which is lighter, it is also certain that it penetrates with more difficulty; for thinner things penetrate where access is denied to thicker ones. Finally, he ascribes to the nature of the windy exhalation that it is not fit to be inflamed or set on fire. From this, it is manifest—by his own concession, as it were—that it is easier for this exhalation to penetrate through the middle region of the air without great hindrance than it is for ignited meteors. For that which is actually fiery, or closer to a fiery state, is more repelled and attacked by cold (which is the predominant quality in the middle region of air), and consequently driven downward, than that which has no potential for inflammation. But truly, by the testimony of the said Aristotle, windy exhalations are not at all fit for lighting or burning, whereas those ignited impressions are entirely prone and ready for inflammation. From these points, it is likely that those thick, hot, dry, viscous, dense, and compact terrestrial exhalations are less fit to ascend into the highest region of the air than those thin and non-flammable ones—both because they are raised into the heights with more difficulty due to their compact consistency, and because they can penetrate with more difficulty due to their thicker and duller composition. Moreover, they are in the most immediate potential for inflammation; indeed, the matter of these things is even accustomed to be ignited in the lowest and middle regions of the air, as daily experience teaches us. Therefore, without doubt, either this matter does not ascend from the earth into the highest region of the air as Aristotle thought, or the wind has its origin from elsewhere. Indeed, to use Aristotle's very own arguments, neither the one nor the other can spring from the earth because of the contrariety that exists between them and the cold middle region of the air, whose nature is to attack its opposites, to resist them mightily, and to depress them downward toward the earth and seas.

But without doubt, everyone will ask: if the matter of such comets and ignited impressions does not flow out from the earth by exhaling, where then is its spring, or from what source does its consistency or essence come? To this question, we think we must respond—not without deliberation—that the source of such impressions is the same as that of the winds and waters: namely, the heavens or the open air. We shall proceed to prove this by reasons resting upon both True Philosophy and Holy Theosophy. First, among philosophers both modern and ancient, it is a common saying that just as fire is nothing other than air that is most thin and dilated, so too thick fire is air itself altered into dryness by divine motion. It is for this reason that they called the <term>ether</term> <note>original: "aetherem"</note> as if it were "fiery air" <note>original: "æthe aerem"</note>—that is, a spirit equally mixed with fire. Although this species of purest air cannot be discerned by us visually in its dissipated and subtle nature, nevertheless, if it is gathered into a mass by the will and act of Divine Wisdom through its angelic ministers, it will appear in the appearance and form of a "luciferous" or light-bearing star (such as a comet). Will this seem arduous and difficult to the Aristotelians? Even by Aristotle himself, the prince of those men, this sentiment of ours was established when he defined a star as being a denser portion of its own orb—as if he had said that a luminous star is a contracted and condensed part of the ether, worked upon by the lucid spirit of the world, from which that star acquires its lucid and fiery form. If this is conceded by Aristotle himself, what shall prevent the aerial spirit, moving in whatever region of its sphere, from being able to acquire a visible form by its own condensation? For a star of the ethereal heaven, though in the consistency of the element of fire or the highest region of the air, is far greater in its simplicity...

Consequently, the crashes of thunder cannot be produced in that place due to the lack of watery moisture, which ought to resist the impulse of the fiery spirits. Hence it happens that, because of the fiery disposition of the place, instead of dark clouds, fiery meteors are sometimes (though rarely) found there. These are not as massive as the bulk of clouds, since the thinness of the region’s consistency cannot produce such a mass in its condensation. Furthermore, the winds are not violent in that region—indeed, they are scarcely sensible—because they find little or no resistance there due to the thinness and dryness of the region's consistency. And this is especially to be considered: that fiery spirits always mix themselves with a substance of their own nature and illuminate it, in the manner of that royal spirit who set his tabernacle in the sun. These bright spirits receive their splendor from that luminous source reigning everywhere invisibly, and especially in his solar tabernacle; from which the bright force of life is not only flashed out on all sides to the stars and every other bright creature, but is even attributed to the angels themselves. It is their office to accommodate the lights received from the source of light to their own proper spheres, from which they are afterward imparted to the elements. Those lights are then received and absorbed by the elemental demons, who pour them into the elements either visibly or invisibly, according to the divine will. These pourings-forth include light, motion, and those **Aristotelian** "influences." Having considered these things, we descend thus to the general description of comets and any fiery impressions:

A Comet or <term>Assub</term> <note>A term derived from Arabic, used by medieval scholars to describe a "falling star" or a comet-like phenomenon.</note> of the superior order is an aerial body, gathered and condensed in the upper region by an angelic breath; it is animated and inspired by a bright spirit through the rays of divine wisdom and the mediation of his angelic ministers. It is ordained by the sacrosanct name of said wisdom according to the will of the Father or Creator, to be perfected here in the lands, waters, and air, and finally, upon dissolution, to be expanded invisibly through the common air.

In this description of a fiery impression of the superior order, the material cause is expressed first: namely, that it is drawn from the source of the air and from its very summit <note>original: "fastigio"</note> and purer part. This seems to be confirmed by these words of **Moses**, which we have often repeated before: *Jehovah shall open to thee (says Moses) his good treasure, the heavens, by giving rain, etc.* *Deuteronomy 28:12.* From which also, as if from a common treasury of all meteors, *Jehovah is said to bring forth the winds.* *Psalm 135:7.* Has it not also been said elsewhere, that *GOD, by means of his wisdom, fits a weight and a measure to the air, and weighs the waters in a measure?*

For in truth, the meteors of the upper region of the air, as far as their bodies are concerned, are nothing other than "spiritual clouds" which do not dissolve into rain like the lower clouds, but finally vanish into the air. They behave much like "spirit of wine" <note>original: "spiritus vini," referring to highly distilled alcohol or ethanol</note> that has been many times rectified; although it is visible in its mass, yet when the glass is opened, it vanishes invisibly into the air and is gradually resolved. Thus, we see that clouds in the upper part of the middle region, which are saffron in color, never dissolve into rain, but are instead accustomed to return and be transmuted into subtle and invisible air, from which they were radically derived. Hence, they are called dry and sterile clouds. In exactly the same way, the air—placed and gathered in the highest region by the power of "ignited demons" <note>original: "daemonum ignitorum," referring here to fiery spirits or angelic beings rather than "demons" in the modern sense</note>—is sometimes reduced into such clouds, though they differ greatly from common clouds in their brightness and purity. Job seems to confirm this same point with these words: <margin>Job 37:21.</margin> *And now men do not look upon the light when it is bright in the upper clouds, which the passing wind has cleansed*, Job 37:21. <note>The text cites verse 20, but modern bibles list this as 21.</note> Whence we also think it worthy of observation that the wind performs its office even in the upper regions of the air, contrary to the opinion of the <term>Peripatetics</term> <note>Followers of Aristotle’s philosophy, who believed the upper atmosphere was too thin for wind.</note>. From these things, it is clear that the matter or consistency of the body of any fiery meteor is air, compressed in a certain dry manner—that is, by the breaths of fiery spirits to execute the divine will—and contracted into one visible mass according to the species of the impression.

Secondly, we have expressed the **formal cause** of the same in a general way: namely, that it is a visible airy body, animated and inspired by a lucid and flashing spirit. This was clearly explained in the Pillar of Fire that preceded the Israelites during the night, and the Star that guided the three Magi of the East and showed the place where the Savior of the world was born.

Thirdly, we have made the **efficient and informing cause** twofold: namely, the primary cause, which is Wisdom <note>original: "sapientia"</note> itself; and the secondary or assisting cause, the angelic ministers, whom we also call spirits <note>original: "daemones"</note>. Regarding the office of the primary cause in this work, we read these things in Holy Scripture: <margin>Psalm 78:15.</margin> *GOD by his wisdom fits the weight of the wind or air and weighs the waters in measure; he makes a decree for the rain and a way for the lightning of the thunders*, Job 28. <note>The author blends Psalm 78 and Job 28 here.</note> From this it is clear that Wisdom is that greatest Angel, under whose command are the fiery angels as well as the airy and watery ones, as it is in his power to rule and dispose the air, waters, and flashing fires. Furthermore, it is written, <margin>Job 38:37.</margin> *Who made the sapphire clouds with wisdom?* Job 38:37. <margin>Proverbs 3.</margin> And elsewhere, *by wisdom the upper clouds distil the dew*, Proverbs 3. <margin>Wisdom 10:17.</margin> And elsewhere, *GOD preceded the Israelites in a pillar of cloud by day, and with a light of fire shining throughout the night*, Psalm 78:15. Or as we find in the Book of Wisdom, 10:17, *Wisdom was a covering for the Israelites by day and a starlight by night*. Indeed, if I were to say that a fiery meteor is the "tabernacle of Wisdom," fortified by its fiery ministers—which either looks upon the sins of men with a threatening eye and pursues them in its wrath with threats, or looks kindly in its mercy—<margin>Wisdom 10.</margin> you will perceive that this deviates very little from the sense of the sacred writings. For it is written, *Wisdom was a covering for the Israelites by day, and a starlight by night*, Wisdom 10. Here, therefore, it mercifully looked upon the Israelites from its tabernacle, which was the Pillar of Fire—one of the primary species among fiery impressions. So also, from such a tabernacle—namely, the body of a comet—Wisdom shone forth and by its light directed the Magi or wise men of the East to the place where Christ, the Savior of the world, was born. But truly, <margin>Leviticus 10:2.</margin> it is written that fire, coming out from the presence of Jehovah—or Wisdom, or the Angel in whom was the name of Jehovah—hidden in the pillar of cloud or fire, killed the sons of Aaron and they died, Leviticus 10:2. <margin>Numbers 16:35.</margin> And elsewhere it is said, *thus the anger of Jehovah was greatly kindled, and fire went out from Jehovah, and consumed those two hundred and fifty men who offered incense, etc.* Numbers 16:35. <margin>Deuteronomy 4:24.</margin> And hence it is that Jehovah in his wrath is called a *consuming fire*: Deuteronomy 4:24. And so it is certain that GOD is accustomed not only to kill sinners visibly by fire sent from a fiery meteor, but also to wound them and stir up a foul pestilence among men by that fire dispersed invisibly through the mediation of his angelic instruments. By such a fiery scourge <margin>2 Samuel 24:16.</margin> seventy thousand men of the Israelites died invisibly, with the Angel of GOD inflicting and striking the blow, 2 Samuel 24:16. Thus we also see that the substance of a comet, being invisibly dissipated through the air, most often produces plagues, famine, and drought of the earth, as is declared through the effect. But I would have you understand that there are, without a doubt, very many comets and other fiery impressions in the air which are entirely invisible to men in both their origin and effect; these are, beyond all controversy, the causes of various epidemic diseases, as discussed more copiously in the chapter *On Invisible Lucid Meteors*. We say, therefore, that GOD, through the mediation of his flaming angelic ministers (among whom we recognize Wisdom as the chief and primary), is the efficient cause not only of any fiery meteor, but also of watery ones and every other kind. And although the <term>Peripatetics</term> and many others ascribe such an office to the stars, the element of fire, and the coldness of the middle region of the air, yet it belongs to a true Christian to attribute such acts to the "Act of Acts" <note>i.e., God as the Prime Mover</note>—namely, to give to God what is of God, and by no means to arrogantly credit these things to creatures. From the lack of such consideration, the monstrous perversity of idolatry arose among the Heathens, along with the neglect of the true worship of God. To this error must be attributed the fact that almost every barbarian nation has attempted to invent and establish a new god for itself.

And although the followers of Aristotle have divided the Comet into only two species—namely the "hairy" and the "bearded"—we, instructed by the learning of others well-experienced in the mysteries of philosophy, gather that there are many more species. Each of these seems to claim a peculiar name for itself because of its different appearance when it shows itself:

*   One they call a **burning lance**, because it is stretched out at length and is of a quite dense size.
*   Another they call **Xiphias** <note>original: "Xiphiam," from the Greek for sword-shaped.</note>, which is a shorter lance, tapering more to a point at its summit.
*   A third they call **Mercurial**, which is bluish, very small, and equipped with a tail.
*   A fourth they call the **soldier**, for it is of a Martian color <note>A reddish hue associated with the planet Mars.</note>.
*   A fifth they call the **aurora**, as it exceeds the brightness of all the stars.
*   A sixth they call the **Rose**, and this bears the likeness of a human face impressed upon it.
*   A seventh they call the **Tenacula** <note>Likely referring to "tongs" or "pincers."</note>, as if standing upon a fiery base, with a wondrous tail that seems to be carried upward.
*   An eighth they call the **Black**, being of a dark color, with a short tail and very little hair.
*   A ninth is called **Ceratias** <note>original: "ceratiam," meaning "horned" in Greek.</note>, named for its horn-like shape of fire and appearance.

To these are added three others, which are not as permanent as the rest: the first is called the **Burning Beam** because of its appearance; the second, **flying sparks**; and the last is called a **Chasma** <note>A "Chasm" or opening in the sky.</note>. In this last appearance, the sky seems to open with a sudden light appearing beneath the clouds, so that a terrible abyss seems to be present. You will find the likenesses of all these meteors depicted and visually described in our "Meteorological Mirror," placed in the locations most suitable to their generation.

## CHAPTER XIII.

### Third Part.

#### *Concerning the fiery meteors of the middle region.*

Among the fiery meteors of the middle region of the air, we consider the principal ones to be flashes, lightnings, and thunderbolts. The latter two rarely happen without that tremendous crash called **thunder**. Thus, thunder seems to be nothing other than an effect between a "luminous soul" (or fiery spirit) acting strongly, and a "dense spirit" (vaporous, cloudy, or watery) resisting perversely. But in truth, just as we see in man that certain necessary organs are required to produce his voice and speech, so the Holy Scriptures testify that the Creator of the world speaks to His creatures in many ways and through many mediums—namely, through thunders, visions, dreams, and so on—concerning which we shall speak more widely below. First, however, we shall speak in a succinct discourse about what the Heathens <note>Meaning the pre-Christian Greek and Roman philosophers.</note> thought concerning the stupendous and profound origin of such meteors, so that we may afterwards transcend to the sense of the Holy Page with a better method.

And although in the preceding pages we have discussed clearly enough that "luminous soul" which gives form to meteors, we will nonetheless offer a few words in this place concerning three types of flashing, which differ among themselves only by degrees of material thickness. **Aristotle** maintains that the general material cause of such luminous meteors is a hot and dry exhalation, raised from the earth into the middle region of the air by the power of the stars. There—partly by the forceful collision and shaking of clouds, and partly through <term>antiperistasis</term> <note>The scientific theory that a quality is intensified when surrounded by its opposite, such as heat becoming more intense when trapped by surrounding cold.</note> (namely, because of the intense cold of that place)—he says this matter is ignited while compressed and enclosed in the "belly" of a cloud, and because of its earthy and compact nature, it tends downward. From this, thunder consequently makes that noise or roar, which arises from the extinguishing of such an ignited exhalation in the water of the cloud. This, I say, seems to be the intention of Aristotle in Book 2 of his *Meteorology* and elsewhere, as well as his followers, both Heathen and Christian. And in truth, Aristotle is somewhat to be excused in such a difficult resolution, since not only he, but almost all other philosophers have seemed to doubt and differ from one another (hardly being consistent with themselves) regarding the origin of lightning and thunder. For **Empedocles** thought that the thunderbolt and flashing were fire intercepted from the rays of the sun descending downward. But **Anaxagoras** thought that fire was a portion of the "ether" falling from on high into the hollow of a cloud, where it strikes; he says the brightness of this light leaping out from the cloud is called a flash, or lightning, or a thunderbolt, and by the effect of this piercing, it makes thunder.

### On the Formal Cause of Meteors.

Others claim that lightning arises from hot and dry winds trapped within tightly compressed and surrounded clouds, which they say burn and ignite the clouds with such winds; from this, a crashing sound is born. There are also some who deny that lightning is generated by fire at all, but instead by an "imagination" or reflection of shimmering water, seen at night in the clouds through the brightness of the stars. But Aristotle seems to rightly refute this opinion, because lightning is visible during the day under the sun's rays. Finally, this operation in nature is so marvelous that some, plunging themselves deeper into the mysteries of GOD and nature and diligently considering the wondrous power and operation of the thunderbolt, have judged it to be not a work of nature, but the highest immediate effect of God—a group in which every true Christian ought to be counted. But we shall first hasten to examine that Aristotelian definition.

He [Aristotle] says its <term>material cause</term> <note>The substance from which a thing is made.</note> is taken from the earth, and he makes the <term>acting cause</term> of its elevation the Astral power. He makes the <term>efficient cause</term> <note>The primary agent or force that produces an effect.</note> and the igniter an external and accidental collision and shaking of the clouds, along with the cold of the region acting through <term>antiperistasis</term> <note>original: "antiperistasin"—a philosophical concept where a quality is intensified by being surrounded by its opposite, such as heat becoming more intense when trapped by cold.</note> in its illumination. Finally, he gives the reason for its downward motion: namely, because a portion of its material is terrestrial, and consequently heavy and compact.

But as for its material cause and the seat of its <term>matrix</term> <note>The "womb" or place of origin where a phenomenon is formed.</note> from which lightning is produced, we are taught by the Holy Bible that they are far different than what that Aristotle thought. In the book of Ecclesiasticus it is found: *Look upon the rainbow, and bless him that made it; very beautiful it is in the brightness thereof. It encompasseth the heaven about with a circle of glory, the hands of the Most High have bended it. By his commandment he maketh the snow to fall apace, and sendeth forth swiftly the lightnings of his judgment. Through this the treasures are opened, and clouds fly forth as birds. By his mighty power he maketh the clouds firm, and the hailstones are broken small. At his sight the mountains are shaken, and at his will the south wind bloweth. The noise of his thunder maketh the earth to tremble, so doth the northern storm and the whirlwind, etc.* <note>original: "Eccl. 43"—referencing Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 43:11–17.</note> From these sayings of the wise man, we gather not only the material cause of thunder and lightning, but indeed of almost all other meteors—both the bright and the dark—indeed even the formal, efficient, and final causes; at the same time, the secret matrix from which the matter of all of them arises is explained there. For as for the matter of meteors, he seems to indicate it first, along with the matrix, when he says: "the treasures are opened, and clouds fly forth," etc. From this it is clear that the "treasure of Jehovah" is the matrix of all meteors—indeed, the very matrix of matter. Hence it is said elsewhere: *Jehovah shall open unto thee his good treasure, the heaven to give the rain unto thy land*, <note>original: "Deut. 28.12"</note>. And elsewhere: *He bringeth the wind out of his treasuries*, <note>original: "Psal. 135"</note>. From this it is clear that by "heavens" he understands the open air in which the clouds are suspended; hence it is found said elsewhere: *GOD sets a weight for the air and weighs the waters by measure, he made a decree for the rain, and a way for the lightning of the thunder*, <note>original: "Iob. 28. 25"</note>. From these it is evident that just as air is contained within air, no differently than a thing contained within its container, so indeed air is the matrix and sanctuary, or treasure chest, of the meteors procreated from the multifaceted air.

Hence, in a more abundant passage, he seems to acknowledge that any of these is a "gathering of spirit," that is, air. Their formal cause is also drawn from the aforementioned description—namely, the <term>Iris</term> or celestial bow [rainbow], where it is said: *look upon the rainbow and bless him that made it: very spacious in its splendor, it has circled the heaven in the circuit of its glory.* Furthermore, the snows, flashes of lightning, mists, clouds, small hailstones, winds (or the breathing South Wind), the thundering voice with its motion, the Northern storm, etc., do not lack their formal differences in their very naming, by which one usually differs from another. The efficient cause is also indicated in what is said: *the hands of the Most High opened it*, and elsewhere: *Bless him who made it*, and *it circled the heaven in the circuit of its glory*, and *by his command he speeded the snow, and speeds the lightnings to send forth his judgment, and for this the treasures were opened, and in his greatness he placed the clouds, and by his will the South Wind blew*, <note>original: "Psal. 135. 7."</note> and so in the rest, and elsewhere: *Jehovah makes lightnings with the rain.* Finally, the <term>final intention</term> <note>The purpose or goal for which a thing exists.</note> of the generation of these meteors is that they might fulfill His will; hence it is said there: *By his will the South Wind blew*, and elsewhere you will find it written: *that the whirlwind, cold, ice, clouds, rains, lightnings, etc.—whatever GOD has commanded these to do upon the face of the world on the earth, whether for a scourge, or for terror, or for performing an act of mercy, he causes them to be ready*, <note>original: "Iob. 38. 8."</note>. And in the prophet Baruch it is found: *The clouds, commanded to pass through the whole world, obey and fulfill the command itself. When lightning appears, it is clear; and the wind itself blows through every region; and when the clouds are commanded by GOD to go through the whole habitable world, they perform what was commanded; and the fire sent from above to devastate mountains and forests does what was commanded*, <note>original: "Baruch. 6."</note>. From these, therefore, it will be permitted to express the description of lightning in this manner:

-> Lightning is a certain fiery air, which is brought forth from the treasure chest of GOD (the heavens) by divine power, and is sent forth to fulfill the will of the Creator here on earth, whether for good or for ill. <-

But if we wish to describe lightning with all its "accidents" <note>In philosophy, "accidents" are qualities that can change without changing the essence of the thing, such as color or timing.</note> and consequently explain the entire essence of thunder (which is a mixed meteor), let it be permitted to describe it in this way by the testimony of the holy scriptures.

It is confirmed thus: In the Apocalypse it is written, *From the throne proceed lightnings. Rev. 4:3.* And elsewhere: *Will you send out lightnings and they will go, and returning say, "Here we are"? Job 38:35.* And elsewhere: *smoke ascended in his anger, and fire broke out from his face, etc. Psalm 17.* And elsewhere: *Clouds and darkness are round about him, fire proceeds before him and shall set fire round about him; his lightnings have shone upon the world, etc. Psalm 97:2.* And elsewhere: *The clouds gave a voice, for indeed your arrows passed through, etc. Psalm 76.* Where by "arrows" he seems to understand lightnings in this place. Whence it is also written elsewhere: *The shafts of lightning shall go directly, and as if from the well-curved bow of the clouds. Wisdom 5:22.* From this he seems to imply that the clouds "gave a voice" because the lightnings passed through and penetrated them.

->Or thus:<-

Thunder is the voice of GOD raised in a cloud, surrounded and covered on all sides by the force of the waters, before whom a fire precedes and sets fire round about him.

Hence Job says: *Will you raise your voice in a mist, and will the force of waters cover you? Job 38:34.* And elsewhere: *Clouds and darkness are round about him, fire proceeds before him and shall set fire round about him. Psalm 97:2.*

->Or thus:<-

Thunder is the voice of God, at which he gives a multitude of waters in heaven, and makes lightnings and rain. Hence it is written: *At his voice he gives a multitude of waters in heaven, and raises the mists from the ends of the earth; he makes lightnings into rain, and brings forth the wind from his treasuries. ->Or thus:<-

Thunder is the multitude of a fountain of waters, or the voice of the clouds, produced by the flashes of God shining upon the whole world.

->Or thus:<-

Thunder is the sound of a multitude of waters, fearing and disturbed at the sight of Jehovah, or a voice or crash going around, which the clouds are accustomed to give; this voice is produced or created immediately by the flashes proceeding from the throne of God and breaking out from the clouds (which are the pavilion of Jehovah) to execute the divine will.

In this description, the <term>material</term> <note>The "matter" or substance through which the sound travels.</note> organ of this kind of voice is the waters, as if fearing and disturbed, whence they are accustomed to give out a voice, or sound, or crash—which indeed produces the power and strength that the bright and shining sight of God, the worker of wonders, brings forth. Hence it is said: *before the brightness in his sight the clouds passed away, hail and coals of fire; the Lord thundered from heaven, and the Most High gave his voice. Psalm 17.* And elsewhere: *The waters saw you, O GOD, and they feared; and the abysses were disturbed, a multitude of the sound of waters; the clouds gave a voice, the voice of your thunder was in a wheel. Psalm 76:17.*

The **formal cause** is also described in that it happens with a crash and flashes.

The **efficient cause** appears to be the lightnings, or rather the fiery gaze of God animating the lightnings themselves and directing them to the goal ordained by God; hence lightnings are like the instruments of God in his wrath, just as a sword is the instrument of a man who strikes, where we say such a man struck with a sword, and not that the sword struck. Therefore, we call GOD himself alone the actor in these things, the father of the thunders themselves, who sends out lightnings like his arrows from his throne according to that passage in the Apocalypse.

The **end**, however, we have established to be the fulfillment of the divine will.

->Or finally, in this manner:<-

Thunder is the voice, or speech, or utterance, or sound proceeding from the mouth of Jehovah, which is directed under the whole heaven with light over the borders or edges of the earth, after which the sound roars or GOD thunders with his excellent voice; and he is not tracked down when his voice has been heard, he who thundering does wondrously with his voice.

We have this confirmed by the words of the Holy Scriptures in this way: *Hear with trembling the voice or speech, or (as another interprets it) the utterance going out from his mouth; he directs it under the whole heaven, that utterance and*

# Section I. Portion IV. Part II. Book III. Member II.

...light over the ends or borders of the earth. After him a sound roars, he thunders with the voice of his majesty, and it is not tracked down when his voice has been heard; the thundering God does wondrously with his voice, etc. <note>original: "Iob. 37." Referring to Job 37:3-5.</note>

Therefore, against the foolish opinions of the Pagans, it is demonstrated that neither exhalations nor vapors, nor the sun with the stars, nor earth or water, nor the elements, nor created nature itself, but God himself—who is the operator of all wonders—is the immediate <term>efficient cause</term> <note>The primary agent or "force" that directly brings an effect into being.</note> of these marvels. We have this confirmed by Holy Scripture, lest we—like the Pagans—falsely attribute these things to nature, or to its elements, or to things <term>composed of elements</term>. <note>The original Latin "elementatis" refers to physical objects created from the four basic elements.</note> These must be attributed first and above all to the Creator, lest in this way we unexpectedly plunge headlong into foul idolatry alongside the Pagans.

But I know well that it will be objected by some that thunders of the sort spoken of in Holy Scripture were miraculous and not at all "natural." In this opinion fall both recent and ancient philosophers: namely, that Thunders are sometimes natural and sometimes supernatural. It is as if those things which are accomplished in the moist nature of the world are not done immediately by GOD, just as those which happen according to the season of the year or the hot weather of the air, or those which occur in winter or by other hidden reasons. Yet it cannot be unknown to a true Christian that GOD is everywhere, and has His dwelling both in the elements themselves and in things composed of elements. For in the highest heaven He is clothed with light as with a garment; in the middle of heaven He placed His tabernacle in the Sun; in the lowest region He made the thick cloud His hut. Indeed, as Job testifies: *Jehovah answered him out of the whirlwind.* Furthermore, He is also on the earth: *For the earth shall bring forth a Savior.* He speaks in the Prophet and through the mouth of the Prophet; indeed, GOD uses every thing of this world as His <term>organ</term>, <note>In this context, "organ" means a musical instrument or a tool through which a force acts.</note> and speaks in various ways according to the variety of the instrument. <margin><unclear>*</unclear></margin> In the simple spirit of the world, His voice is neither heard nor understood except by those who are enlightened or stirred by the spirit; He speaks in angels and through the mediation of angelic instruments, but to mortals He most often speaks terribly in His anger—that is, in thunder. Whence Job says: *Hear with trembling the voice going out from His mouth under the whole heaven, and the light over the borders of the earth. Job 37.*

Therefore, those philosophers are of unsound mind who distinguish thunders into "empty" and "brute"—those, namely, which seem to signify nothing—and "prophetic" or "significant." As if thunders should be called empty, brute, and signifying nothing simply because the intention of God (who produced nothing in the world in vain) was not revealed to them during their creation. *O how hidden are the mysteries of God, and how concealed from the knowledge of profane men!* Nor indeed can I praise the skill of Cicero in this matter, who in his book *On Divination* <note>original: "Lib. De Diuinat." Referring to Marcus Tullius Cicero's *De Divinatione*.</note> seems to deny that any species of divination can arise from the observation of lightning—and this quite thoughtlessly—calling it vain and empty. And yet we are taught the contrary by the Holy Bible, where it is written: *That the great GOD, surpassing our knowledge, extends the clouds like His tent at His pleasure, and lightens with His light from above, and covers the depths of the sea; for by these He judges the peoples, and gives food to many mortals; in His hands He hides the light, and commands it to return again, etc. Job 36.*

From these things it is right to gather that GOD sends lightning to execute justice upon mortals, and also turns lightning into rain for the benefit of mortals. Whence it is said elsewhere: *When He utters His voice, the waters are multiplied in the heaven; He causes the clouds to ascend from the end of the earth; He makes lightnings for the rain, and brings forth the winds out of His treasures. Jeremiah 51:15.* From this it is clear that there is no thunder unless it be the voice of Jehovah. Whence the Royal Psalmist speaks generally of thunder in these words: *The voice of Jehovah is over the waters; the voice of the strong, glorious GOD thunders; the voice of Jehovah is over many waters; the voice of Jehovah is powerful and in His might; the voice of Jehovah is in majesty; the voice of Jehovah breaks the cedars, Jehovah even breaks the cedars of Lebanon, and makes them skip like a calf, Lebanon and Sirion; the voice of Jehovah divides the flames of fire; the voice of Jehovah shakes the wilderness; the voice of Jehovah makes the deer to calve and strips the forests bare; but in His temple He speaks all His glory, etc. Psalm 29.* Here the King makes mention of the terrible voice of Jehovah, and of that peaceful one.

We conclude, therefore, that it is the greatest folly of any Christian, indeed an irrecoverable madness, to place such faith in the vain and lying opinions of the Pagans who toss about empty words concerning thunder. These men try to persuade people that thunders and lightnings are, as it were, accidental things arising from the natural intemperance of the heavens and are not at all sent by God. Thus, looking only at the effect, they desire to falsely hold that effect as the <term>efficient cause</term>. That is to say, they wish to attribute to creatures that which belongs to God, the Creator of every thing. Thus they proceed not only to prattle thoughtlessly but to blaspheme impiously, leading men to idolatry—as if someone attributed the life of a man to his body and not to his soul. Therefore, I would have you know that I have written in this place by no means rashly, but diligently and supported by good foundations; other philosophers, deeper in the hidden mystery of Jehovah, seem to agree with me. Considering the wonderful operation of the lightning bolt, they have judged it to be not a work of nature, but the immediate effect of the Most High GOD.
