Know then that the wise of this world—the followers of the Pagan philosophers—are quite delirious, have been delirious, and will continue to be delirious in their obstinacy. Indeed, they do not concede that God works "all in all," <note>original Latin: "omnia in omnibus"</note> and that His word moves, stirs, and preserves all things. Instead, they ascribe it to created nature, pretending that God acts out of necessity through intermediaries—namely, through secondary and tertiary causes. Thus erring, they are unwilling to understand that God operates solely through His word, and not through other necessary means; and thus by no means through those causes alleged by them, but only *in* them, as if they were mere instruments.

But you, who are nourished by the Holy Bible and governed by the law of Christ, I urge you to conceive and forever turn over in your minds that God created the first substance—namely, water—as wet or moist through His word, and this very substance remains moist even today after the passage of so many thousands of years. Again, from this water, the heaven and the earth (as *Saint Peter* witnesses) were created by means of the Word. Furthermore, He produced the light in the heavens, the sun, moon, and stars, day and night, and all other things by His spoken word, and He imposed their duties upon them; therefore, all those things perform their functions according to that word. Where, then, is the "nature" of the *Peripatetics* <note>The "Peripatetics" were the followers of Aristotle, whose scientific theories dominated universities for centuries.</note> which might perform these things? There is plainly nothing anywhere except the one and only word of God, which works these and all other things, according to the word of the *Evangelist*:

<margin>All things were made through the word, and without it, nothing [was made]; in it was life, etc. John 1.</margin>

From this it is clear that without Him, nothing can exist or act. Insofar as the air is a part of the heavenly substance, it follows that it was made by the word and, as it were, "swims" in the word, inasmuch as the word embraces all things and is moved and governed by the word of God itself. Indeed, within that word—as if in God's universal treasure chest—He has His own particular chests from which various species of meteors are produced. These He has placed under the protection and governance of various angels and spirits (who were also created from and in the air by the word), just as may be gathered from various passages of Holy Scripture to be cited by us below. By their administration (as the Word moves and operates), all meteors in the air are produced, and all storms which usually happen to the world arise in a wondrous way. Hence it is said that "He made his angels winds, and his ministers a flaming fire," etc. <note>Psalm 104:4.</note> Thus, in the beginning of the world, God created the angels along with the air, so that they might perform and execute their task and office in the air concerning the direction of storms, rain, [snow], hail, frost, clouds, lightning, thunder, fire, chasms <note>original: "chasmatum." In historical meteorology, "chasms" were appearances of openings or gaps in the sky, often brightly colored.</note>, thunderbolts, waters, heat, cold, moisture, dryness, and many other things of that kind. This very thing is also done today by His word, all of which will be clearly declared by us in our following Portion, where we will deal with the <term>efficient cause</term> <note>The primary agent or force that directly brings an effect into being.</note> of meteors.

This is indeed unknown to the *Pagan* philosophers and their *Christian* followers, for a lying and false spirit has claimed a seat in their mouths and writings. From this, their ignorance and the vanity of their philosophy has arisen; nor is it a wonder, since they have known neither **GOD** nor His sacrosanct word. Indeed, despising or at least not reading the Holy Scripture, but brooding only on their own delusions, they are accustomed to sew lie upon lie. If these Christian disciples of the *Pagan* *Peripatetics* had read the Holy Bible with the same zeal with which they turned over the false *Aristotelian* books and volumes, they would have found the truth about the air and storms—that those matters do not behave in the way those men wrote in their books filled with imaginings.

But rather, for these species already mentioned, God has His own peculiar treasure chests in the open air, from which He produces winds and storms. The air swims and exists in the word of God and is led by the angels appointed for this purpose, as God's word directs, when, where, and how God wills. Hence *David* said: **GOD'S** angels, most mighty in strength, doing His word, listening to the voice of His command, ministers doing His pleasure, Psalm 103:20. We also read of "the prince having power of the air." <note>Ephesians 2:2.</note>

And although this very thing proposed by us in this discourse might seem trivial to some, it is nevertheless arduous and of the greatest importance, insofar as it also concerns divine honor. It is vital that the children of God truly and fundamentally know and understand that the logic of storms and other visible operations do not happen by their own motion, or by chance, nor even in such an imaginary way as the *Pagans* pose and fashion in their writings. Rather, they are brought forth and proceed from divine providence and from the chambers of the divine treasures, and are sent down from above into this lower world. Thus, if ever dangerous storms arise, they may invoke God, that He might be willing to mercifully turn away that danger of the storm and in its place grant kind rain, and at the same time defend, protect, and preserve the fruits of the earth together with men and cattle from all evil—and also concerning all other matters of trust which can yield to the honor of God.

I would wish you to consider how immense the difference is between the books of the *Pagan* philosophers and the fountain of all truth, and that by adhering to their testimonies, it is necessary that you depart from the fountain of all truth.

->*On the fiery Meteors of the lower aerial region: namely,*<-

The prince of the Peripatetics <note>The "Peripatetics" were the followers of the Greek philosopher Aristotle.</note>, and others who follow his doctrine, count among those eleven fiery impressions they usually mention the *Assub* <note>original: "Assub"; an Arabic-derived term used by medieval and Renaissance scholars for meteors or shooting stars.</note> that appears and disappears. To this number, we may also quite reasonably add the evening redness, since there is no great difference between it and the *Assub* that appears and disappears. These philosophers maintain that the *Assub* is created from a thin exhalation hidden in the clouds, some part of which sometimes appears and sometimes vanishes. But we say that such suddenly appearing and disappearing luminous impressions come from more hidden causes, namely from the secret will of God and the hidden operations of His word and His angelic ministers, whose duty it is to fulfill divine commands with such visible instruments, whether for blessing or for punishment, on the lands and in the waters.

From the Holy Scriptures, we also gather that the clouds scatter their light, which shines all around wherever the will of the Governor drives them, for everything He commands them upon the face of the earth—whether for a scourge, or to show kindness and mercy (Job 37:11-13). Here, he seems to mean not only lightning but every luminous meteor created around the clouds, which the Creator produces in His wisdom in a wonderful and sometimes miraculous way. Thus David speaks: "O Lord, how manifold are your works! In wisdom you have made them all" (Psalm 104:24). <note>original: "Psal. 103. 24." (Vulgate numbering)</note> And elsewhere: "Remember his marvelous works that he has done, his wonders, and the judgments of his mouth" (Psalm 105:5). <note>original: "Ps. 105. 5." (Vulgate numbering)</note> From His wisdom, I say, or His word, all things are produced in a marvelous way; it is His role to "bind the waters in His thick clouds, so that the cloud is not rent under them" (Job 26:8). For God in His wisdom not only sets the weight for the wind and weighs the waters by measure, and makes a decree for the rain, but also a path for the lightning of the thunder and for every luminous meteor.

The same must be thought regarding the evening redness, in which, nevertheless, the nature of the living light and the consistency of the animated body differ. For in the evening redness, it is noted that nitrous spirits <note>original: "spiritus nitrosi"; "nitre" or "saltpeter" was believed by early scientists like Fludd to be a vital aerial substance responsible for weather and life.</note> dispersed everywhere in the air (and rendered invisible due to expansion or hiding) now appear in the open air through condensation. These spirits are observed to appear in the heavens by the blast of hot winds. So we also see that in the extraction of such a spirit of nitre, such a redness appears in the receiving vessel <note>The "recipient" in a chemical or alchemical distillation setup.</note>, an appearance caused by a compelling fiery breath. From this, it happens that unless the artist <note>The "artist" here refers to the chemist or laboratory worker.</note> watches cautiously, the receiving vessel may be shattered into infinite pieces because of the violence of the winds enclosed within (not without great danger to the artist), which we have perceived several times. In the same way, after such appearances in the sky, we have quite often observed stronger winds being produced in the air. But the operator of such an operation is Godlike Wisdom.

Falling stars in the upper part of this aerial region also arise from a tiny portion of that same light, but of a denser substance, from which comets and other fiery impressions of the upper regions originate. These have hidden operations within themselves (however much they are disparaged by men) and produce slow and almost imperceptible effects, according to the will of Him who creates nothing in vain.

The *Ignis Fatuus* <note>translated: "Will-o'-the-Wisp" or "Foolish Fire"</note>, which usually licks the hair of animals, and also Castor and Pollux <note>A term for "St. Elmo's Fire," a weather phenomenon where luminous plasma is created by a corona discharge from a pointed object in a strong electric field.</note>, are secret lights produced in thicker air and governed by the spirits of the place <note>original: "loci dæmonibus"; in this context, "demons" refers to guardian spirits or elemental beings, not necessarily evil entities.</note>, and ordained to fulfill the pleasure of the Creator. Indeed, none of these are produced in the world in a vain or futile way by this most wise and eternal Nature, which inhabits and fills every place. It would be infinite, and perhaps tedious, to explain all these things in a longer discourse; therefore, since it suffices to have spoken of their formal cause, I shall finish this chapter in a few words.

# CHAPTER XIV.
## First Part.

->*On meteors, both those of thinner and coarser consistency, belonging to the earthly nature.*<-

There are also certain luminous, manifest, and visible meteors of the macrocosm <note>The "macrocosm" refers to the universe as a whole, which early modern thinkers believed was mirrored by the "microcosm" of the human body.</note> whose consistency is more corporeal, and they claim an earthly disposition for themselves. By their nature, they tend toward melancholy and scorched bile <note>The author is using the theory of the Four Humors, suggesting these minerals have the same qualities as the bodily fluids associated with Earth (melancholy) and Heat (cholera or bile).</note>, and these are either of a thinner constitution, having the form of a coarser smoke, by which earth, sand, and stones are colored in various ways—namely yellow, black, red, white, etc.—and these smokes usually rise from the winds and the "vessels" of the earth. There is also another species of such meteors, even more corporeal, thick, and gummy, being either sulfurous or bituminous, etc. We will say a few things about what philosophers—both the ancient Pagans and their Christian followers—think regarding the generation of these earthly meteors, so that we may later compare their opinion with the source of all truth.

Thus, they <note>The "philosophers" mentioned above.</note> defined the sulfurous meteor as a certain metallic matter, cooked and joined together from an oily, fine earthy, and fiery substance by the heat of the sun and heaven.

They claim that bitumen is born in the earth from putrefied oily humors.

We, however, say that bituminous substances are nothing other than the effects of sulfur, just as ashes are the effect of burning coals, as we shall discuss more extensively in a further demonstration below—but let us return to the point.

In their description of the sulfurous meteor, we see that they made its material cause an oily and fine earth and a fiery substance; in this part they also expressed the formal cause. They positioned the efficient and "concocting" <note>The process of "concoction" was thought to be a kind of internal ripening or cooking by heat that transformed raw matter into a refined substance.</note> cause to be solar and celestial heat.

But indeed, we have said elsewhere that the internal spirit—not only of the external man but also of the visible earth and of anything constituted by it—is from the air of the universal world, as from it all things were procreated from the beginning in terms of their consistency. And we say that the parts of the universal world's air are linked together with such a bond and continuity—whether they are enclosed in the earth, in man, or in any other thing—that it is necessary for a single part of that same whole to be felt by the entire whole, and a disturbance in one part is also felt by another. From this it is clear that the sulfurous disposition of the mundane air is also the cause of that sulfurous nature in both the earth and man. Therefore, such metallic nature undoubtedly proceeded originally from the mundane air, and that by divine ordination and will, and by the execution of influences or "demons" <note>The word "daemon" here refers to mediating spirits or intelligences that govern the natural world, not necessarily evil spirits.</note> presiding over the celestial bodies, who are governed by the Word, for in it is their life.

Finally, that sulfur is produced in a wonderful way from the treasury of the air by the wisdom of GOD according to His pleasure, and created as if from nothing, and then poured out and sent into the earth as if from the treasury-chest of the heavens, is taught to us by the fact that GOD sent down sulfur <note>original: "sulphur"; in many English Bibles, this is translated as "brimstone."</note> and fire from heaven upon Sodom and Gomorrah, and overthrew the cities with all their inhabitants and everything that thrived in them (*Genesis 19*). From this treasury-chest, GOD is also accustomed to bring forth His lightnings and thunders, and very often to send His fire from heaven, as we read happened in the times of Moses and Elijah. But concerning the occult and mystical method of procreating such meteors, we shall speak more extensively (God willing) in our treatise on the efficient cause of Meteors. As for the procreation of Bitumen, it is most certain and proven by experience that it is generated by the mixing of earth with burnt sulfur, or rather by the embrace of the viscosity of one with that of the other, as seen from the effect of the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah to this very day—namely, the lake called the Dead Sea, which is said to abound in such gums in appearance, which is brought to distant places to be used as mortar for structures, and is not infrequently used among physicians.

Just as there is a difference in the Macrocosm between the glittering, flashing, lightning-striking, and thundering spirit—which is usually a matter of "more or less" (degree), so that they seem to be almost grades of luminous splendor sent out from the clouds by divine mystery—so indeed are there such and so many grades of the fiery spirit in the aerial medium of man himself. It is by means of these that febrile diseases of various kinds present themselves in action, and they are visibly perceived in the serum of the blood or the urine. Among these, a "daily fever" <note>original: "febris diaria." A fever lasting roughly 24 hours.</note> can be rightly equated to a flash, and every barely perceptible hot imbalance to a glittering spirit—or otherwise as it is reported below.

# On the Formal Cause of Meteors.
Q 2

Those fiery meteors that are of a higher nature—that is, those located in a more elevated place, such as species of comets—occupy a more sublime position within the human "air" <note>In this context, the "human air" refers to the vital spirits or the breath of life that Renaissance thinkers believed filled the body, mirroring the atmosphere of the Earth.</note>, specifically within the spirits of life. Because of this, it happens that they do not only lethally affect the "seeds" of such meteors that are scattered in the macrocosmic <note>The "Macrocosm" is the great universe/outer world.</note> air and inhaled by the human spirit, but because of their high position, they even penetrate the very essence of life. From this, plagues, pestilential fevers, and all contagious diseases arise. Experience teaches us that the appearance of a comet usually indicates decay and a sickly disposition not only in humans, but also in plants and fruits; for this reason, they are used to forecast plague and famine. Furthermore, we see that the minimum duration for a comet's appearance is seven days; in that same span of time, pestilential diseases—especially the plague and pestilential fevers—usually reach their end, for the "crisis" <term>crisis: the turning point of a disease where the patient either begins to recover or declines toward death</term> of an extremely acute disease is measured by this kind of continuation.

Therefore, within the human "air," three distinct regions are perceived: the highest place, compared to the supreme region of the atmosphere, where similar phenomena are produced; the middle place, likened to the middle atmosphere with its own adapted meteors; and the lowest place, assigned to thick spirits and humors. The solid body of man corresponds to the Earth. Just as the Earth is subject to many "accidents"—such as sulfurous flames, hot springs, and other such things—so too do gummy substances similar to amber <note>original: "succino." Amber was often categorized with "meteors" because its origins were thought to be atmospheric or resinous.</note>, sulfurous inflammations, and other similar conditions occur in the human body.

# CHAPTER XIV.

## The Third Section.

->Concerning the luminous meteors of the macrocosm formed from the air.<-

We shall explain in the following pages how the South Wind <note>original: "Auster"; the South Wind was traditionally associated in Mediterranean and European medicine with heat, moisture, and the spread of disease.</note>, along with its neighboring winds, makes the air thick and dense, corrupting it and rendering it putrid. This rarely happens without the presence of clouds; however, even without a visible appearance of clouds, it makes the air so thick—though not perfectly obvious to the senses—that it causes objects to appear smaller than they truly are for this reason. These winds produce atmospheric phenomena <term>meteors: in the 17th century, this term referred to any atmospheric phenomenon, including wind, rain, and lightning, not just space rocks</term> that are sometimes hidden and sometimes visible and manifest. These are in turn neutralized and scattered by the blowing of the opposite winds, whose effect is to annihilate and dissipate the Southern influences, making them useless through dissolution. 

From this, their malignant "seeds," dispersed invisibly in the air, enter partly into the fruits and food of men, and are partly drawn by the heart through the medium of the air through the windpipe <note>original: "asperam arteriam," literally the "rough artery," an old term for the trachea</note>. This easily infects the human spirit—specifically that "airy" part of our vitality—from which plagues and putrid diseases usually follow. This is especially true for those who are not well-protected by their own nature against these opposing blasts. Hence, it is that some are poisoned by these types of contagious seeds, while others, by divine will, remain healthy and immune from their malignancy. 

Thus we find it written that God, coming from the south with the brightness of light (that is, with lightning), **"pestilence went before him, and a burning plague followed at his feet; and where he stood, he measured the earth, and he beheld and drove asunder the nations."** <note>original: "Abak. 3. 2." This is a Latin translation of Habakkuk 3:3–6. The word "anthrax" is used here for "burning plague" or "coals of fire."</note> From this it is clear that although by divine command such luminous meteors are sent from the South to punish the impious, God does not usually strike everyone with them, but only some; hence it is said that "He measured the earth." Even the Royal Prophet <note>King David, the traditional author of the Psalms.</note> speaks in these words: **"Fear not the terror by night, nor the arrow that flies by day, nor the pestilence that walks in darkness or the night, nor the destruction that wastes at noonday"**—or as Jerome interprets it—**"from the midday demon; the plague shall not come near your tent, for he shall give his angels charge over you."** <note>original: "Psal. 91." This refers to Psalm 91:5–11. The "midday demon" (daemonio meridiano) was a common medieval personification of the dangers of the South Wind and sloth.</note> In this discourse, by "pestilence in the south," he understands the pestilential seeds which are hidden invisibly in the air, as if by a fog. 

By this first example, therefore, we see how God, hurrying from the south, enclosed by lightning, thunder, and clouds, made pestilence and contagious diseases his messengers, with which he is accustomed to disturb nations and peoples rebellious to him. That God produces all meteors, either as a scourge or to bring benefit to the inhabitants of the earth, Job seems to suggest with these words: **"The whirlwind, the cold, the ice, the frost, the clouds, the rain, the thunder, and the lightning—whatever God commands these to do upon the face of the world on the earth, whether as a scourge or to show mercy, he causes them to be ready at hand."** <note>original: "Iob. 37. 8." This is a summary of Job 37:9–13.</note> Regarding this kind of stormy spirit acting invisibly but sensibly in the air, the wise man speaks thus: **"A spirit of power, or a spirit of strength and virtue, shall stand against the impious, and like a storm or a whirlwind, it shall scatter them."** That such spirits are the angels or destroying ministers of GOD, we shall show in the proper place below.

Luminous Meteors of the Microcosm <term>microcosm: the human body viewed as a miniature reflection of the universe</term> are either:

    *   Universal, such as invisible vapors in the air or from the winds:

        *   Malignant spirit or air in man, animating the humor, which is either:
            *   **Gleaming**, or gently inflaming the spirit of the Microcosm, as in an ephemeral or daily fever.
            *   **Flashing**, or immersing itself somewhat deeper into the phlegmatic humor, like exquisitely bilious fevers.
            *   **Lightning-flashing / Thundering**: Either exciting putrid fevers in the human "air" or purifying it after a hot imbalance <note>original: "intemperiem"</note>.
        *   Spiritual bodies, animated or illuminated by light, which pass into the nature of an invisible breath. These are of the order:
            *   **Higher**, namely when the seeds <term>seminaria: "seed-beds" or invisible germs of disease</term> of pestilence, poison, and contagion are dissolved; and from this it happens that the microcosmic spirit or air is afflicted by various passions and especially contagious diseases.
            *   **Middle**, namely an invisible breath made from a murmuring and roaring of thicker and more seething vapors, and also the burning vapor of all fevers, dispersed through the veins and cavities of the body.
            *   **Lower**, which are either:
                *   **Thin**, such as "smokes" causing a lasting redness of the face, indicating seething winds—either future or present—a white and reddish color quickly rising and quickly disappearing, as in those who are ashamed and in sudden radiations of the face, called in English *flushing in the face*.
                *   **Thick**, such as luminous "smokes" dissolved in the body.
*   Springing from the earth and waters of the Microcosm.

->On the hidden luminous meteors of the Macrocosm of a coarser consistency.<-

Hidden luminous meteors <note>The author uses "meteors" in the Aristotelian sense, meaning any phenomenon occurring in the air or from the earth, including vapors, fumes, and volcanic gases.</note> of the Macrocosm <term>macrocosm: the universe or world at large, as opposed to the human "microcosm"</term>, gushing forth from the earth and waters, come about either:

- **According to the nature of the place**, and these are either:
    - **Terrestrial**, such as fumes:
        - Vegetable, animal, and mineral, which in their own natures smell either good or bad; and sulfurous fumes, such as that poisonous vapor springing from the earth into the "Cave of the Dog" <note>original: "antrum canis." The Grotto del Cane in Naples was a famous 17th-century tourist site where carbon dioxide pooled near the floor, suffocating dogs but leaving humans unharmed.</note> at the Puteolian Promontory <note>The volcanic region of Pozzuoli near Naples.</note>.

        - Foul and stinking.
        - Poisonous.
        - Sweet and healthful.
    - **Happening by chance**, namely:
        - From the sudden eruption of vapor from a putrid and poisonous place.
        - From the breaking of glass, as happens quite often in chemistry <note>original: "chimia." In this period, the word encompasses both chemistry and alchemy.</note>.

**The hiddenly luminous meteors of the Microcosm <term>microcosm: the human body, viewed as a miniature reflection of the entire universe</term>, which are external and gushing forth from waters, are either:**

*   **According to the nature of the thing or place**, and these are either:
    *   **Terrestrial**, such as fumes:
        *   Vegetable, animal, or mineral, which are either taken internally or smelled externally.
        *   Sulfurous, such as the poisonous vapors found in lepers and those affected by the "French disease" <note>original: "morbo Gallico," a common Renaissance term for syphilis</note>.
        *   Bituminous, which congeal into gums or painful tophi <term>tophi: stony deposits, often associated with gout or joint disease</term>.

        *   **Infecting with disease**, such as those:
            *   Found in people with dropsy <term>dropsy: an old term for edema or swelling caused by excess fluid</term>.
            *   Arising from putrid swamps.
            *   Arising from corrupt thermal waters.
        *   **Conducive to health**, such as that chylous <term>chylous: relating to chyle, the milky fluid produced during digestion</term> and natural humor.
*   **Accidental**, such as all fumigations, whether made by art or occurring by chance.

As has been declared previously, such is the regard for the spirit of the worldly air <note>original: "spiritus aeris mundani"</note> in relation to the human spirit, and so close is their connection, that the human spirit can in no way live or be sustained without the worldly air. 

From this it follows that fumes arising from the terrestrial air—whether animal, vegetable, or mineral—possess such a great affinity with the similar humors and human spirit within the body, that they very easily connect with them. Frequently, they convert these internal spirits into their own nature. We see this in the same way that the air of a bedroom is changed from its prior condition into the nature of specific scents by the odors of sulfur, frankincense, or civet <note>a musky perfume derived from the civet cat</note>. 

In this same manner, we sometimes observe the air to be infected with poisonous odors to the destruction of mortals. This is apparent in those who are infected by the plague, smallpox, measles, consumption <note>original: "phthisi," or tuberculosis</note>, or blepharitis <note>original: "lippitudine," an inflammation of the eyes</note>. Through the communion of these airy spirits with the air of the room, the worldly air is quickly infected; from this, it happens that the air tends to infect others dwelling in that same place.

##### *On the Meteors of the Macrocosm arising from simple elements.*

<margin>K.</margin>
Macrocosmic Meteors <term>meteors: in the 17th century, this referred to any atmospheric phenomena, including rain, wind, and lightning, not just space rocks</term> arising from simple elements are either:

*   **Peaceful.** See N.
*   **Tempestuous or stormy**, and these arise either from:
    1.  **Winds, both manifest and hidden; of this kind there are three species:**
        *   **Prester** <term>prester: a fiery whirlwind or waterspout</term>, whether a rain or a flood of fire arising from wind (which can be Smoky, Sulfurous, or Lightning-like).
        *   **Ecnephias** <term>ecnephias: a sudden, violent wind breaking out of a cloud</term>, from several hidden and invisible winds blowing downwards together with great force and violence.
        *   **Whirlwind**, which is twofold, namely either:
            *   Not ignited...
            *   Or ignited, called **Typhomania** <note>literally "Typhon-madness," referring to a violent, whirling fire-storm</note>.
    2.  **Winds and waters together**, such as sea storms and those of lakes.
    3.  **Winds and earth together**, such as **earthquakes** and **chasms** <note>openings or fissures in the ground</note>.
    4.  **All elements together**, namely:
        *   Wind (Hidden, Manifest, and flashing like Thunder).
        *   Water of the clouds.
        *   Earth or a thunder-stone <term>thunder-stone: a prehistoric stone tool once believed to be the physical bolt that fell during a lightning strike</term>.

<margin>M.</margin>
**B**oth the prester and the ignited whirlwind, as well as lightning or a thunderbolt, were said by the Peripatetics <term>Peripatetics: followers of Aristotle, whose natural philosophy dominated universities for centuries</term> to be made of the same matter—namely, an exceedingly hot and dry exhalation that is abundant and copious. They claim this exhalation is ignited by agitation, friction, collision, and struggle, mediated by the heat of the sun. But we, contrary to their doctrine, say that the matter of both the prester and the ignited whirlwind is a sulfurous wind or air, produced from the treasury of God <note>original: "arca DEI thesauraria"</note> or the aerial heaven by the divine will. We maintain that the efficient cause of these things is Jehovah himself, and not a "solar creature" <note>meaning a physical process caused by the sun</note>, and that their purpose is mostly for the punishment of the wicked, although sometimes an ignited whirlwind is created by God for the benefit of the elect.

In this manner, therefore, supported by the authority of the sacred scriptures, I set out to describe both the prester and the whirlwind.

A **Prester** is a great rain, and as it were a flood of fire and sulfur, which Jehovah sometimes sends down from the heavens, as if from his own treasury (for it is his will to make manifest the hidden parts of the air in whatever form he chooses) onto a portion of the earth as a scourge for the wicked.

# ON THE FORMAL CAUSE OF METEORS.

In this description, we define the **material cause** <note>In the philosophy of the time, the "material cause" is the substance a thing is made of.</note> of the **prester** <term>prester: a violent, fiery whirlwind or a "burning" storm-cloud</term> as a fiery or sulfurous rain; however, we establish **Jehovah** Himself as the **efficient cause** <note>The "efficient cause" is the agent or force that brings something into being.</note>, as He is the one who creates it, as if anew from nothing, or produces it from the treasury of God, or from the invisible treasury of the air. The **formal cause** <note>The "formal cause" is the essential nature or shape that makes a thing what it is.</note> is explained by the fact that it is called a rain that is not watery, but fiery and sulfurous. Finally, we have expressed the **final cause** <note>The "final cause" is the purpose for which a thing exists.</note> as being created for the punishment and destruction of the ungodly.

By the testimony of Holy Scripture, we can prove all these causes of the prester in this manner. First, we find these words written by the Royal Psalmist: *Jehovah shall rain upon the wicked burning coals, fire and sulfur, and a wind joined with a diverse prester. Psalm 11:6.* <note>original: "Impluit Iehoua super improbos prunas, ignem & sulphur, ventumq; vario prestere coniunctum"</note> In this passage, the Prophet expresses the matter as well as the form, and even the efficient cause and the purpose. He indicates the **matter** by mentioning coals, fire, and sulfur; and in these words, he also distinguishes the prester from ordinary watery rain by its clearly evident **form**. Then, afterward, he establishes the **efficient cause**—not the sun, which is a mere creature, but Jehovah the Creator, who acts immediately in all things. Finally, he establishes the **purpose**: to torture the wicked and put them to death. David writes elsewhere of the effect of this kind of meteor: *As fire burns the forest, as a flame sets the mountains on fire, so pursue them with your tempest, and terrify them with your whirlwind;* where the Prophet seems to take the "prester" to be a species of whirlwind. Similarly, Moses describes the effect of such a meteor in these express words: *The land is so burnt with sulfur and salt that it can neither be sown nor sprout, nor can any herb grow upon it. Deuteronomy 29:23.* Finally, in Genesis, the parts of our aforementioned description are confirmed in plain and open words: *Jehovah (says the Text) sent down from the heavens a rain of sulfur and fire upon the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah, by which he overthrew the cities and the entire plain, and all the inhabitants and the offspring of the earth, because of the wickedness of those dwelling there.*

Therefore, it will appear most clearly to a wise man who carefully considers these things we have brought forward, how vain is the opinion of the **Pagan Philosophers** <note>original: "Ethnicorum Philosophantiũ"; likely referring to Aristotle and the Scholastic tradition.</note> and even their Christian followers in this matter. Furthermore, when the text says "from the heavens," it understands "the heavens" to be the inner chambers of the air, which we declared in the preceding pages to be the storehouse or treasury of all meteors. This is confirmed by these words of the high priest: *Jehovah shall open to you his best treasury, the heavens, by giving rain in its season. Deuteronomy 28:12.* And it is said elsewhere: *Have you entered into the treasures of the snow? or have you seen the treasures of the hail? Job 38:22.* And so it is with the rest; for it is certain that God has his own treasuries for every species of meteor, and that they are brought forth from a hidden potential into a manifest act according to the pleasure of the Creator. Certainly, this investigation of ours into such meteors ought not to seem irrelevant to wise men, in which we attribute their generation to the Great and Good God, **Jehovah**, contrary to the opinion of the philosophers of this age; we do not attribute it to fortuitous causes in nature, or to created things such as the sun and stars, etc.

For since it is certain, and confirmed by the sacred text, that the world will be deprived of its present form, destroyed, and purified by means of a similar fiery deluge on the day of the last judgment, we believe it must be diligently considered among learned Christians that this error of the Pagan philosophers should be driven into exile from the Christian state, beyond the **Hyperborean mountains** <note>A mythical land "beyond the North Wind"; here used to mean a place of remote exile.</note>, and surrendered to the perpetual oblivion of good men. Namely, the error that the cause of such a meteor (by which the world must perish and be destroyed at the last—that is, changed and purged from its prior form through purification) usually arises from the earth by means of the heat of the sun and stars, and not from God, the father of all wonders, to whom be praise and glory. Was it not for this reason said that the Son of Man will come from the east to the west, in the manner of lightning and a consuming fire? *Matthew 24.* So also Jehovah is called a **consuming fire**, before whose sight nothing can stand, for the mountains melt like wax, etc. *Deuteronomy 4.* And yet the **Peripatetics** <term>Peripatetics: followers of Aristotle's philosophy</term> and the Christians who follow them wish such power to arise only from "imaginable exhalations"—but let us return to the subject.

Since the **matter** of a whirlwind (or **Typhon**) <term>Typhon: a Greek term for a violent whirlwind or hurricane</term> is the same as that of the Prester, although it is observed to be sent forth from the heavens in a different form and smaller quantity, we therefore attribute the following description to it as well, according to the consensus of the Holy Bible. And first, we divide it into the **fiery** or **ignited whirlwind**, and the **non-fiery**, which rotates dust, straw, and sometimes larger things in a circle.

We describe the ignited whirlwind from holy testimony as follows:

An ignited whirlwind is a fiery wind, rolled into a globe or wheel, which comes forth from its inner chamber—from both the Northern and Southern regions, and also from the Southwest—by divine power. It is sometimes made the vehicle of Jehovah, as if from a tabernacle, from which it pleases Him to appear to the saints, to speak to them, sometimes even to snatch them up to Himself into heaven, and most often to send forth His vengeance upon the ungodly. In this, the **material cause** is wind or fiery air; the **formal cause** is that ignited air rolled into a wheel; the **place** is its inner chamber, that is, a cloud appropriate for its generation; the **efficient cause** is the power of Jehovah, by which it is brought out from His own treasures; and the **purpose** is that it may be a seat of the Divine Essence, and as it were a tent from which He is accustomed to speak with His saints, and frequently to pour out punishments upon the ungodly. We have also expressed the regions of the world from which it is most often accustomed to come. And all these things we defend by the authority of the sacred text.

*Out of the inner chamber (says Job) comes the whirlwind, and cold from the scatterers, Job 37:9.* <note>The "scatterers" here refers to the north winds.</note> that is, from the North, as...

# CHAPTER XV.
## Second Part.
->Concerning the storm of the sea or of Lakes.<-

We are taught everywhere in the sacred scriptures that a tempestuous storm, of whatever species, depends on the divine will, as he who claims dominion for himself both over the soul and the spirit. Whence he is called *the Lord God of the soul and the body, the strong God of spirits, Numbers 16:22.* Nor indeed is there any storm which is not performed by the angelic ministers of God, at the inciting Word or will of the divine: whence the Royal Prophet says: *Angels of God, mighty in strength, that do his commandments, hearkening unto the voice of his word, doing his pleasure, Psalm 103:20.* And elsewhere: *Who maketh your angels winds or spirits, etc. Psalm 104:4.* And indeed the most horrendous of all storms is that of the sea, in which the waves like mountains seem sometimes to be raised to heaven, and then suddenly afterward are observed to be thrust down into the abyss of the Pit <note>original: "Barathri," a term for the underworld or a deep pit.</note>.

The Peripatetics <note>Followers of Aristotle’s philosophy.</note> and other followers of Ethnic <note>Pagan or non-Christian.</note> philosophy have attributed the cause of this kind of storm to the winds—not ineptly, but in this agreeing with sacred scripture. But in truth, concerning the origin of the winds—namely, concerning their material and efficient cause—they have judged poorly and incongruously. For they have falsely asserted that the **material cause** is a hot and dry exhalation, breathed out from the earth, while at the same time they claim the **efficient cause** is not Jehovah, by means of his angels, but the sun, the stars, and the cold temperament of the middle region of the air.

We, however, greatly dissenting from those views, say that the material cause is drawn from God’s treasury—that is, the heavens or the air—and we call the internal agent a certain angelic spirit. This spirit is animated by the spirit of Jehovah and is accustomed to stir the waves to fulfill His will; thus, from the authority of Holy Scripture, we describe a **Sea Storm** in this manner:

> A sea storm is a disturbance of the sea by the spirit of a whirlwind (which Jehovah agitates by His word to perform His will in the waters). This entails the exaltation of the waves even unto heaven, and shortly after, their depression down to the abyss, through which the soul of the sailor melts in distress, and all his wisdom is swallowed up; at last, unless Jehovah in His mercy makes the whirlwind stand silent, he is swallowed by the surging waters and thus perishes for his sins.

In this description, we perceive that the **material cause** of the storm is the sea water, and the **efficient cause** <note>In the philosophy of the time, the "efficient cause" is the primary source of change or rest; here, the author argues God is the ultimate actor using weather as a tool.</note> is Jehovah himself, who disturbs the waters by means of His minister—namely, the whirlwind. The **form** of such a storm is depicted by the waves being raised up as if to heaven and then plunged down to the very depths of the abyss. Finally, the **purpose** <note>original: "finis"</note> of such an operation is explained: first, to show those who go down to the sea in ships that human vigor or the power of worldly wisdom is confounded and brought low when the spirit of divine power opposes it; second, that it is in God’s hands to impose silence on that turbulent spirit and return the sea to calm when it pleases Him to have mercy on the sailors, or to animate that spirit until the impious are submerged. And we have this confirmed by the testimony of the royal Psalmist, from whom we receive this discourse:

> *They that go down to the sea in ships see the works of Jehovah and his wonders in the deep. For he commandeth, and raiseth the stormy wind, which lifteth up the waves thereof. They mount up to the heaven, they go down again to the depths: their soul is melted because of trouble. They reel to and fro, and stagger like a drunken man, and are at their wits' end. Then they cry unto Jehovah in their trouble, and he bringeth them out of their distresses. He maketh the storm a calm, so that the waves thereof are still. Then they are glad because they be quiet; so he bringeth them unto their desired haven. Oh that men would praise Jehovah for his goodness, and for his wonderful works to the children of men! etc. Psalm 107:23–31.* <note>The author cites this as Psalm 107:33, following a different numbering system or referring to the surrounding context of the passage.</note>

Indeed, these words of David seem to include all parts of our aforementioned description. Furthermore, that the Father of storms is the Lord of Hosts, acting by means of the winds, seems to be declared elsewhere in these words: *Psalm 48:7.* Similarly, that it is in His power to restrain the waves of the sea and lakes, and to make the turbulent spirit silent and the waves quiet, is gathered from the authority of Job, in which it is said: *By his power he stilleth the sea, and by his understanding he smiteth through the proud waves. Job 26:12.*

We conclude, moreover, that this same thing which has been said regarding waves and storms should also be understood regarding the waves of lakes, ponds, rivers, and so forth.

## CHAPTER XV.
### Third Part.
# *On Earthquakes and their Characteristics.*

The opinion of the Ethnic <note>The term "Ethnics" refers to the pagan Greek and Roman philosophers.</note> philosophers, and especially the Peripatetics <note>The "Peripatetics" were followers of Aristotle, who taught that earthquakes were caused by "pneuma" (wind or vapor) trapped underground.</note>, is that the material cause of an earthquake consists of various vapors enclosed within the earth's cavernous belly and passages. They claim the efficient cause is the resistance and struggle of these vapors against one another, by which they dilate themselves and force a way out through a violent eruption from the earth's caves; thus, according to the lightness of their nature, they rush upward. From this, they conclude that in such a violent eruption from the earth, the mass of the earth is either entirely or partially shaken and caused to tremble. They also maintain that a plague usually follows this commotion of the earth because of the malignancy of the fumes breaking out, by which they say both the air and the waters are commonly corrupted.

If their opinion were fortified by any probability, a stronger faith might be attributed to it by wise men; but, by the faith of God and men! Who, endowed with any prudence and rightly practiced in the contemplation of God’s wonders, has dared to believe and say so assertively that such a massive bulk could be vibrated and shattered by mere smoke hidden in its bowels—and with such a light, yet universal tremor, roar, and disturbance? Or if smoke were the material cause, who, I pray, is the actor in so stupendous a matter? Is it a battle of vapors among themselves? And if it is their battle, who is the primary agent within them? But truly, it is no wonder that these Ethnic philosophers and their Christian followers have erred in the causes of effects, since they were ignorant of Jehovah himself and His word, by whom and through which all things were made and brought into the light.

We, however, affirm that there is an **aerial spirit** in the earth, by means of which the entire terrestrial mass lives and is continued in its being, not otherwise than we see the human body itself preserved in its state and being by its internal air. This spirit cannot persist unless it absorbs and draws in a small portion of the worldly spirit at every moment. But truly, we see by the testimony of Holy Scripture that *Jehovah, by His look alone, struck fear into the clouds and waters, and disturbed the abyss itself, Psalm 77:16.* <note>The author cites Psalm 76:17.</note> *Whence the multitude of the sound of the waters and clouds; indeed, it is said elsewhere that the waters were afraid at the voice of his thunder, Psalm 104:7.* <note>The author cites Psalm 103.</note> *And elsewhere: That the clouds*

# CHAPTER XV.
### Second Part.
## On the Storms of the Sea or Lakes.

We are taught everywhere in Holy Scripture that a stormy tempest of any kind depends upon the divine will, as He who claims command over both the soul and the spirit; whence He is called the *Lord God of the soul and the body, the strong God of spirits, Numbers 16:22.* Nor is there indeed any storm which is not performed by the angelic ministers of God, at the inciting Word or divine will: whence the royal Prophet says: *Angels of God, mighty in strength, performing his word, hearkening unto the voice of his word, doing his pleasure, Psalm 103:20.* And elsewhere: *Who makest thy angels winds or spirits, etc. Psalm 104:4.* And indeed, of all storms, the most horrendous is that of the sea, in which the waves like mountains seem sometimes to be raised to heaven, and then immediately afterward are observed to be thrust down as if into the abyss of the Pit <note>original: "Barathri"—referring to the Greek term for a deep pit or the underworld</note>.

The Peripatetics <note>The followers of Aristotle, who sought naturalistic rather than supernatural explanations for weather</note> and other followers of philosophy have attributed the cause of this kind of storm to the winds—not ineptly, but in this agreeing with Holy Scripture. But truly, regarding the origin of the winds—namely, their material and efficient cause—they have thought poorly and incongruously. For they have falsely asserted that the material cause is a hot and dry exhalation, exhaled from the earth, and at the same time they claim the efficient cause is not Jehovah, through the mediation of His angels, but the sun, the stars, and the cold temperament of the middle region of the air.

# On the Formal Cause of Meteors <note>In the philosophy of the time, "meteors" referred to any atmospheric phenomenon, including rain, wind, and storms. The "formal cause" refers to the defining essence or divine design behind these events.</note>

We, however, disagreeing greatly with those others, state that the material cause is drawn from the treasury of God—that is, from the heavens or the air—and we call the internal agent a certain angelic spirit. This spirit is animated by the spirit of Jehovah and is accustomed to stir the waves to perform His will; thus, based on the authority of Holy Scripture, we describe a **Sea Storm** in this manner:

A **Sea Storm** is a disturbance of the sea by the spirit of a whirlwind (which Jehovah agitates by His word to fulfill His will in the waters). This entails the lifting of the waves even unto heaven, and then their sudden sinking down into the abyss. Through this process, the soul of the sailor "melts in trouble," and all his wisdom is "swallowed up," until finally—unless Jehovah in His mercy makes the whirlwind stand silent—he is swallowed by the surging waters and thus perishes for his sins.

In this description, we perceive that the **material cause** of the storm is the sea-water itself, while the **efficient cause** <note>The "efficient cause" is the primary agent that brings something into being.</note> is Jehovah Himself, who disturbs the waters by means of His minister, namely the whirlwind. The **form** of such a storm is depicted by the fact that the surges or waves are sometimes lifted up as if toward heaven and soon depressed down to the very bottom of the abyss. Finally, the **purpose** <note>original: "finis"—the "final cause" or intended goal of the event.</note> of such an operation is explained: first, to show those who "go down to the sea in ships" that the vigor of the human soul and the power of worldly wisdom are confounded and brought to ruin when the spirit of divine power opposes them; second, that it is in God's hands either to impose silence upon that whirlwind-spirit and restore quiet to the sea waves (when it pleases Him to have mercy on the sailors), or to continue agitating and animating it until the impious are submerged. We have this confirmed by the testimony of the Royal Psalmist <note>King David</note>, from whom we receive this discourse: *They that go down to the sea in ships see the works of Jehovah and His wonders in the deep. For He commands and raises the stormy wind, which lifts up the waves thereof. They mount up to the heaven, they go down again to the depths: their soul is melted because of trouble. They reel to and fro, and stagger like a drunken man, and are at their wits' end <note>original: "omnis sapientia eorum absorbeatur"—all their wisdom is swallowed up</note>. Then they cry unto Jehovah in their trouble, and He brings them out of their distresses. He makes the storm a calm, so that the waves thereof are still. Then are they glad because they be quiet; so He brings them unto their desired haven. Oh that men would praise Jehovah for His goodness, and for His wonderful works to the children of men! etc. Psalm 107:23-33.*

These words of David seem to include all the parts of our aforementioned description. Furthermore, that the "God of Hosts" is the father of tempests by means of the winds is declared elsewhere in these words: *You break the ships of Tarshish with an East wind <note>original: "Euro"—the Eurus or East wind</note>: Psalm 48:7.* Similarly, that it is in His power to restrain the waves of the sea and lakes, and to make the whirlwind-spirit silent and the waves rest, is gathered from the authority of Job, in which it is said: *He quiets the sea by His power, and by His understanding He strikes through the proud <note>original: "percutiat elevationem"—strikes the 'lifting up' or 'swelling'</note>, Job 26:12.*

We conclude, moreover, that the same things said regarding waves and storms must also be understood concerning the waves of lakes, ponds, rivers, and so forth.

## On Earthquakes and Their Associated Phenomena <note>original: "accidentibus"—the outward signs or properties accompanying an event.</note>.

The opinion of the Pagan <note>original: "Ethnicorum"—referring to non-Christian, specifically Greek and Roman, philosophers.</note> philosophers, and especially the Peripatetics <note>Followers of Aristotle.</note>, is that the **material cause** of an earthquake consists of various vapors trapped within the earth's cavernous belly and passages. They claim the **efficient cause** is the resistance and struggle between these vapors. Through this struggle, the vapors expand and force a path via a violent eruption from the earth's dens or caverns, and thus, according to the lightness of their natures, they tend upward in a swift motion. From this, they conclude that in such a violent eruption from the earth, the entire mass of the earth, or at least some part of it, is shaken and caused to tremble. They also maintain that a plague usually follows this commotion of the earth because of the "malignancy" of the fumes breaking forth, which they assert corrupts both the air and the waters.

If their opinion were fortified by any probability, the wise might grant it stronger faith; but—by God and the faith of men!—who, endowed with any prudence and practiced in the righteous contemplation of God's wonders, would dare to believe and say that such a massive weight could be vibrated and shattered with such a light, universal tremor, roar, and disturbance by mere smoke hidden in its bowels? Or if smoke were its material cause, who, I ask, is the actor in such a stupendous matter? Is it the struggle of vapors among themselves? And if it is their struggle, who is the primary agent within them? Truly, it is no wonder that these Pagan philosophers and their Christian followers have erred in the causes of these effects, since they were ignorant of Jehovah Himself and His Word, by whom and through whom all things were made and brought into the light. We, however, affirm that there is an **aerial spirit** in the earth, by which the whole earthly mass lives and is continued in its being, not otherwise than we see the human body preserved in its state and being by its internal aerial spirit—a spirit which cannot persist unless it absorbs and draws in a small portion of the world-spirit every moment. Truly, we see by the testimony of the Sacred Scriptures that Jehovah, by His look alone, struck fear into the clouds and waters and disturbed the very abyss, *Psalm 77:16-17 <note>original: "Psalm 76:17"</note>.* Hence comes the multitude of the sound of waters and clouds; indeed, it is said elsewhere *that at the voice of His thunder the waters were afraid, Psalm 104:7.* And elsewhere: *That the clouds...*

A windy whirlwind, but not subject to inflammation, is a certain invisible spirit proceeding from its divine inner chamber, which, being sent onto the earth, is accustomed to execute the will of the Creator either for good or for evil.

Job 37.* Job also understands this species of whirlwind where it is said: *They shall be as stubble before the wind, and as chaff that the whirlwind carrieth away. # CHAPTER XV.
## Second Part.
-> Regarding the Tempest of the Sea or Lakes. <-

We are taught everywhere in Holy Scripture that a boisterous tempest of any kind depends upon the divine will, inasmuch as He claims dominion for Himself over both soul and spirit; hence the Lord is called the God of soul and body, *The strong God of the spirits. Numbers 16:22.* Nor indeed is there any tempest which is not performed by the angelic ministers of God, at the prompting of the Word or divine will: whence the Royal Psalmist says: *Angels of God, that excel in strength, that do his commandments, hearkening unto the voice of his word... doing his pleasure. Psalm 103:20.* And elsewhere: *Who maketh his angels winds or spirits, etc. Psalm 104:4.* And indeed, of all tempests, the most horrendous is that of the sea, in which the waves seem like mountains to be sometimes lifted up to heaven, and then suddenly thereafter are observed to be thrust down into the abyss of the Pit <term>Barathrum</term>.

The Peripatetics <note>Followers of Aristotle’s philosophy, who sought naturalistic rather than purely theological explanations for weather.</note> and other followers of Heathen philosophy have attributed the cause of this kind of tempest to the winds, not ineptly, and in this they agree with Holy Scripture; but truly, regarding the origin of the winds—namely, their material and efficient cause—they have thought wrongly and incongruously. For they have falsely asserted that the material cause is a hot and dry exhalation, exhaled from the earth, while asserting the efficient cause to be not Jehovah, through the mediation of His angels, but the sun, the stars, and the cold temperament of the middle region of the air.

# On the Formal Cause of Meteors.

We, however, disagreeing greatly with them, state that the material cause is drawn from God's treasury—that is, the heavens or the air—and we call the internal acting agent a certain angelic spirit, which the spirit of Jehovah animates and is accustomed to stir in the waves to fulfill His will. Thus, from the authority of Holy Scripture, we describe a Sea Storm in this manner:

-> A sea storm is a disturbance of the sea by a spirit of the whirlwind (which Jehovah agitates by His word to fulfill His will in the waters)—that is, the exaltation of its waves now even unto heaven, and soon their depression down to the abyss—by means of which the soul of the sailor melts in distress, and all his wisdom is swallowed up, and finally, unless Jehovah in His mercy makes the whirlwind stand in silence, he is swallowed by the watery waves and thus perishes because of his sins. <-

In this description, we perceive the material cause of the storm to be the sea waters, and the efficient cause to be Jehovah Himself, who by means of His minister—namely, the whirlwind—disturbs the waters. The form of such a storm is depicted in that the waves or surges are sometimes raised up as if to heaven and soon depressed down to the lowest abyss. Finally, the purpose <term>finis</term> of such an operation is explained: first, that it shows those who go down to the sea in ships that the vigor of the human soul or the power of worldly wisdom is confounded and brought to ruin when the spirit of divine power opposes it; second, that it is in God's hands either to impose silence upon that whirlwind-like spirit and make it quiet along with the sea waves—specifically when it pleases Him to have mercy on the sailors—or to agitate and animate it until the ungodly are submerged. And we have this confirmed by the testimony of the Royal Psalmist, from whom we receive this discourse:

> *They that go down to the sea in ships see the works of Jehovah and His wonders in the deep. For He speaks, and makes the spirit of the whirlwind to stand, and lifts up the waves of the sea; they mount up to the heaven, they go down again to the depths, so that their soul melts because of trouble. They toss and reel like a drunkard, so that all his wisdom is swallowed up. Then they cry unto Jehovah in their distress, and He brings them out of their troubles; He makes the whirlwind stand in silence, and their waves are still. They celebrate the mercy of Jehovah and declare His wonders to the children of men, etc.* Psalm 107:23.

These words of David seem to include all the parts of our aforementioned description. Furthermore, that the Father of storms is the God of Hosts, acting by means of the winds, He seems to declare elsewhere in these words: *You break the ships of the ocean with the East wind.* <note>original: "Euro"</note> Psalm 48:8. Similarly, that it is also in His power to restrain the waves of the sea and lakes and to make the whirlwind spirit silent and the waves quiet is to be gathered from the authority of Job, in which it is said: *that His power makes the sea to be quiet, and by His understanding He strikes the heaving waves.* <note>original: "percutiat elevationem," literally "strikes the lifting up" or "the pride."</note> Job 26:12.

We conclude, however, that this same thing which has been said regarding waves and storms ought also to be understood regarding the waves of lakes, ponds, rivers, etc.

# CHAPTER XV.
## Third Part.
### On Earthquakes and their accidents.

The opinion of the Heathen philosophers, and especially the Peripatetics <note>The followers of Aristotle, who dominated university science in the Middle Ages and Renaissance.</note>, is that the material cause of an earthquake consists of various vapors enclosed in the earth's cavernous belly and passages. As the efficient cause, they cite the resistance and battle among these vapors, by means of which, expanding themselves, they make a path by a violent eruption from the caves or caverns of the earth; and thus, according to the lightness of their natures, they tend upward in a swift motion. From this, they conclude that in such a violent eruption from the earth, the mass of the earth itself—either in its entirety or only some part—is shaken and caused to tremble. They claim that pestilence usually follows this commotion of the earth because of the malignancy of the fumes breaking forth from the ground, by which they assert both the air and the waters themselves are corrupted.

If their opinion were fortified by any probability, a stronger faith ought to be attributed to it by wise men; but oh, by the faith of God and men! Who, endowed with any prudence and properly engaged in the contemplation of God's wonders, has dared to believe and say with certainty that such a great mass could be vibrated and shattered by mere smoke hidden in its bowels—and with such a slight and yet so universal a trembling, roaring, and disturbance? Or if smoke were its material cause, who, I ask, is the actor in such a stupendous matter? Is it the battle of vapors among themselves? And if it is their battle, who is the primary agent in them? But truly it is no wonder that these Heathen philosophers and their Christian followers have erred in the causes of effects, since they were ignorant of Jehovah Himself and His Word, by whom and through which all things were made and brought into the light.

We, however, affirm that there is an aerial spirit in the earth, by means of which the entire terrestrial mass lives and is continued in its being, not otherwise than we see the human body itself preserved in its state and being by its own internal air—which spirit cannot persist unless it absorbs and draws in a small portion from the worldly spirit at every moment. But indeed, we see—instructed by the testimony of Holy Scripture—that Jehovah by His look alone struck fear into the clouds and waters and disturbed the very abyss. *Psalm 76:17.* From which comes the multitude of the sound of waters and clouds; indeed, it is said elsewhere *that at the voice of His thunder the waters were afraid, Psalm 103.* And elsewhere: *That the clouds*

...clouds passed in His sight. In a not dissimilar way, the Creator is also accustomed to act in the terrestrial air, when the earth seems to tremble and shake as if with fear—namely, at the mere voice and sight of Jehovah. Hence it is said, *the earth is shaken and moved—the foundations of the heavens are moved and shaken when His anger is kindled against it, when smoke rises from His nostrils, and fire from His mouth consumes; coals are kindled by Him, and bowing the heavens He descends with darkness under His feet, and sits upon the Cherubim and flies* etc. <note>original: "2. Sa. 22. 8." – referencing 2 Samuel 22:8-11</note>. From this it is clear that there is a spirit or smoke emitted by God which is the cause of the disturbance and shaking, not only of the open air and its clouds (from which come the sounds of thunder and trembling in the air and clouds), but also in the aerial spirit enclosed within the earth. This aerial spirit is sometimes ignited by the angelic breath or smoke proceeding from Jehovah, much like lightning in a cloud; once ignited, it is forced to burst out of the earth with a massive trembling, no differently than the spirit ignited in a cloud bursts from the caverns of the cloud, not without an immense disturbance and shaking of the watery mass collected in the form of a cloud. For undoubtedly the matter stands thus: just as God made His angels winds, and His ministers a burning and flashing fire <note>original: "psal. 104." – Psalm 104:4</note>, so indeed these windy ministers, both visible and invisible, perform their duties in the execution of the divine will, both in the enclosed spirits and in that universal open spirit. We say, therefore, that just as the World-Spirit <term>spiritus mundanus</term> is the vehicle of God's ministers, through whom and in whom He works whatever pleases Him, so it is necessary that the wondrous nature of these operations proceeds immediately from the divine essence, which is in these ministers like an uncreated soul or a reigning divine word. Thus, we do not say that the flute produced this or that melody, but rather the blower; therefore, however much God uses angels as instruments to produce an earthquake, and even the disturbance of the air and clouds in thunder, nonetheless that entire operation must be ascribed to God as the immediate actor. Hence Job says: *God moves the earth from its place so that its columns tremble, He moves the mountains, etc.* <note>original: "Iob. 9. 5." – Job 9:5-6</note>. And elsewhere, *At the sight of God the earth trembled, and at His touch the mountains smoke,* <note>original: "Psal. 104. 32."</note>. Therefore, it is necessary that we confess with that same Prophet that the depths of the earth *are the footprints in the hand of God,* <note>original: "Psal. 95. 5." – A variation of Psalm 95:4-5</note> and consequently, that it is governed by Him alone—that is, it either rests or is vibrated according to His good pleasure. And although its shaking is sometimes ascribed to the presence of an angel, it is certain that wherever the angel of God is present, there also Jehovah Himself is present; for in the angel is the great name of God, that is, His ineffable word. It is for this reason that Dionysius <note>Dionysius the Areopagite, a Christian theologian and philosopher.</note> quite deliberately calls the Angels *Images* <note>original: "Agalmata" – Greek for cult images or statues</note>, that is, the brightest mirrors receiving the light of God, which is His emanation. For this reason, therefore, it is written: *And behold, a great earthquake occurred; for the angel of the Lord descended from heaven, and his appearance was like lightning,* <note>original: "Matth. 28. 2."</note>. By this he wished to imply that at the sight of the shining essence of the wrathful God in the angel of Jehovah, the spirit of the earth was so agitated and moved that it violently erupted from the bowels of its mass.

We conclude, therefore, that by the authority of the preceding passages it will be (in my opinion) permissible for us to make a description of an Earthquake in this manner:

> An earthquake occurs when the spirit and, as it were, the soul of the entire terrestrial mass—disturbed by the gaze of Jehovah or the breath of His wrathful angel, and incited and agitated by expansion—is forced to violently erupt from its terrestrial body into the open air, in the manner of a huge sigh, with a groan, or like ignited air from a cloud (not without the shaking and ruin of mountains, cities, temples, and royal buildings, and the slaughter of men, and frequently followed by plague); by its impetus the terrestrial mass trembles and is moved, and the open air is infected and poisoned by its malignancy.

-> Or thus: <-

> An earthquake occurs when the terrestrial spirit, at the sight and breath of Jehovah kindled with wrath, and stirred as if by fear and dread, causes its earthy body to tremble and move, in the manner of a man's spirit struck by unexpected fear.

In the first description, we made the material cause of the earthquake the terrestrial spirit or the internal spirit of the earth; for we see this in the distillation of the spirit of nitre <note>A term for nitric acid or its concentrated vapors in early chemistry.</note>: the internal spirit of the nitrous mass, because of the vehement agitation of the fire, leaps out of its body, sometimes destroying the receiving vessel and vibrating into a thousand small pieces with a horrific sound. Similarly, the air itself enclosed in a dense cloud is animated, illuminated, and agitated by expansion by the spirit or the mere sight of the wrathful Jehovah; from this it happens that, with a great disturbance of the clouds, it pierces and splits their sides with violent force and exits with trembling and noise to execute the will of the Creator. Of this kind, therefore, was that famous earthquake of old on the promontory of Puteoli <note>Modern Pozzuoli, Italy, near Vesuvius and the Phlegraean Fields.</note>, which occurred arriving with sulfurous flames, lightning, and tremendous thunder; and that one not many years ago, which is said to have happened with the ruin of the small town of Plurs <note>Pluro or Piuro, a town in Italy destroyed by a massive landslide and earthquake in 1618.</note> in Italy and the subversion of the very high mountain near it, with whirlwind-like <term>typhoneis</term> flames rising from the caverns of the earth and mountain, at the same time as lightning and thunder were sent from on high.

Concerning those earthquakes which proceed from a spirit that is not ignited, the Holy Scriptures have written abundantly, and the experience of men still living testifies to them; therefore, we do not intend to say more words about them in this place.

We have already discussed thunder, clouds, lightning, and the thunderstone <term>lapide fulminari</term> at great length above.

# On the Formal Cause of Meteors.

## Corollary.

We have stated in the preceding pages that the spirit of both the earth and of man, as well as that of any other thing—whether animate or not—is so bound in its substance to the open spirit of the world, which we call the air, that the disposition of the parts is suddenly changed into the disposition of the whole (unless some matter of greater importance prevents it). Hence it is clear that the "seeds" of meteors <note>In this period, "meteors" referred to all atmospheric phenomena, including rain, wind, and lightning, not just falling stars.</note> procreated in the air of the Great World—which are dispersed everywhere in that air through dissolution—very easily penetrate that same air in successive turns. By a certain magnetic inspiration, they are introduced into the particular air of both the earth and the human body, as well as other living things. There, according to their natural appetite, they are accustomed to produce the same or at least similar effects in the air enclosed within these bodies as those they manifestly achieve in the open air.

For example, the appearance of comets is usually followed by plague or pestilential fever in the highest region of the human spirit—namely, in the vital spirits—from which petechiae <note>original: "petechiæ"; small purple or red spots on the skin caused by minor bleeding.</note> or purple spots arise. Similarly, the appearances of lightning and "chasms" <note>original: "chasmatum"; an atmospheric phenomenon appearing as an opening or crack in the sky.</note> very often generate putrid diseases, and so on with the rest, as demonstrated in the following table.

On the Formal Cause of Meteors.

## CHAPTER XVI.

### Part One.

->Concerning the Rainbow, or the heavenly arch.<-

By the Peripatetics <note>Followers of Aristotle’s philosophy, who focused on physical and logical explanations of the natural world.</note>, the Rainbow <note>original: "Iris"</note> is said to be an arch of various colors in a dewy, opaque, and concave cloud, appearing to the eyes of onlookers from the reflection of the rays of the sun positioned opposite to it. They say it cannot be otherwise than arched or semicircular in its figure, although it is certain, and proven by experience, that such an arch—according to the testimony of Holy Scripture—sometimes circles the heavens in a complete ring, as is demonstrated to the eye in our meteorographic mirror <note>A scientific instrument used by the author to observe or simulate atmospheric phenomena.</note>.

In this description of theirs, the "material cause" (from which or in which it is made) is defined as the dewy, opaque, and concave cloud; the "Formal cause" is explained as the many-colored arch; and they make the "Efficient cause" the solar rays, from whose reflection it appears to the eyes of the observers.

But we, from the text of the Holy Scriptures, gather that the Rainbow can be described by the Christian Philosopher in this manner:

> The Rainbow is the circle or arch of GOD, most glorious in its splendor, which the hand of the Most High has thus stretched out, and placed in the clouds on a day of rain, so that it might be a sign of the everlasting covenant which He Himself struck with every living soul that flourishes in the flesh—namely, that there shall no longer be a flood to destroy the entire earth.

Or thus:

> The Rainbow is an arch reflecting among the clouds of glory on a day of rain, which GOD made with His own hands, and He has circled the heavens in the circuit of His glory so that it might be a sign to every living soul of the flesh that the universal flood is restrained.

In these descriptions, the "material cause" seems to be a certain glorious spirit, manifesting itself in its splendor within the misty cloud of heaven. The "Formal cause" is expressed in that it is called a glorious arch in its splendor, placed in the clouds on a day of rain; or that it is an arch reflecting among the clouds of glory, circling the heavens. Furthermore, we have also described its "efficient cause" by saying that it was made and placed or impressed upon the clouds by the hands and, as it were, the finger of the Most High. Finally, although its general effect is to produce rain, nevertheless its principal end and the first of all was that it should be a sign of the covenant between GOD and all flesh, that a universal flood should not come hereafter: as if by this power of His, GOD restrains the clouds from excessive rain, or that its appearance and presence is a sign of remembrance and commemoration of the promise made between GOD and the earth.

From this it is clear that this glorious and reflecting splendor, which the Pagans <note>original: "Ethnici"; referring here to non-Christian classical philosophers.</note> say is many-colored and arises from the rays of the sun, we say proceeds from GOD and His throne full of glory. Indeed, we say with the Holy Bible that GOD Himself, in His person and glory—dwelling not only in the glorious solar body but also present everywhere in the world-spirit—made this wonderful sign and adorned it with the reflection of His glory.

And although it is certain that solar rays seem to be present in this kind of operation, a power far more potent than solar rays undoubtedly concurs in the shaping and generation of this kind of meteor: namely, the wondrous splendor of God, which is hidden or manifested according to His will, as was said regarding the creation of other meteors. For surely, if dewy clouds and solar rays were the sole cause of such an impression, hardly a day would pass without us seeing a rainbow or heavenly arch, since dewy clouds are frequent everywhere in the sky. Furthermore, we have shown elsewhere that GOD is the father of the clouds and of every beautiful flash of lightning, and that each of them has a treasury-chest from which they are drawn out by divine command, according to that saying of the wise man:

<margin>Ecclesiasticus 43:15 <note>The author provides a combined paraphrase of verses 11–22 from the Book of Sirach/Ecclesiasticus.</note></margin>
> *Look upon the rainbow, and bless Him who made it: it is very beautiful in its brightness. It encompasses the heaven about with the circle of its glory, the hands of the Most High have opened it. By His commandment He makes the snow to fall apace, and sends forth swiftly the lightnings of His judgment. Therefore the treasures are opened, and clouds fly forth like birds. By His great power He makes the clouds thick, and the hailstones are broken small. At His sight the mountains are shaken, and at His will the South wind blows. The noise of His thunder makes the earth to tremble, so doth the Northern storm and the whirlwind, etc. (Ecclesiasticus 43:15)*

By which he seems to imply that neither the Sun, nor the stars, nor anything else, but GOD alone is the efficient cause of the rainbow as well as the cloud and all other impressions. Furthermore, as for their claim that the Rainbow is made by the reflection of the sun in the cavity of an opaque cloud, experience teaches us that this is false; for it is usually formed in misty air, in the inner part of the lowest region of the air, and sometimes does not appear to the eye further than three hundred paces away. This is shown by the fact that between a mountain and sometimes a forest set before the eye, we can discern the shining Rainbow, descending as if over the grass dewy with rain—
