# Section I. Portal IV. Part II. Book III. Member III.

...happening; hence it is that, contrary to the opinions of the Peripatetic <note>Followers of Aristotle, who relied on physical observation and logic.</note> philosophers, it is not required that it [the rainbow] be formed in the concavity of an opaque cloud. Indeed, it is very often observed to appear in air that is sufficiently dense yet diaphanous and transparent: through which, as a medium, one may clearly see a mountain or a forest. It is concerning this misty air that the sacred text seems to speak, where it is said by the wise man: <margin>*Ecclesiasticus 50:8*</margin> *A rainbow shining among the clouds of glory*, and other sacred writings seem to testify to such a cloud—namely, misty air. It appears, therefore, that the Rainbow appears among dense clouds, but to the eye, it appears in misty or dewy air. 

And although some philosophers, and indeed experts in optics, wish to discuss and debate the variety of the Rainbow's colors in their own fashion—saying that the diversity of colors arises from the variation of both the cloud and the light, and that thin water in a dewy cloud, otherwise bright air, and dark clouds must all concur to create the different colors—they claim that all these things, when irradiated by the sun, provide different colors: namely, crimson, green, yellow, lemon, red, grey-blue, or sky-blue. (Aristotle seems to treat these matters in the third book of his *Meteorology*). Nevertheless, if we wish to consider the matter a little more accurately, we see it to be otherwise than they supposed. For these rainbow colors are often produced without those specific mediums and in a different subject, as <margin>*Roger Bacon in his book on experimental science*</margin> Roger Bacon teaches in his book *On Experimental Science*, and as common experience also shows.

For in many lower things, colors of this kind are observed to appear: if we take hexagonal <note>Six-sided</note> stones from India or Ireland and hold them against the sun’s rays as they penetrate through a window or some opening into the shade or dark air, we will perceive near the rays all the colors of the rainbow in the same order in which they are arranged in the heavenly arch. Therefore, it is certain that colors of this kind can be produced without the aforementioned conditions [of clouds]; thus, it does not seem to follow that these colors are brought to light solely because of the reflection of solar rays in a dewy, concave, and opaque cloud. 

Nor does it necessarily follow that the solar rays striking directly are the only cause producing such a variety of colors. For according to Roger Bacon, if the operator takes the said hexagonal stone and turns himself to a somewhat darker place, and applies the stone to his half-closed eye, he will immediately discern the said colors of the rainbow in the air. There are, therefore, some who believe that these kinds of colors are created by the property of that stone; yet truly, this is false, because such colors appear in both dark and bright air whether using a crystal or a well-polished glass body reduced to a triangular shape <note>A prism.</note>. 

Furthermore, such colors sometimes appear on the oars of a boat when they are wet with dew and the droplets are dripping as they are lifted from the water; the same also happens when water is violently thrown against the rays of the sun. Yet, as has been said, it is not necessary that we have the presence of the sun for such an appearance, since it often happens that even at night, in the absence of the sun, these colors are observed to appear around a candle. However, we admit that it is necessary for light to be present, without which we cannot discern anything colored—much less colors which cannot be seen without a colored object. But as for the subject in which these colors are visible, we say it can be the air itself imbued with light; for I remember lying in bed in the morning and clearly perceiving the colors of the rainbow in and near the solar rays for a long time.

Therefore, without a doubt, the efficient cause <note>The primary agent or force that produces an effect.</note> of these wondrous colors is more hidden and concealed than can be easily comprehended by the Heathen philosophers, or even by their followers among the Christians of this age. For GOD, who is all and in all, and who fills the worldly spirit everywhere with His brilliance (though it be invisible), is the cause of such a wondrous thing in nature: He who is accustomed to reveal Himself to men through signs, through colors, through lightnings, and infinite other ways. This light in "moist nature" <note>A reference to the primal state of creation before it was fully formed.</note> is called by <margin>*Hermes Trismegistus, Poimandres 1.*</margin> Hermes Trismegistus in *Poimandres* 1 the "voice of light," or the Word, which stood by and nourished the moist nature. 

And another, immersing himself deeply in the mysteries of nature, <margin>*The Art of Chemistry, ch. 9*</margin> in *The Art of Chemistry*, chapter 9, says that this hidden nature is a certain infinite power, procreating like from like, increasing and nourishing all things, and for this reason having the names of all things within itself; participating in no color and yet being the sharer and maker of all colors, the fertile mother of all qualities and things. From this he concludes that this nature is GOD, and GOD is that uncreated nature—the created, creating, and nourishing moist nature—which the Platonists recognize as the *Soul of the World* <note>original: "mundi animam"</note>, existing in its whole and in every part, though existing invisibly within itself like the human soul in its body. 

And Zoroaster—with whom Heraclitus of Ephesus also seems to agree—calls this "invisible fire," from which all things are born. And others among the Hebrew Doctors maintain that it is that fiery vigor which the Spirit of *Elohim* <note>A Hebrew name for God.</note>—which is the fiery love that was carried over the waters—gave to them, and which is consequently dispersed everywhere in the world, though invisibly. For according to the testimony of St. Peter, <margin>*2 Peter 3*</margin> *the heavens and the earth were of old from water, and through water, consisting by the word of GOD*, 2 Peter 3; that is, by the primary emanation from the throne of divinity, by means of which <margin>*John 1*</margin> *all things were made and without it, nothing*, John 1. 

Does not the wise man also clearly discuss the nature of this spiritual sun or invisible light where he breaks out into these words: <margin>*Wisdom 7*</margin> *Wisdom is a spirit having all virtues in itself, simple and yet manifold, looking forth upon all things, containing all intelligible spirits, more mobile than all mobile things, and reaching everywhere because of her purity; inasmuch as she is a certain emanation of the clarity of almighty GOD, pure, more beautiful than the sun, and compared to light she is found prior to every arrangement of the stars, etc.* Wisdom 7. From which it is clear that to this sun and spiritual light, rather than to the physical sun, should be attributed the [operation] of the rainbow as well as all other meteors.

### On the Formal Cause of Meteors.

...operation, which they attribute either to the sun or to the stars, as those which receive and hold their powers and properties from this root of light. Hence we have it written, *How manifold and wonderful are the works which you have made in wisdom, Psalm 104:24.* <note>The Latin text cites Psalm 103, following the Vulgate numbering.</note> And elsewhere, *by his spirit he has garnished the heavens, Job 26:13.* And elsewhere, *GOD by his wisdom set the weight for the air, and weighed the waters by measure, he made a decree for the rain, and a way for the lightning of thunder etc. Job 28:25.* From which it is right to gather, that this holy spirit of discipline, which fills the orb of the earth and is found everywhere in the heavens, although invisible, sometimes renders itself visible through various mediums, as in the matter of the sun, the rainbow, and other meteors <note>In this period, the term "meteor" referred to any atmospheric phenomenon, including rain, wind, and rainbows, not just "falling stars."</note>: for although in itself it is a simple spirit, it is nevertheless manifold with respect to the variety of its operations and appearances. 

But why the need for more words? We have this expressly designated in the sacred scriptures—namely, that it is God and his spirit who is the cause of the Rainbow or the "bow of heaven." In Ecclesiasticus we find these words: <margin>*Chapter 43:12*</margin> *Behold the bow of heaven, and bless him who made it; It is very beautiful in its brightness, it encompasses the heaven in a circle of its glory, the hands of the most high have stretched it out.* So also elsewhere we read that the appearance as of a bow, when it shall be in a cloud on a rainy day—which was the appearance of brightness all around—was the presence of GOD and his ministers in the cloud; similarly in the Apocalypse this same thing is explained. Hence also elsewhere it is found, *as if a rainbow shining among the clouds of glory*, where "clouds of glory" seem to denote a certain glorious actor in the construction of that bow. 

Truly the following text not only vividly depicts the efficient cause <note>The "efficient cause" is the agent or force that brings something into being.</note> of the Rainbow, but also seems to denote its primary purpose; *I will set my bow (says Jehovah) in the clouds, and it shall be a sign of a covenant between me and the earth: And when I bring a cloud over the heaven, my bow shall appear in the clouds of heaven, and I will remember my covenant which I made with you, and with every living soul that lives in flesh, and there shall no more be waters of a flood to destroy all the earth; and my bow shall be in the clouds, and I will see it, and I will remember the everlasting covenant, which was established between me and every living soul of all flesh that is upon the earth, Genesis 9:12.* 

From this discourse it is clear that the "matter" of the Rainbow is the air in the clouds; the "subject" in which it appears is the cloud; and the "form" is openly indicated by the statement that the bow of heaven is very beautiful in its splendor, and has encompassed the heaven in a circle. The "efficient cause" is God, since he is said to "make" it. The "hidden end" or purpose is that it should be a sign of the restrained flood. Therefore it is certain that the spirit of GOD, expanding itself everywhere—though invisibly—both in the heavens and on the earth, is the author and actor of this glorious creature. He composes, alters, and changes all things according to his will, both in figure and in color, and performs all things; in which action he uses his creatures, the angels, as his instruments. And since the reason for the colors and shape of the heavenly bow is treated in an optical manner by experts in the science of perspective, we shall explain below—both with words and with a visual demonstration in our **Meteorographic mirror**—what they themselves have judged regarding the generation of the Rainbow in their own art.

In the true art of Chemistry <note>original: *Chimiæ*; refers here to Alchemy.</note>, those more skilled say that their mystic sulfur <note>A symbolic alchemical substance, not common brimstone.</note> shines like a Rainbow through the waters, and that with almost all the colors found in the Rainbow; and they say it is the rainbow's arc itself, because it is in the middle of pure, liquid, and flowing water, and in the middle above the earth. Therefore they express the whole property of sulfur and its natural likeness through the Rainbow. For the rainbow is not seen in the worldly heaven except when the sun is shining, which the rain usually follows; for when mists or opaque clouds arrive, the Sun himself as well as the arc of the Rainbow is hidden. In exactly the same way, the Rainbow is not seen in the "heaven of the chemists" unless the central sun is shining—which is the incorruptible spirit dwelling centrally in pure sulfur—which arc a "Microcosmic rain" <note>Refers to the internal processes of the human body or the alchemical vessel as a miniature version of the universe.</note> usually follows in a similar manner; but when mists or opaque clouds arrive, the Sun himself as well as the arc of the rainbow is hidden. One who is most experienced in that secret writes these things (*On the Art of Chemistry, chapter 13*). 

And certainly it must be known that, just as the incorruptible spirit of GOD, giving life to all things and acting as the "soul of the world," is said to be in the whole and in every part, so it acts in a small particle according to its action in the whole. And although it belongs to Jehovah alone to create worlds anew—to whom (as Solomon testifies) Wisdom was present as a master-worker composing all things in the creation of the world (*Wisdom 9:10*)—nevertheless, through the mediation of this Wisdom (which Jehovah is accustomed to send to man so that she may be present and work with him in his labor), man has been given a certain knowledge of the constitution of the world, the power of the elements, the beginning, middle, and end of times, the variety of seasons, and the positions of the stars, etc. (*Wisdom 7:17*). For this glorious central spirit, freed from elementary impurity by human labor and industry, is accustomed to reveal the practice of the divine mystery to man, according to the words of the wise man in the place cited above. Therefore, from God alone, the worker of wonders, all these things are perfected—whether they happen in the accustomed course of nature, or beyond human expectation and the foreknowledge of common astrologers—through the mediation of the miraculous Word, in whose power are all things.

As for the "peaceful meteors" of a watery and also earthy constitution, we have discussed them as if in a single word and succinctly in the preceding table; therefore, to bring more about them in this place would be a weariness to me and perhaps unpleasant to the reader.

## CHAPTER XVI.

### Part Two.

#### *On the peaceful earthy meteors of the Macrocosm, which are moist in nature.*

<image-desc>A hierarchical diagram categorizing terrestrial meteors. The text on the left branches through a bracket into two states: coldness (Frigiditate) and heat (Caliditate), which further branch into specific descriptions of marshy, mineral-rich, or stagnant terrains.</image-desc>

Peaceful earthy meteors <note>In this period, "meteors" included all atmospheric and geological phenomena, such as clouds, rain, minerals, and earthquakes.</note> of the Macrocosm <note>The "Macrocosm" refers to the great world or the universe, which early modern thinkers believed was mirrored by the "Microcosm" of the human body.</note>, which are of a more moist constitution, are categorized by either:

* **Coldness**, such as:
    * **Marshy or swampy ground**, which is earth that has become decayed and filthy.
    * **Ground saturated by many small springs**, whether of fresh water or of acidic, alum-rich <note>original: "aluminosis"; alum is a mineral salt used historically in dyeing and medicine.</note>, salt-heavy, or other such contaminated minerals.
    * **Land deeply hollowed out** by stagnant waters.
    * **Earth clumping together** into a muddy mass.

* **Heat**, such as:
    * **Coastal marshes**, or earth made swampy by the flow of salt waters, rendered decayed and unhealthy by them.
    * **Swamps or marshy land** infected by either bitter or sulfurous waters, whether bulging outward or excavated deep into the ground.

**L**ook here (most welcome Reader!), at what others have attempted to express through much speech and a subtle style of teaching—namely, the science of meteorology. I desire to offer that science to your gaze through this "picture," which is, as it were, short, brief, and a visual method of demonstration. In this picture, as if in a highly polished mirror, we have sketched the entire condition, appearance, and position of every thing; and indeed, even the **optical** <note>original: "opticam." The author refers to "apparent" phenomena—things that look a certain way in the sky but do not physically exist in that form, like rainbows or parhelia.</note> reasoning for certain things (by which some impressions appear in the sky as they are not in reality). Therefore, I would wish you to briefly receive the intent for constructing this mirror, the explanation of its parts, and the knowledge of distinguishing one region from another in the Hemisphere.

By the two parallel lines rising above the Horizon, drawn circularly from east to west and outlining the hemisphere, we intend to represent the cavity of the starry or ethereal heaven. And for that reason, we have assigned multiple stations or positions for the **Sun** and **Moon** in the interstice or space between the two parallel lines signifying heaven. This is because it seemed impossible to us that every demonstration in this mirror depending on the Sun and Moon could be referred to a single site or place, and also because various types of impressions cannot be depicted in one part of the picture. For this reason, we call that entire space—comprising the two semicircles beginning in the east and ending in the west with parallel lines—the **Heaven**, in which we have placed the Milky Way, the Sun, and the Moon. The lowest semicircle, however, refers to the image of the **Earth** itself, from which a multiform view of meteorological acts is usually made.

Furthermore, every place interposed between the ethereal heaven and the earth denotes the vast seat of the **Air**, or the extension of the **world spirit**. Within its capacity, as a common medium, the entire logic of our institution and proposal seems to be included and contained. This general location is also divided into three parts by two curved lines forming an arc, which the common people are accustomed to call the **regions of the air**, regardless of their dimensions (about which the common philosophers seem to contend too much). We, however, do not think the lower region of the air exceeds the highest mountains in its dimension or extension...

BEHOLD (most desired Reader!) what others have attempted to express with many words and a subtle style of teaching—namely, the science of meteorology—I strive to offer to your sight through this, as it were, short and brief picture and visual method of demonstration. For in it, as if in a most polished mirror, we have outlined the universal condition, appearance, and position of every meteor; and indeed, even the optical reasoning of certain ones (by which some impressions appear in the sky such as they are not in truth). I would have you briefly receive the intention of the construction of this mirror, the explanation of its parts, and the knowledge of distinguishing the regions in the Hemisphere from one another.

By two parallel lines rising above the Horizon, drawn circularly from east to west and delineating the hemisphere, we intend to represent the cavity of the starry or ethereal heaven. And therefore, we have assigned multiple stations or positions for the Sun and Moon in the interstice or space between the two parallels signifying the heaven, since it seemed impossible to us that every demonstration in this mirror depending on the Sun and Moon could be referred to a single site or place, and also because various types of impressions cannot be depicted in one part of the picture. Therefore, we call that entire space "the heaven," which encompasses the two semicircles beginning at the sunrise and ending at the sunset, in which we have placed the Milky Way, the Sun, and the Moon. The lowest semicircle, however, refers to the image of the Earth itself, from which a multifaceted view toward meteorological objects is usually made.

Furthermore, every place positioned between the ethereal heaven and the earth is the vast seat of the air or the extension of the world-spirit, in whose capacity, as a common medium, the entire system of our design and proposal seems to be included and contained. This general place is also divided into three parts by two curved lines forming an arc, which the common people are accustomed to call the "regions of the air," neglecting their dimensions, about which common philosophers seem to contend too much. We, however, think that the lower region of the air does not exceed the highest mountains in its dimension or extension.

# Clear Explanation

...we [state]: but in truth, we believe the upper region to be vast and exceedingly spacious. We consider the region situated between these two—the middle region—to occupy a moderate dimension between those extremes. Within these regions of the air are contained the principal subjects of our focus (as has been stated); and we believe this must be considered by you above all, and placed before your eyes, as the various seats and locations of **meteors** <note>In the 17th century, "meteors" referred to any atmospheric phenomenon, including rain, wind, lightning, and clouds, not just falling stars.</note>.

In the upper region, we have arranged the divine act and the organs or ministers in and through whom all things in these lower parts—and indeed even in the heavens above—are perfected. We shall distinguish these according to the capacity of our own understanding. Regarding these ministers, who are the beginnings of all things (both perfectly and imperfectly mixed), we shall offer light and brief words in this place, descending from the summit of the "mirror" to its base. We do this because mention has been made of them abundantly in both preceding and following sections, to the honor of GOD, the creator of all, and for the instruction of man, who is the end and perfection of all things.

Since all things created in the world—whether they are simple or spring from simple things (such as the **Angels**, being "otherness" and forged from two things; the stars; and even among sublunary bodies, primarily the imperfectly mixed bodies which are composed in and from the air; and finally the perfectly mixed things such as animals, vegetables, and minerals)—are composed of a **luminous form** (whether apparent or hidden) and **matter** as the subject from which they are made. The nature of matter is to be passive, while the nature of form is to act; without these qualities, nothing in the world could exist or reach the goal of perfection toward which all things tend. Thus, in the first place, we must consider what the source and beginning is in the motion of continuous action, from which diverse acts are rained down and disseminated everywhere through the world. Following that, we must consider what kind of ministers or organs the primary Actor uses, through which he acts or pours out the acts of his emanation. Finally, we believe it should be considered with diligent gaze what the principal subjects in the world are—both in the ethereal heaven and in the air (in which all kinds of meteors, our primary subject here, are usually procreated)—and lastly in the water and the earth, around which the aforementioned acts of God are observed to operate and turn.

In the first or highest place, we find God himself, described as if by letters in the immense and infinite dimension of his divinity. He is an image that can never be painted, nor can his infinity be grasped by the human mind. This infinity we choose to signify or express here by the word <term>Ensoph</term> <note>original: "Ensoph." From the Hebrew *Ein Sof*, meaning "without end" or "the Infinite."</note>, as do the Kabbalists and more hidden theologians. This signifies Infinity, which they have asserted to be the unique fountain of life and divine essence—namely, the boundlessness without which nothing lives and nothing is, for all things proceed from the One. This unique fountain (whose secrets it is impossible to penetrate) they not unwisely divide into a double spring, namely the natural and the spiritual. From this fountain proceed the living waters, which descend primarily as an emanation through a stream into the paternal "luminous gate" called <term>Elion Cheter</term> <note>original: "Elion Cheter." From the Hebrew *Elyon Keter*, meaning the "Supreme Crown," the highest of the Sephirot.</note>, that is, the Supreme Crown, and then afterwards into the Son, <term>Hochma</term> <note>original: "Hochma." From the Hebrew *Chokhmah*, meaning "Wisdom."</note> or Wisdom. Hence the Royal Psalmist says, *with thee is the fountain of life* <note>Psalm 36:9. original: "apud te est fons vitæ."</note>. From this, it was right to gather that GOD in his innermost essence is outside all things and beyond the cavity of the world, nor can he be grasped by the sharp edge of the mind. These emanations, taking on a worldly spirit, are accustomed to take the names and properties of **Angels**. The first three of these, from the number of ten, are ordained to forge the regions of the world, the heavens, and the elements; the first, the Crown, is ascribed to the Father; the second, called Wisdom, to the Son; and Prudence <note>Likely referring to Binah (Understanding/Prudence).</note> to the Holy Spirit. The Royal Prophet also seems to prove this in this speech: *by the word of the Lord the heavens were made firm, and by the breath of his mouth all their power* <note>Psalm 33:6. original: "verbo Domini firmati sunt cœli, & spiritu ab ore eius omnis virtus eorum."</note>. Here, the Lord is the Father, sending out the Word or Wisdom, by means of which heaven and earth were created from the waters (as St. Peter testifies), and by the spirit from both, all power is in them. However, the seven other emanations are received and, as it were, absorbed by the seven remaining Angelic spirits, by means of which the said Angels are shaped; they act and operate according to the property of the Divine name by which they are rained upon those worldly subjects, wherever they are disposed throughout the spacious world. And these are those angels who are said to preside over the Seven Planets, about which more will be said below.

As for these angelic or spiritual receptacles or organs, which are ordained by God to receive the types of divine influences: for the better understanding of the readers, we shall explain them in a few words, along with the channels of influences and the orders of angels who primarily receive them, and finally, to which spheres of the celestial region they lead them by office.

From these, again, ten Archangels (counting the soul of the Messiah among them), created by GOD for this business, receive those emanations as luminous influences from each order. ### Mirror of Meteorological Phenomena

The higher beings receive light, or a lucid emanation, directly from God; they then emit and manifest it to those of the lower orders. For this reason, the Angels are called "mirrors," as they are capable of receiving the light of God. On this point, Dionysius <note>Dionysius the Areopagite, a 5th-century theologian influential in angelology.</note>, Basil, Isidore, Gregory, and others agree. Similarly, just as secret theologians have observed ten distinct hidden properties in GOD through the study of the Holy Bible—perceiving various names of GOD attributed to them by prophets and patriarchs—so too is a specific Angel assigned to each of these emanations. This angel holds a primary and singular duty regarding that property of GOD for which they were destined from the beginning. For it is a general rule among the secret theologians, Kabbalists, and others (with whom Dionysius also seems to agree), that no angel is permitted to undertake a work belonging to another. But truly, because the office of the angel **Metatron** <note>original: "Metattron"</note> was so universal—concerning the formation of the world, the division of darkness from light, the vivification of the world, and the motion of the heavens—he is believed to be that "first wisdom" created before every creature (as the wise man says), through whom all things were afterward made. Thus, he contains within himself the entire perfection of the angelic nature, just as all the solar rays are said to exist within the sun.

We proceed, therefore, to a clear demonstration of this matter, as you have it depicted in the highest region of our "Meteorographic Mirror" in the following manner:

The first emanation, gushing from the eternal fountain of divinity according to the benevolent property of GOD and prone toward kindness, is called **I AM** <note>original: "EHIEH," the Hebrew name for God implying eternal existence</note>. This name of GOD has regard for eternity and the entire wheel of time—namely the past, present, and future. The channel or lucid gate of this fountain of divine grace—the *Sephirota* or Kabbalistic numbering—is the <term>Crown</term> <note>original: "Cheter"</note>, serving as the root of the entire Sephirotic tree. From this gate, the emanation of life and essence flows into the order of the <term>Seraphim</term> <note>original: "Seraphin"</note>, which is the highest order of the first Hierarchy. According to Isidore, these angels are, as it were, fiery, kindling others with a fiery heat and love. They possess that remarkable clarity by means of this most lucid outflow, full of the gift of love and concord; this order is the fountain of Charity. From that first and greatest of all Angels, **Metatron** <note>original: "Metattron"</note>, this lucid influence is received, and he directs it into the highest sphere of the ethereal heaven, called the "First Mover" <note>original: "primum mobile"</note>. By its power, he animates all things, rotating the heaven in the entire world from sunrise to sunset, and from sunset back to sunrise in a natural day. Thus, he seems to animate the entire world-spirit by his motion and light, which is why the Platonists call him the "Soul of the World."

The second emanation is called **THE LORD** <note>original: "IAH"</note>, also from His benevolent and merciful property; for through this divine name, form is dispersed through the entire spirit of the world. The channel through which it passes, and the lucid gate through which it exits, is called by the Kabbalists <term>Wisdom</term> <note>original: "Hochma"</note>, by which all things were made. This emanation directs the fountain-head of its light to the order of the <term>Cherubim</term> <note>original: "Cherubin"</note>, who are therefore said to abound in the fullness of knowledge and the gift of wisdom and understanding. This order entrusts that downward-tending emanation to the guardianship of the Archangel <term>Raziel</term>, who is made the guardian and director of this outflow. He directs it into the eighth sphere (that of the fixed stars), through the middle of which passes that zone or belt of heaven called the Zodiac. Arguing from the etymology of the name, this spirit or emanation acts primarily toward vivification and animation through its power. This influx also generates various meteorological impressions in the air.

The third emanation or divine flow is called **GOD** <note>original: "ELOHIM"</note>. The channel or branch in which it moves, as well as the lucid gate from which it exits, is called <term>Prudence</term> <note>original: "Binah," often translated as Understanding</note>. From here, it descends into the lowest order of the highest hierarchy, namely the <term>Thrones</term> <note>original: "Thronos"</note>, indicating a property of GOD that is severe and full of judgment. From this order, the Archangel <term>Zaphkiel</term> (or as others prefer, <term>Oriphel</term>) receives these flows and leads them into the Sphere of Saturn. Thus, just as Saturn is a heavy, fixed, and melancholic planet, it is said to rain down severe effects upon the lower world, pertaining to judgment and punishment. For this reason, it is called the "Greater Misfortune" by astrologers. Occasionally, sad and dark effects—such as dense clouds, foul mists, thin and dry rains, and sometimes those mixed with thunder—are produced by him in the manner of the separation of the fiery element from chaos.

The fourth emanation from the fountain of the <term>Infinite</term> <note>original: "Ensoph," referring to the Ein Sof or the Boundless God</note> is called **THE MIGHTY** <note>original: "EL"</note>, which indicates mercy in this property of GOD. Hence, its channel or lucid gate is named <term>Clemency</term> <note>original: "Chesed"</note>. This influx of divine light is sent into the highest order of the middle hierarchy, called the <term>Dominions</term> <note>original: "Dominationes"</note>. Through this, power is given against evil spirits, along with the benefits of life and benevolent winds, led into the sphere of Jupiter by the Archangel <term>Zadkiel</term> (or as others prefer, <term>Zaccariel</term>). This is the reason why the planet Jupiter is so filled with benevolence toward the human race and living creatures; thus, it is called the "Greater Fortune" by astrologers, just as Saturn is called the "Greater Misfortune." Among the meteors it may produce in the air are whitish clouds mixed with redness, which usually resolve into light rain or sometimes into wind.

The fifth emanation is named **GOD OF MIGHT** <note>original: "ELOHIM KIBBOR"</note>. This name of GOD implies severity, wherefore the channel or gate from which it flows from the <term>Infinite</term> fountain is called <term>Strength</term> <note>original: "Geburah," often associated with Judgment or Power</note>, that is, punishment. This emanation passes downward into the middle order of the third hierarchy, which is the <term>Principalities</term> <note>original: "Principatus"</note>, which order is...

# A Lucid Explanation

<note>This section describes the 5th emanation, Gevurah</note> ...of power and dominion over rebels, forcing them through force and arms, as it were, toward the true worship and reverence of God. The Angel to whom this influence is entrusted by this order is the severe **Samael**, who leads it into the sphere of Mars. From this sphere, fiery influences and the seeds of wrath are sent down into the lower world. By the power of such influences, the air is seen to be filled with saffron-colored clouds, which sometimes emit thunder, lightning, and tempests; indeed, according to the opinion of astrologers, comets and fiery impressions <note>Atmospheric phenomena like meteors or auroras</note> arise from here. It is for this reason that, due to the infected and malignant heat of this Martial influence, fevers, plagues, and hot diseases are sometimes observed to be introduced among mortals; hence, Mars is frequently called the "Lesser Misfortune" <note>original: "Infortunium minus"</note> by astrologers.

The **Sixth Emanation** is called **ELOAH**; being most full of every bright virtue, it has for its channel **Tipherith** <note>Tiferet</note>, which signifies grace, beauty, and clarity. This influence directs its power into the lowest rank of the Middle Hierarchy, which is the order of **Powers** <note>original: "Potestatum"</note>, whose duty it is to subject wicked angels or spirits to themselves through force and authority, as Gregory says. This order commits that influence to the power and guardianship of **Michael**, the great Angel who made this emanation his own inner nature. By its virtue, he subjected the Dragon <note>Lucifer or the Devil</note> and his entire company to himself. This Angel, therefore, conducts this influence into the sphere of the Sun, over which he presides, from which he later pours it out liberally into the lower realms. Upon contact, life is multiplied in growing plants, generation occurs on land and in the sea, and all things are refreshed by a dignity worthy of solar grace and beauty.

The **Seventh Outflowing** is called by the Kabbalists **JEHOVAH ZEBAOTH** <note>The Lord of Hosts</note>. Its channel or Sephirotic gate is called **Netzeth** <note>Netzach</note>, meaning "Triumph," through which this emanation goes forth. It descends into the highest order of the Lowest Hierarchy, which they call the **Virtues**, in which divine power shines forth; for as Isidore says, the angels of this order receive illumination, purification, and perfection from the orders of the Middle Hierarchy. The Archangel <note>Likely referring to a specific commentator like Pico della Mirandola or Archangelus of Borgonovo</note> in his *Commentary on Kabbalistic Dogma* seems to assert that it is into this order that influences from *Tipherith* are directed, which indeed seems probable because of its bright, clear, and beautiful condition, wherein the light of GOD shines wonderfully. However, we follow Dionysius and Isidore here. This influence is received from this order by the good Angel **Anael**, and is carried down into the sphere of Venus. By its presence and virtue, good influences—pleasing to the human race—are scattered everywhere through the sublunary air, water, and earth. By its presence, thin clouds and sometimes light, sifting rain are produced. This is also why this planet, namely Venus, is called the "Lesser Fortune" <note>original: "Fortunium minus"</note> by astrologers.

The **Eighth Emanation** is called **ELOHIM ZEBAOTH**, according to its property. It has for its gate or Sephirotic channel **Hod**, which means "Praise." Through this, it descends into the order of **Archangels**, from which it is remitted to the Archangel **Raphael**. He conducts it into the sphere of Mercury, who is (according to the opinion of the Poets) the great messenger of Jove <note>Jupiter</note>. From there, it is later sent into the sublunary region, where it sometimes creates swift winds in the air, which are not infrequently accompanied by copious showers and rain. Furthermore, this influence is observed to act in various ways within man: specifically, it grants good sense, makes the wit sharp, and the memory fertile.

The **Ninth** is called **SHADDAI** <note>original: "SADAI"</note>, whose bright gate is **Iesod** <note>Yesod, meaning Foundation</note>. Descending through this, it passes into the order of **Angels**, from which it is committed to the guardianship of **Gabriel**. He directs it into the sphere of the Moon, which rains down moist and cold influences into the air, water, and earth, creating various and multiform impressions in them—namely winds, rains, and other things of this sort.

Finally, the **Tenth** is called **ADONAI**, that is, "Lord." Its channel is **Malchut** <note>Malkuth</note>, meaning "Kingdom," from which this emanation descends into the sphere of souls (as the Kabbalists maintain), led by the soul of the **Messiah**. From there, it is finally carried down into the elements, where for the most part severe effects are produced due to the disobedience of man.

Furthermore, I would have you know in passing, according to the intentions of the Magi and Kabbalists, that each of the aforesaid angels is a great Prince, having the power of much liberty to dispense these gifts of GOD—or these properties of His—either mercifully or severely according to His will among the creatures of this sublunary world. Their powers seem to increase more according to their common and natural or customary disposition in the annual course, in the dominion of their planets and signs, and consequently in their ordained times—namely years, months, days, and hours—and in the elements, parts of the world, and the very winds appropriated to them. And certainly, to speak more truly, the dominion belongs neither to the signs nor the planets, but is in respect to the more abundant divine outflowing, which comes to it more at one time than another, according to the divine will. Consequently, the Angel or Intelligence of a planet or star is like its internal spirit moving it, whose central soul is that very emanation of divinity, by which it is continually intoxicated as if by divine nectar. Therefore, it is poorly said by those skilled in Magic that the Angels act in the dominion of a sign or planet; rather, the sign and planet are stronger or more powerful according to the greater or lesser strength of their Intelligence in the divine emanation which it receives. Furthermore, it must also be understood that every one of these powerful Angels (seven of whom are said to stand before the face of God) rules over many legions, with which they are accustomed to act both in heaven and in the elementary region.

# Clear Exposition
<meta>catchword: Similitude-</meta>

But now we have arrived at the proposed task at hand, namely to the exposition and explanation of the forms, locations, and qualities depicted in our **Meteorographic Mirror** <term>Catoptro Meteorographico: A "mirror" or visual diagram used by the author to illustrate and explain atmospheric phenomena.</term>. Regarding their location, we find it to be either common or proper: we call the "common" location the entire space of air between the ethereal heaven and the earth. We establish three "proper" locations as the regions of the whole and common air. We see the upper region filled with **comets** of various kinds and differing shapes, and simultaneously with **chasms** and **burning beams**, concerning which we speak only a word here, as they are treated more fully elsewhere.

As there are various species of comets, so too have the Philosophers assigned them names consistent with their appearances.

The **Fiery Lance** <note>original: "Lanceam ignitam"</note> they called the first species, as it is stretched out in length.

The **Sword** <note>original: "Xiphias"</note> is a shorter lance, and this species of comet is tapered to a sharp point.

The **Mercurial Comet** is one that is somewhat bluish in heat, small in size, having a minute and long tail.

The **Soldier** is so called because it has a Martial <note>Meaning the reddish color associated with the planet Mars.</note> color, and this comet is also tailed, as you have it delineated in the Mirror.

The **Dawn** <note>original: "Aurora"</note> has the appearance of a star, but excels every star in its clarity and splendor.

The **Rose** is a comet great in size and round, which seems to present and carry a human face.

The **Hook** <note>original: "Tenaculum"</note> is a comet which, as if erected upon a fiery base, is tailed in a marvelous manner.

The **Black Comet** is of a dark color, endowed with a short and brief tail, and it seems in some way to be adorned with a very thin head of hair.

The **Horned Comet** <note>original: "Ceratias"</note> is so called from the appearance of its heat or the shape of its fire.

There are also other fiery meteors which are sometimes visible in this region, which we nevertheless by no means call comets; for while comets are ignited in such a way that they are not quickly extinguished, these other appearances—such as the **Chasm**, the **Beam**, and **flying sparks**—are less so, having arisen from a matter or spirit that is less firm and more inconstant. But since we have spoken of these before, and also explained their forms in our Mirror, we have decided not to make a longer discourse in this place.

For the other meteors, both luminous and dark, without further explanation in this place—namely for their forms and locations—I judge that you should be referred primarily to an inspection of our Mirror, and for their order, to the aforementioned table or classification for the sake of brevity.

### *Concerning Meteors which are seen, but are not such as they appear.*

Now, however, we come to those meteors which exhibit a certain shape or image in the air, and yet they are not what they seem to be. But truly, since this will appear difficult and hard to consider at first glance to those who are ignorant and unskilled in the **science of optics**, we have therefore expressed the reason for those appearances in the manner of perspective in our Meteorographic Mirror. We have done this with proper and consistent demonstrations, by which you may more easily reach a certain knowledge of such visions in the air without great fatigue. In this business of demonstrating, I confess that I follow and imitate the doctrine of **Vitellio** <term>Vitellionis: Referring to Witelo, a 13th-century Polish friar and scientist whose "Perspectiva" was a foundational text on optics.</term> concerning the nature of seeing. By this we are taught that we see through the action of a visible form upon the eye and the "passion" (or reception) of the sight by such a form.

Meteors of this kind, whose logic we gather solely from the science of optics (since they are not what they appear to be), are **Mock Suns** <note>original: "Parelii"</note>. These occur when the sun is rising or setting at an angle, in the lower part of a cloud, and this in the lowest part of the air region. They are the shapes or images of the Sun or Moon which are represented in a dewy cloud, no differently than an image seen in water or a mirror. We show <gloss>show</gloss> the reason for this vision through **pyramidal lines** <note>The cone-shaped visual rays that 17th-century science believed traveled between the eye and the object.</note> from the place of sight to the objects of the Sun and Moon in the lower part of the cloud, just as it is demonstrated in our Mirror.

<meta>This page continues the specific explanation of atmospheric phenomena, moving from the general classification of "meteors" to the optical mechanics of rainbows, halos, and mirages. It builds on the previous page's distinction between the upper and lower regions of the air.</meta>

# Mirror of Atmospheric Phenomena <term>Catoptri Meteorographici: Literally a "Meteorological Mirror," referring to a treatise or diagram explaining how atmospheric phenomena reflect and refract light.</term>

Similarly, the **celestial arc** <note>original: "arcus coelestis," referring to a rainbow.</note> is most often seen either at the rising or the setting of the sun, but rarely at midday, except occasionally during the winter season. And this occurs through divine power, sketching itself from the moist air to our sight; for the sight is not reflected by lighter things, but rather objects that are lighter in color and moving stir the sight. But now, contrary to the common opinion of philosophers, we believe it must first be understood that the rainbow does not form in a cloud, but in the lower part of the lowest region of the air, as was declared by us in the preceding pages. This is because it is observed to be not very far from the eye—namely, not more than three hundred paces away. We have proof of this because we can perceive the object shining with its **four colors** <note>Before the modern convention of seven colors (ROYGBIV), many Renaissance observers identified only three or four primary colors in the rainbow.</note> between our eye and a mountain or a forest that is not far distant. Indeed, we have even sometimes seen the rainbow itself descending upon the grass by means of a dewy rain. If you wish to know the clear reason for this matter, you must correctly gather and understand these things which are now to be said, with diligent attention, casting aside the vain opinions of many philosophers which are overwhelmed by mists and darkness.

In a thick, clear substance (such as water), a small, round image of the sun is reflected; in a thinner substance, a large round image is reflected. If it is thinned further, it becomes even larger, though everything around the center of the image appears bare, because the scattered rays are not brought back to a single point. Now, in that lighter air, the rays are scattered, just as we are accustomed to gathering rays with glass lenses to burn objects; and surely this has great momentum toward that sudden constriction of the air. When the air is further thinned and changed into a moist, droplet-filled, and misty breath, the greatest roundness is perceived—not of the image itself, but of the represented light. Thus, by certain steps, we can move from the first and smallest reflection to the largest. The arc is colored by light scattered further into the moisture; only a semicircle is seen because the earth stands in the way, but if the observer is placed in a higher location, the circle appears whole. This is proven by experience and demonstrated through the principles of sight and objects explained in the science of mirrors.

The **halo** <note>original: "Corona"</note> is also formed in the same way, except that it is created between the sight and the sun.

The **enlargement of the sun** at its setting occurs from the refraction of light in thicker air.

The **discoloration of the moon** without enlargement usually occurs from the light passing through misty air that is not particularly thick.

**Perpendicular lines** <note>Sunbeams or "crepuscular rays" breaking through clouds.</note> are created because of the unevenness of the clouds, with sunlight transmitted through the gaps.

**Evening redness** arises from the penetration of light through the lower parts of the clouds.

**Temples, buildings, and men walking in the air** <note>Mirages, such as the Fata Morgana.</note> sometimes appear to our eyes, no differently than the images of bodies are usually seen in a mirror. So writes Pliny: that there are some who have sight so weak that they can see themselves in the air as if in a mirror, and this happens especially when the South wind is blowing.

### CHAPTER I.

->*On the efficient cause in general.*<-

It is a marvel that even the **Peripatetics** <note>Followers of Aristotle’s philosophy.</note> themselves established the definition of an efficient cause as being "that from which the principle of motion and rest originates," and yet they either remained ignorant of, or at least refused to acknowledge, the **Act of acts** or the **First Mover** <note>original: "primum rerum omnium motorem," a reference to the Aristotelian concept of the 'Unmoved Mover' which the author here identifies with God.</note> of all things. Instead, they preferred to understand this through "primary qualities," which they call "active" qualities. Thus, they wrongly accepted the effects proceeding from the Mover—namely the divine Word, creating and illuminating all things—as the efficient cause itself. Some, searching more deeply into the nature of that first mover, concluded that it was the very act of **Fate** and a kind of internal nature. 

We, however, being instructed by the doctrine of the Sacred Scriptures, say that the sole Actor of all things and the sole Mover in all things is **GOD**, specifically the divine Word or the **Holy Spirit**. David says: *By the word of the Lord the heavens were established, and all the power of them by the spirit of his mouth* <note>original: "Verbo Domini... firmati sunt coeli." A paraphrase of Psalm 33:6.</note>. From this, it follows that not only are the world and the parts of the world perfected by Him as the sole Actor, but every act, power, and work within it—whether of the earth, the heavens, or the elements—is perfected through the mediation of His spirit. Hence it is said elsewhere: *Come and see the works of GOD; say unto God, how wonderful art thou in thy works, Psalm 66:5.* And elsewhere: *GOD does whatever he wills in the heavens and on the earth, in the seas and all the deep places, Psalm 135:7.* And elsewhere: *Thy works are wonderful and vast, all of which thou hast made in wisdom, Psalm 103:24.* 

But perhaps some will respond that these things are to be understood and accepted as referring to things produced during the **Creation**, and not to the natural production and progression of things; they might argue that the various meteors, which arise according to the state and disposition of the time, do not proceed from God, but from things created by God—specifically from heat or cold acting as the primary qualities in nature. But, good GOD, how absurd it is to think that heat can be produced except where there is a fiery nature, which is endlessly...

...to move infinitely, and that fire or light could act where the incorruptible spirit—acting internally and centrally as a "form"—did not incite it! For this reason, we find these words written: *God made the fire grow mild so that it would not burn; now God makes the fire burn, for the creature serving you is stretched for punishment against the unjust, and is relaxed for beneficence for those who trust in you. Wisdom 16.* <note>original: "Ignem mitescere fecit Deus... Sap. 16." Referring to the Wisdom of Solomon, Chapter 16, describing the plague of fire in Egypt.</note> Hence it is also said elsewhere (from which it is clear that fire itself is ruled and moved by an internal agent): *Hearken to this, O Job; stand still and consider the wondrous works of the mighty God. Do you know when God disposes them, so that the light of his cloud may shine? Do you know the balancings of the thick cloud, the wondrous works of the God perfect in knowledge? Job 37:14-16.* <note>The Latin text cites Job 37. 13, but the passage matches verses 14-16 in modern bibles.</note> And elsewhere: *Will you send out lightnings and they shall go, and returning say to you: "Here we are"? Job 38:35.* And elsewhere: *Bringing up the clouds from the ends of the earth, he made lightnings into rain; he who brings forth the winds from his treasuries.* <note>Psalm 135:7.</note> There are infinite other passages that tend to confirm in plain words that God himself, or divine wisdom, is the efficient cause of "hot" meteors. <note>In this context, "hot" meteors refer to phenomena involving heat or light, like lightning.</note>

Furthermore, the same must be said concerning "cold" effects, for the sacred text says: *By his breath, the mighty God produces ice and narrows the breadth of the waters. Job 37:10.* And elsewhere: *Sending his word to the earth, his command runs most swiftly; he who sends snow like wool, and scatters frost like ashes; he casts down his ice like morsels; who can stand before his cold? Psalm 147:15-17.* And elsewhere: *Who has fathered the frost of heaven? Job 38:29.* Shall we answer along with the **Peripatetics** <note>Followers of Aristotle’s school of philosophy.</note> that it is cold, or the north wind, or a hot and dry exhalation? Certainly, if we consider the matter to its core, we will perceive that all these things are to be attributed to God alone, and not at all to created things. For in this way we could assert that a sword is the efficient cause of a wound, when it should be ascribed to the hand of the man striking it; and yet in truth, neither the sword nor the hand are the efficient causes, but the spirit acting within the man. This spirit is driven and directed as a vehicle by that First Actor of all things, who dwells everywhere and acts according to His will—whether for a man's punishment or for his benefit—in the manner of lightnings (which are God's ministers for executing the divine will). Hence the wise man says: *God brings every work into judgment with every hidden thing, whether it be good or evil. Ecclesiastes 12:14.* Yet that which seems so to man must not be considered wickedness or evil. For as Job says: *Far be it from the mighty God to do wickedness, and from the Almighty to do iniquity. Job 34:10.* For He renders to a man according to his work, and causes him to find according to his way. And elsewhere: *God does whatever He wills, and no one shall ask Him, "What or why do you do thus?" Wisdom 12:12.* But it is our purpose to discourse more at length throughout this entire section regarding the act and operation of the Almighty **Jehovah**, not only in the wonders of meteorological matters but also in the perfect production of compound things, as well as His ministers and primary instruments through which He is accustomed to work both in the heavens and on the earth. In the last two parts of this section, however, we shall speak in a worldly manner, regarding the effects of both the God-like and angelic divinity as efficient causes—namely the sun, the moon, and the stars, with their hot or cold influences upon the celestial region, and the primary qualities of the elements (fire, air, water, and earth), along with various types of vapors among those elements.

# CHAPTER II.

->What God is in Himself and through Himself, with no consideration given to created things:<-
->In the resolution of this doubt, the testimonies of the Philosophers, the Cabalists, and finally the Sacred Scriptures are explained.<-

**Simonides** (an excellent philosopher, deservedly celebrated by Aristotle himself and Cicero for the depth of his knowledge) is said to have requested the space of one day to resolve the doubt when he was asked by the tyrant **Hiero** <note>Hiero I, ruler of Syracuse in the 5th century BCE.</note> exactly what thing God was. Therefore, when the tyrant returned to him the following day, he asked again that he be made certain regarding that doubt; but then the philosopher requested the space of two days for the resolution of the petition or question. When that time had finished and the tyrant returned, he doubled the time and requested four days, and thus he doubled the space of time at every turn. Finally, when the king demanded from him the reason for this doubling of time, he is said to have received this response: *“The more I think about this most exalted matter, the more obscure it appears to my intellect, as it is something that dwells in a certain light which human spirits are unable to reach or attain.”* And in this, he seems to agree with the Sacred Scriptures, by which we are taught that God dwells in "inaccessible light." <note>1 Timothy 6:16.</note> But indeed, that heavenly Teacher through the Gospel of Saint Matthew teaches us the way by which we may attain knowledge of both God the Father and the Son, asserting that no one can know the Son except the Father, and again, that no one can reach knowledge of God the Father except the Son, or he to whom the Son wishes to reveal Him. Therefore, it is certain that judging a nature so supreme is a very difficult, or rather impossible, thing unless we are instructed by the Word of God and the Sacred Scriptures. And although we may know God *a posteriori*—that is, from His creatures and His glory in the most luminous...

...although we may discern God by his garments <note>The "garments" of God refers to the visible world and the physical laws of nature which clothe the invisible creator.</note>, nonetheless, to scrutinize his greatness is beyond the capacity of human intellect; for his greatness is (according to the Prophet) not to be grasped, *Psalm 145:3,* and much less is his pure essence granted to be seen by human and fleshly eyes, according to that saying of the Prophet and Evangelist: *No one has ever seen God. 1 John 4.*

We shall therefore follow, in our description of God, partly the doctrine of the most excellent philosophers, and partly that of the Cabalists <note>The "Cabalists" refers to practitioners of Kabbalah, a tradition of Jewish mysticism that was heavily adapted by Christian scholars during the Renaissance to explain the mysteries of creation.</note> in those matters where they agree with the Holy Bible; and finally, we shall declare in a few words what is to be gathered from the Word of God for a living description of God.

We gather therefore from the testimonies of divine writers that God has a dual nature regarding us: namely, a **hidden** nature and a **manifest** nature. The **hidden** nature is that in which, before the creation of the world, he seemed to human understanding to rest in infinite darkness and to do, as it were, nothing. Instead, he reflected his heat and power back into himself, and did not apply the rays of his light to the creation of the world at all. And this same thing must also be said concerning his rays or essence resting and hidden within the dim and shadowy things of the world; in what manner he is described by Mercurius Trismegistus <note>Mercurius Trismegistus is the legendary Hellenistic figure to whom the "Hermetic" writings are attributed; he was viewed as a contemporary of Moses who possessed ancient wisdom.</note> in these words: *The Monad* (he says) *generated a monad before the creation of the world, and reflected its heat into itself; that is, it shone only for itself.* <note>original: "Monas... ante mundi creationem monadem genuit..."</note> By these words he seems to hint that the divine nature—the luminous fountain, the act of all active things, the origin of life, the ocean of form—reflected the rays of its fiery and purely formal nature back into itself. From this it happened that before there was any will in him to create the world, an infinite abyss was overwhelmed in shapeless darkness and was void. Indeed, the said Philosopher seems to imply this in another place: *There was* (he says) *an infinite shadow in the abyss.* In this speech, he seems to agree with Moses, who says that *darkness was upon the face of the deep.* And this was that "matter in potentiality" <note>The term "matter in potentiality" refers to the Aristotelian concept of *materia prima*, or prime matter, which exists as a possibility but has not yet taken a specific form.</note> of the Peripatetics, which they called the "first matter," whence this sort of hidden nature is called by some "divine power," as will be declared below. Furthermore, just as the Philosophers considered that divine nature—concealed by darkness and gloom and not yet expanding itself—mathematically, so indeed they called it the **Arithmetical Unity**, and sometimes the **Geometrical Point**. I say a **Unity** simple in itself, without any respect to number; and a **Point**, having no relation to a circumference, but insofar as they are considered in either art in their simple nature: indivisible, of no quantity, quality, or substance, and yet the principle of all these things. For once it is expanded, it becomes everything that is, or everything that can be understood within the ten categories <note>The "ten categories" (predicaments) are the fundamental classes of being defined by Aristotle, such as substance, quantity, and quality.</note>, as will be more broadly declared in the description of the manifest God; in which this simplest unity of all will be shown to be fortified by its peripheral numbers, just as a point is by its circumference.

In the art of the Cabalists, the more skilled have called this divine power, thus hidden, the **Dark Aleph** <note>Aleph is the first letter of the Hebrew alphabet. In this mystical context, the "Dark Aleph" represents God in his unmanifested state, before light was created.</note>, just as they called that which is manifested and shining forth from the darkness the **Bright Aleph**. But truly, by the **Dark Aleph**, they understand a numbering according to the Cabalistic system, namely *Hochma* <note>original: "Hochma" (Chokhmah), the Hebrew word for Wisdom, the second Sephirah in the Kabbalistic Tree of Life.</note> or Wisdom, or that Monad which the Monad generated before any creation, the heat of which it reflected back into itself. This divine wisdom, emanating from the father and returning to the bosom of the father before the act of creation, the wise have called the "Principle" or "Beginning," about which it is written in the book *Bahir*: *Nothing is the beginning except wisdom. Reuchlin, book 3, On the Cabalistic Art.* <note>Johannes Reuchlin (1455–1522) was a German humanist who introduced Kabbalah to Christian scholars.</note> For, he says, in the infinite itself, the very essence of the three highest numberings of the Cabalistic tree—which we Christians call the three persons in divine matters—is most absolute; since it is retracted and remaining in the abyss of darkness, as if idle, or as they say, looking toward nothing, it is therefore called **Ein** <note>original: "Ein" (Ayin), the Hebrew word for "nothing" or "naught," used to describe God's state before manifestation.</note>, that is, **nothing**, or non-being, as well as "no end" <note>A reference to "Ein Sof" (Without End).</note>, because we, being penalized by such a thin poverty of intellect regarding divine things, judge concerning those things which do not appear no differently than we judge concerning those things which are not. But when it shows itself so that it is "something" and truly subsists, then the **Dark Aleph** is converted into the **Bright Aleph**. And then, just as the **Dark Aleph** was called the **Small Aleph**, so the **Bright Aleph** was called the **Great Aleph**; so they say. By the **Bright Aleph** they understood the Word or the divine emanation by means of which all things were made, about which we will speak more fully in the following chapter, where we will discuss the Manifest God, that is, the **Bright and Manifest Aleph**. Whence it is clear that the same relationship exists between the **Small Aleph** and the **Great Aleph** as exists between **Alpha** and **Omega**, which is called by the Cabalists the **Small or Dark Aleph** and the **Great or Bright Aleph**. *I am the first and the last* is read elsewhere, but to the point.

The **Small or Dark Aleph**, and as it were "nothing," insofar as it is hidden by darkness, is like a unity without number, and a point without respect to a circumference: for that "smallness" denotes all things in potentiality, as that which, by revealing itself, suddenly also reveals, creates, and brings into act everything that is; all of which is contained in this emitted divine light.

Hence it is that in our Cabalistic discourse, in which we made mention of the **three fathers**, matching most aptly with the **three mothers** of the Cabalists, we placed the **Aleph Mother** as most highly consistent with the **Iod Father**. For just as **Aleph** represents the mundane darkness, namely its chaos, so **Iod** <note>Iod (Yod) is the tenth letter of the Hebrew alphabet and represents the first point of creation or the seed of all things.</note> is the immediate act of Jehovah, emitted from the whirlpool of the dark Abyss, from which the mundane **Aleph** or "First Mother" receives its splendor. For as the **Small Aleph** among the Cabalists denotes unity in Arithmetic, so **Iod** carries the number ten, which is signified by a unity and a Cipher <note>In the decimal system, 10 is written as 1 (unity) and 0 (the cipher).</note>; this divine unity, shining forth, makes the unity in potentiality—namely the **Dark Aleph**, which is as it were nothing—and through the **Cipher** something in act is denoted, by illuminating the formless waters

...and by driving away the shadows. The second mother of the Cabalists <note>The "Mothers" in Kabbalah are the three primary Hebrew letters (Aleph, Mem, Shin) from which all creation is said to derive.</note> was **Mem**, which we have demonstrated corresponds with the second letter of the Tetragrammaton <note>original: "Tetragrammati"; the four-letter holy name of God, YHWH.</note>, namely **He**. For just as **Mem** is the Hieroglyphic of pure waters, so also **He** denotes a clear spirit or aspiration. Finally, we have made **Vau** in the four-letter name the father, and as it were the masculine act, or the uncreated sun of that same Cabalistic mother **Shin**: for just as **Vau** denotes the degree of emanation in the solar palace, as he who *placed his Tabernacle in the sun*, so also **Shin** is the Hieroglyphic of fire. But more on these matters later.

Finally, we are taught by the sacred letters that God was hidden in respect to us, when he existed concealed in his own existence before the world was created. And in that respect, God’s own name was *I am*, <note>original: "Ego sum"</note> as is held in Genesis chapter 17. <note>Genesis 17:1 in the Vulgate begins "Ego sum Deus omnipotens" (I am God Almighty).</note>

For it was sufficient for him that he alone existed, when nothing besides himself was in the infinite mystery. And hence it is established that he spoke these things through the mouth of the prophet: *I have not spoken in secret from the beginning; from the time before it was done, I was there; and now my Lord has sent me and his spirit,* Isaiah 48:16. <note>The original text cites Isaiah 40:16, but the quote provided is from 48:16.</note> Indeed, this seems to refer to Wisdom or emanation, which the Wise Man says was created before all things; concerning which elsewhere: *The power of God, created before all things, is the end and beginning of all,* Ecclesiasticus 1. <note>The author is likely paraphrasing Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 1:4, "Wisdom hath been created before all things."</note> By these words he seems to imply the very same thing that the Cabalists intended: namely, that this power was the dark **Aleph**, inasmuch as it existed before all created things; and that it was the bright **Aleph**, the primary emanation from the fountain of light, insofar as the name of the "end and beginning of all" is attributed to it. Hence Wisdom says in her own person: *The Lord possessed me, Wisdom, in the beginning of his way, before his works, before any time; I was anointed before the age, when there were no depths I was brought forth, etc.* Proverbs 8:22.

We conclude, therefore, that God, before the creation of the world, shone back only upon himself, and that he delineated the world in his own Ideal and archetypal sanctuary according to his own pattern, before he willed to forge that world into a physical form, as will be more clearly explained in what follows.

## CHAPTER III.

->*Concerning the manifest God and his office and power in the creation of things, according*<-
->*to both the Philosophers and Cabalists, as well as the Fathers of Theology, all of whose*<-
->*opinions are clearly confirmed by the testimony of the sacred letters.*<-

This Wisdom, therefore, which was with God before any thing was created; this most holy Word, <note>original: "Verbum"</note> which was contracted in the dark beginning before the creation of the world, shining only to itself, was God himself, or the power of God, and his Virtue and emanation, which is no less to be divided from the God-form essence than the rays of the sun from the sun, as Hermes Trismegistus <note>A legendary Hellenistic figure often cited as the author of the Hermetic Corpus, which combines philosophy, alchemy, and magic.</note> testifies in *Pymander* 12, where he is accustomed to repeatedly call him "Pymander" and "Mind" or "God." This is (I say) the God-form spirit, this immediate emanation from the Father, which the aforementioned leader in divine Philosophy calls in one place *a light exceedingly sweet*, by which all things are revealed and formed. *The Mind* (he says) *by divine power changed its form, and suddenly revealed the universe, and I saw all things converted into a light exceedingly sweet and pleasant.* By these words he seems to argue that the hidden God or the dark Aleph (which he signifies through divine power) revealed himself for the revelation of the world and the driving away of shadows. And elsewhere, he calls this spirit a holy splendor, emanating out of the darkness. His words are these: *There was an infinite shadow in the abyss, but water and spirit were present in the chaos; however, a holy splendor flourished, which led out the elements from under the sand and moist nature, and the heavy things submerged in the shadows settled under the moist sand.* By these words, the Philosopher seems to declare not only the emanation of the spirit of that Wisdom out of the darkness, but also its harmonic power, by means of which the quarreling members of chaos itself are bound together in concordant peace and arranged among one another. This, therefore, is that spirit of fire of which Plutarch speaks thus: *God is an intellectual spirit of fire not having form in itself, but transforming into itself all things which it wills, and assimilating itself to all things and all things to itself*; which indeed it does not effect by means of elemental fire, but through itself alone or through a seraphic heat which is closest to the divine fire. By these things, therefore, the Philosopher wishes to make known that every act in the nature of things is to be attributed to the creative intellectual spirit of the highest condition, and not at all to creatures; and especially he seems to confirm that the existence of the world and of every thing in the world proceeds from a fiery act of this kind of divine spirit, which act he recognizes as being God, inasmuch as it is most pure. Hence, therefore, Hermes Trismegistus seems to conclude: That there is nothing in the nature of things which does not represent the image of divinity; and the Platonists call this spirit, thus infused in all things, the <term>Anima mundi</term> <note>World Soul: a conceptual spirit that permeates all of nature, connecting the divine to the physical.</note>. Whence also by another, this heat or divine light is defined as an "essentiality containing within itself all things, though they be diverse." And Zeno the Philosopher recognizes it to be the ruler...
