### On the Efficient Cause of Meteors.
<note>In this context, "meteors" refers to any atmospheric phenomena, including wind, rain, and lightning, rather than just falling stars.</note>

...of this world, from which the principal winds are observed to blow; for this reason, they are called the **Cardinal Winds**, as was declared by us in the preceding sections. For this reason, the Teachers of the Hebrews attribute the care and dominion of the Eastern wind to the Good Angel **Michael**; likewise, they attribute the West to **Raphael**. The former is called *Subsolanus* <note>The wind from under the sun</note> and the latter *Favonius* <note>The favorable or west wind</note>. To **Gabriel** is given the prefecture of the North and the principal wind of that region, while the governance of the South is given to **Uriel**.

And it should be known that although four spirits or demons are assigned to the office of the cardinal winds—namely, **Oriens** to the direction of the East wind, **Paymon** to the West, **Egyn** to the governance of the North, and **Amaymon** to the prefecture of the South—who also have many legions or cohorts of demons serving under them to execute their malice, nevertheless these evil angels (even though they are permitted to harm the sky, the earth, and the sea) are subject to the dominion of the aforementioned good angels. Thus, without their leave and permission, or rather the will and Word of GOD reflecting in them, they can do no evil on the lands, in the water, or in the air, as will be more clearly shown in the following discourse.

But the Teachers of the Hebrews, those most skilled in secret Theology <note>Kabbalah</note>, seem to distinguish this with even more expressive words. For **Rabbi Isaac Levi**, in the *Book of the 10 Numerations* <note>original: "Lib. de 10. numerationibus," likely referring to the ten Sephirot</note>, after he had spoken quite openly about the four Cardinal winds, continues thus:
> From those four winds he created angels who are presided over them by day and by night; for Michael, who is on the side of mercy, is **Mamona**, that is, the prefect over the Eastern wind until midday; and until the night, Raphael, who is also on the side of mercy, rules the Western wind; then Gabriel, in the power of judgment and severity, is the prefect over the Northern wind during the middle of the night and two measures of the world; but **Noriel** presides over the South.

These are his words. And the *Book of Secrets* <note>original: "Liber Arcanorum"</note> acknowledges that these presidents have many species or legions under them. **Joseph Castaliensis** <note>Joseph Gikatilla, a 13th-century Kabbalist</note> in the book called *The Gate of Light* <note>original: "Porta lucis"</note> seems to agree with this, saying:
> That from the earth all the way to the firmament there is no empty place, but all is full of forms; some of them pure, some capable of grace and mercies, and there are many foul, harmful, and tempting images below, all dwelling and flying in the air.

And elsewhere, Joseph Castaliensis has this:
> From the earth to the firmament there is no empty place; rather, the whole is composed of species: some for peace, some for war, some for good, some for evil, some for life, some for death. And all of that is in the lower habitation in which we dwell.

And all these spirits, if they are good, are animated by the good angelic winds; if evil, by the evil ones. From this it is clearly evident that those winds, which are considered by the **Peripatetics** <note>Followers of Aristotle's natural philosophy</note> and even by us common folk as "natural impressions," are referred to the orders of spirits when considered in **occult philosophy**. Hence we also read in the Sacred Page: *The spirit of the storms which fulfills his word, Psalm 148*. And elsewhere: *Who makes his angels winds, etc., Psalm 104*. Furthermore, the **Book of Revelation, chapter 7**, makes mention of the Angels in whose power is the force of the winds.

The four elements of the sublunary region, as they are diverse in nature, also claim for themselves diverse leaders and prefects appointed to them by God. Under their command exist great crowds of spirits or demons. Those under the command of the **Seraphim** are endowed with a fiery nature, and for this reason, by natural inclination, they choose the element of fire as their homeland. But if they descend further down outside its limits (which frequently happens in the domain of Mars in the heavens), they produce thunders, flashes, and lightnings and other things of that kind in the air, because of the conflict that the watery spirits have with them. By a similar reasoning, we see in the human body that the bilious or sanguine humor, when outside its natural place and seat, putrefies and disturbs the human "air" with hot meteors <note>referring to fevers or inflammations</note> and induces diseases. This same thing which was said of the fiery spirits is to be understood of the aerial, watery, and earthly spirits, who serve their own leaders and, by natural effort, choose that element over which their prince has dominion as their homeland. Hence they are called aerial, watery, and earthly spirits, because they participate more in those natures.

Finally, according to the doctrine of the Kabbalists and the Hebrew Doctors, we understand that there are **72 strong angels** of the whole earth, by whose assistance Moses is said to have divided the Red Sea. For these are called by them the "Angels of Division," and they say that God divided the earth according to the number of these angels. Whence we read in the book called *The Gate of Justice* <note>original: "Porta Iustitiæ"</note>:
> That all nations were left and handed over into the power of the seventy prefects, that is, the Princes of the angels, and these are said to be accustomed to being familiar to men, and to be the presidents of the seventy-two regions of the earth,

as **Reuchlin** <note>Johann Reuchlin, a German humanist and scholar of Greek and Hebrew</note> holds, who in the third book *On the Art of the Kabbalah* sets out to list their names according to the opinion of Rabbi Solomon and others in this manner:

**Vehuiah, Ieliel, Sitael, Elemiah, Mahasiah, Lelahel, Achaiah, Cathetel; Haziel, Aladiah, Lauiah, Hahaiah, Lezalel, Mehahel, Hariel, Hakamiah, Louiah, Caliel**, and so with the others as may be found in the place cited before.

And so you have all the kinds of good angels distinct and divided according to the partition of the world. Those more versed in Sacred Letters seem to relate this further, as the letters symbolize them: the Holy Letters are said to be symbols for created things, and consequently for the angels assigned to those created things, as we shall declare below.

### Chapter IV.

->*On the distinction between wicked and malignant Demons.*<-

**J**ust as God, who is the Commander of light, is the Commander of goodness, so also the Devil, who is the great Prince of darkness, is the author and operator of evil. From this it follows that just as God uses good angels—who are therefore called angels of light—as His ministers, so conversely the Devil has many troops of <term>Demons</term> <note>original: "Dæmonum"</note> under his command. These are divided into legions, to whom it is given to invade and harm the aerial spirit of both the <term>Macrocosm</term> <note>The "Great World" or the universe at large.</note> and the <term>Microcosm</term> <note>The "Little World," referring to the individual human being as a reflection of the universe.</note> in a malignant manner. Therefore, relying on these matters confirmed by the authority of many trustworthy writers, I shall proceed to distinguish the multitude of <term>Evil Spirits</term> <note>original: "Cacodæmonum"</note> in this manner:

| Evil spirits act malignantly regarding either: | | |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1. Spirit only** | — Of the Macrocosm [A] | |
| | — Of the Microcosm [B] | |
| **2. Spirit and body together** | — Of the Macrocosm alone [C] | |
| | — Of the Microcosm alone [D] | |
| | — Of both together [E] | |

The entire composition of both the world and man consists of spirit and body. However, because the universal spirit of both worlds is divided into three regions (as has been frequently declared by us before): First, there is the **Empyrean heaven**, which is the seat of the good angels, from which the malignant angels were banished into exile, as it were, to the dense and lower region of the universal spirit because of their ambitious rebellion. To this superior region of the mundane spirit corresponds the **intellectual or rational spirit** in man, which is the angelic seat of the mind.

Next, in the world, there is the middle seat of this universal spirit, which is called the **ether**; in this, the **Olympic Spirits** <note>original: "Dæmones Olympici" — In Renaissance occultism, these were spirits associated with the planets and the governance of the cosmos.</note> or Demons act. These are called the distributors of **Fate**, because (according to the pleasure of the supreme creator) they pour down both malevolent and benevolent influences into the region of the elements. It is from these that both sublunary demons, good and bad alike, receive their powers in acting and their domains. From this it is clear that **Satan**, who is the Prince of the Air, can do nothing without permission and varied influence, according to the diverse disposition of each <term>Sephirotic numbering</term> <note>A reference to the Sephiroth of the Jewish Kabbalah, the ten attributes or emanations through which the Infinite relates to the universe.</note> or "luminous gate." To this middle region of the world-spirit corresponds the **vital spirit** in man, which sometimes inclines toward higher things and sometimes toward lower and transitory things.

Finally, the spirit of the **sublunary world** is that which (by divine permission) the great Prince of darkness commands. To this corresponds the **natural spirit** in man, which **Paul** seems to call the "animal soul" <note>original: "animam animalem"</note>, whose appetite is occupied with the flesh and its pleasures. Hence, the Prince of the Air is said to have power and to work in the "children of distrust," as will be shown below. What the orders of Evil Spirits are in the elementary air, and what their conditions are, may be gathered from the following members of the Cacodæmonic division.

| Evil spirits in the sublunary spirit of the world—namely, the air—exercise their powers and differ in rank, as some are: | |
| :--- | :--- |
| **1. Principalities or Spirits of a superior order** | — Emperor |
| | — Kings [F] |
| | — Dukes [G] |
| **2. Subjects or those of an inferior condition** | — And subjected to the aforementioned leaders, who are divided from one another into cohorts and legions [H]. |

Just as in the Empyrean Heaven one may find Principalities, Archangels, and Angels of a benign condition, so indeed **Lucifer**, once cast down from that throne with his angels, has similar ministers under him, distinct in rank and dignity. We have this confirmed even by the Apostle, whose authority is this: *Put on* (he says) *the armor of God, that you may be able to stand against the snares of the Devil, for our struggle is not against flesh and blood, but against Princes and powers, against the world-rulers of these darknesses, against spiritual wickedness in high places, etc.* (Ephesians 6:12). By these words he evidently teaches that the Devil, as the supreme king and emperor of wickedness and malignancy, has under him his own ministers eminent in condition, whom the Apostle calls "Princes and powers," "world-rulers of darkness," and "spiritual wickedness." Hence also the said Apostle says elsewhere, *You walked according to the age of this world...*

This liberty and power is assigned to them at certain fixed times, years, months, days, and hours in the quarters of the world, the winds, and the elements; each of these Princes also has several orders of inferior demons under him, as will be seen more fully below.

But truly, since the mercy of God is said in the sacred scriptures to excel His severity, the Creator has assigned greater power and virtue to His good Princes than to His malignant ministers; indeed, He has given them dominion over those malignant and devastating spirits or angels. This is also excellently denoted by these words of the Apocalypse, chapter 7: *I saw four Angels standing upon the four corners of the earth, holding the four winds of the earth...*

## CHAPTER IV.
### *On the Distinctions Between Depraved and Malignant Demons.*

Just as God, who is the Commander of Light, is the Commander of all goodness, so too the Devil, who is the great Prince of Darkness, is the author and worker of evil. From this it follows that just as God employs <term>good angels</term> <note>original: "bonis angelis"</note> as his ministers—who are thereafter called angels of light—so, conversely, the Devil holds under his command many troops of demons. These are divided into legions, to whom it is given to invade and harm the <term>aerial spirit</term> <note>In this period, "spirit" often refers to a subtle substance that links the physical and spiritual realms, found in both the atmosphere and the human body.</note> of both the **Macrocosm** <note>The "Great World" or the universe.</note> and the **Microcosm** <note>The "Little World" or the individual human being.</note> in a malignant manner. Relying, therefore, on these matters confirmed by the authority of many trustworthy writers, I shall attempt to distinguish the multitude of **Evil Spirits** <note>original: "Cacodæmonum"</note> in the following way:

Evil spirits are malignly engaged either around:
*   **The spirit only**
    *   Of the Macrocosm [A.]
    *   Of the Microcosm [B.]
*   **The spirit and body together**
    *   Of the Macrocosm alone [C.]
    *   Of the Microcosm alone [D.]
    *   Of both at once [E.]

The entire composition of both the world and man is made of spirit and body. However, because the universal spirit of both worlds is divided into three regions (as has been frequently declared by us before): 

First, there is the **Empyrean heaven** <note>The highest, fiery level of heaven, traditionally the dwelling place of God and the highest angels.</note>, which is the seat of the good angels. From here, the malignant angels—on account of their ambitious rebellion—were banished, as if into exile, to the dense and lower region of the universal spirit. To this upper region of the world-spirit corresponds the **intellectual or rational spirit** in man, which is the angelic seat of the mind. 

Next, in the world, there is the middle seat of the universal world-spirit, which is called the **ether**. In this region, the <term>Olympic Spirits</term> <note>original: "Dæmones Olympici"; spirits associated with the planets and the celestial spheres who manage the functions of the cosmos.</note> or Demons operate. These are called the "distributors of Fate" because they pour down both malevolent and benevolent influences (according to the will of the supreme creator) into the region of the elements. It is from these spirits that both the good and evil sublunary demons receive their powers for acting and their various dominions. From this it is clear that **Satan**, who is the Prince of the Air, can do nothing without permission and a varying influx, according to the diverse disposition of each <term>Sephirotic numbering</term> <note>original: "numerationis sephiroticæ"; a reference to the ten Sephirot or attributes of God in Kabbalah, often visualized as gates or channels of divine energy.</note> or "shining gate." To this middle region of the world-spirit corresponds the **vital spirit** in man, which sometimes inclines toward higher things and sometimes toward lower and fleeting matters. 

Finally, the spirit of the **sublunary world** <note>The region below the moon, including the earth and its atmosphere, subject to change and decay.</note> is that which (by divine permission) the great Prince of Darkness commands. To this corresponds the **natural spirit** in man, which Paul seems to call the "animal soul" <note>original: "animam animalem"; the soul concerned with physical life, instincts, and sensory desires rather than spiritual intellect.</note>. Its appetite is occupied with the flesh and its pleasures. Hence, the Prince of the Air is said to have power and to "work in the children of disobedience," as will be shown below. What the alternating orders of these Evil Spirits are, and what their conditions may be, can be gathered from the following members of the classification of demons:

Evil spirits exercising their power in the sublunary spirit—namely, the air—differ in rank, as some are:
*   **Principalities or Spirits of a superior order.**
    *   Emperor.
    *   Kings [F.]
    *   Dukes [G.]
*   **Subjects or those of an inferior condition**, who are subject to the aforementioned leaders and are divided from one another into cohorts and legions [H.]

Just as in the Empyrean Heaven one may find Principalities, Archangels, and Angels of a benign condition, so too **Lucifer**, having once been cast down from that throne with his angels, has similar ministers under him, distinguished by rank and dignity. We also find this confirmed by the Apostle, whose authority is this: 

> *Put on (he says) the armor of God, that you may be able to stand against the snares of the devil. For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against Principalities and powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places &c. Ephesians 6:12.* 

By these words, he clearly teaches that the Devil, as if the supreme king of wickedness and malignancy, has ministers under him eminent in condition, whom the Apostle calls "Principalities," "Powers," "Rulers of the Darkness of the World," and "Spiritual Wickedness." Hence also, the said Apostle says elsewhere: *You walked according to the age of this world...*

# On the Efficient Cause of Atmospheric Phenomena.

### CHAPTER IV.

->*On the Distinction between Wicked and Malignant Demons.*<-

Just as God, who is the Commander of light, is the Commander of goodness, so also the Devil, who is the great Prince of darkness, is the author and worker of evil. From this it follows that, just as God uses <term>good angels</term> <note>These are spirits of light who act as divine messengers and agents of providence.</note> as his ministers—who are thereafter called angels of light—so, conversely, the Devil has many troops of demons under his command, which are divided into legions. To these it has been given to invade and harm the aerial spirit of both the <term>Macrocosm</term> <note>The "Great World," or the universe as a whole.</note> and the <term>Microcosm</term> <note>The "Little World," referring to the human being as a reflection of the universe.</note> in a malignant manner. Therefore, relying on these matters confirmed by the authority of many trustworthy writers, I shall attempt to distinguish the multitude of <term>Cacodemons</term> <note>original: "Cacodæmonum." From the Greek for "evil spirits."</note> in this manner:

Wicked demons are malignantly engaged with either:
*   The spirit alone:
    *   Of the Macrocosm (A)
    *   Of the Microcosm (B)
*   The spirit and body together:
    *   Of the Macrocosm alone (C)
    *   Of the Microcosm alone (D)
    *   Of both together (E)

The entire composition of both the world and man is made of spirit and body. But in truth, since the universal spirit of both worlds is divided into three regions (as has been more often declared by us before)—for first, there is the **Empyrean heaven**, which is the seat of the good angels, from which the malignant angels were banished into exile, as it were, to the dense and lower region of the universal spirit because of their ambitious rebellion; and the intellectual or rational spirit in man, which is the angelic seat of the mind, corresponds to this superior region of the worldly spirit. 

Next, there is the middle seat of this universal spirit in the world, which is called the **ether**; in this, the **Olympic** Angels or Demons <note>In this context, "Olympic" refers to spirits associated with the planetary spheres or the upper atmosphere, not necessarily the Greek gods.</note> act, who are therefore called the distributors of **Fate**, because (according to the pleasure of the supreme creator) they pour down both malevolent and benevolent influences into the region of the elements; it is from them that both the good and evil sublunary demons receive their powers in acting and their domains. From these things it is clear that **Satan**, who is the Prince of the air, can do nothing without permission and various influxes, according to the varying disposition of any <term>Sephirotic numbering</term> <note>A reference to the Sephirot of the Kabbalah, representing the ten attributes or emanations of God.</note> or "shining gate." The vital spirit in man, which sometimes inclines toward higher things and sometimes toward lower and fleeting things, corresponds to this middle region of the world’s spirit. 

Finally, the spirit of the sublunary world is that which (by divine permission) the great Prince of darkness commands; the natural spirit in man corresponds to this, which **Paul** seems to call the *animal soul* <note>original: "animam animalem." The lower part of the soul shared with animals, focused on physical survival and sensation.</note>, the appetite of which is occupied with the flesh and its pleasures. Hence, the Prince of the air is said to have power and to work in the "children of disobedience," as will be shown below. Moreover, what the orders of Cacodemons in the elementary air are, and what their conditions are, may be gathered from the following members of the Cacodemonical division:

Wicked demons exercising their powers in the sublunary spirit of the world—namely, the air—differ in rank, as some are:
*   Principalities or Spirits of a higher order:
    *   Emperor
    *   Kings (F)
    *   Dukes (G)
*   Subjects or those of a lower condition, subjected to the aforementioned leaders, who are divided among themselves into distinct cohorts and legions (H).

Just as one may find Principalities, Archangels, and Angels of a benevolent condition in the Empyrean Heaven, so indeed **Lucifer**, once cast down from that throne with his angels, has similar ministers under him, distinct in order and dignity. We have this confirmed even by the Apostle, whose authority is this: *Put on (he says) the armor of God, that you may be able to stand against the snares of the Devil, because our struggle is not against flesh and blood, but against Principalities and powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places, etc. Ephesians 6:12.* By these words he clearly teaches that the Devil, as the supreme king and emperor of wickedness and malignancy, has under him his own ministers eminent in condition, whom the Apostle calls "Principalities and powers," "rulers of the darkness of the world," and "spiritual wickedness." Hence also the said Apostle says elsewhere: *You walked according to the age of this world,*

From these testimonies of the wise, therefore, we gather what the Sacred Scriptures understood by this supreme king of the <term>Cacodemons</term> <note>Evil spirits.</note> in those places already cited by us: *God will come from the South, his glory has covered the heavens, and the earth is full of his praise; his brightness shall be as the light, there his strength is hidden; death shall go before his face, and the Devil shall go forth before his feet.* <note>Habakkuk 3:3-5. And hence it is that this commander of the dark air is deservedly called *Meririm*, or the demon scorching in the south, by whose malignant blasts the entire region of the elements is intoxicated and contaminated whenever God permits: and he is also called **Satan** by the Holy Bible and by the <term>Cabalists</term> <note>Followers of Kabbalah, a tradition of Jewish mysticism that influenced Western occultism.</note>.

It is a dogma of the Cabalists that every one of the prefects of the good angels is a great prince, and possesses immense power over the demons subjected to them—whether they be overseers of the stars of the Zodiac, or of the wandering stars [planets], or of the cardinal points of the world, the winds, and the Elements. This liberty and power is assigned to them at certain fixed times, years, months, days, and hours within the quarters of the world, the winds, and the elements. Both the royal Cacodemons and the princes of the good angels have dominion over the Cardinal Points, the Winds, and the Elements of the world, inasmuch as it is their task to present and execute the severe commands of God the Creator upon these lower things. In exactly the same way, the principal Good Angels are accustomed to act toward creatures kindly and according to divine mercy. Therefore, according to the doctrine of the Cabalists and Hebrew doctors, just as four leaders are recounted in the army of God who preside over the Cardinal points of the world, its winds, and the four Elements in the world—namely, **Michael, Gabriel, Uriel, and Raphael**, who are accustomed to govern all things in the sublunary world kindly through their good legions, with God having pity on His creatures—so, by a contrary reasoning, in the army of Satan, four standard-bearers of vengeance are said to carry the sails [of destruction]: namely, **Samael, Azazel, Azael, and Mahazael** (whom others call *Oriens, Amaymon, Paymon, and Egyn*). These are kings and prefects over the evils of corruption and death, just as the four aforementioned royal good angels are most opposed to them by nature and office. But truly, since the mercy of God is said in sacred letters to excel His severity, the Creator has indeed assigned greater power and virtue to His good Princes than to His malignant ministers; indeed, He has given them dominion over those malignant and devastating spirits or angels. This is also excellently denoted by these words in the 7th chapter of the Apocalypse: *I saw four Angels standing over the four angels of the earth, holding the four winds of the earth.*

And I saw another angel ascending from the rising of the Sun, having the seal of the living God, and he cried with a loud voice to the four Angels to whom it was given to hurt the earth and the sea, saying: Do not hurt the earth, nor the sea, nor the trees, until we have signed the servants of our God in their foreheads. <note>original: "Et vidi alterum angelum..." from Revelation 7:2-3.</note> From these words, it is clearer than light that we must conclude, first, that there are four royal angels whose commands are assigned to the four corners or hinges of the world, and also the powers of the winds blowing from them; secondly, that these royal <term>Cacodemons</term> <note>Evil spirits; from the Greek 'kakos' (evil) and 'daimon' (spirit).</note> are malignant and harmful, as it is in their power to hurt and affect with evil the earth, the sea, and the creatures within them; and finally, that these are subjected to the command of a good angel, because he himself commands and they offer obedience. ## On the Efficient Cause of Meteors. <note>In the early modern period, "meteors" referred to all atmospheric phenomena, including rain, wind, lightning, and even spiritual entities inhabiting the air.</note>

->Ff 2<-

...of the power of this air, etc. *Ephesians 6.* <note>The author likely refers to Ephesians 2:2 and 6:12 regarding the "Prince of the power of the air" and "spiritual wickedness in high places."</note> by which he means Satan, who is the prince or emperor of the air. Under his empire are (according to the teaching of the **Hebrew Doctors**) four kings or standard-bearers, who are said to carry the wide sails of Satan—namely, those kings cited previously. Along with their leaders, the Apostle calls them in another place *Princes, Powers, and lords of darkness in this world.* <note>original: "Principes, Potestates, & dominos tenebrarum, in hoc mundo, Ephes. 2. 2."</note> Under their command are legions of a fourfold condition, according to the four <term>triplicities</term> <note>In astrology, a triplicity is a group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element (Fire, Earth, Air, or Water).</note> of the Zodiac. For each of these there are three Princes; for example, in the **Fiery Triplicity**, there are the overseers of **Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius**. Their influences in the elementary kingdom are committed to the custody of **Samael** <note>In Jewish lore, a prominent archangel often associated with severity or the accuser.</note> if they are ill-disposed, or **Michael** if they are well-disposed.

It is for this reason that our Savior, following the twelve overseers of the celestial signs, makes mention of legions of angels, saying: *Do you think that I cannot ask my Father, and he will even now send me more than twelve legions of angels? Matthew 26:53.* We have spoken previously of these twelve overseers of the signs and the lords of the four triplicities, which are related to the gates of the heavenly city—namely, three in the East, and just as many in the West, and also in the South and North, along with the angels who are their guardians. By a similar logic, the wicked angels are also organized into legions. Thus, when Christ asked the demon, *What is your name? he answered, My name is Legion, for we are many.* <note>Mark 5:9.</note> From this we can observe that the substance of a demon is very minute, like a **solar atom** <note>original: "atomus solaris"; this refers to a mote of dust visible in a sunbeam, considered the smallest possible physical particle.</note>, and consequently, there is an infinite multitude of demons flying everywhere in the air. 

This is also confirmed by the express words of the **Hebrew Doctors**, whose opinion is that from the earth all the way to the <term>firmament</term> <note>The sphere of the sky or the heavens.</note> there is no empty space, but everything is full of forms. Some of these are pure and capable of grace, while below there are many foul, harmful, and tempting images dwelling and flying in the air. Similarly, in the *Gate of Light* <note>original: "Porta lucis"; referring to the *Sha'are Orah*, a major Kabbalistic work by Joseph Gikatilla.</note> it is held that there is no empty space from the earth to the firmament, but that it is entirely filled with species—some for war, some for peace, some for good, some for evil, some for life, and some for death. All this is in the lower habitation in which we dwell, as **Joseph Castaliensis** <note>A Latinized name for the author of the *Gate of Light*, Joseph Gikatilla.</note> reports. From this, it is evident to us that there is an infinite number of demons, both bad and good, in this elementary region where we breathe. Some are from the region of the East, some of a Southern nature, some Western, and others Northern, according to the quarters of the world and also the triplicity whose temperament and condition they share.

Furthermore, they are named after the nature of the planet by whose influences they are chiefly animated and quickened: some are called **Saturnine**, others **Jovial** (of Jupiter), **Martial** (of Mars), **Solar**, **Venereal** (of Venus), **Mercurial**, and **Lunar**. These are subjects of the Angels or Intelligences presiding over those planets. Thus it happens that when Saturn is predominant in the horoscope or celestial scheme, because of its copious influences at that time, the spirits in the elements that share in its nature tend to predominate, and so it is with the others.

Finally, each of these is called by a general name based on the element in which they naturally participate, and in which they commonly and most willingly live as if in their own homeland. In this, many who are most skilled in the mysteries of demons agree. For first, the **Cabalists** and **Hebrew Doctors** say that the demons are squalid and most foul enemies to the human race; hence, in contrast to the good angels, they are called **Angels of opposing strength**. However, they admit that some of these wander through the highest region of the air, and these they call **igneous** (fiery); those who are accustomed to wander closer to us they call **aerial**; those who terrify the land they call **terrestrial**; those who inhabit lakes and rivers and often shake the sea they call **aqueous**; and finally, those they call light-shunning and dark, they place underground as **subterranean**. **Psellus** <note>Michael Psellus, an 11th-century Byzantine scholar whose work *On the Operation of Demons* was highly influential in the Renaissance.</note> seems to confirm this from the confession of Marcus, saying that only six kinds of these demons are found in the elementary region.

<image-desc>A large curly bracket on the left groups the word "Of which" with the following six numbered points.</image-desc>

**Of which:**
1. The first is **fiery**, which is seen to wander about the high region of the air.
2. The second is **aerial**, which wanders near to us.
3. The third is **aquatic**, which immerses itself in moisture, namely in lakes, ponds, rivers, and the sea.
4. The fourth is **terrestrial**, which for the most part is occupied around the earth.
5. The fifth is **subterranean**, which is accustomed to dwell under the earth.
6. The sixth and last is **light-shunning**, inscrutable, and dark.

These kinds of <term>Cacodemons</term> <note>Evil spirits.</note> are said to hold God, the Angels, and even humans in hatred. We shall soon speak more widely of their properties and conditions.

Section I. Portion IV. Part II. Book IV. Member II.

### *On the evil Demons concerned with the human spirit.*

->Evil demons <term>Cacodæmons</term> <note>From the Greek 'kakos' (evil) and 'daimon' (spirit).</note> who concern themselves with the human spirit are distinguished into eight ranks, of which:<-

1. The **First** infects with Idolatry and vain or false worship, and lures one to the adoration of himself.
2. The **Second** contaminates with lies, deceives with false whispers, and leads into error.
3. The **Third** inflames with anger and fury, and invents arts to kindle various passions in them.
4. The **Fourth** fills with revenge, vengeance, and cruelty.
5. The **Fifth** deludes with illusions and false miracles.
6. The **Sixth** ignites with the discord of wars and the heat of devastations.
7. The **Seventh** slanders, explores, and accuses before the sight of God.
8. The **Eighth** casts one into errors and danger through temptations and snares, and stains with despair. <note>original: "in sex distinguuntur gradus" — The introductory text in the original Latin says 'six,' but the list clearly provides eight distinct ranks. This is likely a typographical error in the 17th-century printing.</note>

---

The first rank of evil demons <term>Cacodæmons</term> infesting the human spirit with Idolatry is the order of those who are called <term>pseudothei</term>, <note>original: "pseudothei" — Greek for 'false gods.'</note> that is, false GODS; for it is their nature to falsely attribute the name of GOD to themselves, and to entice the human spirit toward their own cult and adoration through false and deceptive demonstrations. The prince of these is thought to be **Beelzebub**, that is, the ancient God, <note>original: "vetustus Deus" — While Beelzebub is traditionally 'Lord of the Flies,' the author here interprets the name as 'Ancient God' to signify his long-standing deception of humanity.</note> who is so bold that he did not hesitate to tempt the spirit of the Savior of the world himself by saying, *if you will fall down on the ground and worship me, I will give you all these things. Matthew 4.* Of this rank also were the Gods of the Midianites, who, through the daughters of Moab (with whom the people of Israel committed fornication), seduced that people from the worship of the true God, and persuaded them to adore them and to immolate sacrifices or burnt offerings. *Numbers 25.* Such also was the spirit of the Oracles, namely of the Delphic Apollo, etc.

The second rank encompasses those who are accustomed to introduce and whisper falsehoods into the spirits of men; and of this order was that lying spirit which, by divine command, entered into the mouths of the Prophets of Ahab: *1 Kings 22.* Similarly, that spirit which strikes terror and dread into the spirits of men, of whom it is written: *Behold, I will put a spirit in him, so that when he hears a rumor, he shall return to his own land. 2 Kings 19.* Furthermore, the prince of this order is called by those skilled in magic **Python**, that is, the serpent.

The third rank consists of those who, through the love of iniquity and the flame of anger and fury, set the human spirit on fire; and so that they may more easily perform this duty, they invent games, such as cards, dice, and other such things by which they move men to passion and anger. Such was that demon named **Theuth**, <note>original: "Theutus" — Referring to the Egyptian god Thoth, whom Plato mentions in the *Phaedrus* as the inventor of dice and games of chance.</note> whom Plato says is the master of games, specifically of dice; the Hebrews establish the prince of these as **Belial**: which is interpreted as "without a yoke," disobedient, a transgressor, etc.

The fourth rank or order is that which not only drives the human spirit toward revenge and vengeance, but also has itself become the author of Divine vengeance. The royal Psalmist seems to show a precaution against the invasions of a demon of this sort into the human spirit with this speech: *Refrain from anger, and forsake burning wrath, lest you be incited to do evil; for evildoers shall be cut off. Psalm 37:8.* And the wise man says, *Be not hasty in your spirit to be angry, for anger rests in the bosom of fools. Ecclesiastes 7.* And elsewhere, *Make no friendship with an angry man, and with a furious man do not go. Proverbs 22:24.* Furthermore, that he is an avenger and a minister carrying out God's vengeance is indicated by this passage cited from Holy Scripture; where a demon of this kind is called, *The spirit of the power of God, winnowing and pursuing the unjust with justice. Wisdom 11:21.* And concerning him elsewhere: *the spirit of power and the spirit of virtue shall stand against them. Wisdom 5:24.* The Kabbalists and Mages make the prince of these **Asmodeus**, <note>In Jewish apocryphal texts like the Book of Tobit, Asmodeus is a powerful demon of lust and wrath; here the author derives the name from a Hebrew root suggesting one who executes judgment or 'justice.'</note> that is, "the one executing justice."

The fifth rank is of those who delude with illusions and false miracles; the magicians of the Egyptians required their assistance when, attempting a feat against Moses, they produced so many deceptive miracles in the presence of Pharaoh. The <term>cacomagi</term> <note>Evil sorcerers or practitioners of 'black' magic.</note> and poisoners implore such aids in their business. Finally, the mages themselves affirm the Prince of these to be **Satan**, of whom it is said in the Apocalypse that he seduces the whole world, performing great signs, and making fire descend from heaven to earth in the sight of men, so that he may seduce those dwelling upon it.

<meta>catchword: Sixth</meta>

<header>On the Efficient Cause of Meteors.</header>

The **sixth rank** is said to sow discord, devastation, and longing through the human spirit; the Prince of these is called *Apollyon* <note>original: "Apollyon" — Greek for 'Destroyer.'</note> in the Apocalypse, and *Abaddon* by the Hebrews, which is to say, the exterminating and wasting one. To this order also belonged that Angel standing between heaven and earth, whom Jehovah sent to destroy and lay waste to Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 21:15). And also he who slew every man of valor in the camp of the King of Assyria (2 Chronicles 32).

The **seventh** is accustomed to slander, spy upon, and accuse spirits in the presence of Jehovah: the magi call this one *Astaroth*, that is, the "searcher" or "scout," and in Greek *Diabolos*, <note>original: "Diabolum" — The root of the word 'Devil,' meaning an accuser or slanderer.</note> which is to say, the slanderer and calumniator.

The **last** rank attempts to deceive the human spirit with temptations and snares, leading it into error and despair; the Prince of such demons is said to be *Mammon*, whom they interpret as "Cupidity" or "Greed."

## On the Demons acting evilly concerning the spirit and bodily members of the Macrocosm. <note>The 'Macrocosm' refers to the universe or the world at large, viewed as a reflection of the 'Microcosm,' which is man.</note>

->By divine will, Demons sometimes act malignantly toward the bodies and spirits of the sublunary macrocosm, <note>The 'sublunary' realm refers to the earth and atmosphere, everything 'below the moon' where change and decay occur.</note> resulting in:<-

| Realm | Effects |
| :--- | :--- |
| **In the Dense Air** | Inflammation from lightning, turbulence of winds, thick fogs and vapors, and the redness of evening. |
| **In the Cloud** | Burning fire and cinders, dark gloom, and the falling of hail, snow, and thunder. |
| **In the Sea** | Disturbance of the waters, the rising and falling of waves, and the internal agitation of the sea-spirit. |
| **In the Earth** | Tremors and concussions, destructive fire sent from the heavens, the opening of chasms and fissures, floods, and periods of dryness or sterility. |

The schools of Theologians recognize that the sixth rank of evil demons <term>Cacodæmons</term>, according to their own division, consists of those who are the "powers of the air." However, we include all the aforementioned ranks within this order, since we do not intend to define a separate species that is not already contained under one of the aforementioned winds, the Cardinal governors of the world, or the four Elements. But because all these demons are powers of the air itself, or sublunary spirits, we therefore say that the remaining evil spirits—whether they concern themselves with humanity or any other thing in the world—are included under their command. 

The school of Theologians thus acknowledges that these aerial powers mingle themselves with thunder, lightning-bolts, and flashes, corrupting the air and bringing about pestilences and other evils. The Apocalypse seems to affirm that the Princes of these are those four angels holding the four winds, in whose power it is to harm the sea and the earth. Their Prince is identified as *Meririm*, <note>original: "Meririm" — A name often associated in occult tradition with the 'Prince of the Power of the Air' mentioned by St. Paul.</note> that is, the "boiling spirit" or the demon who rages at Midday. <note>This likely refers to the "destruction that wastes at noonday" mentioned in Psalm 91:6.</note> 

But Paul calls him the "Prince of the power of this air," who works in the children of disobedience. And a certain wise man, profound in the mysteries of God and nature, speaks in his treatise *On the Revelation of Divine Majesty* in these words: 

*“Together with the air, God also created by His word angels and spirits, who perform and execute their duty and office in the air concerning the direction of storms, both evil and good: rain, snow, hail, frost, clouds, lightning, thunderbolts, thunder, the ceraunian stone <note>original: "lapis cerauneus" — Historically, this referred to 'thunderstones' or meteorites believed to fall during storms.</note>, fire, atmospheric chasms <note>original: "chasmatum" — Refers to 'chasms' or openings in the sky, a term used in older meteorology to describe certain light phenomena or aurorae.</note>, comets, the flooding of waters, heat, cold, humidity, dryness, and many other things of that kind; and this very thing still happens even today through His word. Concerning all these things, those secular 'wise men' or philosophers write books for themselves that are wonderfully inept, in which not even a single point, much less a whole letter, is true. Rather, whatever has flowed from their brains into the pen and onto the paper is all that can be read in them—which is nothing other than pure, unadulterated lies. Indeed, even the spirit of the mouth in those 'wise men' is entirely lying and false; yet they still wish to be called wise. This happens solely because they know neither God nor His most holy word, etc.”* So he says.

<meta>This page continues the discussion on how spiritual entities affect the material world. ### Section I, Portion IV, Part II. Book IV. Member II.

Just as the lowest region of the Macrocosm is subject to various passions and changes, so too is its "aerial spirit" <note>The 'aerial spirit' refers to the subtle, invisible medium of the atmosphere that was thought to connect the physical and spiritual realms.</note> observed to be divided into various degrees of physicality. Before any specific degree is reached, both the external body and its internal spirit are afflicted and agitated by the angelic spirits or ministers of God—namely, those that act as winds and those that act as burning flames. For David confessed that "God makes his angels winds, and his ministers a burning fire" (Psalm 104:4) <note>original: "faciat angelos suos ventos, & ministros suos ignem vrentem"</note>. And in the preceding psalm: "That the angels of God, most mighty in strength, carry out the word of God, listening to the voice of His command, and that they are the armies and ministers of God doing His pleasure" (Psalm 103:20). In this speech of the Royal Psalmist, we are taught that there are three primary orders of angels: the first and superior order, receiving the divine efflux immediately from God, is accustomed to "carry out"—that is, to receive and emit—the word of God; the second "listens to" and pays attention to that word which is issued by the Supreme Commander, and then commits that mandate to the legion assigned to its dominion for execution; the third order is that which immediately "does" and executes the pleasure of the Creator.

Recent theologians also seem to admit this same point: namely, that the superior orders of Angels receive light or emanation immediately from God, which they afterwards impart and communicate to the lower orders by flowing into them.

God uses some of these Angels to execute the effects of His wrath and vengeance; these we call malignant and <term>cacodemons</term> <note>From the Greek 'kakos' (evil) and 'daimon' (spirit); refers to spirits that cause harm, though the author notes they are still servants of the divine will.</note> in respect to us, though they are nonetheless necessary ministers of God. Thus God used Satan as His minister to tempt Job. So too was that destroying Angel of Jehovah, whom David saw with eyes raised, standing between heaven and earth with his sword drawn in his hand and extended against Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 21). And also that one whom Jehovah sent to cut down every man of valor in the camp of the King of the Assyrians (2 Chronicles 32). Such also was that evil spirit of Jehovah that beset Saul, and so forth. Some He also uses in His kindness, who are called good and benevolent spirits; such was the Angel who appeared to Elijah in the desert and offered him food, and the one whom God sent before Moses and the Israelites to keep them on their journey through the desert (Exodus 33). And that Angel who redeemed Jacob from all evil (Genesis 48). And the angels who met him on his journey (Genesis 32). Finally, all those angels whom God sends before the righteous (Genesis 24:7). Similarly, by the ministry of good angels, the spirit of the Macrocosm is governed kindly and peacefully, just as it is disturbed by the dominance of tumultuous spirits, and even sublunary bodies <note>Objects or beings existing below the moon, i.e., on Earth.</note> are seen to fall ill.

The first "incorporation" <note>The process by which a spirit takes on a more physical form.</note> that occurs between the simple air and a perfectly mixed body is "habitual" or misty air. In this air, various preternatural impressions are produced by evil spirits: namely, inflammation from a <term>prester</term> <note>A 'prester' (from Greek 'prethein', to burn) was a classical term for a fiery whirlwind or a lightning strike accompanied by a powerful blast of wind.</note> and flashes of lightning, disturbance from winds and whirlwinds, gloom from mists and thick vapors, evening redness, and so on. Regarding the intemperance of the air caused by a prester, the Holy Scripture speaks thus: "Behold, a whirlwind came out of the North, and a great cloud, and a fire infolding itself, and a brightness was about it, and out of the midst of the fire as it were the appearance of amber, and out of the midst thereof the likeness of living creatures and a spirit in four wheels," etc. (Ezekiel 1). By these things the Prophet wishes to suggest that the soul of both that cloud and that prester was that spirit—or rather the driver of that chariot—and that the Lord who was carried in it was Jehovah Himself, as we can gather from that entire chapter. And Isaiah says: "He shall be visited by the Lord of Hosts with thunder, and with earthquake, and great noise, with storm and tempest, and the flame of devouring fire" (Isaiah 29:6). And Jeremiah says: "Behold, the whirlwind of the Lord goes forth in fury, a falling tempest; it shall rest upon the head of the wicked" (Jeremiah 30:23). And the Royal Psalmist: "Upon the wicked he shall rain coals, fire, and brimstone, joined with a stormy whirlwind" (Psalm 11:6). And elsewhere: "As the fire burns a wood, and as the flame sets the mountains on fire, so persecute them with thy tempest, and make them afraid with thy storm" (Psalm 83:15). And of the whirlwind, Isaiah says it comes from the South (Isaiah 21:1). And Zechariah: "The Lord God shall blow the trumpet, and shall go with whirlwinds of the south" (Zechariah 9:14). And Job says: "Out of the south comes the whirlwind: and cold from the scatterers" (Job 37:9)—that is, from the spirits or demons who, by their blowing, do the will of God from the North. We conclude, therefore, that its internal part is the stormy spirit of God, executing the word and will of God, as the Prophet David recognizes. Whence the wise man says: "The spirit of the power of God shall stand against the impious, and like a whirlwind shall scatter them" (Wisdom 5).

Furthermore, clouds are the vehicles of God which are carried and animated, and by violent motion are seen to be borne in the air and preternaturally disturbed by the angels of God and His presence. In His presence, angelic ministers always stand and assist; hence the Prophet says: "He ascended upon the Cherubim, and flew upon the wings of the winds; He made darkness His secret place; round about Him His pavilion was dark waters and thick clouds of the skies. At the brightness that was before Him His thick clouds passed, hail stones and coals of fire. The Lord also thundered in the heavens, and the Highest gave His voice; hail stones and coals of fire. Yea, He sent out His arrows, multiplied lightnings, and discomfited them" (Psalm 18:10-14). In this speech, the Prophet clearly teaches that the ministers of the Lord are the Cherubim and the winds—as if he had said, the angels listening to His voice, and the winds or angelic spirits, the fiery ministers executing His pleasure, as he confesses elsewhere. And elsewhere he says: "The waters saw thee and were afraid; the depths also were troubled. The multitude of the sound of the waters gave a voice; the clouds sent out a sound: thine arrows also went abroad. The voice of thy thunder was in the wheel; thy lightnings lightened the world: the earth trembled and shook" (Psalm 77:16-18). And elsewhere: "The waters shall be afraid at the voice of thy thunder" (Psalm 104:7). Finally, in even more express words, David reveals all this in the following: "God, clothed with light as with a garment, stretching out the heavens like a skin: who lays the beams of His chambers in the waters: who makes the clouds His chariot: who walks upon the wings of the wind: who makes His angels spirits, and His ministers..."

<meta>This page continues the exploration of how divine and angelic agencies govern the natural world. Having previously discussed the "aerial spirit" and the higher angelic orders, the text now moves through the specific elements—Air, Water, and Earth—explaining how both benevolent and malevolent spirits act as the "efficient causes" of weather, storms, and geological disasters according to the will of God.</meta>

# On the Efficient Cause of Meteors. <note>In the 17th century, "meteors" referred to any atmospheric phenomenon, including rain, wind, lightning, and rainbows, not just falling stars.</note>

...your ministers a burning fire; the Deep is like a garment of his clothing; the waters shall stand above the mountains; at your rebuke they shall flee; at the voice of your thunder they shall be afraid (Psalm 104:2-7). By these words, it seems argued that Jehovah is the prince and supreme commander who has his tabernacle in the clouds, whom both fiery and windy angels serve; it appears that the clouds are thrown into confusion, fear, and roar at the sight of his splendor, and finally, that they behave in a preternatural manner. The third step of progression from the invisible nature of the air to a perfectly mixed body is water, the primary element of which is the sea. This sea, along with rivers and lakes, is either rendered peaceful by the good spirit of Jehovah or is disturbed by the evil spirit of Jehovah and stirred up to the harm of sailors. Hence the Royal Psalmist says: *You break the ships of the ocean with the East wind* (Psalm 48:8) <note>original: "Oceani naues perfringis Euro"</note>; that is, by a vehement blast sent by Samael <note>Samael is often identified in post-biblical Jewish lore as an archangel of fury or the "Poison of God," here associated with the harsh East wind.</note> or the east by divine will. And elsewhere: *You who disturb the depths of the sea* (Psalm 65). And elsewhere he acknowledges that the sea is stirred up by the rebuke of Jehovah, and that the sea, seeing Jehovah, fled (Psalm 114:3). And Job says: *By his power the sea grows quiet, and by his understanding he strikes down pride* (Job 26:12). By this, one may see that it belongs to God both to disturb and to render quiet the sea, or the element of water. But the Royal Prophet also expresses this most excellently and indeed in very clear words elsewhere, saying: *Those who go down to the sea in ships, they see the works of Jehovah and his wonders in the deep; for he speaks and makes the spirit of the whirlwind blow, and lifts up its waves; they mount up to the heaven, they go down again to the depths, so that their soul melts in trouble; they toss and reel like a drunkard, so that all their wisdom is swallowed up. Then they cry to Jehovah in their distress, and he leads them out of their troubles; he makes the storm a silence, and their waves are still; they celebrate the mercy of Jehovah and preach his wonders to the sons of men* (Psalm 107:23–31). Here, therefore, you see primarily that Jehovah is the commander of all powers and the first actor and operator of all things; secondly, that in his severity, he deals severely with the elements of the world because of the sins of men; and then afterward, that he acts through his angelic ministers, who are always ready—according to their own office, whether good or evil—to fulfill the commands and pleasure of the Divine. For he says: *And he makes the spirit of the whirlwind blow.* But at the repentance and cries of men for mercy, he makes the tumultuous storm stand still. This spirit of the whirlwind is an angelic wind, executing the severity of God upon the sea. At Jehovah's command, this spirit acts upon the internal spirit of the seas and lakes in an insane, tumultuous, and furious manner—not unlike how that evil spirit of Jehovah acted upon the internal aerial spirit of Saul himself, or how the demon called "Legion" acted in the possessed man (who, being cast out by the power of Jesus, entered into the pigs), or as seen in those vexed by the worst epilepsy (who swell up greatly and cast foam from the mouth), or in those affected by that rabid disease called Lycanthropy <note>term: Lycanthropy/Werewolfism. Here used to describe a state of violent, animalistic madness.</note>, who are tossed and carried here and there in a violent manner. Thus does that violent spirit act with his legions in the sea, lakes, ponds, and so forth.

Finally, since the earth is the thicker part of water, we have now arrived at it; we say that it too is sometimes tossed and struck by the evil spirits of God. Hence the Sacred Page says: *The earth shook and trembled, the foundations of the heavens were moved; it was shaken because his anger was kindled against it* (2 Samuel 22:8). And elsewhere: *God shakes the earth out of its place, so that its columns tremble; he transfers the mountains* (Job 9:5). And elsewhere: *At God's look the earth trembled, and at his touch the mountains smoke* (Psalm 104:32). But truly, in such an act of God, he himself uses spiritual ministers destined for that work, who, at the command of the angelic prefect, shake the earth, produce vast chasms in it, vomit fires from its bowels, and are accustomed to perform many other terrible things on the earth. Hence also, when God was angry because of the impiety of the Jews, it was said: *Behold, there was a great earthquake, for an angel of the Lord descended from heaven, and his appearance was like lightning, etc.* (Matthew 28:2). Sometimes also, through his avenging angels, Jehovah sends down fire and sulfur upon the earth, by which it is subverted and treated preternaturally. *And Jehovah* (says Genesis) *rained upon Sodom and Gomorrah sulfur and fire from the heavens, and he overthrew the city and the entire plain, and all the inhabitants, and the growth of the ground, etc.* (Genesis 19:24). But that Jehovah used his angels in such a business is explained in that very context. And elsewhere it is said: *The land is burnt with salt and sulfur, so that it cannot be sown nor sprout, nor can any herb grow in it, etc.* (Deuteronomy 29:23). This indeed Jehovah produced for the inhabitants of the earth through the mediation of his ministers because of their sins. And elsewhere: *Jehovah shall make the rain of your land powder, or dust shall descend from the heavens upon you until you are destroyed* (Deuteronomy 28:24). Furthermore, in another place the Psalmist says: *He turns a fruitful land into saltiness because of the wickedness of those who dwell in it; on the contrary, he turns a desert into a pool of water and a parched land into water-springs, etc.* By which he seems to argue that in his severity, God renders the land dry and sterile just as much as he suffocates it with an excessive flood of waters because of the sins of men; which he himself is said to do through his ministers by the Cabalists <note>The Cabalists were practitioners of Jewish mysticism (Kabbalah), whose ideas about the hierarchy of angels were influential in Renaissance occult philosophy.</note> and those well-versed in the deeper mysteries of God.

For just as they have assigned angelic prefects to the elements—namely, Seruph to fire, Cherub to air, Tharsis to water, and Ariel to earth, who are good leaders—so indeed under them act four malevolent spirits: namely, Samael from the fiery part, Azazel from the aerial part, Azael from the aquatic part, and Mahazael from the earthy part. Under their command (as was said before) are many orders of inferior demons. Therefore, both fiery and bright tempests with such comets proceed from the fiery angels; likewise, aerial impressions come from the aerial angels, as do those things which disturb the waters from the aquatic ones; and it belongs to the earthy spirits, as Psellus <note>Michael Psellos (11th century), a Byzantine philosopher and historian whose work on demons was widely cited in the Renaissance.</note> testifies, to cause chasms in the earth, to shake foundations, and to send up flame-breathing winds.

There is no doubt that the **Evil Spirits** <note>original: "Cacodæmones"</note>, as they are deadly enemies to mankind, afflict the human spirit and body in the same way they afflict the spirit, water, and earth in the **Macrocosm** <note>The "Great World" or the universe at large.</note>. For since man is the "son" of the world in terms of his composition, and since he is also considered the end-goal of all creatures, it follows that these wicked demons are ordained by God for the punishment of sinning humans, just as good angels are ordained for obedience, protection, and prosperity. However, all these spirits, being ministers of God ordained for the punishment of the world and of men, are able to achieve nothing unless it is permitted to them by God. This is clearly shown by the example of Job (*Job 1-2*) and the demoniac whom Christ liberated (*Matthew 8:31*). Hence the demons said to Christ, *If you cast us out from here, send us into the herd of swine*, and He said, *Go.*

Therefore, when God curses a man or a people, then these destroying angels are ready to carry out the will of God. In this way, when God cursed the people for the sin of **David**, the destroying angel was immediately at hand to destroy Jerusalem (*1 Chronicles 21*). Furthermore, at the word of **Jehovah**, the angel was ready in a moment and cut down everyone of great strength in the Assyrian camp—namely 185,000 men (*2 Kings 19*). Thus we see that the immediate inflictor of the plague is the destroying angel of God, who is also called the "Waster" and the "Exterminator" in other places.

Yet truly, just as human sin is the occasion for disease and death, so the devil is not only ready to inflict evil, but he also typically invites man to sin with secret allurements so that he may be admitted to such a duty and execution. For **Evil Spirits** of this kind, and especially those of an aerial nature, are easily able to work themselves in through secret whisperings because their composition is familiar to our own external or "aerial" spirit. They impel the human **phantastic sense** <note>The faculty of the mind responsible for imagination and forming mental images.</note> and incite it toward that which will seem evil in the eyes of God, so that afterward the spirit may have power over the man's aerial spirit and body. For he cannot penetrate into the "human heaven" (which is the temple of the Holy Spirit), because he is an exile from heaven. **Adam** mourned this cunning of the devil too late; led by the allurements of the serpent, he fell from heaven into the sphere of sin. Indeed, even the Royal Prophet [David], however wise and sublime of mind, could not safely escape the devil's deceits, but was caught in his snares; as a result, not only he but the entire people were vexed by the plague for that same sin. Do we not read this in express words in the Holy Page? Namely, that the Devil incited David to count the people of Israel, so that by this...

# On the Efficient Cause of Meteors <note>In the early modern period, "meteors" referred to any atmospheric phenomena, including the "vapors" and "spirits" within the human body that were thought to cause disease.</note>

## Gg
<meta>catchword: For</meta>

In this way, He brought a plague upon him: *1 Chronicles 21.* However, even when a human sins, it is not within the power of the destroying angel to afflict him with evil unless **God**, setting aside His mercy and putting on the cloak of severity, has said "let it be" or "I shall strike." Thus, in Exodus, we have this pronounced by **God**: *I am about to send all my plagues upon your heart, and upon your servants, and upon your people in all the earth, Exodus 9:14.* And elsewhere: *The Lord will make the pestilence cling to you, and the Lord will strike you with consumption, and with a burning fever, and with inflammation, and with extreme burning, and with drought, and with blight, and with jaundice <note>original: "morbo regio," literally "the royal disease," a historical term for jaundice</note>, which shall pursue you until you perish. And the Lord will strike you with the boils of Egypt, and with tumors, and with scab, and with an itch, of which you cannot be healed. And the Lord will strike you with madness, and blindness, and astonishment of heart, so that you shall grope at midday just as a blind man gropes in darkness. And he will strike you with malignant boils in the legs and knees, so that you cannot be healed, Deuteronomy 28.*

Once these things are pronounced by **God**, the evil angel is prepared like a "let it be" with his subordinates to carry out what **God** has spoken. Thus, indeed, it is said that the devil struck Job with terrible boils from the sole of his foot to the crown of his head: *Job 2.* And yet Job, in this adversity of his, said: *the arrows of the Almighty are within me, the poison whereof drinks up my spirit; the terrors of God set in array against me do oppress me, etc.* And elsewhere: *You have lifted me up to the wind; you have caused me to dissolve in substance: Job 30.* By these examples, therefore, one may see that where the destroying angel is permitted to afflict a person with disease, that entire work—though performed through an intermediary minister—is ascribed to God, who afflicts with disease through evil angels, just as, conversely, He restores health through good ones.

However, evil angels do not afflict with disease, nor do good ones bless a person with health, of their own accord; rather, both health and disease come from **God** through the angels. From this it follows: *If you diligently listen to the voice of the Lord your God and do what is right in my eyes, I will put none of the diseases upon you which I brought upon the Egyptians, for I, the Lord, shall be your creator <note>original: "creator tuus," here implying the one who sustains or restores your nature</note>, etc.*

This means: I will bring it about and command that good angels—such as **Raphael** <note>The name Raphael means "God heals" in Hebrew</note>—with their angels, shall cure you, or I will send my word through an angel, etc. Hence, *Raphael* is as if we were to say "God healing."

We conclude, therefore, that it is **God** who strikes and who heals, but He does this through His ministering angels, whose role it is to do His pleasure. Thus, there is no evil demon who can strike without the permission of the good ones, nor can a good angel grant permission or cease his protection (for everyone has their own good guardian angel) except at God’s command. Mention of these types of spirits, contrary in their condition, is made where it is said: *that the good spirit of the Lord departed from Saul, and an evil spirit from the Lord troubled him. Wherefore his servants said: Behold now, an evil spirit of God troubles you, 1 Samuel 16:15.* So it is also manifest that evil angels, or **demons** <note>original: "Cacodæmones," meaning "bad spirits"</note>, are the instrument of **God** in His severity, just as the good are in His mercy. David also confesses this in this clear speech: *he cast upon them the fierceness of his anger, wrath, and indignation, and trouble, by sending evil angels among them. For he struck all the firstborn, and spared not their animals from death, etc. Psalm 78:49.* From these it is sufficiently clear that although Moses speaks of "the destroyer" or a destroying angel, nevertheless many angels or demons were assisting in that work. **Artesius** <note>Likely referring to a medieval medical or alchemical authority</note> declares the fitness of demons by which they have power over humans abandoned by **God** in these words: "There are certain infirmities in which the devil joins himself when a humor <note>The "humors" were the four bodily fluids: blood, phlegm, black bile, and yellow bile</note> departs from its proper temperament and disturbs health itself; and this happens most especially in infirmities arising from **cholera** <note>Yellow bile</note>. The cause of this is as follows: because the devil’s internal nature is fire, just as his external nature is air, he can easily be joined, God permitting, with the human air <note>The "vital spirits" or breath within the body</note>."

So says he. But it is the role of good angels to bind the elements in harmonious peace, seeing as they are children of concord. Therefore, when these angels vacate their office by divine will, it happens that the evil demons, who are the offspring of discord, suddenly invade and attempt to turn human harmony into dissonance. From this it is clear that demons, according to their elemental natures, are accustomed to procreate various diseases in the human body.

Hence **Albohali** <note>Abu Ali al-Khayyat, an 8th-century astrologer</note> says that **Melancholy** <note>A condition of excess black bile, often associated with depression or madness</note> is from a demon. And **Alzarabius** <note>Al-Zahrawi, a medieval physician</note> says that ailments invade humans from the transgressions and curses of demons who are called *Alhabinables*. And **Psellus** <note>Michael Psellos, a Byzantine philosopher who wrote on demonology</note>, from the revelation of Marcus, says that aerial spirits or demons bring harm to humans by approaching the **phantastic spirit** <note>The part of the soul responsible for imagination and mental imagery</note> that is within us, because of the similarity of their two natures. For in this way, words of disturbance and pleasure sound within us—not by emitting a voice through a physical stroke and sound, but by sending forth their speech without sound, whispering into the ear in a silent manner. They present various colors of the imagination according to their will, insofar as they are aerial, for air is capable of all colors. From this, the phantastic essence transmits figures and colors, and whatever forms they themselves wish, into our animal spirit. Thus they cause us much trouble, suggesting wills and plans, representing forms, stirring up memories of pleasures, and frequently inciting images of passions in those who are awake and asleep. Sometimes, by titillating our thighs and groins, they suggest and sharpen insane and wicked loves; these disturb the soul with a certain art and sophisticated fraud. But indeed, the watery and earthy demons do not devise anything wisely, nor do they perform anything with cunning, except that which is troublesome, and they hurt in the manner of **Charonean spirits** <note>Spirits of the underworld, named after Charon, the ferryman of the dead</note>. And it is the property of these to corrupt whatever they approach, whether it be a four-footed beast, a human, or a bird.

### Section I. Portion IV. Part II. Book IV. Member II.

These spirits suddenly cause harm and sometimes destroy by agitating the bodies and minds, perverting the natural faculties. They often kill both humans and beasts by fire, water, or by casting them over precipices. Such spirits do not attack humans and animals so much out of a mere will to do harm (though they are the most bitter enemies of mankind) as out of a greed for **life-giving heat**. This is especially true of those who dwell in deep, extremely cold, and dry places. Because they contract an immense coldness devoid of moisture, they crave the **moist and vital heat** of living things. To obtain this, they rush into irrational animals and fly toward lakes and pits; they flee the heat of the sun and fire because it is parching and burning, but they love animal heat, which is moderate and mixed with a sweet moisture—especially human heat, because it is more perfectly balanced. 

From this, it happens that when they invade bodies, they disturb them significantly by obstructing and filling those channels <note>The "channels" refer to the nerves, which early modern medicine believed were hollow tubes.</note> in which the <term>animal spirit<gloss>The "animal spirit" (spiritus animalis) was thought to be a very fine, subtle vapor that traveled through the nerves to facilitate movement and sensation; it is not "animalistic" but relates to the "anima" or soul.</gloss></term> resides. When the animal spirit is compressed by the density of these demonic bodies and shaken within, it follows that the limbs vibrate and are convulsed. Their primary faculties function poorly, and their movements become numb and erratic. If one of these invading demons is of the **subterranean** kind, it shakes and destroys the person it occupies, crying out through them, using the victim's spirit as if it were its own instrument. If it is a **light-shunning** spirit, it brings on a heavy lethargy, suppresses the voice, and makes the obsessed person appear as if dead; for this type is the most earthy of all others, and is exceedingly cold and dry. Thus, wherever it creeps in, it blunts, dulls, darkens, and destroys all the vital power of the soul.

Therefore, this kind is called **mute and deaf**, and it does not depart from the occupied person unless it is driven out by divine power—specifically through prayer and fasting. **Psellus** <note>Michael Psellus (c. 1017–1078) was a Byzantine philosopher and politician famous for his treatise on demonology.</note> learned these things from the observations of **Marcus**, who lived for a long time in the desert so that, through conversation with demons, he might learn their duties and properties.

We conclude, therefore, that demons are accustomed to inducing such diseases in nature and disposition as correspond to their own condition and quality among the elements; wherefore, **fiery** demons cause fiery diseases, **aerial** ones cause windy diseases, **watery** ones cause watery diseases, and **earthy** ones cause numb and terrestrial diseases. Yet sometimes they mingle together, and thus produce a "spurious" or hybrid disease, as will be explained more fully below.

**Evil demons <note>original: "Cacodaemones"</note> infect the spirit and body of both worlds <note>The Macrocosm (the universe) and the Microcosm (man)</note>, either by corrupting:**
- **The Air**, whether:
    - **Open**, namely that which moves everywhere through the region.
    - **Enclosed and exhaled**, whether from:
        - **A Meteor** <note>In this period, "meteor" referred to any atmospheric phenomenon.</note>:
            - **Fiery**, such as a comet.
            - **Watery**, such as a cloud.
        - **Water.**
        - **The Earth.**
- **The Water.**
- **The Earth.**

The schools of physicians acknowledge that when the mind or spirit is disturbed, the body is also disturbed, and vice versa. This is also a well-worn and proven fact in the **Macrocosm** <note>The greater world/universe.</note>: when the air of a place or region is corrupted, the water and earth are also corrupted, as are the creatures—especially the humans living there. In this, the Holy Scriptures agree, saying: *And the Lord shall strike you with corrupted air,* etc. And elsewhere: *The Lord shall strike you with poverty, fever, cold, heat and burning, corrupted air, and blight,* etc. **Deuteronomy 28:22**. And **Solomon**, in that place where he reveals the manner of curing diseases through prayer, speaks in these words: *If a pestilence or corrupted air has arisen, or mildew, or blight,* etc. **1 Kings 8:37** <note>original: "3. Reg. 8. 37," following the Vulgate numbering.</note>. From these, it is evident that it is granted to the ministers of God to corrupt the air, as it is their role to execute the Lord's ordinances. For they are accustomed to sow the seeds of contagion through the open air, which the Royal Prophet <note>King David</note> also seems to verify in this discourse: *Fear not the terror of the night, nor the arrow that flies by day, nor the plague that walks in the darkness or night, nor the destruction that wastes at noonday*—or, as **Jerome** interprets it, *from the noonday devil* <note>original: "dæmonio meridiano." This was a common medieval personification of sloth or sudden midday heatstroke.</note>—*the plague shall not come near your tent, for he shall give his angels charge over you, and keep you in all your ways,* etc. **Psalm 91**. From this discourse, it is clear first that the air is infected by the **noonday devil** and his legions, and second, that God appoints good angels to preserve men from the evil ones.

The School of Theologians seems to infer almost the same thing as the Prophet when they define the sixth rank of **Evil Spirits** as those who are called **aerial powers**. They mingle themselves with thunder, lightning, and bolts, and are reported to corrupt the air, and by this means induce pestilences and other evils.
