### On the Efficient Cause of Meteorological Phenomena

The Book of Revelation mentions those to whom it was given to harm the earth and the sea—that is, to infect the waters and the land. But as the primary king of these, they establish **Meririm**, who is the "midday demon," a burning spirit and a raging demon of the noon. Paul (as was said above) calls him the "prince of the power of the air" and the "spirit who works in the children of disobedience." The prophet **Habakkuk** also seems to understand this when he speaks these words: *“God appearing from the south, his glory covered the heavens, and the earth was full of his praise; his brightness was as the light, and horns were in his hands; although the hiding-place of his strength was there, the plague went before him, and burning coals went forth at his feet. Where he stood, he measured the earth,”* and so forth. <note>Habakkuk 3:3-5. The author uses a specific Latin translation where "meridie" (south/midday) and "anthrax" (burning coal/pestilence) are key terms.</note> However, **Jerome** interprets this passage thus: *“Death shall go before his face, and the devil shall go forth before his feet.”* From this context, we must primarily gather that God, in His wrath, is accustomed to punishing the rebellious and the impious not immediately, but through the mediation of a destroying angel; it follows then that the southern region is the chief seat of pestilential corruption.

From these things, therefore, we see what kind of agreement exists between the spirit of the <term>Macrocosm<gloss>The "Macrocosm" refers to the entire universe or the world at large, viewed as a giant living being.</gloss></term> and the <term>Microcosm<gloss>The "Microcosm" refers to "man" as a "little world" that mirrors the structure of the universe.</gloss></term>. Since man is the son of the Macrocosm, being composed of its members and elements, it is necessary that when the spirit of one is infected, the spirit of the other is also infected. Hence, we observe that when the air is corrupted by a comet or by ill-omened thunder and tempests, human plague and contagious diseases follow—and indeed, even the sterility of the earth and consequent famine. We also see that the entire air of a city or place can be rendered corrupt by the contagious breath of a single man infected with the plague. Likewise, we notice the air in some places is infected and contaminated by the poisonous exhalations of lakes; indeed, we note that certain spots of earth are unhealthy and contagious, while the lands of other regions are very healthy. This is usually assigned to the demons who frequent and inhabit those places by those who have immersed themselves somewhat more deeply into the mysteries of God and nature. Finally, manifest experience stands as witness that plague sometimes accompanies an earthquake, because imprisoned evil spirits—if they are malignant and poisonous—corrupt and infect the air as they exit. From this, it is necessary that a specific plague follows, especially in that place where the earthquake occurs. And in the *Margarita Philosophica* <note>The "Philosophical Pearl," a famous 16th-century encyclopedia by Gregor Reisch.</note> we find these words added: "Perhaps in the blessing of that church, he remembers the salt and water when he says: *Let there be no pestilent spirit or corrupt air there.* For the tempests of darkness frequently use these spirits, either to harm men in their bodies or to alienate their senses and deceive them with visions." By these spirits, the eyes and faces of those who enter subterranean caves or dens are sometimes changed—especially the faces of those who receive responses from demons, which they are accustomed to give in such caves. And certainly, insofar as earthquakes usually occur while the North Wind (**Boreas**) is blowing, it is certain that dark spirits break out violently by its force, especially those called **Benlohim** <note>Hebrew: "Sons of God," here interpreted as a class of spirits.</note> because of the stupor and terror they cause; whence **Ovid** speaks thus in the person of the North Wind:

Where by "spirits of the dead" (manes) he understands the spirits shut up in the bowels of the earth, who, being disturbed and stirred up from their nests like birds gathered in a great multitude, are accustomed to ascend and break into the open air from the earth with a great noise, like a sudden cannon shot, and contaminate the air of the place with their poisonous breath.

But truly, hear briefly what the Magi and the wise judge concerning this kind of contagion of air, water, and earth. The ancient Greeks name six demons who, being malicious toward men, draw the water of the **Styx** in their hands and scatter it upon the lands, from which calamities, plagues, and famines follow. Some call these by the general name **Telchines**, others **Alastores**; but their particular names are **Acteüs, Megalesius, Ormenus, Lycus, Nicon,** and **Mimon**. But we, while not at all disagreeing with the said Greek sages on their names, wish to add something more regarding their duties. For since that infernal river is referred to only a single element (namely water), yet we observe many various kinds of diseases according to the various dispositions of the four elements, let us be granted leave if we demonstrate that those four **Telchines** <note>In Greek myth, the Telchines were original inhabitants of Rhodes, often depicted as malignant sorcerers or smiths who could control the weather.</note> have in their office the duty of scattering and disseminating through the lands and air the contagious and corrupted waters of the four infernal rivers, drawn in their hands: namely, the river **Phlegethon**, which is fiery; **Cocytus**, which is airy; **Styx**, which is watery; and **Acheron**, which is earthy. From these, diseases are produced in both the Macrocosm and Microcosm that are fiery, airy, watery, and earthy.

For just as the elements, when properly ordered, contribute to health (being governed by health-bringing angels), so those elements when poorly disposed and ordered toward corruption by evil angels produce infirmities. Of these worst-disposed elements, preserved in their malignancy, the poisonous dregs are those from which those four contagious and poisonous rivers of the infernal kingdom seem to gush as if from fountains. # Concerning the Efficient Cause of Meteors <note>In early modern science, "meteors" referred to any atmospheric phenomena, including weather, comets, and earthquakes.</note>

The Book of Revelation makes mention of those to whom it was given to harm the earth and the sea—that is, to infect the waters and the land. From these things, therefore, we see the nature of the harmony between the spirits of the <term>Macrocosm<gloss>The "Great World" or the universe.</gloss></term> and the <term>Microcosm<gloss>The "Small World," referring to the human being as a reflection of the universe.</gloss></term>. From these, diseases are produced in both the Macrocosm and Microcosm that are fiery, airy, watery, and earthy.

The poisonous dregs of these elements, which are most poorly disposed and preserved in malignancy, are those from which those four contagious and poisonous rivers of the infernal kingdom seem to spring as if from fountains. Section I. Port, IV. Part. II, Book IV. Member II.

These [demons] strike suddenly and sometimes destroy, agitating both bodies and minds, and they pervert the natural faculties. They often kill both humans and beasts by fire, water, or by casting them over a precipice. Such spirits act not so much out of a specific will to do harm (though they are indeed the most bitter enemies of mankind) as out of a greed for **vital heat**. They invade both humans and beasts, especially those spirits that dwell in deep, freezing, and dry places. Because they have contracted an extreme coldness devoid of moisture, they long for the **vital, moist heat** <note>In ancient and medieval medicine, "vital heat" and "radical moisture" were considered the two essential components of life. Without them, the body becomes cold and dies.</note> found in living things. To obtain this, they rush into irrational animals and fly toward lakes and pits; they flee the heat of the sun and fire because it is drying and burning, but they love animal heat, which is moderate and mixed with a pleasant moisture. They especially desire human heat because it is more perfectly balanced. 

From this, it happens that when they invade bodies, they cause no small disturbance. They block and fill those channels <note>original: "meatus"</note> in which the **animal spirit** <note>The "animal spirit" (from the Latin *anima*, meaning soul) was thought to be a subtle fluid or gas that traveled through the nerves to facilitate movement and sensation.</note> resides. Because the "animal spirit" is compressed by the thickness and density of the demonic bodies and is shaken within, the human bodies are consequently vibrated and convulsed. Their principal faculties fail in their actions, and their movements become sluggish and erratic. Among these invading demons, if one is of the subterranean type, it shakes and destroys the person it occupies and cries out through them, using the sufferer's breath as its own instrument. If the demon is one that flees the light, it brings on a profound lethargy, stifles the voice, and renders the possessed person as if dead; for this kind is more "earthy" than all others, being exceedingly cold and dry. Thus, whenever it creeps into a person, it blunts, dulls, darkens, and destroys all vital power.

Therefore, this kind is called **"mute and deaf,"** and it does not depart from those it occupies unless it is driven out by divine power—specifically through prayer and fasting. Psellus <note>Michael Psellus (c. 1017–1078) was a Byzantine monk and scholar whose work on demonology was highly influential in the Renaissance.</note> learned these things from the observations of Marcus, who lived in the desert for a long time so that, by having conversation with demons, he might learn their duties and properties.

We conclude, therefore, that demons are accustomed to induce such diseases in nature and temperament as match their own condition and quality among the elements; wherefore **fiery** demons cause fiery diseases, **aerial** ones cause windy or gaseous ailments, **watery** ones cause watery diseases, and **earthly** ones cause sluggish and grounded ailments. However, they sometimes mix together, producing a "bastard" or hybrid disease, as will be explained more fully below.

In this, the Holy Scriptures agree, saying: *And the Lord shall strike thee with corrupted air, etc.* <note>original: "aere corrupto." This likely refers to various translations of Deuteronomy 28.</note> And elsewhere: *The Lord shall strike thee with poverty, with fever, and with cold, with burning and with heat, with corrupted air, and with mildew, etc.* (Deuteronomy 28:22). By these passages, it is evident that it is granted to the ministers of God to corrupt the air, as they are the ones who carry out the Lord's commands. For they are accustomed to scatter the "seeds of contagion" through the open air, which the Royal Prophet <note>King David, the traditional author of the Psalms.</note> also seems to verify in this discourse: *Thou shalt not be afraid of the terror of the night, of the arrow that flieth in the day, of the plague that walketh in the darkness or night, of the destruction that wasteth at midday*—or as Jerome interprets it—*from the **noonday devil**; the plague shall not come nigh thy dwelling, for He shall give His angels charge over thee, and keep thee in all thy ways, etc.* (Psalm 91). From this discourse, it is clear, first, that the air is infected by the noonday devil and his legions, and second, that God appoints good angels to preserve men from the evil ones.

And the School of Theologians seems to infer almost the same thing as the Prophet when they define the rank of the **Evil Spirits** <note>original: "Cacodæmonum"</note> as belonging to those who are called "aerial powers." These spirits mix themselves into thunder, lightning, and bolts, and are reported to corrupt the air and, by this means, bring about pestilences and other evils. ### On the Efficient Cause of Meteors. 
<note>In this period, "meteors" referred to any atmospheric phenomena, including wind, rain, lightning, and even plagues, not just falling stars.</note>

The Book of Revelation mentions those to whom it was given to harm the earth and the sea—that is, to infect the waters and the land. But they establish that the primary king of these is *Meririm*, who is the "noonday devil," a parching spirit and a raging demon of the midday. Paul (as was said above) calls him the "prince of the power of this air" and the "spirit who works in the children of disobedience." <note>original: "principem potestatis aeris huius, & spiritum qui operatur in filijs diffidentiæ"</note> The prophet Habakkuk <note>original: "Abbakuk"</note> also seems to understand this when he says: *When God appeared from the south, His glory covered the heavens, and the earth was full of His praise. His brightness was as the light; horns were at His side, though His power was hidden there. Before Him went the pestilence, and burning coals went forth at His feet. Where He stood, He measured the earth, etc.* (Habakkuk 3:3). But Jerome interprets this passage thus: *Death shall go before His face, and the devil shall go forth before His feet.* From this context, we must primarily conclude that God, in His wrath, does not usually punish the rebellious and the impious directly, but rather through the mediation of a "destroying angel." Furthermore, we see that the southern region is the chief seat of pestilential corruption.

From these things, we see what kind of correspondence exists between the spirit of the **Macrocosm** <note>The "Macrocosm" refers to the universe as a whole.</note> and the **Microcosm** <note>The "Microcosm" refers to the human being, viewed as a miniature version of the universe.</note>. Since man is the "son of the Macrocosm"—being fashioned from its members and elements—it is necessary that when the spirit of one is infected, the spirit of the other is also infected. Hence, we observe that when the air is corrupted by a comet or an ill-omened thunderclap and storm, human plagues and contagious diseases follow—and indeed, even the sterility of the earth and subsequent famine. We also see that the entire air of a city or place can be rendered corrupt by the contagious breath of a single man tainted by plague. Similarly, we notice the air in certain places is infected and contaminated by the poisonous exhalations of lakes; indeed, we note that certain spots on earth are unhealthy and contagious, while other nearby seats of the earth are very healthy. This is usually assigned to the demons who frequent and inhabit those places by those who have immersed themselves somewhat more deeply into the mysteries of God and nature. Finally, manifest experience stands as a witness that a plague sometimes accompanies an earthquake. This is because the "evil spirits" <note>original: "spiritus praui"</note> trapped within, if they are malignant and poisonous, corrupt and infect the air as they exit. From this, a specific sequence of plague must follow, especially in the place where the earthquake occurred. In the *Margarita Philosophica* <note>A famous 16th-century encyclopedia of knowledge by Gregor Reisch.</note> (Book 9, Chapter 17), we find these things added: *Perhaps in the blessing of that church, he mentions salt and water when he says: "Let there be no pestilent spirit or corrupt air there." For the "storms of darkness" often use these spirits, either to harm men in their bodies or to alienate their senses and deceive them with visions. By these spirits, the eyes and faces of those who enter subterranean caves or dens are sometimes changed—especially those who receive responses from demons, which they are accustomed to give in such caves.* So says that author. And certainly, insofar as earthquakes usually occur while the North Wind <note>original: "Borea"</note> is blowing, it is certain that the "spirits of darkness" burst forth violently by its force—especially those called the *Benlohim* <note>Likely a corruption of the Hebrew "Bnei Elohim" (Sons of God), here associated with stupor and terror.</note> on account of the stupor and terror they cause. This is why Ovid speaks in the persona of the North Wind:

They draw, I say, fiery waters and those raging with parching poison from the contagious flame of the infernal river Phlegethon. That is, they convert the influxes of the element of fire into a poisonous nature, which they are seen to contaminate everywhere through the assigned place—whether it be more general and public, such as a region or city, or more private, such as a house, family, or only a private man—according to the divine pleasure, the spirit being maliciously scattered in this manner. When they have dispersed these through the earth and waters, aerial decay is usually produced, and so on for the rest. We could compile an infinite volume on the reasoning and mystery of this kind of infection, but since the present subject constrains us within narrower limits, we shall descend with a light leap to the properties and offices of the angels—first the good, and then the evil ones.

Thus also a candle, brought into this or 그 part of the dark air, does not cease to look upon and illuminate the entire darkness of the place. Furthermore, it must also be considered that as heaven is everywhere, God is also present, namely everywhere in the vast spirit of the world, in the water, and in any point of the earth, so indeed all and each of the angels are accustomed to claim for themselves the privilege of ubiquity; but wherever an angel is not in its distinct essence, there the rays of its essence are nonetheless accustomed to be poured in, which operation is properly called **influence** <note>influence: From the Latin "influentia," literally a "flowing in" of power or essence.</note>, about which the **Cabalists** have spoken so many and such great words, which can no more be divided or distinguished from the essence of the angel than solar rays from the sun; but back to the purpose.

<margin>*(Revelation, book 3, On the Cabalistic Tree)*</margin>

It is from this, therefore, that a non-significant voice <note>non-significant voice: A sound or word that does not have a conventional meaning in human language, often used in incantations or mystical prayers.</note> can do more in magic than a significant one, for any voice is powerful in magic insofar as it is formed by the voice of God, because that in which nature exercises magic is the voice of God; but that voice of God is not like that of a man, but like the **Word of Jehovah**, which (as **Jehovah** testifies) is in the angel, so that the voice of the angel is mixed from the divine will or the luminous word, and the angelic nature or the spiritual and aerial organ; wherefore it is established that it is very hidden and familiar only to the mind. But truly, sometimes having assumed a body, they are accustomed to strike our ears at the same time with an articulated voice, as we find everywhere in the holy page.

# Section I. Portion IV. Part II. Book IV. Member II.

It is also their property to sometimes take on various appearances and forms, subjected to our physical sight. For this reason, they sometimes appear in human form, sometimes they are seen in the form of fire, and occasionally they take on the form of air and wind. Not infrequently, they are perceived in the appearance of a river or water, or they are clothed in the forms of birds, or gems, or precious stones. Others dwell within a human spirit; in this way, the Prophet Zechariah saw an angel coming out of him, who spoke to another angel. Sometimes they are discerned in the shapes of letters and characters, and occasionally in the sound of a voice, and thus in many other kinds of visions, which are contained in abundance within the sacred font <note>original: "fonte sacro", referring to the Holy Scriptures</note>; and the more secret Theologians <note>likely referring to practitioners of Christian Kabbalah or Neoplatonic mysticism</note> seem to support this assertion of ours. 

The reason why they are so suited and adapted to taking on any form is that they are endowed with a spiritual and aerial substance of unique purity. To that extent, they perceive all **intelligible forms** <note>forms that can be understood by the mind rather than just seen by the eyes</note> within themselves, and consequently, all intelligible forms are compatible with them. From this, it follows that they are filled with species and images—that is, every type of intelligence and every physical likeness formed by intelligence shines through them. This is not unlike how every color is reflected in the air, or every object in a mirror. However, those objects in the air and the mirror come from the surrounding area, but this angelic impression comes from their own center, and according to their own will and pleasure, as *Psellus* <note>Michael Psellus (c. 1017–1078), a Byzantine philosopher and politician whose works on the classification of spirits were highly influential in the Renaissance.</note> seems to suggest.

As for the disposition of good angels, it is certain and confirmed by holy writings that they are the opposite of the evil ones in their conditions. Whatever is good, they are naturally inclined and ready to perfect by their natural disposition.

### The Passion of Angels.
<note>In this context, "passion" refers to the philosophical concept of "being acted upon" or "undergoing" something, rather than just emotional suffering.</note>

Angels suffer very little from physical mass, since their outer nature is a spirit most pure, subtle, and light—which is also best declared by the words of the Evangelist Luke in the final chapter. But we say that angels "suffer" insofar as they receive the influxes of divine light in abundance; that is, their spiritual bodies are aptly prepared to receive the impressions of divine light, which they then afterwards, by divine command, impart and communicate to lower beings. 

But truly, the most holy page <note>the Bible</note> teaches us that the evil angels both suffer and are even tormented because of the dense and dark mass of their substance, for their place is the infernal lake; but of these, we shall speak a little further below. Furthermore, even good angels, insofar as they are subject to the command and mandates of God, are thought to "undergo" the signs and impressions of the divine will—but in a pleasing manner, for they are said to serve God without compulsion.

### Common Property.

We call the "common property" of a good angel that which is concerned not only with themselves, but with universal things, whether uncreated or created, in this world. From this, their office <term>office: a formal duty or role (Latin: *officium*)</term> is properly named, both toward God the creator of all things, and toward His creatures; for an angel is by nature a middle-point between creatures and God.

-> B <-
-> The office of a good angel toward <-
-> the creator consists in: <-
- Receiving His light,
- Worshipping and revering Him,
- Listening to His voice,
- Carrying out His word and pleasure.

The supercelestial angels of the higher order worship God and the unique Creator as the firmest and most stable unity. They are solely occupied with Him and are not said to preside over the physical bodies of the world, nor over the administration of lower adaptations. Their role is to receive God’s light and flow it down to the lower orders, by means of which individual duties are distributed to each. Some of these are assistants at the divine tribunal and continually praise God their creator; others are ministers to Him and to us. 

However, the celestial or "Olympic" angels, beyond divine worship, are assigned to the spheres. Their role is to entrust those influxes, which they received from the higher orders, to the spirits <note>original: "dæmonibus", here meaning spirits or intermediaries in a general Neoplatonic sense, not necessarily "demons" in the modern sense</note> of the lower order. These spirits use these various descending lights in infinite tasks in the air, in the waters, and on the earth for the preservation and multiplication of creatures. Finally, all good angels in general are said primarily to revere and worship—indeed, even to see—the face of the creator, whether it be in the highest, middle, or lowest heaven.

The third office of good angels toward God is to listen to His voice. Thereafter, such is their obedience toward their creator in bringing His mandates to completion that, through the fourth degree of their office, they set about executing them immediately and willingly. Hence, those skilled in Theology assert and agree that angels serve God without compulsion, and His mandates

# On the Efficient Cause of Atmospheric Phenomena <note>original: "De Causa Meteororum Efficiente." In the 17th century, "meteors" referred to any phenomena in the sky or air, such as wind, rain, and lightning, rather than just space rocks.</note>

Just as God first created angelic beings for his divine worship and service in the world from the beginning, so too, in the second place, he set them over creatures in general—namely, the Macrocosm and the Microcosm—and thereafter over those things within the Macrocosm made for the use of the Microcosm, so that they might oversee and care for them.

That great and supreme angel or intelligence animating, inspiring, and moving the entire spirit of the macrocosm from sunrise to sunset (for he holds command over the first movable sphere <term>the *Primum Mobile*, the outermost sphere of the heavens</term>) is the one whom the Kabbalists call *Metatron* <note>original: "Mittatron"</note>, the Sacred Page calls *Wisdom*, and the Platonists call the *Soul of the World* <note>original: "Animam mundi"</note>. All other angels in the world, both good and bad, are said to offer him obedience; of him, we shall speak more specifically and fully below. 

There are also other Angelic Princes or Leaders who reign immediately under the leadership or command of this angel, who oversee the parts of the world. Some are rulers of the heavens and the ether, some of whom preside over the Zodiac, others over the triplicities <term>groups of three zodiac signs associated with an element</term>, and some over the faces or decans <term>10-degree divisions of the zodiac</term> and even the quinaries <term>5-degree divisions</term>. Others are placed over the remaining stars of the firmament, for there is no star in heaven that does not have its own prefect. Others command the spheres of the planets by day and by night, etc. Some have their powers and seats in the Empyrean heaven <note>the highest, most spiritual part of heaven</note>, and others have the regions of the world as well as the elements in their custody: 

Namely, *Michael* is the eastern Angel, *Gabriel* the Northern, *Raphael* the western, and *Uriel* the southern—of whom we spoke before—and also those who have command over the four elements: namely, *Seruph* over fire, *Cherub* over air, *Tharsis* over water, and *Ariel* over earth. 

Furthermore, 72 angels are called the "angels of division" by the Kabbalists, for it is their office to divide the earth itself into just as many distinct parts, which are called different kingdoms. Each of these angels presides and reigns spiritually over the aforementioned kingdoms—not that they descend from heaven to dwell there (as the Kabbalists would have it), but insofar as they dwell in the super-celestial world, they nonetheless care for these lower things and govern earthly matters through their influences. This seems to be confirmed by Ecclesiasticus <note>The Book of Sirach</note>, where we read that a ruler is appointed over every nation. Furthermore, Moses says in his song: *When the Most High divided the nations, he set their bounds according to the number of the Angels of God.* <note>A reference to Deuteronomy 32:8 in the Septuagint version</note>

However, our intention leads us to believe that these 72 angels (since the starry heaven is related to the earth by the wise because of its fixity) are those leaders who have primary force and power in the quinaries of every sign, which are the half-parts of the decans or decurions. For example, in every sign there are 30 degrees; every ten-degree segment is called a "decan," and thus the five-degree segment is the middle part of the decan. Therefore, in every sign there are 6 quinaries; this number, multiplied by the twelve signs, produces 72, which is exactly the number of the 72 leaders whose task, according to the Kabbalists, is to divide the earth into kingdoms. I have conceived this idea in my mind, which, although it is not to be found anywhere in writing as far as I know, nevertheless the matter itself indicates it is probable—both because every kingdom is subject to the fate of change (which is seen in the shifting of Monarchies) and in that struggle held between Gabriel and the Prince of the Persians <note>A reference to Daniel 10:13, where angels represent the spiritual interests of specific nations</note>. Hence it is likely that such rulers are "Olympic" <term>associated with the planets and stars</term> and not at all Empyrean. This seems even more probable because, according to the observations of Astrologers, the kingdoms and provinces of the earth are placed under particular signs of the Zodiac, which are the causes of alteration both in the nature of places and the condition of the inhabitants, which usually differs between one kingdom and another neighboring it. Furthermore, others are placed over the waters and have others under them...

### Section I, Portion IV, Part II. Book IV. Member II.

...infinitely many demons; hence the sea gods Neptune, Thetis, Proteus, and Nereus, and hence the nymphs of the rivers, the Nereids, etc.

There are also other good angels of a lower condition who are accustomed to administer the particular creatures of the world; for in the empyrean heaven <term>the highest, most spiritual realm of heaven</term>, angels of the higher order receive divine light directly from God by way of influence, and they emit and manifest that light to those of the lower order, who then finally diffuse that same light into the lowest parts of the world. For this reason, they are called "mirrors" <note>original: "specula"</note> because of their power to receive the light of God. Furthermore, the order and harmony of these angels—and even of those subjects of theirs flowed into and dispersed everywhere throughout the world—is so great that no order among them is permitted to undertake or approach a task destined for another.

Furthermore, in the ethereal heaven, every sign of the Zodiac, every triplicity <term>a group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element</term>, every decan <term>a ten-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign</term>, and every quinarius <term>a five-degree subdivision</term> of any sign enjoys its own princely angel by whom it is ruled and governed. This prince has many legions and cohorts under him; indeed (as has already been said), there is no star to be found in the entire firmament over which a Prince does not preside, and which is not inhabited by infinite angels of a lower order. The same must also be said of the Planets or wandering stars, to which royal leaders are assigned, by whom they are directed, preserved, and enriched by influences from on high. Among these, the Prince or Prefect of Saturn is *Zabkiel*, of Jupiter is *Zaphkiel*, of Mars is *Samael*, of the Sun is *Michael*, of Venus is *Anael*, of Mercury is *Raphael*, and of the Moon is *Gabriel*, etc. Many legions are subject to them within their spheres or legions. Indeed, it is affirmed by some skilled in occult theosophy <term>divine wisdom concerning the hidden mysteries of nature</term> that angels agree with humans in many aspects of nature, and even in number. They conclude that as many humans are to be saved as there were angels who fell from heaven in the battle between the dragon and Michael, so that those to be saved may fill the place of the angels cast out of heaven. They also say that as many are to be damned as there were angels who remained on Michael's side in heaven after the victory. From this, they wish to conclude an equality in the number of humans and angels; if this were true, it would consequently be probable that there are as many Saturnine angels as there are Saturnine humans, and as many Jovial, Martial, etc.

In the lowest part of the world, there are also angels administering to every creature. Some are said to preside over animals, others over plants; indeed, the sages of the Kabbalists <term>scholars of Jewish mysticism</term> maintain that there is no herb or plant on earth that does not have an appropriated star in the firmament, and consequently an angel, who strikes it and says to it, as it were, "grow and multiply." Others are said to preside over precious stones, others over metals, and so on for the rest.

But since the ancient Hebrews attributed all things or species in creation to the sacred letters <note>the Hebrew alphabet</note>, whose symbols represent as many orders of angels as there are sacred letters, they therefore assigned a specific office over creatures and a specific species to each of these letters and the angels symbolizing them. For example: For the outpouring of life into the world, transmitted directly from God—*Ehieh* <note>the divine name "I Am"</note>—there is the order called *Haioth* <note>Chajoth ha-Qodesh</note>, that is, the "holy living creatures" or "animals of life," who symbolize the letter *Aleph*. For the influencing of forms, the *Ophanim*, that is, "forms" or "wheels," through whom God—*Elohim*—distinguished Chaos, are linked with *Beth*. For joining form with fluid matter, there is the order of *Aralim*, that is, the "great, strong, and robust ones," who obtain that power from Jehovah by whom they are illuminated, linked with *Gimel*. The order through which God—*Elohe*—fashioned the images of bodies, the *Chachmalim* <note>Hashmallim</note>, refers to *Daleth*. That through which *Elohim Gibbor* draws forth the Elements refers to *He*. That through which God—*Eloha*—produces metals, the *Malahim* <note>Malakhim</note>, refers to *Vau*. That through which *Jehovah Sabaoth* produces Vegetables, the *Elohim* (that is, "Gods"), refers to *Zain*. That through which *Elohim Sabaoth* procreates animals, the *Bene Elohim* <note>Sons of God</note>, refers to *Heth*. That through which God—*Shadai*—cares for the human race, the *Cherubin*, refers to *Teth*. That through which God flows into the sons of men with knowledge of things and wondrous industry, the *Issim* <note>Ishim</note> (that is, "nobles" or "men"), who are the lowest in all the hierarchies, refers to *Iod*. Through the one dwelling in the first movable sphere, *El Shadai*, the spirit of life and reason is communicated; that angel is called *Metattron* <note>Metatron</note>, who is the "active intellect" of the sensible world, referring to *Caph*, just as the final *Caph* refers to the circuit of the fixed stars. To *Lamed* are referred the spheres of the planets, which are called the "wanderers," and specifically the angel of Saturn is referred to it. To the open *Mem* is the sphere of the angel of Jupiter; to the closed *Mem*, the sphere of Mars, and so on for the rest.

Finally, others say that the forms of the elements are ruled by divine power through the angels called *Issim*, and by the power of the heavens, and by the power of primary matter, which is the source and origin of all elements. Inanimate things and minerals, which are called "elemented" and "mixed," are ruled by the celestial spheres and the separate intelligences, which are called *Issim*. Furthermore, all vegetables, fruits, and crops, and things born of the earth, are governed by the intelligences of heaven and those separate ones called *Issim* by the power of divine influence. Likewise, the sensitive and creeping things of the earth, and those that move forward, as well as the fish of the waters and the birds of the air—and indeed whatever irrational things have vital motion—are ruled by the power of God through the spirits of heaven and their subjects, called *Issim*. All these spirits are called "ministering angels" (according to the Apostle) sent forth into ministry. Finally, the offices of the angels are distinguished by a more general distinction according to their Hierarchies. For they make the higher hierarchy have care over the super-celestial region and contemplate divine providence; their highest order is the *Seraphim*, namely in the goodness of God; the second is the *Cherubim*, namely in the essence of God as form; the third is the *Thrones*, namely in wisdom. The second Hierarchy looks toward the ethereal world and administers in the heavens; its first order, the **Dominations**, issues commands in heaven which the others execute. The second, the **Virtues**, administers the heavens and sometimes conspires to perform miracles. The third, the **Powers**, wards off those things which might disturb the divine law. The third hierarchy contains ministering spirits <note>original: "dæmones ministros"; here "demons" refers to spirits in the classical sense, not necessarily evil beings</note> who descend to care for lower things. The first order of this group, the **Principalities**, cares for public affairs—namely principalities, magistrates, provinces, and kingdoms—and their Princes are those 72 previously mentioned. The second, the **Archangels**, is involved in sacred matters and the divine worship of men, directing men in their duties and offering their prayers and sacrifices to God. The spirits of the third and last order are accustomed to arrange even smaller matters, and guardians are present for individuals: some of these administer virtue to the tiniest herbs, pebbles, and all lower things; nevertheless, these creatures do not receive gifts from the angels themselves, but from God through the angels, as was said by the Prophet Daniel:

This means that according to the images and acts of the internal agent of any elemental creature, the external appears, no differently than a sheath is formed to the shape of the sword; all this work is completed by ministering angels. For an angel is defined as an intermediate power between God and nature or a created thing, from which such operations occur in them as appear to us—even those which nature either would not do, or would do differently, which some say come from a "hidden property" <term>occulta proprietatē</term> and others because it is simply so; finally, all things are done and brought to their conclusion by God through angels.

*Pico della Mirandola* <note>An influential Italian Renaissance philosopher known for his "Oration on the Dignity of Man"</note> says that human affairs ought to be governed not by bodies but by the mystery of angels, as they mediate by nature and dignity between God and man. Whence (he says), "when you descend from God to the earth, descend through heaven; but when you descend from God to men, descend through angels." Thus we read in the Prophets of the angel of the Persians, Greeks, and Hebrews providing for his people; and in Plato and all the Platonists we read of "local gods" set over cities, kingdoms, and men. And Orpheus, with the Pythagoreans, says that "all things are full of Gods," all of whom they nevertheless refer back to the one Jove. ### Section I, Portion IV, Part II. Book IV. Member II.

...and dedicated to the guardianship of reason, it is governed by an angel of the highest order. Here, according to Iamblichus <note>Iamblichus (c. 245–325 AD) was a Neoplatonist philosopher who wrote extensively on theurgy and the soul's relationship to the divine.</note> and the doctrine of the Egyptians, it is called the **good spirit** <note>original: "dæmon bonus"</note>, the **good genius**, and the **sacred intelligence**. According to the testimony of Iamblichus, this spirit is not infused into man by the stars or planets, but from a more exalted origin—namely, it is said to be infused into man by the presiding ruler of the world and the angels, and it is specifically destined for the government of the mind and the rational soul.

Therefore, it is by the virtue of this spirit that man is granted the power to rule over the stars and to transcend the tyranny of fate, insofar as it is the role of this spirit to direct the life of the soul and to continually present good thoughts to the mind. It longs to illuminate our inner selves and intends to do so at every moment, although it is not granted to us to notice this very operation because of our own darkness—except when we have been purged and purified. Once we live tranquilly and peacefully, then not only is it perceived by us, but it even seems to converse with us in its own language and speech. As for what kind of language such an angel uses, and what kind of voice it employs in its speech, we have declared this above. Finally, it acts to lead us toward sacred perfection, to render us ready for divine worship, and to keep us safe from the snares and malice of the Devil.

The second is what is called the **spirit of birth** <note>original: "dæmon genituræ"</note>, which is also called the **genius of life**. This is believed to be from the order of the Olympic or ethereal spirits, which is why it is said to descend at birth from the higher regions in the manner of a celestial influence. This is the guardian of life and the executor of its functions; for just as it procured the power of life for the body at the very beginning of birth, so it takes care to communicate that power and attracts suitable nourishment for its preservation through a magnetic and occult <note>In this context, "occult" simply means hidden or not visible to the naked eye.</note> power from the heavens. It draws this daily—indeed, at every moment—chiefly from that star, whether planetary or fixed, from which it most participates. Finally, according to the goodness of such a spirit—that is, according to the greater or lesser fated influence of its presiding star—the health and happiness of the person born will be greater or more meager throughout their life.

We classify the spirit of the lowest condition and place as the **elemental spirit**, which some call the **evil genius**. In truth, unless it is well-corrected in its ways by the highest spirit (which we have called the "sacred" one), it will always be prone to the pleasures of the flesh and the vanities of this changeable world, according to the natural condition of its place. Indeed, it comes from that region of the world in which the "prince of the power of the air" <note>A biblical reference to Ephesians 2:2, often associated with the realm of fallen spirits or the lower atmosphere.</note> is accustomed to exercise his force.

Others say that the third spirit of a man is the **angel of his profession**. They say that when one's profession is changed, the spirit is also changed. However, we can boldly contradict them in this, because a profession belongs to the realm of reason and intellect. Therefore, we leave the perfection of a profession to the direction of the **sacred spirit**, whose role it is, in its office, to share in the Holy Spirit and His gifts. It is the sacred spirit's role (as the Holy Scripture testifies) to distribute various sciences to men according to their varying capacities—as was done for **Bezaleel** <note>The biblical craftsman (Exodus 31) filled with the Spirit of God to build the Tabernacle.</note> and the others whom Exodus mentions more fully in chapters 28:3, 31:2, and 35:30. For this reason, we make the sacred angel the distributor of sciences and arts—whose role is to give art, science, and intellect—rather than another spirit of lesser condition. If a person sometimes chooses or changes one art for another because of their own "dark" condition, this is not the fault of their guardian and governor, but the error and depravity of their own blind and carnal will.

I know also that **Astrologers** attribute the masteries and professions of men to the star of their birth, and consequently to the angel governing that star: for example, they attribute the merchant's art and mathematical sciences to **Mercury**; warlike masteries and blacksmiths to **Mars**; and the arts of medicine, music, etc., to the **Sun**. But to these we reply that the **Olympic spirit** at birth is always subject to the **sacred spirit**, just as the **Elemental spirit** is subject to the **Olympic**. There is always a relationship of one to the other. First, God pours out His luminous property through the gate he has adopted into a specific order of angels of the empyrean heaven. These angels immediately commit that influence to the archangel of the sphere (either the star of the eighth orb or a planet of the ether), who in turn pours it into the elemental region. He commends it to the spirit of his orb wandering there in the air. This spirit—along with the empyrean nature or influx (which we call the **sacred angel**) and the celestial or ethereal nature (which we call the **spirit of life**) and itself (which we call the **elemental nature**) involves itself in the spermatic mass for the procreation of the one being born.

But since we have spoken more fully of these three spirits in Treatise 1, Section 2, Portion 4, Book 3, Part 2, we do not wish to consume more time in this subject by drawing out the thread of this discourse, so that we may more quickly reach the enumeration of the angels who are occupied with human affairs. Regarding the spirits who have power over the morals and faculties of the human body: just as lower things represent higher things, we say that there are also spirits in the elemental world who have a relationship in their condition to those celestial spirits in the Olympic world. By natural inclination, they exercise their powers in accordance with the powers of the celestial souls—namely, the mind, reason, imagination, and the motor or life-giving power.

**Fiery spirits** follow the mind, where they join in and assist with more sublime contemplations. **Airy spirits**, following the reason, favor the rational power and separate it in some way from the sensual and vegetative powers; these are said to serve the active life just as the fiery spirits serve the contemplative life. **Watery spirits** serve the imagination and the senses by natural inclination and contribute to a life of pleasure. Finally, **earthly spirits** favor the vegetative or natural faculty. These spirits are further distinguished according to the natures of the Planets and the names of the stars into **Saturnine**, **Jovial**, **Martial**, and so on.

->### On the Efficient Cause of Meteors.<-

And here it must be carefully observed that, just as humans are found on earth who take on the nature of any given planet or star, so too do demons dwell in the world of each planet, endowed with the condition of each element. From this, it happens that by the various **aspects** <note>In astrology, "aspects" are the geometric angles between planets that were believed to influence earthly events.</note> of the planets toward one another in the heavens, various effects are produced in the lower realms. This is because the demons closer to the nature of each planet meet and join, as if in the middle of a path, at the point of an aspect—if it is a "good" one, namely a **Trine** or **Sextile**. In this way, they flow downward into the elemental world in the manner of an influence.

But if the aspect is malevolent, especially involving planets of contrary conditions, then spirits of contrary nature or elements clash at the point of the aspect—namely in **Opposition**, **Square**, and **Conjunction**. Thus, they produce malevolent and turbulent effects, not only for human life but even for the world-spirit itself. I would have you hold this as a secret mystery: it is from this that life becomes more harmonious and healthy for some people, while for others it is turbulent, sickly, and full of strife. Some excel in genius and intellect, while others are dull and devoid of good reason, and so on for others.

Nevertheless, the holy angel holds command over the rest, both the Olympian <note>Here referring to celestial or planetary spirits.</note> and the Elemental ones. For the spirit of the rational life that is a deserter and a sinner is ruled by the spirit of the rational life that is pious and just. These spirits of the just are the holy angels; for, as **Thomas Aquinas** says, "inferior spirits are compelled by superior ones." This is also evident in the command held by that angel who went out from **Zechariah**, ordering another angel to hurry to Jerusalem; and also the spirit in the Apostles, who cast out demons from the possessed; and the **Angel Raphael**, who put **Asmodeus** <note>A powerful demon mentioned in the Book of Tobit.</note> to flight; and in many others. For it is certain that those spirits who are more filled and intoxicated with the divine nectar of divinity are more powerful than those who are more destitute and in need of divine light, and thus are darkened.

**Athanasius** says that the function of the **Seraphim** order is not only to immediately receive the divine outflow of light and to magnify God with unending hymns and restless praise—as they are closest to Him—but also to pray to Him for our salvation. So we read it written in the Apocalypse: *And another angel came and stood before the altar, having a golden censer; and much incense was given to him, that he might offer it with the prayers of all the saints upon the golden altar which is before the throne of God.* (Revelation 8:2). Furthermore, **Job** seems to suggest that there are angels performing intercession for men. Elihu says: *If there be an angel speaking for the man, to declare his righteousness, He will have mercy on him, and will say, "Deliver him, that he may not descend into corruption"; he shall pray to God, and He will be favorable to him, and will restore to man his justice.* (Job 33:23). This kind of angelic order is called **procuratorial**, because it is seen to ardently plead the cause of man before God.

There is also the office of a single angel who, as the **Cabalists** <note>Followers of Jewish mysticism (Kabbalah), whose ideas were often integrated into Renaissance Christian thought.</note> maintain, acts as a vicar in heaven. He offers rational souls to God in no different a way than common vicars or priests are accustomed to offer the body of Christ in the Mass on earth. They say this is **Michael**, who is that great prince (witnessed by Daniel) standing for the people of God or the elect. They say he performs a perpetual priesthood as the great priest of God in heaven; hence, he is called by the more secret theologians in Hebrew <term>Cofhengadol</term> <note>original: "Cofhengadol" (Kohen Gadol), meaning High Priest.</note>, that is, the **High Priest**. Furthermore, this angel is appointed the prince of Christ’s army over all the souls to be received, as the Archangel writes in his commentary on the Cabalistic dogma.

There is also another order of angels who are immediately present to man in this life, called **Doctrinal**. The role of these angels is to instruct him in the truth of things—present, past, and future alike. Thus **Gabriel**, speaking to the prophet Daniel, says: *I have come to teach you what will happen to your people in the latter days.* (Daniel 11).

There are also angels of another condition present to man himself, called **Tutelary** (guardians), such as **Raphael**, who defended **Tobit** against evil spirits (Tobit 8). The royal prophet <note>Refers to King David, traditionally the author of the Psalms.</note> speaks of these to the elect: *Fear not the terror by night, nor the arrow that flies by day, nor the plague that walks in the darkness or night, nor the destruction that wastes at noon (or the noonday demon); no plague shall come near your tent, for He shall give His angels charge over you, and keep you in all your ways, etc.* (Psalm 91). **Jacob** also spoke of such an angel in his blessings: *The angel who redeemed me from all evil, bless these boys.* (Genesis 48). And those of whom it is written: *He has given His angels charge over you, and in their hands they shall bear you up, lest you dash your foot against a stone.* (Matthew 4:11).

There are others who are called **Ministerial** or **Administering** angels, of whom the Apostle says: *Are they not all ministering spirits, sent forth for those who shall receive the inheritance of salvation?* (Hebrews 1). Of this kind were also those who approached Christ on the mountain and ministered to Him (Matthew 4:11).

There is also the **Auxiliary** order, whose role is to assist the elect and the people of God against enemies and foes. Such were those angels of God who met Jacob on his journey, whom he called the **Army of God** when he saw them; through their mediation, he gained victory over the malevolent spirit of his brother (Genesis 32:1). Such an angel also existed in the time of **Hezekiah**, King of Judah, sent by God, who slew 185,000 of the Assyrian enemies (2 Kings 19). Such also was the angel whom **Judas Maccabeus** sought from God for his aid, by whose power he and his small band of men slew 35,000 of the enemy (2 Maccabees 15:22).

### Section I. Portion IV. Part II, Book IV. Member II.

There are others to whom the duty of consolation is assigned, such as the angel who was the comforter of Hagar in her great grief. And the angel who rescued Peter from prison. And that angel seen by the sorrowing Apostles after the resurrection of Christ.

Others are admonitory: for these are accustomed to place our sins before the eyes of the mind so that we may correct them; they also warn us of the Divine will, instructing us on what must be done. Similarly, they often visit men, warning them not to sin, and they awaken and rouse them from the sleep of sin and vice.

Others are assistants, who assist men in their ordinary business, like the angel who provided food and drink to Elijah and Daniel in their times of need.

Others are leaders and conductors on journeys, of whom Jehovah speaks, saying: *My angel shall go before you on the journey, and elsewhere, Behold, I send my angel before you, to keep you in this way, and to bring you into that place which I have prepared, Exodus 32:34.*

Besides these, others have the duty of taking the souls of the deceased into custody, about whom we read in Luke; the soul of Lazarus was carried into the bosom of Abraham. Finally, the duty of curing diseases and healing wounds is assigned to others; thus it is handed down by the holy word that Tobias was healed by Raphael; and that pool stirred by an angel, which healed those plunging into it by the touch of the angel, and so in many other cases. <note>The author refers to the Pool of Bethesda described in the Gospel of John.</note> But here we think this should be observed first: that although these orders seem to vary, since they receive their names from more particular duties, nevertheless all these orders reported by us here are called—most aptly according to the Apostle Paul in the place cited before—by a more general term derived from their more universal duty: Ministering Spirits or angels <note>original: "Spiritus seu angeli Administratorii"</note>, sent for the salvation and preservation of both the bodies and souls of men. Hesiod <note>Ancient Greek poet, c. 700 BCE</note> seems to intend this when he speaks in this sense: *Three times ten thousand are they upon the earth, many who nourish mortals, watchers of mortal men from Jove, who surely observe justice and pitiable deeds, clothed in air, going everywhere over the earth;* <note>original: "Ter decies mille sunt supra terram..."</note> And these watchers mentioned by Hesiod are called Spirits by the Latins, each of whom (according to the sense of the Cabalists) <term>Cabalists: followers of Jewish mysticism who developed complex systems of angelic hierarchies</term> is destined for the care of lower affairs. These are called Mammona or Mathon, or by the Greeks *daimonia* or *daemones* <term>demons: here used in the original Greek sense of "divine spirits" or "mediators," which could be good or bad, rather than the modern sense of purely evil beings</term>, used here in a good sense rather than a bad one.

We conclude, therefore, with a certain wise man in the *Revelation of Divine Majesty*, who describes the more open and manifest duties of angels thus: that the first among all is that great spirit who holds apart the immense and widely extended water which is called heaven, and preserves it in its essence, wonderfully granting motion to all growing and living things. In the second place are positioned the Cherubim, who guard and observe the tree of life; other angels announce future things and teach men; others destroy Sodom and Gomorrah; others kill and repel enemies; others send down snow, rain, lightning, and thunder upon the earth, and so on; each one executes his own peculiar task. Yet all together they serve God, while they carry out His will in all things—in the heavens, in the air, and on the earth, and in all places whatsoever—and that in various and wonderful ways. Sacred Scripture testifies to this, namely that spirits and angels have always indicated to those men to whom they were sent that they were dispatched and delegated by God to announce or command this or that to them, or even to carry out matters among them according to the divine will. From this, the state and condition of angelic duties can be gathered and perceived: there is the greatest diligence, devotion, and zeal there, to omit nothing, to delay nothing, but to perform all things exactly and even in the blink of an eye, and to bring back the report of their execution, by which God himself is praised, honored, and celebrated. In this execution there is no respect of persons, no consideration of reward, gifts, or presents; nothing wicked, nothing perverse, nothing unjust is performed there. There the words of God, His decrees and commands, are not twisted, changed, or corrupted, but all things are carried out according to the divine standard without any depravity.

No one is there who would break, deprave, or keep the word of God in part while rejecting it in part, as the children of men are accustomed to do.

->Sect. I. Port. IV. Part. II. Lib. IV. Membr. II.<-

By us it has been declared that a certain wise man in **Secret Theography** <note>original: "Theographia secreta"; refers to the study of divine writing or secret knowledge of God.</note>, in his own treatise titled *The Revelation of Majesty* (*On the Spirit, ch. 78*), breaks forth into these words: All things were created through the word of God; therefore, all things are likewise governed, moved, and guided through the word. For this reason, the wise men or philosophers of the world rave <note>original: "delirant"; suggests a state of being misguided or out of one's mind.</note> when they fail to grant that God works all in all, and that His word moves, stirs, and preserves all things. Instead, they attribute these things to created nature, pretending that God works through intermediaries—namely, through secondary and tertiary causes. They are unwilling to understand that God works solely through His word and not through any other means or the aforementioned alleged causes, but only *within* them. God created the first body—namely, water—as moist and humid through His word; thus, no other cause is seen in water that makes it wet and moist. Above and within the water, God created the hidden air through His word so that it might float upon the waters, impel and move them, and preserve them in their liquid and fluid substance; this same thing happens even today. Together with the air, He also created angels and spirits by His word, who perform and execute their duty and office in the air regarding the direction of storms, rain, snow, hail, frost, clouds, lightning, and the **ceraunian stone** <note>original: "lapidis ceraunii"; a "thunderstone" or "thunderbolt," once believed to be a physical stone that fell to earth during a lightning strike.</note>, fire, chasms <note>original: "chasmātū"; likely referring to atmospheric openings or vast floods.</note>, inundations of water, heat, cold, warmth, moisture, dryness, and many other things of that kind. So says that author. From this, it is clear that God does not work through angels as intermediaries, but through the Word *within* the angels. This is also what Rabbi **Muahem Racanat** <note>Menahem Recanati, a 13th-14th century Italian Kabbalist.</note> says in his commentaries on *Exodus 14*: *The characters flying above in the foundation of spiritual wisdom are administrative spirits, used to perform every thing through them, and their operations are known to the Kabbalists.* But lest anyone, led by vain superstition, think that all things are bestowed upon human mortality from heaven by the angels themselves, we therefore assert with **Reuchlin** <note>Johann Reuchlin, a famous German humanist and scholar of the Kabbalah.</note> (*On the Art of the Kabbalah, book 3*) that all things are done by the very majesty of God even in the angels, as if through instruments. This is also testified by the Prophet Daniel, saying to King Nebuchadnezzar: *According to his will, he does in the army of heaven and among the inhabitants of the earth.* For the word of God has impressed its own character upon every angel; hence Jehovah says of the Angel whom He placed at the head of the desert journey as a leader for Moses: *He will not bear your transgressions, because my name is in him.* And it is from this that the names of the angels end in *El* or *Iah*, such as *Michael, Haziel, Hahaiah, Iehuiah, Habriah*, etc. From this, it is clear that it is God in the angel who acts and incites the angelic creature to accomplish this or that according to His will, and not the angelic creature itself. However, insofar as the whole angel is considered—namely, its internal and external—it is indeed said to be done by the angel according to the worldly sense or the men of the world. Therefore, an angel, whether good or bad, can do nothing against the divine will, but is moved where and when it pleases God (or the Word marked within him) to lead him, so that he may execute his office in this or that place according to the Divine property leading or carrying him away.

Regarding the **star of Christ**, as the Magi intended when they said, *For we have seen his star* (*Matthew 2*), it was as if they had said it was led by His angel. Likewise, regarding the pillar of fire in which there was an angel, whom Jehovah placed before the Israelites on their journey, it is said: *Wisdom was a covering for the Israelites by day, and a starlight by night* (*Wisdom 10:17*). Concerning the whirlwind and the fiery chariot in which Elijah was snatched up into heaven (*2 Kings 2:1*); of the Angel having a face shining like the Sun, whose feet were like two pillars of fire (*Revelation*); of the 7 Angels by whose trumpet-blast stars fell and infected the sea and the land (*Revelation 8*); of the riders running through the air (*2 Maccabees 5:2*); and other such fiery wonders in the air, the sacred writings make mention. Also, regarding the **prester** <note>A "prester" is an archaic term for a fiery whirlwind or water-spout.</note> or fiery whirlwind which God sent through the mediation of angelic ministers (as history testifies) *upon Sodom and Gomorrah* (*Genesis 19*). Of which it is also said elsewhere: *He rained coals, fire, and sulfur upon the wicked, and a wind joined with a rare prester was the portion of their cup* (*Psalm 11:6*). Concerning the fire of God falling from heaven, similarly of violent winds, and of the whirlwind of the Lord, of which it is said: *Behold, the whirlwind of the Lord, a fury going forth, a rushing storm rests upon the heads of the impious* (*Jeremiah 30:23*). And elsewhere: *Behold, a whirlwind came from the North, and a great cloud, and a fire infolding itself, and a brightness was round about it, and out of the midst thereof the likeness of living creatures* etc. (*Ezekiel 1*). And elsewhere: Of all these things, *we shall be visited by the Lord God of hosts, in thunder, and shaking of the earth, and a great voice of whirlwind and tempest, and the flame of devouring fire* etc. (*Isaiah 29:6*). And also that when Jehovah was angry with them, *the earth was moved and trembled, the foundations of the mountains were shaken: and that smoke ascended from his nostrils, and fire from his mouth devoured, that coals were kindled by him, and that he bowed the heavens and came down, and darkness was under his feet* (*2 Kings 22:8*); and *that he ascended upon the Cherubim, and that he flew, and glided upon the wings of the wind, and that he made his darkness a hiding place round about, sifting the waters from the clouds above the heavens, and that because of the brightness in his sight the clouds were kindled, coals of fire fly out, and that the Lord thunders from heaven, and that the Most High gives his voice and sends his arrows, and scatters the impious with lightning, and that he makes the effusions of the sea appear, and the foundations of the world were revealed by the rebuke of the Lord, by the breath of his fury*, as we have it elsewhere in express words in the sacred source. In this we are taught that the attribute is given to Jehovah, even though He acts through the mediation of the Cherubic angels and His windy spirits, of whom it is said: *Who makes your angels winds, and your ministers a burning fire* (*Psalm 103/104*). So that from this testimony it is confirmed that God is the sole author and creator of these following meteors <note>In this historical context, "meteors" referred to any atmospheric phenomena, including rain, wind, and lightning, not just space rocks.</note>—namely, Earthquakes, Vapor or smoke, Lightning, the ceraunian stone, Clouds, Winds, Rain, Thunder, sea storms, etc.—all of which He, in His wisdom, guides through His angelic instruments, Himself being the central leader through His word...

### On the Efficient Cause of Meteors. <note>In the 17th century, the term "meteors" (meteorum) referred to all atmospheric phenomena, including rain, wind, lightning, and rainbows, not just falling stars.</note>

...is accustomed to produce; but this especially must be noted: that just as He produces good things—conveniences and benefits for the earth, water, and their creatures—through good angels, so He sometimes employs His evil ministers, both in His wrath toward the impious and to test His chosen ones. This is clearly declared in the History of Job; for Satan said to Jehovah,
> “Put forth your hand, and touch all that he has,” etc.
And Jehovah responded,
> “Behold, all that he has is in your hand.”
With this said, the power was given to Satan (and not before) to move the spirit of the Sabeans against Job’s servants, to send fire from heaven which burned up his sheep, and to send a great wind from the region of the desert, which struck and collapsed the four corners of the house upon Job’s children. Again, appearing a second time in the presence of Jehovah, he said to Him:
> “Whatever a man has he will give for himself; but put forth your hand, and touch his bones and his flesh,” etc.

By these words, Satan seems to confess that none of the things inflicted upon Job should be attributed to himself, but to Jehovah—whether it be the turning of the Sabeans' spirit, the calling down of fire from heaven, the stirring of the violent wind, or finally the infliction of diseases. Instead, he suggests all this was done by God, saying:
> “Put forth, I pray, your hand, and touch all that he has,” etc.
And then later:
> “But put forth, I pray, your hand, and touch his bones and his flesh,” etc.
And yet, nonetheless, he himself was the minister of the temptation and the divine execution. Hence Jehovah said:
> “Behold, he is in your hand.”
By these things it is clearly enough declared that whatever is performed by God, He is accustomed to execute through the mediation of His ministers, whether good or evil. In this sense, the Apostle speaks thus: *There are those who are called Gods in heaven and on earth, yet for us there is one God the Father, from whom are all things, and we in Him, and one Lord Jesus Christ, through whom are all things and we through Him* (1 Cor. 8:6). Here, by "Gods," he understands the angels. Hence David says, *The gods of the nations are demons, but the Lord made the heavens* (Psalm 96). And in Job they are called the sons of God (Job 1). From this, the Platonists said that all things are full of Gods. We have already spoken abundantly above, with many testimonies brought forth from the sacred page, concerning the overflowing snow and the harmful hail, and concerning the cold, ice, frost, and hoar-frost proceeding from the breath of Jehovah.

Finally, just as from the good angels Michael is assigned the protection of the East wind, Uriel that of the South, Raphael of the West, and Gabriel of the North—who affect the air with favorable and propitious breezes and produce meteors beneficial to the world—so indeed among the malignant spirits, Samael blows malevolently from the east, and likewise his other associates, namely Mahazael, Azael, and Azazel.

Furthermore, God is accustomed, through and in His windy spirits, to bring forth floods and deluges—either fatal or very beneficial to mortals—on account of men's disobedience and sins. As in the flood of Noah, He is said to have dried the waters by no other means than through the winds. Elsewhere it is said, *He turns the desert into a pool of water, and the dry land into water-springs* (Psalm 107:33). And that this is so is proven by these words: *With a strong East wind, Jehovah drove back the sea all that night, and turned the sea into dry land* (Exodus 14:21). And in another place: *By the blast of the nostrils of Jehovah the waters were gathered together* (Exodus 15:8). And then later: *You blew with your wind, and the sea covered them.* The Cabalists <note>Followers of Jewish mysticism; the author likely refers to Christian Cabalists like Johannes Reuchlin.</note> said that seventy-two angels were present at the division of the sea, counting those of the pillar of cloud and the pillar of fire; these seventy-two are called the "angels of division," as Reuchlin <note>original: "Reucl."; refers to Johannes Reuchlin, author of *De Arte Cabalistica*.</note> has it in book 3 of *The Cabalistic Art*. But however it may be, it is certain that just as floods of this kind are produced with the greatest intemperance and disturbance of the air, so the action of the turbulent spirit of God is required in the fulfillment of such divine will and command. It is the office of this spirit to carry out the word and pleasure of God, which we also have confirmed by the sacred page, which says *that the stormy wind fulfills the word of God* (Psalm 148:8). Furthermore, that this spirit is the cause of restlessness and storms at sea and the disturbance of lakes is to be drawn from these words of the Prophet: *He causes the spirit of the whirlwind to blow, and lifts up its waves; they mount up to heaven, they go down to the depths, etc. Then he makes the whirlwind stand in silence, and their waves are still, etc.* (Psalm 107). From these things it is clear that God acts to disturb the seas, lakes, and rivers through angels or "windy" ministers, whom the Prophet calls stormy spirits, fulfilling His word or will. He spoke and made the spirit of the whirlwind blow—that is, the stormy spirit. So it is said elsewhere, *With the East wind you break the ships of the ocean* (Psalm 48:7). And elsewhere, *He drove the East wind in the heavens, and by His power He brought in the South-west wind, and rained upon them.* From this, he seems to have understood those angels mentioned in the Apocalypse who held the winds so they would not blow, and made them blow again to harm the sea, the earth, and the fruits. The sacred page also mentions the corruption of waters in various places, and experience denotes that in many places of any region the air is infected with foul qualities, from which intermittent fevers mostly arise; and where the breath is more poisonous, it induces pestilential diseases, as in Scanderone <note>modern-day İskenderun, Turkey; historically notorious among travelers for its swampy, "unhealthy" air.</note> in the East.

Finally, Psellus <note>Michael Psellus, an 11th-century Byzantine philosopher and demonologist.</note> testifies that the subterranean genus of demons produces openings in the earth, shakes foundations, and even stirs up flame-vomiting winds. We also see that a great earthquake is said to have occurred because (it is said) an angel of the Lord descended from heaven, and his appearance was like lightning (Matthew 28:2). It is as if the Evangelist had said that by the appearance of that great angel, the demons, moved by terror, stirred and shook the earth, specifically because of the Creator's wrath. Hence elsewhere:
> The earth is shaken and moved, the foundations of the heavens are moved and shaken when His wrath is kindled against it.
