Just as in the Great World <note>The Macrocosm, or the universe at large.</note> there are found three regions of spirit, differing from one another in nature, dignity, and purity—namely the empyrean, the ethereal, and the aerial or elemental—so also are there found just as many species of spirit in man, or the Small World <note>The Microcosm.</note>, derived from those of the Macrocosm. Of these, the **intellectual or rational spirit** relates to the empyrean, the **vital spirit** to the ethereal, and the **natural spirit** to the elemental. 

In truth, that aerial spirit is the vehicle for the other two, just as the mundane air is the vehicle for influences—both the angelic ones sent from the empyrean heaven and the stellar ones falling from the ethereal heaven—since without this medium it would be impossible for them to be carried down to the earth. Hermes Trismegistus <note>A legendary Hellenistic figure, regarded as the author of the Hermetic Corpus, which combined philosophy, magic, and theology.</note> describes this communication of spirits and the duty of the air in that work most excellently in these words: 

> *The human soul (he says) is carried in this manner: the mind in reason, reason in the soul, the soul in the spirit, and the spirit in the body; where, diffused through the veins, arteries, and blood, it moves the living creature everywhere and sustains and transports the mass of the body.* (Hermes Trismegistus, Pimander, 10).

It is as if he had said: the trace of the Divine Word is in the empyrean spirit; the empyrean spirit descends, as if through a medium, into the ethereal spirit, which is the food of life (for through its veins the Soul of the World breathes); this vital spirit, along with the rational spirit (in whose center is the Divine Mind itself), descends into the air. Since the air is the vehicle for the others, it transfers them into the human body, in which it is disseminated everywhere through the blood (Genesis 5, 9). 

God himself seems to acknowledge this same thing, affirming that the soul of man is in the blood. From this we see that in the fabric of the internal man, three spirits are found, of which the lowest is air, the highest is divine, and the intermediate seems to participate in both. Hence it is that Plotinus and all the Platonists, following Hermes Trismegistus, placed three things in the internal part of man: the supreme, the lowest, and the middle. They establish the supreme as that divine thing which they call the Mind—that is, the Mind illuminated by the Intellect—which Moses calls the very "breath of life" <note>original: "spiraculum vitae"</note>, namely inspired into us by God or by His spirit. And that part is never damned or suffers. 

The lowest part they made the sensitive and natural soul, which they called the *Idolum* <note>An "image" or lower reflection of the soul.</note>, and the Apostle Paul calls the "animal man" <note>original: "hominem animalem"; the man governed by natural soul/senses rather than spirit.</note>, of whom he speaks thus: 

> *I see another law in my members, taking me captive in the law of sin.*

The middle is the intermediate spirit governed in a certain way by reason, which participates in both extremes; by means of this, they say the "animal soul" is joined with the Mind. But we also have this confirmed by Holy Scripture, for in one place we have: *The spirit of the strong God made me, and the breath of the Almighty gave me life* (Job 33:4). Of which spirit God himself speaks thus: *My spirit shall not remain in man forever* (Genesis 6:3 <note>Corrected from the text's 6:17</note>). 

In this speech, He intends the "breath of life" which He breathed into the first man; that is, the super-celestial spirit full of the Divine Mind, breathed out from the solar tabernacle in an ethereal spirit most full of life. Furthermore, mention is made of another spirit which is more familiar to beasts than to men, whence the wise man says: *the spirit of man and of the beast and their end is the same in all; as this one dies, so dies that one* (Ecclesiastes 3:19). In this speech, he seems to intend the aerial and sublunary spirit, which alone is subject to changes, corruption, and infirmities. Solomon understood this when he spoke in this manner: *The spirit of a man sustains and will bear his sickness* (Proverbs 18:14). And the Royal Psalmist, intending the same, says: *My soul is filled with evils* (Psalm 88:4).

Having known and most carefully weighed these things, it is worthwhile to consider that, just as Lucifer with his angels (full of pride, malice, and envy) was cast down from the kingdoms of the heavens into the lowest region of the world, filled everywhere with common air, so indeed his malice and violence avail nothing against the supreme or middle spirit in man. Rather, his entire force, power, and command is ultimately in the air, both of the Macrocosm and the Microcosm. Hence he is called by the Apostle: *The prince of the power of this air, who works in the children of disobedience* (Ephesians 2:2). And elsewhere: *Your struggle is not against flesh and blood, but against princes and powers, against the lords of darkness in this world, against the spirits of wickedness under heaven* (Ephesians 6). 

By these words, he seems to argue that just as the malignant demons, the enemies of men, were banished from heaven into the region under heaven (according to that passage in the Apocalypse <note>The Book of Revelation.</note>: *The devil, the dragon, the ancient serpent was cast out, who deceives the whole world* (Revelation 12)), so indeed their force and effort are occupied in the air under heaven, and not in that of the heaven itself, or the stellar, or the angelic heaven. For just as the good angels have their chief power in the good spirit, both of heaven...

# On the Efficient Cause of Atmospheric Phenomena <note>original: "De Causa Meteororum Efficiente." In this period, "meteors" referred to any atmospheric phenomenon, including wind, rain, and lightning.</note>

### Ii

...of both the middle and the highest [regions], so indeed do the evil spirits (whom Paul calls the lords of darkness) exercise their powers in the air and the sublunary or sub-celestial parts.

For since the air is external to the demon, and insofar as they are spirits of darkness, it is necessary that they have a close relationship both with the thicker air of the lowest order within man, and with the air of the world. Thus, they are able—and quite frequently accustomed—to join their aerial bodies with the thick spirit in man, producing in him such languors and diseases as are of the same nature and condition as the wind from which they are sent, or the element in which they more gladly rejoice and delight to dwell according to the disposition of their nature.

Concerning this communion of the demon with the aerial spirit, that wise man Artephius <note>A legendary alchemical author, often claimed to have lived for over a thousand years.</note> also testifies, when he speaks in this manner concerning fiery demons (as it seems) by way of explanation:

> *There are certain infirmities to which the Devil joins himself, namely when a humor <note>The "four humors" (blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile) were believed to govern human health and temperament.</note> departs from its proper balance and disturbs health itself. This happens most especially in infirmities arising from **cholera** <note>original: "cholera"; here referring to yellow bile, the hot and dry humor associated with fire and anger, not the modern bacterial disease.</note>, and the cause of this is because the nature of yellow bile is hot and dry like fire. The substance of the Devil, however, is composed of two things: namely, fire and air. His visible part is air, but his hidden part is fire. For this reason, he most easily joins himself with the aerial spirit of man when the fiery humor holds an unnatural mastery.* 

With these golden words, he clearly seems to declare that which we have already put forward. But because we have spoken more diffusely and fully on this subject in Chapter 5 of our *Mystical Anatomy of the Blood*, I refer you to Section 1, Portion 3, Part 3, Book 3, Chapters 5 and 12 of our *Triple Anatomy*.

We conclude, therefore, that those spirits who have power only over the air—or over the spirit in man which is subject to "fantastic" <note>Related to the "phantasy" or imagination.</note> changes—are either fiery or aerial. For it is the property of the **fiery** ones to inflame the air with a perceptible heat, exciting anger, fury, strife, contentions, and quarrels without any other manifest physical impediment. And just as the fiery angels of a holy condition are said to follow the mind of celestial souls (as those who concur in the contemplation of higher things), so indeed do these [evil] spirits kindle fire in the human air to darken the rays of the mind; they strive with great effort to carry the whole man headlong against the laws of reason. The **aerial spirits** also play their parts quite subtly in the human spirit so that they may more easily deceive him. For as it is the nature of the celestial order of aerial spirits to follow reason and favor the rational faculty—separating it from the sensual and vegetative faculties and serving the active path (just as the fiery ones serve the contemplative)—so indeed do aerial spirits of the worst condition use tricks and deceptive illusions to deceive men. They insinuate themselves into their spirit in such a way that they change their reason like **Proteus** <note>A Greek sea god capable of changing his shape at will; used here to describe shifting deceptions.</note>, making those things appear rational and approved by reason which are, in truth, nothing but fabricated and false images.

The manner by which they deceive men, and how they act secretly within the aerial spirit of man to seduce him from the true or sincere contemplation of God, is best described by Psellus <note>Michael Psellus, a Byzantine monk and scholar famous for his treatise on demonology.</note> from the revelation of Marcus:

> *They do not (he says) act upon the "fantastic" spirit of man by approaching it as spirits themselves, but they secretly remind us and whisper words of perturbation and pleasure to us. They do not send forth a voice by some striking or sound, but emit their speech without sound; for they speak by whispering in a hidden manner. Since they are able to be coupled with the aerial spirit because of the proximity of their natures, they need no sound at all in their hidden speech; rather, their speech, conceived as if by the will, creeps into the listener without any sound at all.*

In this way, therefore, demons of this kind are accustomed to converse with men secretly—so much so that we are not even allowed to perceive from where the war is being brought against us. Furthermore, just as air, when light is present, receives various colors and forms and transfers them into those things which can naturally receive them (as is clearly seen in mirrors, in water, and other such reflective surfaces), so also do the demonic bodies—receiving "fantastic" essences, figures, and colors from within themselves, and whatever forms they wish—transmit them into our very animal spirit. Hence, in this way, they provide us with much business, alluring us to various desires and suggesting various counsels. They show various forms, stir up memories of pleasures, and excite images of passions, both while we are awake and while we sleep. Sometimes, indeed, by titillating the thighs and groins of men, they incite them to lust and subject them to insane loves, sharpening them—especially if they perceive the humors of the body to be agreeable to this. But these spirits, putting on the **helmet of Pluto** <note>A classical metaphor for invisibility.</note>, disturb the soul with a certain art and sophisticated fraud. Over these cohorts of demons are many princes, of whom St. Paul speaks in this manner in the place cited above:

> *Your struggle is not against flesh and blood, but against Principalities and Powers, and the lords of darkness in this world, against the spirits of wickedness under heaven (Ephesians 6).*

That is, against the aerial demons and their legions, whose commander is that supreme Prince of this air who is accustomed to work in the "sons of defiance" <note>original: "filio diffidentiae"; usually translated in Bibles as "children of disobedience."</note>.

Concerning these Princes of the militia, mention has been made by us before: one of whom, by his office or...

...appropriately named **Beelzebub**, that is, the **Ancient God**, <note>original: "Vetustus DEVS." While Beelzebub is traditionally "Lord of the Flies," the author here interprets the name as a "False God" or "Ancient God" of the heathens.</note> under whose authority are those demons called the **False Gods** <note>original: "Pseudothei." From the Greek *pseudo* (false) and *theos* (god).</note>, who wish to be considered and worshipped as Gods; from this source, they scatter the seeds of idolatry in the human spirit. In this way, they entice humans toward sin; such was the one who tempted Christ, asking to be worshipped. Another is called **Python**, that is, the **Serpent**, under whom are the lying spirits and legions; he seduced Adam and Eve away from obedience to their creator with his lies, and with his false assertions he is accustomed to contaminate the children of Adam even to this day, so that they are rendered disobedient to God.

A common medieval etymology for Belial, signifying one who refuses the yoke of God's law.</note> the disobedient transgressor and apostate; the demons under his command are called **vessels of iniquity** by Jacob in the *blessings of Simeon and Levi, Genesis 49.* They are called **vessels of wrath**, **vessels of death**, in *Psalm 7* by the royal Psalmist; **vessels of fury** by Isaiah: *Isaiah 13*; **vessels of wrath** by Jeremiah, *Jeremiah 50*; and **vessels of slaughter and destruction** by Ezekiel, as they are likewise the inventors of evil arts.

The fourth is **Asmodeus**, that is, **the one executing judgment**, and under his command are said to be the avengers of crimes.

The fifth is **Satan**, under whose command are the **demon magicians and illusionists**; it is written of him in the Apocalypse that he seduces the entire world, performing great signs and making fire descend from heaven to earth in the sight of men, and thus seducing them.

The sixth is called **Meriris**, that is, the **raging and burning spirit**, to whom are subjected those spirits who produce storms in the air and infect the spirits of men with plague and corrupted air.

The seventh is called **Apollyon**, or **Abaddon** in Hebrew, that is, the **Exterminator and Destroyer**; under his governance are the demons called **Furies**, who are the sowers of evils, discords, wars, devastations, and so forth.

The eighth is **Astaroth**, that is, the **Explorer or Spy**, called in Greek the **Devil** <note>original: "Diabolus," meaning accuser or slanderer.</note>, that is, the **criminator and accuser**, who in the Apocalypse is called the **accuser of the brothers**, accusing them day and night in the sight of our God.

The last is **Mammon**, which is interpreted as **Greed or Covetousness**; he holds under him the demons of ambush and the tempters, and these are present to every human being.

By these types of **Evil Demons** <note>original: "Cacodæmonum." From the Greek *kakos* (evil) and *daimon* (spirit).</note> then, as they are the "powers of the air," the human spirit or air is afflicted in various ways; for they do not know how to actually reach his ether and intellectual spirit, as they have been expelled from heaven. The Devil is said to act in the spirit alone, or generally, and that from the beginning, as the producer and author of sin, which he produced in Adam by his lies, by which all the human race from then until this day has been contaminated. For (as the wise man says) God created man for an incorrupt condition, and made him in the image of his very own nature, but through the envy of the Devil, death entered the world, *Wisdom 2:23*; where by "death" he intends the sin that was the cause of death. Whence it is said, the Devil was a murderer from the beginning, and stood not in the truth, because there is no truth in him, *John 8*; and elsewhere, the Devil sins from the beginning, *1 John 3.* And the Apostle says: Sin entered into this world through one man, and death through sin, and so death passed upon all men, in whom all have sinned, *Romans 5.* But the author of this kind of sin was that spirit seducing with his lies.

### On the Efficient Cause of Meteors.

ii 2
<meta>catchword: Furthermore</meta>

Since there is such a natural proximity between the aerial spirit of man and the external spirit of a demon, it is very easy to believe that from the slightest cause, this demonic nature—by means of the air constantly breathed in through the mouth—can enter the human body. It joins with the air naturally enclosed within and, penetrating through the ears and nostrils, mingles with the phantastic spirit <note>The "phantastic spirit" refers to the faculty of imagination and the processing of mental images.</note>. Thus, it can entice and incline the nature and condition of that air toward its own will through secret appearances and persuasions.

Hence, it is said by Saint Paul: *You walked according to the Prince of the power of this air, who now works in the children of distrust <note>original: "diffidentiæ." Often translated as "disobedience," but here used to mean those lacking faith.</note>: Ephesians 2:2.* For where faith is present, he has no power; wherefore it happens that this prince, with his angels, tries in every way through secret whisperings and persuasions to first instill distrust into the human spirit, so that he may afterward have force and power over it.

How much indignation with GOD this Prince of malice brought upon the Israelites, by seducing them from the true worship of GOD to the adoration of himself, is expressed everywhere in the holy scriptures. Indeed, by his cunning, he enticed Solomon—the wisest of all men—to the worship of **Astaroth**. Furthermore, by the cunning of this same being, **Beelzebub** was held as an ancient God among the heathens.

False imaginations and appearances are also introduced to the human spirit by his primary minister, **Python**, along with his subjects. By these, not only common men but even the very Prophets of God are deceived, as is declared in the history of King Ahab: *A certain spirit, coming forth into the sight of Jehovah, said to him: I will go forth and be a lying spirit in the mouth of all the prophets, etc. 1 Kings 22.*

This kind of demon also imprints false hope upon the human spirit, just as we see a false and fictitious image superficially fixed in a mirror. Of such Hope, the wise man speaks thus: *The hope of the impious is like down carried by the wind, and like thin foam driven by a storm, and like smoke dissolved by the wind. Wisdom 5:15.* The effect of this vain hope is that it makes the soul sick, as Solomon testifies: *Proverbs 13:12.* And this is the reason why he imprints vain hope into the aerial spirit of man: so that this spirit, through its contact with the human "heaven" or the spirit within the co-ether <note>The author uses a "microcosmic" theory, where the human spirit mirrors the heavens; the "co-ether" is a subtle substance connecting the internal and external worlds.</note>, may mark it with false reflections of the thing expected.

He is also accustomed to inflate fury and wrath into the human spirit, by which the soul is evilly affected and reason is covered by a veil of error, so that during that time great crimes are usually committed. Concerning such a passion, the Sufferer <note>Referring to Job.</note> says: *The fool tears his soul in his fury: Job 18:4.* In this diabolical passion, Cain was drenched in his brother's blood, and his soul was miserably defiled by brotherly slaughter.

How much evil and how much misery did the disobedience of Adam toward GOD bring upon himself and his posterity? *Genesis 5.* How much affliction of both soul and body the obstinacy and disobedience of the Israelites during their journey through the desert caused, you have excellently explained by Moses: *Exodus 33.* Indeed, the fountain and origin of all sins is disobedience.

Furthermore, he seals deceitful, disguised, and treacherous imaginations like false Idols into the aforementioned spirit, and thereby renders hearts treacherous and weak; thus Satan is said to have entered into Judas and driven him with his hostile spirit to betray his Lord.

He also agitates human spirits toward discord, contention, and the desire for arms or war. This he accomplishes sometimes through the infection of the air—as after the appearance of a comet—and sometimes through secret whisperings and agitations.

We must therefore struggle, according to the admonition of the Apostle in *Ephesians 6*, against these spirits of malice under the heaven; wherefore the wise man gives us these lessons: *He loves transgressions who loves strife. Proverbs 17:19. And elsewhere: It is an honor for a man to cease from strife. Proverbs 20:3.*

And elsewhere: *When contention ceases, ignominy shall cease. Proverbs 22:10.* His first and principal minister in this action is called **Abaddon**, or **Apollyon**, under whom there are also infinite particular spirits ordained for this business.

And sometimes there are evil demons who are ordained by God to strike fear and terror into the aerial spirit of man, so that it is suddenly struck with a great stupor.

Regarding such a spirit, the sacred page speaks thus: *Behold, I will put a spirit in him, that he may hear a rumor and return to his own land. 2 Kings 19:7.* Furthermore, in another place it is said: *Be amazed and wonder, waver and stagger; be drunk, but not with wine; stagger, but not with drunkenness, for the Lord has mingled for you a spirit of deep sleep. Isaiah 29:9.* The Archangel says the name of God, **Elohim**, denotes dread and terror, whence the angels who correspond to it are called **Bene Elohim** <note>Sons of God.</note>, to whom he assigns the Northern region <note>original: "Aquilonarem." In biblical and mystical tradition, the North is the direction from which evil and judgment arise.</note>, as it is from there that all evil comes. Hence it is likely that such an office of terrifying and stupefying is assigned to these kinds of angels or demons.

Hence, those who are struck by sudden stupor and dread seem to grow stiff as if with cold and to be shaken as if with trembling.

### Section I. Portion IV. Part II. Book IV. Member II.

Furthermore, they also afflict the soul with sadness, sorrow, desolation, and mourning, as we see in melancholics <note>In the 17th century, "melancholy" was seen as both a physical disease caused by "black bile" and a spiritual condition where the soul was vulnerable to demonic manipulation.</note>. This disease is said to be caused chiefly by demons creeping into the human spirit and deluding it with false ideas. From this, they induce painful and pitiable symptoms within the aerial spirit of man. Hence Job says (since his spirit was contaminated by Satan): *My face is foul and swollen with weeping; finally, the shadow of death is on my eyelids. Job 16.* And elsewhere: *My spirit is narrowed within me. Job 21.* And the royal Psalmist says: *A broken mind brings on sickness, and when I look for one to grieve with me, there is no one; I am greatly weakened and crushed; I roar because of the groaning of my heart; my sighing is not hidden from you, my heart palpitates, and my strength has left me, etc.* And elsewhere more clearly: *Wasting of the soul, indignation, and sorrow make the mind fail, and groaning fills my years.* And in another place: *My spirit overwhelms itself within me; in my midst, my spirit seems desolate within itself. My spirit is consumed by your spirit; lead me into a level land—that is, into the right way, etc. Psalm 143.* <note>The author interprets the Latin "spiritus meus consumitur" as the human spirit being overwhelmed by a divine or external spiritual force.</note> But nevertheless, to a spirit so afflicted, he shows the way by the direction of his own mind, by which he may snatch himself from the power of the malignant spirit, saying in another place: *Why are you cast down, my soul, and why do you clamor within me? Hope in God, for I shall yet praise him, etc. Psalm 42:6.* By which he clearly teaches that there is another spirit in man <note>The "intellect" or "higher reason," which the author believes sits above the lower "animal spirits."</note> which stands above his lowest spirit and commands it, against which malignant demons can prevail neither by force nor by cunning—which Job also indicated in all his afflictions by his firm hope and patience.

Sometimes [the demon] drives the human spirit with the spurs of despair, so that he may snatch the whole man away into a "bad death," <note>original: "malam mortem." Likely referring to suicide or a death without repentance.</note> which indeed we read happened to Judas, the betrayer of the Savior of the world, and also to Saul.

Regarding the remaining impediments of the spirit—namely pride, gluttony, avarice, and others of this kind—the deceitful aerial spirits are accustomed to bring these impressions upon it in a pleasurable way, as if by flattering and subtly persuading, as was declared above.

Finally, among all the impressions of the Cacodemons <note>From the Greek "kakodaimon," meaning an evil spirit or devil.</note> upon the human spirit, blasphemy is the most dangerous to both the soul and the body. Those of whom David spoke in *Psalm 139* were obsessed by this kind of spirit of blasphemy, as was that blasphemer born of an Egyptian father and a Hebrew mother who cursed the name of Jehovah in the camps of the Israelites, *Leviticus 24.* Hence, where this spirit has insinuated itself into the lowest spirit of a man, it renders him not only hateful to men, but even rebellious and reprobate to God Himself.

We conclude, therefore, that the malignant spirits who have power only over the human spirit—without manifest contact with the body—are very thin, subtle, and of a higher condition in their aerial disposition. For those who are of a grosser consistency—whether vaporous, aquatic, or earthy—these are accustomed to strike the spirit in the body, and the body along with the spirit, by manifest and more sensible contact. Hence, spirits of a grosser consistency and fiery nature produce fiery diseases in both the spirit and the body that are perceptible to the senses, such as fevers; but if they are more earthy, then they bring on inflammations of the body and its solid parts, and so on for the rest, as will be discussed more broadly below. Meanwhile, it should be known that those spirits who act chiefly upon the phantastic spirit—that is, in the upper region of the human spirit—are spirits of subtle consistency; those, however, who operate upon the sensitive spirit <note>The "sensitive spirit" was thought to govern the five senses and physical movement.</note> are somewhat grosser in their constitution, etc. For just as there are differences in the sublunary air <note>The "sublunary" region refers to everything beneath the moon, which in traditional cosmology was the realm of change, decay, and the four elements.</note>, so there are also among the angels; and according to their nature in their own disposition, they are said to be either thicker or thinner.

# On the Efficient Cause of Meteors. <note>original: "De Causa Meteororum Efficienti." In this context, "meteors" refers not just to falling stars, but to any phenomenon occurring in the air—including vapors and disturbances within the "aerial spirit" of the human body.</note>

-> Evil spirits, acting maliciously in both body and spirit at once, typically produce: <-

| In the **Air** or the aerial spirit of the **Microcosm**: <note>The "Microcosm" is a central concept in Hermetic philosophy, viewing man as a "little world" that mirrors the structures and elements of the "Macrocosm" or universe.</note> | In **Water** or the phlegmatic element; attacks: | In **Earth**, or the solid part of the body; affections: |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Gases** <note>original: "Flatus"</note> leading to: **Bloating**, **Hypochondria**, **Colic**, **Dizziness**, **Epilepsy**, **Hysteria**, **Contagion**. | Leading to: **Paralysis**, **Epilepsy**, **Dropsy**, **Catarrh**. | Leading to: **Apoplexy**, **Stupor**, **Hemorrhoids**, **Knotted & Hard Tumors**, **Sulfurous eruptions**, **Scabs**, **Leprosy**, **Psoriasis**, **Carbuncles**, etc. |
| **Heat and fires** leading to: **Plagues**, **Fevers**, **Rages & madness**, **Inflammations**, **Painful conditions**. | **Discharges** leading to: **Bowel issues**, **Fistulas**, **Female complaints** — as inducing agents. | |

<column-break/>

Just as the power of the subtler aerial spirits is chiefly occupied with the **phantastic spirit** <term>phantastic spirit: the faculty of the soul responsible for imagination and forming mental images</term> of man in the disturbance of the mind alone (as has been said), so indeed some spirits of an inferior order have the duty to afflict both the body and the spirit simultaneously with plague and sickness. Thus we see that just as the highest portion of the air differs from the middle, and the middle from the lowest, so also we perceive that the "meteors" in these three regions differ from one another in both consistency and quality. And yet, nevertheless, as we have fiery meteors in the upper region, so we also have them in the middle and lowest, which communicate by a natural reason with earth and water. Therefore, the more a "meteor" is produced high up in the air, the less commerce it is observed to have with earth and water, and the more with air and fire; and all these things are governed by the spirit of that place.

It is therefore not surprising if some fiery spirits act upon the human spirit alone, inciting in it madness, **lycanthropy** <note>The delusion of being transformed into a wolf.</note>, anger, and heat, while others disturb the spirit and, through the spirit, the humors <note>The four bodily fluids—blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile—believed to control health and temperament.</note> and the body at the same time. Likewise, others are observed to reign in the humors and afflict the limbs of the body alone, while the aerial spirit remains untouched and free from feverish heat. For these are all, without a doubt, angelic ministers through whom God afflicts the spirits and bodies of sinners, not otherwise than the "Fountain of Truth" <note>A title for God or Christ.</note> testifies that He acts beneficially with men through good angels. Whence it is written: *He wounds and He binds up; He strikes, and His hands will heal. Job 5:18.* And elsewhere it says, *That God speaks by chastisement through pain in the bed, and makes all the bones waste away. Job 33:19-21.* And yet this is certain: although that duty is attributed to God, nevertheless His striking angel performs it, which even Satan himself confessed, saying, *"Put forth your hand against him," etc.* and nevertheless Satan himself afflicted Job with a most foul ulcer from the crown of his head to the soles of his feet. *Job 2:7.* Whence God is called, as it were, the **Ordainer** who brings on this or that disease, and yet He uses vengeful ministers to bring His decree into action.

It is therefore in the Divine will to afflict man with **aerial diseases**, in which manner Job was also vexed, as if by a hypochondriacal wind <note>In this period, "hypochondria" referred to the upper abdomen; "hypochondriacal winds" were vapors thought to rise from there to disturb the mind.</note> along with that Diabolical plague. Whence he was forced to say: *You have lifted me up into the wind or the blast; you set me upon it and cause my substance to dissolve. Job 30:22.*—as if he had been either stretched out by "windy bloating" <note>original: "tympanitide ventosa"</note> or by a gas from every side, which also very often happens in fevers where diseases are complicated. And **Albohali** <note>Al-Khayyat (c. 770–c. 835), a Persian astrologer whose works on "revolutions of the years" and medical astrology were influential in the West.</note> boldly says that windy and melancholic diseases are from evil demons. But...

It classifies various ailments (from hysteria to leprosy) based on whether they affect the air, water, or earth elements within the human "Microcosm," using the biblical suffering of Job as a primary example.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the discussion on the "aerial spirits" as the efficient cause of disease. Having established the theoretical framework for how these spirits interact with the human body (the Microcosm) in the previous section, the author now provides biblical evidence for diseases caused by spiritual intervention and begins a new chapter on the hierarchies of angels and the divine emanations known as Sephirot.</meta>

The royal Psalmist seems to assert that these aerial diseases proceed from wicked spirits with these words: *He cast upon them the fierceness of his anger, wrath, and indignation, and trouble, by sending evil angels among them.* <note>Psalm 78:49; the text cites 78:74, likely a variant or error in the source manuscript.</note> And elsewhere in the Holy Scriptures, we read that by the prayer of Elisha, a multitude of besiegers was struck with **scotomia** <term>scotomia: a dizziness accompanied by a darkening of the vision, often thought to be caused by vapors</term>, as seen in 2 Kings 6. It is also recorded that this same thing happened by angelic power to the Sodomites before the door of Lot’s house. Mention is also made of griping of the belly with painful colic, where it is found written: *You shall be shaken by a disease of the intestines, until they fall out because of that sickness,* 2 Chronicles 21. Does not the Holy Scripture intend to describe these types of flatulent or "windy" spirits where it is said: *The spirit of God blowing like a wind, and justice pursuing the unjust* (Wisdom 11:20) and elsewhere, *A spirit of power and a spirit of virtue shall stand against them, and like a storm and a whirlwind it shall toss them* (Wisdom 5:23). For of such a nature is the spirit of "windy" Epilepsy, of Vertigo and Scotomia, and of the **suffocation of the matrix** <term>suffocation of the matrix: an old medical term for hysteria, then believed to be caused by the womb moving upward and compressing other organs</term>, which is accustomed to disturb and toss the patient in the manner of a Macrocosmic whirlwind.

But to come to the effects of the "burning" spirits—namely plagues, fevers, rages, and madness, and other things of this sort—these are without doubt produced by malignant spirits of an aerial and fiery condition. Hence Job says: *The arrows of the Lord are within me, the poison whereof drinks up my spirit,* and *the terrors of the Lord set themselves in array against me.* <note>Job 6:4</note> Here, by "terrors," he understands evil angels inducing terrors, according to that which was cited from the Psalm: *He cast upon them his wrath and indignation through evil angels.* (Psalm 78). And elsewhere it is said: *You shall not be afraid for the terror by night; nor for the arrow that flies by day; nor for the pestilence that walks in darkness; nor for the destruction—or the demon—that wastes at noonday.* <note>Psalm 91:5–6</note> And elsewhere it is said: *Jehovah shall smite you with a consumption, and with a burning fever, and with an inflammation, and with an extreme burning, and with drought, and with blasting.* <note>Deuteronomy 28:22</note> In these cases, when Jehovah speaks, it is understood as Jehovah ordaining and His angelic ministers executing the command. For thus, when God afflicted the Israelites with a plague, David saw the angel of the Lord striking between heaven and earth; similarly it is said: *Jehovah shall smite you with madness and blindness.* <note>Deuteronomy 28:28</note> Even **Phrenitis** <term>phrenitis: acute delirium or inflammation of the brain</term> and **Lycanthropy** <term>lycanthropy: a form of madness where the patient believes they have turned into a wolf</term> arise from such an occult cause, namely from the stirring up of a malignant Demon, as is clear from that possessed man living in the tombs, moved by a tumultuous rage, who was agitated by a "Legion" of demons (Mark 5).

The Sacred Scriptures make ample mention of the afflictions of Paralytics, Epileptics, and Lunatics, as well as the uterine flows of women and cases of **Gonorrhea** <note>original: "Gonorrhoeae"; in this period, it referred generally to any discharge of seed or fluid, not strictly the modern venereal disease.</note>. Likewise, they speak of the Leprosy of Miriam, Naaman, Gehazi, and that on the forehead of King Uzziah; the gout of Asa; the hemorrhoids of the Philistines; the **King's Evil** <term>King's Evil: scrofula, a tubercular swelling of the lymph nodes</term>, ulcers, scabies, itching, and many other such things expressed in the Holy Word. In the place designated for them in the following volume, God willing, we shall speak of these more fully (see 2 Kings 2, 2 Chronicles 26, 2 Chronicles 16, 1 Samuel 5).

We conclude, therefore, since in this section you have the ministers of God described—both the benevolent and well-doing ones, and the malevolent ones who afflict with malicious disease—acting upon the world and its creatures as well as upon Man, who is the end and perfection of all creatures. Hence, among the Kabbalists, Man has for his appropriated symbol the last of the holy letters, namely **Tau**. God uses these ministers—if they are good—in mercy, goodness, and kindness toward the world and man; but if they are evil, He uses them in turn in His severity, wrath, and vengeance as a scourge for both the Macrocosm and the Microcosm.

Indeed, it must also be understood in this place that even His good angels sometimes execute the vengeance of God and His people upon men and the world; nevertheless, in this respect, they are regarded as "evil angels" by those who suffer their scourge. Hence Jehovah said: *Behold, I send my Angel before you... provoke him not, for he will not pardon your transgressions: for my name is in him.* <note>Exodus 23:20–21</note> But of these matters we shall speak more fully in the following volume, where we shall treat the causes of health and disease.

## CHAPTER VI.

Although we have already made clear mention of the nature of the ten **Sephirot** <term>Sephirot: in Kabbalah, the ten attributes or emanations through which the Infinite (Ein Sof) reveals itself and creates the universe</term> or divine numerations (which are diverse lights descending from a single root, by whose favor all things are created, and once created, are either nourished or changed from one state to another according to the property of God) in Tract 2, Section 1, Portion 2, Part 1, Chapter 3 of the *Theosophical, Kabbalistic, and Physiological Discourse*; nevertheless, because they seem to pertain primarily to this subject of ours concerning the natures of both good and evil angels (seeing as they seem to receive their offices from these properties of God), it has come to my mind to discuss them briefly in this place and re-examine the discourse.

<meta>This page continues the discussion on the spiritual causes of physical phenomena. Having previously mentioned how "windy" or "aerial" spirits cause diseases like epilepsy and vertigo, the author now transitions to a macrocosmic view: how divine energy descends from the Sephirot (the ten emanations of God in Kabbalah) through the angelic hierarchies and into the planetary spheres, where they influence both the weather (meteors) and human health.</meta>

# On the Efficient Cause of Meteors. 255

The influences of the first **Sephirah** <term>Sephirah: one of the ten attributes or emanations in Kabbalah through which the Infinite reveals itself</term>, namely those which descend from the "Luminous Gate" of **Kether** <note>original: "Cheter"</note> or the "Crown," over which the name *Ehieh* <note>Hebrew: "I Am," the divine name associated with the highest emanation</note> presides—which is said to represent God the Father—glide and flow downward into the first order of Angels, the **Seraphim**. From there, they are led further down by that great Angel **Metatron** into the *Primum Mobile* <term>Primum Mobile: the "first moved" sphere in the geocentric model, which carries all other spheres from east to west every 24 hours</term>, attributing to it the force and vigor by which it turns the celestial orbs from the east to the west in the space of a single day. For this reason, Metatron is established as the governor of the *Primum Mobile*, from which he liberally rains down essence and the faculty of motion upon the lower things. For, according to the Kabbalists, *Ehieh* bestows the gift of being, and thus it is Metatron’s office to flow vital things into creatures. This is the reason why he is considered the **Soul of the World** <note>Anima Mundi: a concept where the universe is a living being with an underlying spiritual soul</note>. In this action, the property of God brings mercy and kindness to the world.

The outflows of the second **Sephirah**, or "Luminous Gate," called **Chokhmah** <note>original: "Hochma"</note> or "Wisdom"—over which the divine name *Yah* or *Jehovah* presides—fall into the order of the **Cherubim**. From that order, they are entrusted to the guardianship of the Archangel **Jophiel**, or as others prefer, **Raziel** <note>original: "Ruziel"</note>, so that through him they may be introduced into the eighth sphere <note>the sphere of the Fixed Stars, beyond the planets</note>. From there, they are poured into the lower realms, both celestial and elementary. By their power, the fixed stars—both within the Zodiac and outside its belt—are observed to act upon the lower things, producing various likenesses of life, especially of animals. Hence the "Zodiac" is named from the Greek word *Zoon*, which means "animal." And it is from this that **Cecco d'Ascoli** <note>original: "Cichus Esculus," a 14th-century Italian polymath and astrologer</note>, in his book on the sphere, not ineptly asserted that every animal on earth or in the void symbolizes and agrees in nature with some sign in the Zodiac of the same name. Furthermore, **Maimonides** <note>original: "Moyses Arabicus," the medieval Jewish philosopher Maimonides</note> says that every animate thing has a star in the heavens flowing into it, to protect and preserve its essence.

But truly, since every heaven or sphere, and consequently all its stars, have their own great Angel to move and govern them, and to lead the influences from God through the "intellectual heaven"; and since many principal leaders are subject to each of these royal Archangels, who have many legions of spirits of lower condition under their dominion, we therefore say that each of these spirits <note>original: "dæmonum," used here in the classical sense of intermediary spirits, not necessarily evil beings</note> has its own peculiar office both in the heavens and in the elements. **Hermes Trismegistus** <note>the legendary Hellenistic figure associated with alchemy and magic</note> seems to confirm this in part in *Pimander*, Book 3, with these words:

> *The Gods were recognized in the ideas of the stars with their signs, and the stars were numbered according to the Gods who inhabited them,*

where by "Gods," he seems to mean spirits. The influence of the third **Sephirah**, which is **Binah** or "Prudence" <note>usually translated as "Understanding"</note>—over which the name of God *Elohim* presides—passes through the order of the **Thrones** and is received by the Archangel **Zaphkiel**, or as others prefer, **Jophiel**. He leads it into the sphere of **Saturn**, where it has its own peculiar virtue and property distinct from the other planets. Hence, this planet rains down Saturnine influences, or Saturnine spirits and species, upon the earth, especially at that time when it has dominion in the sky; for then its effects appear more evidently in the elements. These effects are for the most part gloomy and not at all favorable to the world or the human spirit, which is why it is called the **Greater Misfortune** by astrologers.

The influences of the fourth "Luminous Gate," called **Chesed** or "Clemency"—over which the name of God *El* presides—descend into the order of the **Dominations**. Through them, they are carried down by the Archangel **Zadkiel** into the sphere of **Jupiter**, mercifully tempering its nature. Thus it happens that the outflows sent down from it are benevolent and gracious to both the air and the human spirit, as they are said to nourish and cherish natural strengths. Hence, it is called the **Greater Fortune** by astrologers.

The luminous influences of the fifth Gate, called **Geburah**—that is, "Punishment"—over which the name of God *Elohim Gibor* <note>God the Mighty</note> presides, penetrate through the order of the **Powers**. They are led by the Archangel **Camael** (or **Samael**) into the sphere of **Mars**, where they animate the fiery spirits of Mars with a burning and inclement severity. Therefore, this planet is not without reason called the **Lesser Misfortune** by astrologers. For just as the influences of Saturn are accustomed to act harshly upon the elements of the world and its creatures by way of extreme cold and dryness, so the Martial spirits bearing arms under the leadership of **Samael** afflict the fiery air of the world with burning, lightning, comets, and many other troubles, and they infest the human spirit with heat, fever, plague, and inflammations.

The sixth Luminous Gate is called **Tiphereth**, which is "Grace" <note>usually translated as "Beauty"</note>, over which the name of God *Eloah* superintends. It flows through the order of the **Virtues**, and the Archangel **Michael** is, by office, the receiver of its influences. He translates them into the sphere of the **Sun**, from whose golden world gracious, splendid, and life-giving virtues are rained down into the lower parts. These are called **Solar spirits**, which never act maliciously unless they are corrupted by the spirits of the wicked planets.

The seventh, called **Netzach** <note>original: "Netzeth"</note> or "Triumph" <note>usually "Victory"</note>, over which the name of God *Jehovah Sabaoth* is placed, sends its benevolent inspirations into the order of the **Principalities**. From there, they are led down by the Archangel **Hanael** into the sphere of **Venus**. Thus it happens that the favorable spirits of Venus emit inspirations into these lower parts; for this reason, Venus is called the **Lesser Fortune** by astrologers, as she is nearer in nature and condition to the human race after Jupiter.

The eighth, called **Hod**, that is, "Praise" <note>usually "Glory"</note>, over which the name of God *Elohim Sabaoth* presides, sends out and transfuses its influences through the order of the **Archangels**. These are received by the Archangel **Raphael** and are applied to supply the virtues of the orb of **Mercury**, who again pours his spirits into the lower world, which are imparted everywhere from the said property of the Creator.

### Section I. Portion IV. Part II. Book IV. Member II.

The ninth **Sephirah** <term>Sephirah: one of the ten divine emanations in the Kabbalah that act as channels of God's creative power</term>, called **Yesod** <note>original: *Iesod*</note> or "redemption," over which the divine name **Shaddai** <note>original: *Sadai*; the Hebrew name *El Shaddai* is often translated as "God Almighty" or "The All-Sufficient"</note> presides—meaning God who is sufficient unto Himself—sends the inflows of its light into the order of angels. From there, the Archangel **Gabriel** receives these influences and pours out and directs them into the sphere or globe of the Moon. Within this sphere, there are several Princes of angels corresponding to the various **Mansions of the Moon** <term>Mansions of the Moon: 28 divisions of the lunar orbit, each associated with specific spiritual and earthly effects</term>. These spirits, in various ways depending on the Moon’s changing relationship to the Sun, rain down these outflows into the lower regions. Each of these spirits has legions beneath them which, in their own time and according to the Moon's motion, exercise their powers in the elementary world. 

For a more exact observation of this matter, we have presented here these **Intelligences** <term>Intelligences: the presiding spiritual beings or angels of celestial bodies</term> according to the number of the mansions they govern, together with their meanings and the names of the mansions.

# On the Efficient Cause of Meteors.

Finally, the tenth numbering, **Malkuth** <note>original: *Malcut*</note>, which is called "Kingdom," and over which the name **Adonai** <note>original: *Adonai*; meaning "Lord"</note> presides, sends its influences downward into the order of holy souls, as the **Cabalists** <term>Cabalists: practitioners of Kabbalah, a tradition of Jewish mysticism that explores the nature of God and the universe</term> say. There they imagine these influences are committed to the power of the soul of the **Messiah**, and that this order communicates them to these lower regions. From these things, therefore, it is right to see and notice that whatever exists in this world—whether it be super-celestial or angelic, or celestial and starry, or finally elementary—it is evident and clear that all this comes from an immediate emanation from **GOD**. For it is His power or **fiery breath** <note>original: *spiraculum igneum*</note> by means of which, and in no other way, all things in the world are made, brought into action, and endowed with motion. This is according to the words of the sacred page: "GOD fills all things." And elsewhere: "GOD is the Father of all, who is above all, and through all, and in us all" (Ephesians 4). And elsewhere: "From GOD are all things" (1 Timothy 6). And elsewhere: "GOD works all things in all" (Ephesians 4:6). And elsewhere: "The incorruptible Spirit of GOD is in every thing" (Wisdom 12). 

But this is also explained most excellently and with a somewhat clearer thread in another place, where the Apostle seems to declare in plain words (2 Corinthians 5) that neither angels, nor the stars over which they preside in heaven, nor spirits, nor men, nor any other creatures on earth—however much the title of "Gods" might be attributed to them—can work anything by themselves or in themselves. Rather, it is only He who created heaven and earth, who is "all in all." The words of the Apostle are these: "For though there be those called gods in heaven and on earth, yet to us there is but one GOD the Father, from whom are all things, and we in Him; and one Lord Jesus Christ, through whom are all things, and we through Him" (1 Corinthians 8). From this, John says: "By the Word all things were made" (John 1). Of this the Prophet also says: "God says this, creating the heavens, stretching them out, establishing the earth and those things that sprout from it, giving breath to the people who are upon it, and spirit to those who walk upon it" (Isaiah 42:5).

By these citations it is clear that from this divine emanation or breath of GOD—which the angels serve as ministers according to the will of Him who sent it—heaven, earth, and all things were made, and without it nothing exists. Wherefore also these primary angels are called by the royal Prophet "angels of God, most mighty in strength, fulfilling His word, doing His pleasure or His will" (Psalm 103). But even these are not said to "make" things themselves, but rather God does so by means of His Word or emanation. Therefore, the wise believe that all operations—both good ones, according to their benevolent inflows, and evil ones, according to the disposition of malevolent inflows—are usually performed by **GOD**, as the immediate actor, through the angels acting as the instruments in which **GOD** works.

For as was said before, the Name, or the Word, or the divine Light dwells within the angels, and it stirs the angelic composition to execute the divine will; nor can they move to perform this or that without His action. No more can we move or act unless by the impulse of the divine act, according to that saying in the Acts: "In GOD we live, and move, and have our being" (Acts 17). "From Him, in Him, and through Him" (says the Apostle) "are all things; to Him be praise and honor." And this is the reason why philosophers say He is "the center of every thing, whose circumference is nowhere"—that is, outside of all things. And this Prince or Disposer of created nature was called by **Zeno** <note>Zeno of Citium, the founder of Stoicism</note>, along with Saint John, the **Logos** <term>Logos: the "Word" or "Reason"; in this context, the divine intellect that orders the universe</term> or Word that produces understanding of itself and depends on no other. The Hebrews call Him **Shaddai** <note>original: *Sadai*</note>, that is, "Self-Sufficient" in every business. This Word, insofar as it is diffused throughout the entire nature of things, is called by the **Platonists** <term>Platonists: followers of the philosophy of Plato, who often spoke of a "World Soul"</term> the **soul of the world** <note>original: *mundi anima*</note>.

But here perhaps some may wish to object that if **GOD** or this divine emanation does all things, then **GOD** is also the author of evil and sin. To this we respond with Elihu to that patient man [Job]: "Far be wickedness from the strong GOD, and iniquity from the Almighty; the strong GOD does not act wickedly, nor does He pervert judgment" (Job 34:10-11). And yet it is said by the wise man that God does whatever He wills, and "no one is to ask Him, what or why do You do so?" (Wisdom 12:12). How then can we judge the divine act, or say of it that He has acted either well or poorly toward the world or toward man? "The secrets of GOD" (says the Holy Bible) "no one knows, but they remain with GOD." And yet elsewhere we read "that good and evil, life and death, poverty and honor are from GOD" (Ecclesiasticus 11:14). And in another place we find this: "Consider the works of GOD, that no one can correct whom He has despised; in the good day enjoy good things, and beware of the evil day; for as He made the one, so He made the other, so that man may not find just complaints against Him" (Ecclesiastes 7:14). And elsewhere it is said: "Is there evil in a city which the Lord has not done?" And elsewhere: "**GOD** has power over life and death; He leads down to the gates of death and brings back again" (Wisdom 16). And in another place this same thing is explained more clearly: "With Him is wisdom and strength; His is counsel and understanding. Behold, He withholds the waters so that they dry up, and He sends them out so that they overturn the earth; with Him is strength and power; both the wanderer and the one who leads into error are His. He makes counselors go mad, and makes judges fools; He looses the bond of kings... He makes leaders go mad and perverts the most cunning. He increases nations and destroys them; He expands nations and leads them away; He takes away the heart from the chiefs of the earth and makes them wander like a drunkard, groping in the dark where there is no light" (Job 12).

Finally, since the cause of original sin was unbelief, and that unbelief was introduced by **GOD** from the beginning, certainly it would be difficult (it seems to me) to deny that **GOD** Himself introduced the origin of that sin into the world for the exaltation of His name and glory. For that ancient serpent could not have enticed Eve to disobedience by her unbelief without the incitement and will of God, since (as the Apostle says) all things are moved by **GOD**. Indeed, the Devil can in no way act or move without the divine will and permission, which he himself confesses in these words: "Stretch out...

Sect. I. Port. IV. Part. II, Lib. IV. Membr. II.

*“...stretch out your hand a little, and touch all that he possesses.” Job 1:11. And elsewhere, “But put forth your hand now, and touch his bone and his flesh,” etc.* <note>original: “paululum manum tuam, & tange cuncta quæ possidet... Alioqui mitte manum tuam, & tange os & carnem”</note>

Satan says these things to **Jehovah** <note>original: *Iehouam*</note>, and yet it was nevertheless Satan who brought the wind from the desert, who called down the fire of **GOD** from heaven, who moved the hearts of the neighboring **Sabeans** <note>A people from the kingdom of Sheba, located in modern-day Yemen or Ethiopia</note> against Job, and who afflicted him and struck him with a malignant ulcer from the sole of his foot to the crown of his head. Therefore, when he says, “put forth your hand and touch him,” he seemed to imply that God incited the Devil himself—as if he were his own servant whom he uses as a whip against men—or that He granted permission to do this. For it appeared this way based on the result; and indeed, Jehovah seems to acknowledge this same thing in express words, as found in the Prophet **Isaiah 54:16-17**: *“Behold, I have created the smith who blows the coals in the fire and produces a vessel for his work; I have created the destroyer to ruin.”* <note>original: “Ecce ego creans fabrum sufflantem in igne prunas... Ego creaui interfectorem ad disperdendum”</note> By these words, He seems to intimate that the Devil was expressly created by God to lead us into sin and to be a destroyer for us.

Furthermore (says the **Apostle** <note>Referring to St. Paul</note>), if there were no law, there would be no sin; but man's disobedience was the cause of external law and severity. That **Spiritual Legislator** <note>Christ</note> desires to heal the wounds of this law in his mercy through faith (which is the internal law or the anchor of Christ) and to wipe away the scars. If He had not given the law, sin would not have been introduced. However, **GOD**, insofar as He is not subject to the law, cannot sin, nor can He act unjustly, since He gave the law not to Himself but to man. Consequently, He cannot be called the author of sin. Therefore, He does whatever He wills, and yet in Him there is no iniquity. We say with Job (as above): *“Far be it from the mighty GOD to do wickedness, and from the Almighty to do iniquity: for the mighty GOD does not act wickedly, nor does He pervert judgment.” Job 34:10-11.* <note>original: “absit à DEO forti improbitas... non enim agit DEVS fortis improbe”</note>

And yet, for no sin of Job's, but solely to fulfill His own will (which might appear as injustice in the eyes of men), He laid His hand upon Job. But nevertheless, to demonstrate that there is in truth no injustice in GOD despite all this, the wise **Elihu** <note>The youngest of Job's friends who defends God's justice</note> broke out into the aforementioned words for Job's consolation. GOD certainly holds in His secret counsel what is to be done, yet His actions are not to be judged according to the imaginations of men. For sometimes He appears to act severely, and occasionally—indeed, most often—He appears to act mercifully toward the world and man. Yet all His actions are consistent and uniform within Himself; the entire difference lies in their effect regarding men. Whatever He Himself does, He does so that His name may be celebrated among men, and that He may be rightly known and celebrated by them. So that they might acknowledge His final mercy, He placed unbelief and sin among men, so that He might finally extend His mercy to them when they sin anew. *“For GOD does whatever He wills, and no one is going to ask Him, what or why do You do so?” Wisdom 12:12.* <note>original: “Nam DEVS quicquid vult facit, & nemo eum est interrogaturus quid aut cur ita facis?”</note> But the Apostle seems to signify all of this to us in the clearest words—words truly golden and to be contemplated with a clear eye: “GOD has shut up all things in unbelief, that He might have mercy on all.”

> O the depth of the riches of the wisdom and knowledge of GOD! how incomprehensible are His judgments, and His ways past finding out! For who has known the mind of the Lord? or who has been His counselor? or who has first given to Him, that it should be repaid to him? For from Him, and through Him, and in Him are all things: to Him be honor and glory forever. Amen. Romans 11:32-36.

What can be more brilliant than these words of the divine Apostle? In them, he seems primarily to assert that GOD placed and concluded all things in unbelief, or as the **interlinear translation** <note>original: *testamentum interlineatum*; likely referring to a polyglot Bible or a specific scholarly edition with Greek/Latin word-for-word translation</note> has it better:

“GOD has concluded all in unbelief, that He might have mercy on all.” The reason is so that He might make men obligated and grateful to Him for His mercy. Furthermore, it is so that this or that man might not say and argue that this is impossible and contrary to the sense of the **Holy Scriptures** <note>original: *sacrarum literarum*</note>, which seem to pronounce that many—indeed, the greater part of men—are to be damned, and the smaller part saved. Because this saying might seem harsh and improbable, the Apostle responds to such inconsistency, saying: *“O the depth of the knowledge of GOD! how incomprehensible are His judgments! For who has known the mind of GOD? or who has been His counselor? or who has first given to him?” etc.*

By these things, he seems to argue that the sense of Holy Scripture is so deep that it is not within human perception to comprehend what GOD intends for Himself. Does not the Apostle confess elsewhere that *“the letter kills, but the spirit gives life”*? And Christ Himself admitted that He spoke in mystery and in the manner of parables, and He warned His disciples to do the same. Nevertheless, we ourselves wish to be judges and expositors of divine counsels and judgments. But let us proceed to the final clause of the conclusion: *“For from Him, through Him, and in Him are all things,”* etc.

From this, therefore, he concludes that neither this—whether it be some mark of unbelief or an act of the Devil—nor that—whatever it may be of goodness—exists except from God; for from Him, through Him, and in Him are all things. This is true even though, in human consideration, we refer those things which happen to us badly and perversely to the Devil or the **Prince of Darkness**, while we attribute those things which happen kindly and mercifully to God. And yet, the Sacred Scriptures show that GOD brings evils upon men in His heat and wrath, just as they conversely confirm that all benefits to men proceed from GOD in the property of His mercy.

### Concerning the Efficient Cause of Meteors. <note>In this context, "meteors" refers to all atmospheric phenomena, including wind, rain, and lightning, rather than just falling stars.</note>
Kk 2
<meta>catchword: Chapter.</meta>

The Cabalists <note>Jewish mystics who studied the hidden meanings of the Hebrew Bible</note> also wisely indicated all of this through the differences of the various titles attributed to GOD in the sacred text. These various names, as the wise have observed, produced various effects in the biblical passages cited. Because of this, they assigned to these names various luminous properties, which they believed descended through as many "bright gates"—differing in quality—as there are names.

And they called these gates Sephirot, or the "numerations" of the Cabalists. They fashioned some of these as leaning toward severity and others toward mercy, according to the nature of the matter being treated in that part of the sacred page where those divine names are recited. From those properties of God, they observed Him to be either severe—inclined toward the cursing of the world and man—or inclined toward the blessing of those creatures. For this reason, they attribute to Him the name and office of both "Destroyer" and "Preserver." Do we not also see that this spirit, creating and working all things, is the author of both corruption <note>decay or breaking down</note> and generation <note>birth or creation</note>? In corruption, the form is taken away and the thing is destroyed—and what can happen to a creature more grievous than death and the deprivation of life? Yet in generation, it acts in the opposite way, namely by adding the nourishment of life, by preserving, and by not destroying at all.

From this it followed that the mystic poets, who were well-versed in the deep mystery of nature—namely Orpheus, Hesiod, Euripides, Aeschylus, etc. (with whom Proclus <note>A Neoplatonist philosopher</note> also seems to agree)—called GOD by the name of Apollo or Phoebus during the day. They say he carries grace in his right hand and a bow in his left. They call Him Dionysus during the night, whom they say tears things and himself into seven parts; but in his daytime state, insofar as he is called Apollo, he is said to once again assemble those things which he tore apart at night. For this reason, he is called the leader of the number Seven, which results from one, two, and four added together <note>1 + 2 + 4 = 7</note>, from which results the Octave <note>original: *Diapason*, the fundamental interval in musical harmony</note>, which is perfect harmony. Thus, the number Seven is attributed to him insofar as he is the author of both life and dissolution. These are composed of the first odd number, namely three, and the first even number, which is four <note>3 + 4 = 7</note>. For the number two is called the "number of confusion" by the Pythagoreans. From even and odd numbers or proportions—as if from the passive and the active—all things are generated, and by that same path they are also resolved. But generation comes from the supernal light, which participates in the number three; whereas corruption is of the lower regions and the "tearing night." In this act, he is called "Dionysus the Tearer," and in the daytime "Apollo the Comer," for by his presence all evils are dispelled. Hence, by the ancients, he was called *Appellin* instead of Apollo. And the Athenians called him *Alexicaton* <note>original: *Alexicaton*, from Greek meaning "averter of evil"</note>, that is, the dispeller and driver-away of evil; and by Homer he was called *Ulion* <note>original: *Vlion*, likely from Greek *oulis*, meaning "healing" or "health-giving"</note>, that is, the author of health, since by his unity all things are preserved in perfect consonance. But as he suffers division, he is referred to by the even number and is the God of darkness, deprivation, and destruction. It is in this sense that David seems to speak:

> *You take away their spirit, and all things left behind fail in themselves. But he also wrote more clearly: When God sends forth his spirit, the creatures are recreated; when he hides his face, they are troubled; when he takes back their spirit, they expire and return to their dust. Psalm 104:29-30.*

From these things, therefore, we see that it was the opinion of the Pagans <note>original: *Ethnicorum*</note> that the same God, in respect to his contrary properties of severity and mercy, was sometimes the Prince of Darkness, destroying all things, and sometimes the Prince and Commander of Light, generating and vivifying all things. But in the resolution of this doubt of ours, I most willingly submit myself to the most learned theologians of this age; nor indeed would I have cast myself headlong into a sea of such controversy, had not the necessity of rendering an account of the subject at hand—namely, the Cabalistic Sephirot and the dual contrary properties contained within them—compelled me. But now, I shall hasten with a light step to the history of the Angels who have duties concerning these Sephirotic influences.

Section I, Portion IV, Part II. Book IV. Member II.

# CHAPTER VII.

->Concerning the Angels of the Sephirot, and first of all concerning that great and imperial Angel of light called Metatron, and then afterwards concerning that great Angel of darkness, opposite to him in nature and disposition.<-

From the two-fold <note>original: "bina," referring to the duality of mercy and severity</note> arrangement of divine properties poured out from the Sephirotic parts, two orders of Angels arise, opposite in nature and condition. One of these is engaged in benevolence, while the other is engaged in malice toward the human race, which is the goal of creation. On this foundation are established those philosophers <note>Referring to the Pre-Socratic philosopher Empedocles</note> who placed two principal powers in the world, namely strife and friendship, the latter of which reconciles things while the former disperses them. From this it followed that, just as it was the role of Apollo, according to the intention of the Poets, to compose and unite with the bonds of harmony, so it was the property of Dionysus to destroy what was composed through the antipathy of discord and to scatter what was united. And yet, both Apollo and Dionysus represented only a single essence of divinity, emitting the operation of its acts in a two-fold form and according to its own will—namely, either in mercy and piety, or in its severity and indignation toward its creatures. For just as we see in the same fire—unchanged in both its shape and quality—a benevolent and life-giving nature as well as a destructive and malevolent one (inasmuch as it tends to scorch when a combustible thing is brought too close, yet warms a living creature sweetly and kindly from a distance), so it is with these: the same and immovable source acts either kindly or destructively according to the varying method of its rays or its emitted emanation, following its own will and pleasure.

For this reason, therefore (insofar as He is accustomed to act immediately through His angelic ministers, who are called the intermediaries between God and His creatures), He created and made them like vessels: some fit to receive His benevolent outpourings, others malevolent ones tending toward severity. It follows, then, that regarding these two properties, some angels are called good, others evil; some friends of men, others enemies; some preservers, others exterminators, wasters, and destroyers; some of life and health, and again others of death and diseases. But since all angels whatsoever, insofar as they are intellects, terminate in one spiritual Christ <note>The author identifies the Logos or the "World-Soul" with the highest angelic intelligence</note> as the royal, greatest, and primary angel, who contains in himself both the nature of angels and of GOD, and in whom all things end (for "from him, in him, and through him are all things," as the Apostle <note>Saint Paul in Romans 11:36</note> and Plato in his letters say), so those skilled in hidden <term>Theosophy</term> <note>literally "divine wisdom," referring here to mystical knowledge of God's workings</note> called this Messiah of the world the good, royal, and greatest angel who predominates over the others. He receives his flows of life and the primary essence of the world from *Ehyeh* <note>original: "Ehiieh," the Hebrew name for God meaning "I AM"</note> through the Crown <note>original: "Cheter," the first Sephirah, Keter</note> and directs them into the <term>primum mobile</term> <note>the "first moved" sphere, the outermost part of the universe that moves all other celestial spheres</note>, from which motion, act, and existence are then imparted to both celestial and lower creatures, and even to the demons and spirits wandering everywhere through the world. I have judged that the <term>Cabalists</term> <note>Jewish mystics and their Christian followers who interpreted the Bible through hidden systems</note> considered this primary Angel to be the Angel of Christ, as will be explained more broadly below. Others have called him Michael, the presiding officer of the Sun itself; but since it might seem uncertain to the reader how the wise understood one for the other—and quite sensibly accepted them— we will briefly reveal our opinion on this matter.

They indeed called this great Angel *Metatron* <note>original: "Metattron"</note> insofar as he was the first emanation of the world's life and existence, by whose presence all things in the world's cavity are illuminated, and darkness is driven toward the center. And as an emanation or flow of this kind was made benevolent by the first <term>Sephirah</term> *Keter* <note>original: "Cheter"</note> or "the Crown," he is therefore related to the guardianship, office, and even existence of the greatest angel, Metatron. But insofar as this primary light, thus spread through the spirit of the world, was contracted on the fourth day of creation into the mass of the Sun by the power of the influx of *Tiphereth* <note>the Sephirah associated with Beauty and the Sun</note>, so this great name Metatron passes into that of *Michael*, as will be seen more broadly below; thus, in this, the Cabalists seem not to have strayed far from the truth. Therefore, I have proposed to speak significant words in this place concerning the imperial power of such a great angel under both names, because he is the great distributor of life, form, and existence both to the world and its creatures, and especially to man; the nourisher and sustainer of souls, the kind favorer of health and salvation, and the benevolent author of position and generation. And insofar as he is opposed by the malevolent prince of this world, who is contrary to him in all things by nature and condition—being the destroyer of life, the enemy of health, and the leader and author of deprivation and death—as will be seen in the following chapter.

Moreover, the nobility of this angel is so great with respect to his first lineage, and his dignity so great with respect to his office, that he is considered not only prior in birth and place to every creature, but also superior in position and duty to all spirits of his kind, and richer in gifts. As for what pertains to his origin and lineage, he is said to be Wisdom herself, who came forth from the mouth of the Most High before all things. *Wisdom (says the Wise Man) was created before all things, and the understanding of prudence from everlasting; the fountain of wisdom is the word of GOD on high, etc. Ecclesiasticus 1:4-5.* For when the will existed, it immediately flowed out through the bright gate of *Keter* or the Crown,

...crown, that primary emanation by whose power all things were brought from nothingness into being and action in the blink of an eye; and this very emanation is called Wisdom, from which then later a second outflow through the bright gate emerged immediately from the secret bosom of the Almighty. But the wise man also seems to confirm this elsewhere as follows:

> *Wisdom is a pure emanation or a certain flow of the clarity of almighty GOD, or the splendor and brightness of eternal light. Wisdom of Solomon, Chapter 7.*

And it is for this reason that this God-like Angel—that emanation or flow of divine majesty—is taken for the spiritual Christ, as stated before; as if in him, as their king, are the angels. He contains and embraces the nature of both angels and God, and in him all other things find their limit. Hence it is that the Cabalists say the angel <term>Metattron</term> <note>Metatron is a high-ranking angel in Jewish mysticism, often called the "Prince of the Presence."</note> is the Prince of Faces, because he is the mediator who introduces souls before the face of God. This is the office of the spiritual Christ himself, who is the true Wisdom, which first proceeded from the mouth of the father like a son. And it seems the Prophet intended to speak of this Angel when he says:

For in this respect, this angel is seen to be taken for Christ in many places of the Holy Scriptures. From this, therefore, the more secret Theologians hold that this is the angel to whose guardianship God committed Moses and the Israelites, to lead them through the desert, in whom was the name of Jehovah. They say he has dominion in the world in the same way that the mind—which is the intellect—is said to rule in the human spirit. Concerning his power—namely his expanded and universal authority—a certain man profound in occult Theosophy breaks forth into these words: "First among all is that great spirit who preserves the immense and most widely extended water, which is called heaven, in its destiny and essence, and marvelously grants motion to all growing and living things."
