And this is the reason why he is held by the Platonists and other wise men to be the Soul of the World (<term>Anima Mundi</term>), which the Cabalists understood by the "green line" <note>In the Zohar, the "green line" (Kav ha-Yarok) is said to encompass the entire world and emit the spiritual light of creation.</note> that is said to encircle the universal spirit of the world. From this it follows that some wish this Angel <term>Metattron</term> to be the final <term>Midah</term> <note>Hebrew for "attribute" or "measure."</note> or property of the Archetypal world, which is called by others <term>Cheter Elion</term> <note>Keter Elyon, meaning "The Supreme Crown," the highest Sephirah.</note>—that is, the supreme crown. Thus <term>Metattron</term> has for his meaning the "Gift of GOD": for the life and form of the world was the greatest of God's gifts, which includes all other gifts. Therefore, all those more skilled in mystical Philosophy seem to fall into this opinion, agreeing with the saying in Ecclesiasticus: that just as this <term>Metattron</term>, or this Soul of the World, is the first thing created among all creatures, so indeed is he said to contain within himself the perfection of all creatures, since they are accustomed to receive their forms from him as if from a universal fountain. And this is the reason why Rabbi Moses <note>Likely Maimonides (Moses ben Maimon).</note> says this Angel <term>Metattron</term> is the prefect of the universe, or the primary Active Intellect, from whom all forms flow, and consequently by whom all individual virtues in the world—and especially human ones—are governed. All of these Rabbi Breseth <note>Possibly a reference to Bereshit Rabbah, a midrashic text on Genesis.</note> also called angels, and others called forms. And those who wish the mystery of the Angels (which was created along with natural things) to be contained under the common name of Michael—as an appellation of the angelic species—seem to suggest this same thing, by which it is established that all angels are of the same species.

We say, therefore, that whether the angel be <term>Metattron</term> or Michael, he is nothing other than the white and pure emanation or power of God, which we previously called Wisdom. He is clothed in the mundane spirit—his presence having illuminated it—as if with a garment. This is held by the Cabalists to be the power of the <term>Tetragrammaton</term> <note>The four-letter name of God, YHWH.</note> wrapped in the mundane spirit since the origin of the world, in the same way that the Messiah himself was surrounded by flesh in the middle age of the world. From this it follows that <term>Metattron</term> is called an Angel insofar as there is "otherness"—that is, consisting of the created mundane spirit as an external part, and the uncreated divine spirit (namely the pure clarity of God or the emanation of clarity) as his internal part. This presence is everywhere in the world, filling, permeating, and producing all things, as it is the Word of God creating all. For this reason, he is held by the more secret Theologians to be the spiritual Christ, or <term>Messiah</term>, or the power of the <term>Tetragrammaton</term>, as said before. The wise man in Ecclesiasticus understood this when he said that Wisdom was created before all things—that is, mixed with the mundane spirit in the manner of a creature. In this state, expanded everywhere, he established the heaven with its regions and the earth, gave them life, and brought them into being; and this occurred during the first three days of creation, according to the opinion of Moses. Wherefore we also have it written by the royal Psalmist:

> *By the Word of the Lord the heavens were established (and elsewhere: by his wisdom), and all their power by the spirit from his mouth.*

However, when the third day was completed, <term>Metattron</term> (whom for the aforesaid reasons the Platonists called the Soul of the World) contracted his rays, which were dispersed everywhere, into one polished mass of the world—namely, into the sun. Hence also God was said by David to be clothed with light as if with a garment; in this respect he is sometimes called an angel, and sometimes Jehovah. Jehovah himself gave the reason for this, saying: *"Behold, I send my angel before you; do not provoke him, for my name is in him."* For all Cabalists agree that this angel was <term>Metattron</term> or Michael. ### Section I. Portion IV. Part II. Book IV. Member II.

We observe that its property was to animate the entire mundane spirit <note>The "spiritus mundi" or world-spirit, a subtle substance believed by Renaissance philosophers to connect the physical world with the spiritual realm.</note> and to order the regions of the heavens and the elements according to the delineation of the Archetype <note>The "Archetype" refers to the original divine blueprint or the mind of God.</note>, arranging them in harmonious peace. Thus, after three days had passed, it chose a denser tabernacle, so that it might more easily look upon the elemental creatures—namely animals, as well as plants and minerals—and rain down upon them the gifts of vivification, germination, and generation. Similarly, the frameworks of the entire world which Metatron <note>Metattron</note> created in the beginning, Michael intends to preserve until the very end, just as he has regard for those things created after the fourth day. 

Therefore, we see that both Metatron and Michael agree as one: namely, in the nobility of their lineage, as they proceed from the mouth of the Most High, and in their office and duty, namely in the vivification of the world and the distribution and preservation of souls or forms. Furthermore, just as it is the duty of the angel Metatron to introduce souls before the face of God (as the occult theologians maintain)—whence he is also called the Prince of Faces—so too is it Michael's duty to offer souls in heaven (as the Archangel states in his *Commentary on Cabalistic Dogma*). For he says:

*Michael is the high priest, sacrificing the immaculate souls of men to the blessed God in the upper world; and elsewhere he says, Michael performs a perpetual priesthood in heaven as the great priest of God; for just as the high priest on earth offers the souls of animals to GOD, so Michael, the spiritual Priest, offers rational souls to the same in heaven.*

By the same token, Metatron is said to have been the leader of Moses, through whose mediation it is handed down that Moses obtained the grace of speaking with GOD face to face, as mentioned above: *With him,* says Jehovah to Aaron and Miriam, *I speak mouth to mouth.* Finally, just as it was the duty of the great angel Metatron to repel the darkness, to strike down the horrific shadows, and to cast down everything of impurity from heaven into the earthly abyss, so indeed Michael, that great angel, is said to fight for the souls of all against the ancient serpent, who continually seeks to devour them. In this battle, Michael prevailed, having cast the Dragon out of heaven, and he reigns and flashes forth in a glorious manner in heaven, keeping the dragon or the prince of darkness always under his command and empire. Hence we read in Daniel that *Michael is always helping the people of God.* The words are as follows: *Michael the great Prince who stands for the children of the people—that is, for the elect. Daniel 12.*

Led by these and other reasons, philosophers skilled in the divine mysteries teach that the angel Michael is the very same as Metatron, and that Michael (whom they make the guardian of the <term>Sephirah Tiphereth</term> <note>original: "Sephiroth Typherith". For it is he who gives life not only to celestial but also to earthly creatures, and truly preserves and defends their lives against the Prince of Darkness. 

But we also have all of this confirmed from the Apocalypse, namely that this Angel is that spiritual *Christ*, and the *Messiah* of the entire universe, or the *Word of God*, which according to John is the light of the world, *from which all things were made and without which nothing was made, in which is life, etc. John 1.* For first we read that John himself, being caught up in the spirit, proclaimed and trumpeted with a loud voice: *I am Alpha and Omega, the Beginning and the end, who was like the son of man, whose eyes were like a flame of fire, and his feet like the purest brass glowing as if in a furnace; he wore a golden girdle, and in his right hand he held seven stars, and his face shone like the sun, and his voice was like the murmur of many waters, etc. Revelation 1.*

By these words, that thrice-great angel Michael seems to be most clearly and plainly described. According to Trithemius <note>Johannes Trithemius (1462–1516), a German abbot, polymath, and influential figure in Renaissance magic.</note> and others most well-versed in true magic, Michael is the prefect and leader of the celestial sun, who placed his seat and Tabernacle in the sun. This is also declared by his appearance, which is most similar to the sun: for just as the face of a man claims its position in his upper part, while his feet rest upon the earth, so indeed the face of this Angel is likened to the sun in heaven, and his feet to the air glowing and flashing in a furnace—thereby indicating the solar rays which strike the earth and the elemental region everywhere. 

And just as we observe the sun to be the lord and, as it were, the emperor of the entire sky, giving life and light not only to its own spirit but also to all its stars (which are said by the more eminent philosophers to have received their luminous power and their act of existence and essence from it, no differently than an earthly Emperor is accustomed to grant dignity and the power of acting to the rulers, princes, or magistrates subject to him), so indeed we see here this imperial angel, bearing the solar figure in his countenance, holding seven stars in his right hand. By this, John seems to signify that the seven stars and the angels presiding over them are under his power. For as the material Sun is accustomed to impart its light and virtue to the other stars, so indeed Michael, who is the spiritual or internal Sun in heaven, is accustomed to attribute luminous force and vigor to the other angels, as one who is superior to them in office and order. 

For Dionysius, Basil, Origen, and others <note>Pseudo-Dionysius the Areopagite, Basil the Great, and Origen were early Christian theologians whose works shaped angelology.</note> testify that angels of a higher order receive light more abundantly than those below them, and they also admit that the lower angels receive their light and virtue from the higher ones by way of influence. Therefore, it is clear that this Angel is the most powerful of all in heaven. For this reason, the secret theosophists say (as has already been mentioned) that the mystery of angels created together with natural things is encompassed under the common name of Michael, as a designation for the angelic species. By this (they say), we are taught that all angels are of the same species, but individual bodies, whether celestial or earthly, have their own rulers of virtues and prefects of operations. ## Regarding the evil Angel created by God, whom He uses together with his followers in His severity and wrath.

**JUST AS** it was the will of the world's creator, whose light flows out from the bright gates, to act as severely with the world because of the sin of man as He does mercifully in His grace; so indeed it pleased Him to procreate two leaders of angels, most opposite in nature and condition, of whom one contends and fights with the other for the safety and preservation of souls, lives, and things created and generated. This Prince, having innumerable angels under him who are subject to him and agree with his nature in goodness, we have called *Metattron* <note>Metatron</note> or the great Angel *Michael*, of whom we have spoken so many and such great words in the preceding chapter. Thus, indeed, Satan—the dragon against whom we read that Michael fought manfully and with triumph—is the devastator of lives, the exterminator, the open enemy of salvation, the foe of the generation of man, and the constant accuser and slanderer of souls before God. From this it is clear that, just as Michael is observed in his nature to be most full of piety, goodness, and affability toward men, so on the opposite side, Satan abounds in all iniquity, malice, and cruelty against the human race. In the execution of his most wicked will, he has many legions of evil demons under him, all of whom are said to be most ready to commit every kind of crime. He also has under his jurisdiction, or in his army, leaders and standard-bearers, imitating in this business the government and arrangement of **GOD** the Best and Greatest, whose seat and place he dared to usurp (seized by violent ambition). Therefore, just as four standard-bearers are reckoned in the army of **GOD**—namely Michael, Gabriel, Raphael, and Uriel—so in the army of Satan, the avengers Samael, Azazel, Azael, and Mahazael carry the widest sails <note>The author uses "carrying wide sails" as a metaphor for having great influence or prideful display.</note>. But leaving these particular angels aside, I shall now turn the style of my discourse chiefly to the Emperor himself—the supreme Prince in malice and in the office of violence and iniquity.

Many names have been imposed upon this head and leader of malignant spirits by the sacred scriptures, encompassing great hidden mysteries concerning his condition. In the first place, he is called *Lucifer* <note>Meaning "Light-Bringer."</note>; for such he was made in his origin by the Creator—specifically, clearer and more splendid than the other Angels, as Gregory <note>Likely referring to Pope Gregory the Great (c. 540–604 AD), a major authority on angelology.</note> seems to assert. For this reason, he is said to have surpassed the other angels in dignity and power. But it is handed down that he, eventually puffed up by pride and ambition, lost his beauty and clarity, and for this reason, he put on a foul and dark appearance; and so, he was cast down from heaven. The Prophet describes this in open words:

> How you have fallen from heaven, Lucifer, who rose in the morning! In this discourse, John excellently describes, first, the dark and foul condition of Lucifer once he was poisoned by pride, for which reason he assigns to him the names "Dragon" and "Serpent" (which are the most hostile of all animals in the world to the human race).

Secondly, he describes the manner by which he was ejected from heaven—namely, by the invincible pursuit of the great Angel Michael. Finally, the misery of the earth, the water, and the other elements, and their inexplicable calamity is judged because of the presence of such an implacable Dragon, who with his spirits circles the earth and seas, greedily and constantly seeking whom he may devour. A certain unknown author, though one quite profound in the mysteries of creation, seems to explain the entire history of Lucifer—both in his happiness while he was good and his unhappiness when he was turned to evil—in this manner, as we have found it expressed in a certain old manuscript:

> **GOD** created the air out of the dust of the first matter, both good and evil in the same or equal quantity of weight in all places. That air was created eternal by the perfect and uncreated God. And from the clear air, God created Lucifer with his companions or company, so that he himself was a certain shining air, clearer than the rest of the air; and that light which was Lucifer shone. Thus, therefore, all the darkness of the evil air was created or rendered good and clear without sin, and for that reason, in the beginning, evil was restrained or subdued or corrected under the good; for indeed, evil air can be most excellently corrected and amended by good air. But truly, that did not happen in Lucifer and his company; for when that Angel, Lucifer, saw that it would come to pass that the light hidden in the first matter of the waters would shine and be separated and elevated above the angelic creatures themselves, he was then kindled with hatred and envy against the human creature. And then that dark air, which lay hidden in the clear air, came forth and opened itself in Lucifer; and that dark and impure air overcame and conquered the clear and pure air. Thus, therefore, in the beginning, this angel Lucifer was offended. For when he saw the sacrosanct Trinity painting and sketching a certain clear mirror, he wondered whom it concerned; for there was formed a sort of circle surrounding this most holy Trinity on all sides, in which was the Sun of that clear mirror, containing in itself all the virtues of the Trinity itself. Therefore, he thought to himself: "If God has all these remarkable virtues enclosed within Himself, then certainly I, Lucifer, have all great vices on the opposite side; and so, through that which is comprised within me, I am not inferior to them. If, therefore, I produce or release all my vices, all these virtues of God will surely flee from them; and by that means, I shall be exalted above the counsel of the most high God."

# On the Efficient Cause of Meteors.

...and place him in his stead; for he is God and he flees from my malice: Thus, therefore, Lucifer, by his entirely free will, conceived or introduced vices, and consequently he then fell through all the choirs of the Angels with all his companions. For the heavens could no longer hold him, as they rightly recognized him along with all his associates who favored or adhered to him. Lucifer and his companions were ignorant of the strength or power of divine omnipotence, from which nothing at all is hidden, and likewise they did not know that all things are compelled to serve and be subject to Him—namely, the good as well as the evil—for no powers prevail against Him. In this way, therefore, the first sin was brought about and committed in heaven. Yet **GOD** had created Lucifer without sin, with clear and pure air; sin, however, was "dark air." For Lucifer and his company consisted of elements of air that were impure, yet mixed with clear and pure elements of air that covered, subdued, and restrained the impure air itself. But Lucifer, of his own accord and through his free will, produced and, as it were, sent out into the light the impure air of sin while he was still in heaven. For Lucifer was the impurity of the air, and heaven was purged as soon as Lucifer and his company were excluded and cast out from it; and Lucifer fell before Adam was created. Thus says that author <note>original: "Hæc ille"; a standard scholarly shorthand indicating the end of a cited passage from another writer.</note>. In this history of Lucifer (which this Author undoubtedly saw inscribed in the secret and mystical book of nature and observed in the new creation), he clearly denotes that Lucifer was created from both clear and dark air together, and that his "pure air" was his exterior, gleaming with a wonderful brightness, which so illuminated and tempered the wicked or dark air that the whole of Lucifer as created by God was originally good and free from sin. Truly, his malice and envy were the cause why his hidden darkness gradually overcame his bright exterior, and thus obscured and suppressed the exterior with its own shadows, and darkened it on all sides in a manifest way with dark air. Because of that sin, he was banished in exile from the place of light, by the mediation of the bright angels, into a place of darkness—namely, air of this kind. Hence, whereas he was previously called Lucifer <note>Lucifer means "Light-bringer" in Latin.</note> because of his brightness and was exalted in dignity above all the bright angels, he is now called by some *Lucifugus* <note>meaning "Light-fleer" or "he who flees the light"</note>, that is, fleeing the light of God and of the good angels. Nevertheless, in this light of darkness, he holds dominion over all the angels of his company. For this reason, he is called by the Apostle in one place the *prince of the power of the air, who works in the children of disobedience (Ephesians 2:2).* And elsewhere, the *Prince, power, and lord of darkness, the spirit of malice under heaven (Ephesians 6).* And John, in the Apocalypse <note>The Book of Revelation.</note>, called this Prince the *great and red dragon, the ancient serpent, because of his poisonous nature and subtlety (Apocalypse 12).* He is called the Devil (*Diabolus*) as if "rushing downward," and Satan as if "the contrary" or "the adversary." Elsewhere he is called *Behemoth*, as if a bull or a terrible beast like a bull, and elsewhere *Leviathan*: as if an "addition" or "apposition" of a thing *(Job 40)*; for as Gregory says, he is accustomed to add and, as it were, sew evil to evil, sin to sin, and grief to grief. He is also called the "Criminator," whence in the Apocalypse <unclear>it is written</unclear>, *The accuser is cast down.* Furthermore, he is named the *Lion* because of his open and manifest violence; hence Peter says, *As a roaring Lion (1 Peter, last chapter).* And by the Apocalypse he is called *Apollyon*, that is, the Destroyer or Devastator; he not only attempts to destroy men and other creatures but also to turn virtues into vices. Hence we also read what is written in the Prophet Isaiah:

> *Behold, I have created the smith that bloweth the coals in the fire, and that bringeth forth an instrument for his work; and I have created the waster to destroy. No weapon that is formed against thee shall prosper; and every tongue that shall rise against thee in judgment thou shalt condemn. This is the heritage of the servants of the Lord, etc. (Isaiah 54:16-17).*

By these words, the Prophet clearly teaches that the Devil was expressly created by God to lead men into error and to make them sin, so that he may afterwards destroy them; wherefore he calls him a "smith blowing the coals of fire" and "bringing forth his vessel." Just as a smith, by means of fire, is accustomed to shape and adapt iron for his purpose into this or that form, so that he may more easily complete the work he set out to do, so indeed the Devil is accustomed to prepare his instruments, both for deceiving the human spirit with flattering whispers and for openly harming the bodies of men and other creatures. This is why he sometimes stirs up winds to harm and destroy men and beasts; hence it is written in Job:

> *Suddenly a vehement wind rushed in from the region of the desert, and shook the four corners of the house, and falling, it crushed your children (Job 1:19).*

Sometimes he calls forth fire from heaven and uses it to perpetrate his deadly deeds; hence in the same chapter we read:

> *The fire of **GOD** fell from heaven, and having touched the sheep and the boys, consumed them (Job 1:16).*

Occasionally, he afflicts the body with sores and plagues; thus it is said that *Satan struck Job with a most grievous ulcer from the sole of his foot to the crown of his head (Job 2:6).* Sometimes he stains the air with corruption and is accustomed to introduce the plague to fulfill the pleasure of his creator; for we read in the prophecy of Habakkuk:

> *GOD will come from the South, his glory covered the heavens, death shall go before his face, and the Devil shall go out before his feet (Habakkuk 3:3).*

Or, the plague or a wasting sickness shall go before in the midday. From this it is clear that the Devil is a minister of God, always ready at His feet; he contaminates the air with plague, and in this specific property, he is called *Meriris* <note>In Renaissance demonology, particularly in Agrippa’s "Occult Philosophy," Meriris is identified as the demon of the "noonday devil" mentioned in the Psalms.</note> by the Hebrew Magi, or the "burning demon at noon." Agrippa says this is that great Prince of Malice, who is said by the Apostle to have the power of the air of this world—that is, the <term>sublunary air</term> <note>The air below the sphere of the moon, which in ancient science was the realm of change, decay, and weather, unlike the eternal heavens above.</note>, which is dark air and greatly subject to changes, compared to the empyrean or ethereal air, which are much clearer and purer. Finally, this is he who has will over all the winds of the sublunary world; hence, by God’s command or permission, he causes thunders, lightnings, winds, clouds, rains, and tempests, as much in the air as in the sea.

...sea, chasms <note>original: "Chasmata"; in early science, these were seen as "gaping" openings in the sky or the earth</note>, comets, mists, floods, snows, hailstorms, earthquakes, and all other meteors <term>meteora: in the Renaissance, this term referred to any atmospheric phenomenon (weather), not just falling space rocks</term>, he [the Devil] is sometimes permitted to bring about beyond the laws of worldly nature. This is possible even though all the aforesaid things are nonetheless the works and creatures of **GOD**, which cannot be stirred up in this world by the Devil unless God commits them into his hands. Hence the Devil said to Jehovah <note>the Hebrew name for God</note>: "Stretch out your hand a little, and touch all that he possesses"; And Jehovah answered, "Behold, all that he has is in your hand, only do not stretch out your hand against him" <note>A reference to the Book of Job, chapter 1</note>. With this said, the fiery Angels of **GOD**—who are called God’s ministers—and those of the wind, were for that time under his command. Whence it was said, "The fire of **GOD** fell from heaven," not the fire of the Devil, and yet this occurred by the command of the Devil. From these things it is clear that these harmful angels, although they are under the jurisdiction of the Devil, are nonetheless called the most powerful and strong angels of **GOD**, carrying out His word or will as much in the quality of His severity as in the elements themselves. 

From this, the four corners of the earth and the world, and the four winds blowing from them, seem to be those four standard-bearers <term>antesignani: elite leaders who stand before the standards in an army</term> who are said to carry the vast sails of Satan, inasmuch as he is the great prince of all the air. For those four angels, or spirits, or demons, who are said to hold the reins of the winds, are said to have empire over the four quarters of the world: namely, **Oriens** or (as the Hebrews will have it) **Samaël** has command over the East Wind; **Paymon** or, as they will have it, **Azazel**, presides over the West wind; **Ægyn** or (as they hand down) **Azael**, over the North; and **Amaymon** or, as they will have it, **Mahazael**, over the South.

But in truth, the goodness of almighty **GOD** is clearly declared in this: that just as He saw best and foreknew that sin would be introduced into the world before anything else was introduced—and for this reason ordained the Devil from the beginning to punish it—so indeed His mercy has so far prevailed over His severity that He created and established good angels of ineffable virtue. He especially established a single, most powerful Prince who might so surpass the Devil (who destroys the creatures of **GOD**) in strength and power, that in battle he not only drove him out from the kingdom of heaven, but also dominates him in this sublunary <term>sublunary: the region between the earth and the moon</term> world. The Devil is subjected to the pleasure of this Prince, who would restrain and hinder the evil spirits of the winds in their malevolent duties, and even, according to the divine will, correct the malignancy of those blasts and direct them to prosperous effects by his infinite virtue, whose role it is to bring life to all things, and to preserve and cherish all things. And this we have gathered most clearly from the Apocalypse <note>The Book of Revelation</note>:

> And I saw four angels (says the Revelator) standing upon the four corners of the earth, so that they should not blow upon the earth, nor upon the sea, nor upon any tree; and I saw another Angel ascending from the rising of the sun, having the seal of the living **GOD**, and he cried with a loud voice to the four Angels to whom it was given to harm the earth and the sea, saying: Do not harm the earth or the sea, nor the trees, until we have marked the servants of our God on their foreheads. (Revelation 7).

By these words, he seems to hint that the great and good Angel ascending from the east—whose role was to preserve those whom **GOD** had chosen from the injury of the said malignant spirits and their angels—held power and command over those destroying spirits; for at his command, they immediately offered their obedience. However, how these spirits appointed over the evil winds hold the reins of the winds, and how they are subjected to the command of the four great Angels of God, we have delineated in the following visual description.

### Section I, Portal IV, Part II, Book IV, Member II

...not otherwise than the **internal man** <note>original: "homo internus"; referring to the soul or the spiritual essence of a human being</note> is said to be made in the image of God, and possesses a **Superintendency** over all other things. Just as the Sun is given the chief place in the heavens as the highest of all planets and first in dignity, so the **eastern angel**—being dedicated to the sun—is said to be **Michael**. For this reason, he is to be preferred over the others in dignity and rank, and he stands on the side of **mercy** <note>original: "clementiæ"</note>.

The Archangel **Raphael** rules the region opposite to him and governs its spirit, namely the prefect of the West wind <note>original: "Venti Fauonii"</note>; likewise, **Gabriel** rules the Northern region, and **Uriel** the Southern. We find this same arrangement confirmed among the Hebrew Doctors. For **Rabbi Tedacus Levi**, in his *Book on the Ten Numerations* <note>A reference to the Sephirot in Kabbalistic tradition</note>, after explaining the four winds—North, South, East, and West—eventually proceeds thus: "From these four winds He created four Angels who are appointed over them by day and by night." **Michael**, who is of the side of mercy and compassions, is appointed as the *mamona* <note>original: "mamona"; here meaning a prefect or governor</note>, that is, the overseer of the East wind. Until midday and until night, **Raphael** rules the West wind, who is likewise of the side of mercy. Then **Gabriel**, by the power of judgment and severity, is the prefect over the North wind during the half-night and two measures of the world; **Noriel** <note>Often identified with Uriel</note> presides over the South. 

Furthermore, each of these has under him an Angel of the nature of a **Prince of the air**, each of whom has many species under him, which the *Book of Secrets* <note>original: "liber arcanorum"</note> contains. This also seems to be confirmed by what is read in the **Porta Lucis** <note>original: "Porta lucis"; The "Gate of Light," a primary text of Kabbalah by Joseph Gikatilla</note>: *"From the earth,"* it says, *"unto the firmament there is no empty place, but all is full of forms. Some of these are pure, some are capable of grace and mercies; and below there are many false, harmful, and tempting images, all dwelling and flying in the air. Some are for peace, some for war; some for good, some for evil; some for life, some for death; and consequently, some for health and healing, and some for disease and infirmity. And all this is in the lower habitation in which we exist,"* as **Joseph Castaliensis** <note>Latinized name for Joseph Gikatilla</note> reports. From this it is clear that good Angels are intermingled with the foul and the evil, so that the actions of the wicked demons (who hold God and men in ineffable hatred) may be tempered, repelled, and mitigated.

**Bartholomew** <note>Likely referring to a medieval scholastic or legendary source</note> seems to support this assertion of ours, speaking thus: *"The whole endeavor of demons or wicked spirits is to do evil, and to disturb and molest men; for this reason, they very often disturb the elements, stirring up tempests in the air and water, and corrupting the fruits of the earth,"* as is explained in the *Apocalypse* <note>The Book of Revelation</note>. They would bring far greater evils upon the inhabitants of the earth if the good Angels did not blunt the edge of their violence. From this, it is clear that they can do nothing except by **divine permission**, as the good Angels act as their **bridles**; but once permission is given, the good Angels not only cease their protection but are also accustomed to contribute to the punishment of creatures, as we read everywhere in the Sacred Scriptures. 

Regarding the protection of the good Angels against the assaults of the evil Angels, the Royal Psalmist <note>King David</note> speaks thus: *"Fear not the terror of the night, nor the arrow that flies by day, nor the plague that stalks in the darkness, nor the assault of the noonday demon; no scourge shall come near your tent, for He will command His Angels concerning you in all your ways"* (**Psalm 91**). By this speech, he clearly seems to hint that God has ordained to defend good men from the assaults of wicked demons through angels contrary to their natures. This was elegantly demonstrated through the protection of the Archangel **Raphael** in the book of **Tobit**, who, by repelling the assaults of the demon **Asmodeus**, preserved Tobit himself immune from his rage.

We conclude, therefore, that it is most certain that just as Lucifer (now called **Satan**) was made the universal **Prince of this air** after his fall and exile from heaven—according to the words of St. Paul—his principal effect comes from the **South**. This is the place from which rot, plagues, and wasting diseases are sent out, and where thunders are very often emitted. Hence, he is called **Meririm** by the Hebrews (as was declared before), which means the "demon raging and fuming at noon." Or, as **Habakkuk** and the Royal Prophet say in the places cited before, the "pestilence" or "destroying demon" in the noon or the South. 

Similarly, just as this Prince of the Air divides his aerial kingdom into four quarters—namely East, West, South, and North—and assigns a prefect to each part by divine command (whose duty it is to make the winds blow perversely), so great was the mercy toward the creatures in the sublunary heaven, and especially toward man, that in place of this Prince of great wrath and malice in the air or this world where we live, God placed a still greater Prince, full of grace and mercy. This Prince also has three other companion angels joined to him, similar in property and goodness, who have power and authority over those spirits acting as Satan’s lieutenants, who have power over the winds. 

Thus, as **Meririm** with his spirit is accustomed to rage in the South, so **Michael**, the great Prince who has superintendency over Meririm, claims the eastern pole of the world for himself. In this position, he takes care of the actions of **Samael** (or as others say, **Oriens**), as has been said more often. For these are the words of **Cornelius Agrippa** (*De Occulta Philosophia*, Book 3, Chapter 24): *"Among the evil spirits, four most powerful kings preside over the others according to the four parts of the world, whose names are **Uriens** (or **Oriens**), king of the East; **Amaymon**, king of the South; **Paymon**, king of the West; and **Egyn**, king of the North. The doctors of the Hebrews perhaps more rightly call them **Samael**, **Azazel**, **Azael**, and **Mahazael**, under whom many other princes and presidents dominate, as well as innumerable demons of private offices."* 

And yet, in his *Scale of the Number Four*, Agrippa says: *"There are four Angels presiding over the corners of heaven: **Michael** in the East, **Raphael** in the West, **Gabriel** in the North, and **Uriel** in the South. There are four Prince demons harmful in the elements: **Samael**, **Azazel**, **Azael**, **Mahazael**. There are four Princes of demons over the four corners of the earth: **Oriens**, **Paymon**, **Egyn**, **Amaymon**."* From these things, it is clear that this author is not consistent with himself <note>original: "non sibi constet"</note>, because he makes a distinction here between the four princes harmful in the elements and those over the four corners of the world who have care of the winds...

...are said to be: Furthermore, on the same scale he says there are four Prefects of the elements: namely, **Seraph** of fire, **Cherub** of air, **Tharsis** of water, and **Ariel** of earth. But to show our own mind’s opinion on this matter, we say that it is more probable to consider that since the entire sublunary region of spirit is filled with both the goodness of God and the malice of the Devil, it seems likely that every element has its own good Prince and likewise a bad one. Both are ministers of the divine property, for God uses the former to do good in His mercy, and the latter to punish and do evil in His severity. Therefore, we say that just as there are four good princes—**Seraph, Cherub, Tharsis, and Ariel**—so there are four evil and avenging ones: **Samael, Azazel, Azael, and Mahazael** in those same elements. And since the Winds participate in the nature of the Elements—namely, the East wind in fire, the North in earth, the West in water, and the South in air—the elementary Spirits, whether evil or good, receive their strengths from the Spirits of the winds, blowing either for good or for ill. Hence, it is certain that the East wind <note>original: "Ventum Eurum"</note> participates both in heat and in the violence of Samael, and so it is with the others. We also affirm that the royal spirits on the side of Satan who have power over the Winds—namely, **Uriens, Paymon, Egyn, and Amaymon**—are subject to the commands of those good angels who preside over the corners of the world: namely, **Michael, Raphael, Gabriel, and Uriel**. They are especially subject to that imperial Angel of goodness and life, **Michael**, who has force and power over the Prince of darkness or the dark air, because of the victory he reported over the Dragon. Therefore, under his supreme command are all demons, both of the Winds and of the elements, whether they be good or evil.

Here it must also be considered in passing that, according to the position of the gates in the celestial city (three of which were situated toward the east, three toward the west, and just as many toward the north and the south), the same holds true for the winds. For in every region of the world there are three winds: namely, the East wind <note>original: "subsolanus"</note> with its two wings, and the South wind <note>original: "Auster"</note> toward the south, and the North-east wind <note>original: "Cæcias"</note> toward the north, and so on for the others, as you have clearly depicted in the demonstration above. And since you have the Zodiac of the starry sky divided in the likeness of the gates of the heavenly Jerusalem—namely, into four triplicities <note>A "triplicity" is a group of three Zodiac signs belonging to the same element.</note>: the Fiery and eastern, the Airy and southern, the Watery and western, and the Earthy and northern—three signs are assigned to each of these triplicities. Namely, **Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius** to fire; **Gemini, Libra, and Aquarius** to air; **Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces** to water; and finally **Taurus, Virgo, and Capricorn** to earth. Similarly, because a proper prince of Angelic nature is assigned to each triplicity, and a peculiar angel is likewise assigned to each sign under him, it seems likely to me that not only is a Prince Angel ascribed to the cardinal point, but also to each windy gate in that region, which must have a relation to its sign, under whose power it falls. We have mentioned the demons of the triplicities and the peculiar spirits of each sign before, when we spoke of the demons of the Zodiac. We could indeed compile great volumes on this subject, but since we shall discourse more openly on these things elsewhere, we will not speak more of them in this place.

You have here, benevolent readers, how clearly described and, as it were, vividly depicted are the two great Princes of intelligences, differing greatly in property and nature. The former, who is the most powerful of all, is an Angel of light: merciful, good, the author of health and life, the solace and rest of the world, the driver away of death and diseases, who hates evil and fosters and nourishes good benevolently. We have declared him to be the dispenser of divine mercy, benevolence, and kindness; the guardian of souls and indeed of bodies. From his region come those good angels of men, whom we have called sacred and good spirits <note>original: "genios"</note>; he is the author and actor of the world's salvation and human resurrection (seeing as he obtained victory against the Devil and Death). But the other Prince is most opposite to this one in condition and will, for as an Angel of darkness he is accustomed to seethe with severity and impiety. He delights in evil actions; he is the author of diseases, pains, and destruction; the scourge and unrest of the world; the destroyer of life and the bringer of death into the world. He hates the good and fosters and nourishes evil strenuously. We have declared him to be the dispenser of severity, malevolence, and indeed of universal impiety; the destroyer of souls and indeed of bodies. Under his rule are those evil and depraved demons called evil spirits <note>original: "mali genii"</note>; he is the author of the world's ruin and man's damnation. And so you see these two Angels are entirely contrary to one another in quality. We shall therefore treat of these specifically in the following volume, where we will discourse copiously on health and disease.

Sect. I. Port. III. Part. II. Lib. I. Membr. III.

# Part II.
## OF THE THIRD MEMBER
### *BOOK ONE.*
### *On the celestial efficient cause of meteors, as the Astrologers say.* <note>In this period, "meteors" refers to all atmospheric phenomena including rain, wind, and lightning, while "efficient cause" refers to the primary agent that brings something about.</note>
### CHAPTER I.

->*Whether there be in truth any celestial efficient cause or not. That the cause of idolatry among mortals is their ignorance, whence arise so many errors in the world, and so many judgments of divine severity justly sent upon men.*<-

Since in the preceding pages it has been most aptly and clearly declared by us that it is God alone, who by His various emanations—with varying power and property—works in various ways, both in the heavens and on the earth, by means of His angelic organs. We have said that these organs are the means through which God primarily acts in this world, and that the other creatures of the world are merely vehicles for the said Angels. It follows by consequence that it is a monstrous error among created beings to attribute any essential act in the world to mundane creatures—whether they be angelic, celestial and stellar, or finally elementary—and not to God alone. This may also be gathered from these passages of Holy Scripture, for in it we read: *He ascended upon the Cherubim, and flew or glided upon the wings of the wind; He made darkness His secret place round about Him, sifting the waters from the clouds of the heavens, and the Most High gave forth His voice; He sent out His arrows and scattered them, even the lightning:* etc. <note>original: "ascendit super Cherubin, & volauit seu lapsus est super alas venti... misit sagittas suas, & dissipauit eos fulgur."</note> 2 Samuel 22:8-15. In this discourse, it is denoted that God is present first in the **Cherubim** <note>A high order of angels associated with divine presence and the throne of God.</note>, in which He sits as if in a vehicle; and then the Cherubim fly (driven by divine light) upon the wings of the winds; and then that spirit in the Cherubim and the winds collects the thick clouds, and then emits His voice or His thunders from them, and even sifts the waters from the clouds of the heavens. It is not said that God sat upon the Cherubim, and then the Cherub flew upon the wings of the wind, and the wind gathered the clouds, and the stars—and especially the Sun—attracted the vapors and exhalations, and finally the coldness of the middle region of the air condensed them, and the stars melted the clouds thus collected and released them as rain. Rather, the Holy Scriptures strive to attribute all these works simultaneously to the one God. Therefore, those who have attributed any actions in nature to either Angels or stars have done so in vain, for these things do nothing themselves, but only God acts through them. They act as organs, and not out of their own power or existence. Reuchlin <note>Johannes Reuchlin (1455–1522), a famous German humanist and scholar of the Hebrew Kabbalah.</note> seems to express this best in this manner: *On the Art of the Kabbalah, Book 3.* "Lest anyone, led by vain superstition, should think that all things are conferred upon human mortality from heaven by Angels, and not rather that all things are done by the Majesty of God through the Angels; we are taught even regarding the angels from the fountain of all truth, *that God does according to His will in the army of heaven and among the inhabitants of the earth*," Daniel to the King. And in another place we find: *There are indeed those who are called Gods in heaven and on earth, yet to us there is but one God the Father from whom are all things, and we in Him, and one Lord Jesus Christ through whom are all things and we through Him,* 1 Corinthians 8. By which the Apostle seems to declare that although mundane Angels and demons may seem to be Gods—indeed, even some men are held as Gods in a superstitious manner, to whom divine honors are usually paid in the extreme degree of idolatry, while they falsely attribute all actions, both good and bad, to them and even to the stars of heaven—nevertheless (says he), to us, that is, to true Christians, there is only one God the Father from whom all things radically stem, namely from the immense fountain of the **Ensoph** <note>original: "Ensoph" - The Kabbalistic term 'Ein Sof', referring to God as the Infinite or the Divine Origin before any self-manifestation.</note>, and one Lord Jesus Christ containing within Himself both the nature of all angels and of GOD, as He is that great Angel of the world and the true Wisdom first emanating from God—namely, *the Word through which all things were made, and we through Him*: whence also the Apostle says elsewhere, *From Him, through Him, and in Him are all things*, Romans 11:36. And elsewhere: *GOD the Father of all, who is over all and through all, and in us all*, Ephesians 4:6. And in another place, *All things are of God, but God is one*, 2 Corinthians 5. But the Apostle strives to declare this more expressly in these words, *GOD works all things in all*, 1 Corinthians 12. Arguing from this, that there is in truth no operation—not even through the mediation of angels, demons, or stars—unless it be essentially from God. For as the rays are by no means to be divided or segregated from the Sun, so indeed the rays or emanations sent forth from the fountain of all actions are not to be separated from their source, the unique and individual divine essence. This essence cannot be divided or distinguished into parts, for it is a pure unity that does not suffer any separation, even though it immerses itself into the multitude of the material world, even unto the center of the entire abyss.

He warns against the idolatry of attributing independent power to stars or spirits, citing both Scripture and Kabbalistic philosophy to emphasize divine unity.</summary>

# On the Efficient Cause of Meteors. <note>In this context, "meteors" refers to all atmospheric phenomena, such as rain, wind, and lightning, while the "efficient cause" is the primary agent that makes them happen.</note>
<meta>catchword: Saturn</meta>

<margin>Deuteronomy 32:17</margin>
In vain, therefore, did the ancient Magi <note>original: "Magi"; ancient Persian priest-scholars often associated with magic and astrology.</note> attribute the actions of the one God to demons, which are merely the laborious works of God alone and are by no means to be considered gods. This is the very root of the idolatry of the nations mentioned in the Fountain of Truth <note>A common way of referring to the Holy Scriptures.</note>, where we read: *They sacrificed to demons and not to God, to gods whom they did not know* (Deuteronomy 32:17). This is also the reason why an express law was given against the worship of demons at the very beginning of the Mosaic Decalogue <note>The Ten Commandments.</note>; and elsewhere we are warned that sacrifices must not be offered to demons, as in *Leviticus 17:7.*

In vain also have astrologers attributed the movements, virtues, and operations of influences to the stars or heavenly bodies, and especially to the Sun and Moon, which are the works of the Divine Wisdom or Word, and could not exist at all without His life-giving gift. For this error was also the occasion of great idolatry among the heathens and gentiles. For example, the Egyptians worshiped the Sun, whose houses and statues the Babylonian king is said to have shattered (*Jeremiah 43*). Furthermore, the Jews also fell into this damnable error, of whom it is said: *The chariots and horses of the Sun were removed from before the temple of the Lord* (2 Kings 23:11). <note>The original text cites "4. By these things we are taught that just as God is the sole author and actor in this world, so to Him alone—and not to any created thing—is praise, honor, adoration, and worship to be offered. Whatever happens to us or to the world should not be derived from the creature, but we should believe it proceeds from the power of the Creator and the act of His emanation, sent into the creature as if from a vehicle; for the creature itself, without His act, is plainly dead and possesses no value or standing in itself.

But since it is the custom of the world to affirm that celestial influences and their virtues are derived from the stars according to the teaching of the ancient astrologers—and consequently to say with the heathens that Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Orion, Corvus, Cassiopeia, and the other fixed stars, as well as Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, the Sun, etc., among the planets, are the causes of this or that alteration in the air, earth, and water—we shall follow in their footsteps for the better understanding of our readers. We will name and call the planets and fixed stars the causes of storms and meteors in the air, but with this condition: that we always hold in our memories that it is not the star we have named, but the Divine influx emitted from the Divine Sephirotic gates <note>The "Sephirot" are the ten attributes or emanations in Kabbalah through which the Infinite reveals itself.</note> into the sphere and body of the planets. This influx, rained down into the lower worlds by its angelic minister according to the will of the *Ein Sof* <note>original: "Ensoph"; the Infinite or Boundless Godhead in Jewish mysticism.</note> or the Infinite Father, for either the punishment or the benefit of mortals, is the procreative fountain and origin of every kind of effect in the air, water, and earth.

These things being first considered by a true Christian, we shall hasten to the description and living explanation of the triangle in our *Meteorographic Mirror* <note>original: "Catoptro meteorographico"; likely a specific diagram or instrument the author created to predict weather.</note>. Astrologers say that the efficient cause of all species of comets are the stars, both fixed and wandering <note>Planets.</note>. # On the Efficient Cause of Meteors.

### CHAPTER III.

->*A detailed explanation of the wheel depicted on the right-hand side of the empty region of our Meteorological Mirror, as well as the opening of the gates, floodgates, and great valves.*<-

For your better understanding, we have depicted this wheel here in this place so that you may more easily grasp what is contained within it by looking at it. In this wheel, taken from our Meteorological Mirror <note>original: "Catoptro nostro Meteorologico"</note>, one may see a double description: namely, the "openings of the great valves of heaven," which are described in the upper sphere, and furthermore the "openings of the gates of heaven," which are revealed in the parts circling the center of the sphere. 

Regarding the opening of the great valves of heaven, it should be known that the floodgates <note>original: "cataractæ"</note> and great valves of heaven are said to open when the Moon, moving away from a conjunction, a square aspect, or an opposition with the Sun, Jupiter, or Mars, is led and passes directly toward Saturn, Mercury, and Venus, or vice versa. That is, if the Moon, moving away from a conjunction <note>☌</note>, square <note>□</note>, or opposition <note>☍</note> with Saturn, Mercury, or Venus, is carried toward the Sun, Jupiter, or Mars; for then, according to the opinions of all astrologers, rains in abundance and consequently great floods are to be expected.

Similarly, the opening of the gates must be gathered from the observation of the lower sphere. For where you observe in the order of the sphere a square line marked with a □ between the Sun and Saturn, or the Moon and Saturn, or Venus and Mars, or finally Mercury and Jupiter; likewise, a diametrical line or line of opposition marked with a ☍ between the Moon and Saturn, or between the Sun and Saturn, or between Jupiter and Mercury, or finally between Mars and Venus; or finally, where you see the Moon ☾ with Saturn ♄, or Jupiter ♃ with Mercury ☿, or Venus with Mars with this sign ☌ (that is, in conjunction), they say the gates of heaven are open or about to be opened immediately, so that copious rains and showers are to be expected. This is a secret observation among astrologers, and a science not widely published by them. 

But indeed, <term>Aomar</term> <note>Likely referring to the Persian astrologer Abu Ma'shar, known as Albumasar, who was a primary authority on weather prediction in the Middle Ages.</note> maintains in his observations that if the Moon moves away from Venus and, after its departure, applies its rays to Mars, or if it moves away from Mars and applies itself to Venus, it then opens the floodgates of heaven; but if it moves away from Jupiter, applying to Mercury, or rather proceeds to Jupiter after being separated from Mercury, it opens the gate here again. Such are his views. 

However, we hold in the highest esteem that which we have previously condensed and reduced into the aforementioned sphere (as it is proven by long experience), and consequently, we believe it is far to be preferred over the rules of others. Nevertheless, use your own judgment, and I advise you to follow what seems more probable to you in this matter. Regarding the remaining celestial signs in the changing of the air, we have spoken more fully in our Astrological Treatise, described in our *Technical History*, therefore I believe you should be referred to that place.

### CHAPTER IV.

->*On the heavenly efficient cause of the Winds, where our opinion on the Winds*<-
->*is incidentally introduced and supported by strong reasons.*<-

After Freigius <note>Johann Thomas Freig (1543–1583), a German humanist scholar who wrote extensively on the physical sciences.</note> made mention of the causes of winds, he himself immediately speaks thus (led by better reasoning and departing from the opinion of Aristotle): *“Although the entire discussion about winds, just like other meteors <note>In the 17th century, the term "meteors" referred to any atmospheric phenomena, including wind, rain, snow, and lightning, not just falling stars.</note>, is full of the wonderful works of God, for which no firm and sufficient efficient causes <term>Efficient cause: the primary agent or force that produces an effect.</term> in nature can be put forward; nevertheless, it is useful to see how far human reason can progress.”* 

Sacred Scripture says indeed that God produces winds from His storehouses, from which we hear their blowing, but we know not whence they come or whither they go. So says Freigius. And indeed, both the Peripatetics <term>Peripatetics: followers of the philosophy of Aristotle, who famously walked about while teaching.</term> themselves and Pliny <note>Pliny the Elder, the Roman author of Natural History, who cataloged many strange natural phenomena.</note>, that accurate investigator of causes, are so wrapped in clouds of obscurity and ignorance that when they see themselves caught in the mud of ignorance, they subtly attempt to excuse themselves in part with vain distinctions. They say that some winds are "miraculous"—those, namely, for which no cause in nature can be rendered. Of this kind is the one described by Pliny, who says there is a certain cave on the coast of Dalmatia <note>A region on the eastern coast of the Adriatic Sea, in modern-day Croatia.</note> with a vast, steep opening; if a light weight is cast into it, even on a day that is otherwise calm, a stormy wind like a whirlwind is immediately seen to arise. 

They also judge to be of this kind those winds breaking out from the rocks of the province of Cyrenaica <note>An ancient region in modern-day Libya.</note>; hence they hold those rocks as things so sacred that they think it a profanation to touch them. For if they are touched even once by hands, the South Wind <note>original: "Auster"</note> is immediately stirred up, churning the sands, which is why they consecrated these rocks to the South Wind. 

But as for those winds for which they could devise some cause within the possibility of nature, they called these "natural," and judged their efficient cause in their usual manner. From this, anyone can see how uncertain is the opinion of men engaged in vain philosophy regarding such profound matters, and how inconsistent is the judgment of human wisdom. Furthermore, even among the fathers of the Astrologers, there seems to be great hesitation and instability in their opinion regarding the efficient cause of winds. For just as the Peripatetics divide their natural winds into "regular" and "sudden"—and the regular ones again (which they define as those that begin and end at fixed times) into "general" or "principal" (namely, those that blow from the four cardinal points) and "particular" and "minor" (which are observed to blow in certain provinces)—so indeed the Astrologers, looking deeper into...

-># On the Efficient Cause of Meteors. #<-

Ascending in the investigation of these causes, those who seek the truth claim that impetuous winds—whether sudden or general—and especially those that blow from the North toward the West, belong to Mars, and they say such winds are subject to him. Others, however, consider the winds as children of Titan, Astraea, and Aurora <note>In Greek mythology, the winds (Anemoi) were the offspring of Astraea (star-night) and Eos (Aurora/Dawn).</note>, generated by the heat of the sun, which renders the air subtle and thin, particularly at dawn; indeed, even Aristotle admits that winds are produced by the heat of the Sun. Yet all winds are said to receive the commands of Juno, because they blow only in the air, and Juno is the name given to the air. Others say that among the fixed winds, those they call *Prodromoi* <note>original: "Prodromos"; Greek for "forerunners."</note> (as they precede the Etesian winds) occur during the hottest time of summer, around the time the Dog Star <note>Sirius, the brightest star in the constellation Canis Major.</note> rises, preceding the Sun as it enters the first part of Leo by about 8 days. Furthermore, the Etesian winds, which are Northern winds, are constantly observed to blow for 40 days, preceded by these forerunners. Ptolemy is eager to attribute these winds to Jupiter, saying it is he who stirs them up, which is why he claims they are more fertile and healthful than others. They begin to blow immediately after the solstice and the rising of the Dog Star, as Aristotle says; however, Pliny says the Etesian winds blow two days after the rising of the Dog Star, while the sun is in Leo, and so on for the rest.

From these examples, you see that there is such great difficulty in finding the causes of the winds that even the Philosophers themselves have been unable to judge anything certain or firm about them. Instead, whatever they do, they gather from results and long experience and practice; they see everything *a posteriori* <term>a posteriori: reasoning based on observed facts and experience rather than theoretical deduction</term> and not *a priori*.

But we, as becomes a Christian, do not cease to scrutinize the mystery of the winds and other meteors <note>In this period, "meteors" referred to any atmospheric phenomena, including wind, rain, and snow.</note> in a more profound manner. We do this neither from Aristotle nor from any other book of the Heathen Authors, who were ignorant of the acts of the Divine Word (through which, according to the Bible—the fountain of all truth—all things were made). Most of them were ignorant, though the Divine Plato must always be excepted. Instead, guided by the instruction of the sacred pages, as well as by the infallible reason and demonstration of philosophical probability, we have immersed ourselves (not without great delight) into the most internal cause of these creatures. With every effort, we have sought the opinion of the Hebrew Doctors in this matter, as it was their role to be more practiced in the mysteries of the Jews, and especially in the exposition and interpretation of the Holy Bible. From Rabbi Tedaco Levi <note>Likely a reference to a Kabbalistic commentator or a specific medieval Jewish scholar.</note>, who counts ten in his book, he says, speaking of the four Cardinal Winds: "From those four winds, God made four Angels appointed over them by day and by night. Michael, who is on the side of mercy, is appointed over the East wind, and Raphael rules the West wind. Then Gabriel, in the power of judgment and severity, is appointed over the North wind, and Noriel or Uriel presides over the South." These are his words. And in the book of secrets, we find that each of these has many legions under him, which they employ in their business to fulfill the will of the Creator.

We, however, are forced to disagree with that Doctor in certain respects when considering the matter to its core. For it is certain and beyond all doubt, as proven by the experience of sailors, that the Cold Zone of the Antarctic region of the world is no less stiff with cold and frigid effects than the Boreal <note>Northern</note> zone—namely with constant frost, snow, and rime. These effects are produced by the wind blowing from the Antarctic pole no differently than the cold effects from the Boreal or Northern winds. Thus, it seems hardly probable that a fiery spirit such as Uriel (whose name signifies the "Fire of God") or Meriri <note>A biblical term often associated with a "bitter" plague or a noonday demon.</note> (who signifies a demon burning at midday) should have dominion or power in that region where the polar star of the Antarctic hemisphere has its seat. For this is certain, and to be denied by no one: just as the Northern hemisphere is divided into its temperate and cold Earthly Zones, extending all the way to the polar star, so too it is apparent that the opposite hemisphere is distinguished into as many regions of similar condition. Specifically, the space of the Torrid Zone is that situated between the equinoctial line <note>The Equator.</note> and the Tropic of Capricorn, and the Temperate Zone extends in latitude from the Tropic of Capricorn to the Antarctic circle. Finally, they measure the Cold Zone from the Antarctic circle to its own polar star.

By these facts, it is clearly established that the wind blowing from the Antarctic pole is governed by neither Meriri nor Uriel nor Noriel, since it is contrary to fire in nature and condition, being instead extremely cold. Therefore, we must consider seriously that a more suitable seat for the aforementioned angels is in the center of the Torrid Zone—that is, around the equinoctial region—because that place best agrees with the natures of Uriel the good Angel and Meriri the evil demon. Therefore, it should be understood that when it is said that Uriel or Meriri are the presiding Angels of the south, this is said in respect to us and the Jews, who are north of the Equator. Hence, the guardianship of the south is ascribed to the planet Jupiter, as his climate passes between Ethiopia and Judea; Uriel serves him and has dominion over him, just as when Saturn is dominant near the Equator, Meriri has greater power in the air. We say, therefore, that the reason why the wind proceeding from the southern region is so pestilential to us and usually renders the air so corrupt (and this happens when the wrath of Jehovah is kindled against the Northern world) is because the very cold and very dry blasts from the Antarctic pole, passing through the torrid or burning seats of the prefects Uriel and Meriri, mix with the natures of those blasts. Thus, heat is mixed with cold, and dryness with Jovian moisture and even fiery dryness; this incongruous mixture, blowing toward the Northern parts, results in a struggle of hot with cold—

### Sect. I, Port. III, Part. II. Book I. Member III. ###

...and when moisture gathers with dryness in the clouds, it produces rain through natural liquefaction, sometimes mixed with lightning and thunder. But if *Meriri* <note>In Hebrew tradition, *Meriri* is a spirit or demon associated with "bitter" destruction and pestilential heat.</note> is accustomed to rage in his region, then the air is rendered more corrupt and becomes more pestiferous; likewise, the thunders sound more unnatural, or rains are poured out in excessive abundance. Indeed, this can be very easily discerned from these words of the Prophet Habakkuk: *God [Jehovah] will come from the South, his glory covered the heavens, and the earth is full of his praise. His splendor will be like light, there his strength is hidden; death shall go before his face, and the Devil shall go forth before his feet; or, as others interpret, the pestilence precedes him, with a wasting plague in the south; Habakkuk 3:3.* <note>original: "Iehoua veniet ab Austro... anteuenit ipsum pestis, & lue vastante in meridie; Abak. 3.3."</note> A similar respect holds true with our Northern Wind [Boreas], during which snow, hail, ice, and frost are produced. Yet truly, this wind, penetrating through the equinoctial region, breathes such a temperament to those of the Antarctic hemisphere—and especially the temperate zone—as the wind of the Antarctic pole breathes to us: namely, a cloud-bearing, rainy, contagious, moist, and hot wind. For a wind of that sort participates in diverse natures because of its diverse mixture; it is the most mixed and composite of all the winds of heaven, behaving in the manner of a "rude and undigested chaos" <note>A reference to Ovid's *Metamorphoses*, describing the state of the universe before order was imposed.</note>, whence it consists of qualities repugnant to one another. The cause of its greater or lesser depravity depends on whether it is led and directed by the good Angel *Uriel* (also called *Noriel*) or by the evil spirit called *Meriri*.

Therefore, as we see that in each hemisphere the final climate toward either pole is ruled by the Moon, so also the North [Boreas] or the Northern pivot is governed by the Kabbalists. Consequently, the Moon holds dominion there among the stars, though not without the great power and operation of Saturn. For in every celestial motion we see a circle—both in the hours of the day and in the counting of months in childbirth—and so it is in every other thing: where the Moon ends, Saturn immediately begins. Therefore, in the extreme regions where the distance of the sun is longer, these two planets are observed to be joined in operation. Hence, not only from the Kabbalists but from the effect itself, we see that the Moon (over whom Gabriel presides) and then Saturn (from whom the constrictive quality proceeds, speaking in the Astrological manner) hold dominion at the poles. But Saturn especially regards the Antarctic pole, although he works his effects in both. The intermediate place—namely that through which the axis of the poles passes, where the meridian circle cuts the equinoctial line at right angles—is the place where Jupiter is said to have his seat. Whence the spirit breathing from that region is moist and hot, and is likened to air. Furthermore, the Sun claims for himself the point of the *subsolanus* [the East wind], namely that exact part in the east where the equinoctial circle is said to cut the Horizon; over this pivot *Michael* is appointed, who is the intelligence of the Sun. But truly the point from which the *Eurus* [the South-East wind] blows—namely that direct place where the Tropic of Capricorn cuts the Horizon in the eastern region—is governed by Mars. Consequently, an evil Angel of a fiery condition called *Samael* <note>In Kabbalah, Samael is often the angel of severity or the accuser, associated here with the heat of Mars.</note> presides over that region; he is the prefect of Mars, whence this wind is said to blow with such violence, such glow, and such fiery heat. We also have this confirmed from Holy Scripture: *With an East wind [Eurus] you break the ships of the Ocean; Psalm 48:8.* <note>original: "Euro perfringes naues Oceani: Ps. 48 8."</note> Furthermore, we are taught elsewhere that the East wind scorches the fruit and herbs of the field, *Genesis 41:6.* And in Jonah it is said: *God sent a sultry East wind that greatly burned Jonah as the sun rose, etc. Jonah 4:6.* But this wind is somewhat more moist for us than the *Caecias* [North-East wind], because it blows through the region of Jupiter and, in the path of its motion, it catches up and condenses the Northern air. Yet, the closer one approaches to its source, the drier and more turbulent its blasts are found to be; therefore its blasts are more furious in the Mediterranean and Indian seas than among us, and they also cause more desiccation there. On the other hand, the *Caecias* wind, which blows from that point of the east where the Tropic of Cancer intersects the Horizon, participates in the dryness of the North; hence it is governed primarily by Mars, and also has something of Saturn’s stypticity [astringency]. For this reason, it is considered the worst, driest, and most impetuous wind; from its malice, depravity, and inconstancy, it earned this name *Caecias* <note>The name Caecias was sometimes associated with the Greek word for "evil" or "blindness."</note>. This wind is therefore ruled primarily by the angel Samael and, in a smaller portion, by the spirit or demon named *Azael* <note>Azael is a figure often linked to fallen angels or the spirits of the desert.</note> appointed in the North. Thus it is occupied in malice, the gathering of clouds, and constant violence. Mars rules that entire side of the eastern world through his Angel, yet in such a way that he is subjected to the command of *Michael*, who causes the wind to blow benevolently from the western equinox.

So also, throughout the entire western region, Mercury extends his dominion. In the *Africus* [South-West] cavern, he is governed chiefly by an Angel (either good or evil) of the south, and joins with him. For Mercury is inconstant, and is accustomed to be good with the good and evil with the evil. Furthermore, in the *Africus* wind, which is between the *Austro-Africus* [South-South-West] and the *Favonius* [West wind], he joins himself with the tumultuous Angel of the South; hence he usually blows in a furious manner—indeed, this wind is the strongest of all, because Mercury is the most "windy" among all other planets.

But from that point where the equinoctial line cuts the western part of the Horizon at right angles, we say that *Favonius* (in Greek, *Zephyrus*) blows. Over this presides *Anael* <note>The angel traditionally associated with Venus and love.</note> along with the good Angel *Raphael* <note>The angel of healing, often associated with Mercury, but here linked to the restorative West wind.</note>. Therefore, it emits blasts that are healthful, though moderately cold and moist (after the manner of the female sex), which the solar spirit makes wholesome, spermatic, and fruitful by meeting them. Finally, the *Corus* [North-West wind], which blows from that intersection of the Tropic of Cancer that occurs on the western Horizon, participates in the nature of both Venus...

## MEMBER III.
# BOOK TWO.
### *On the elementary Efficient cause.*
#### CHAPTER I.
##### *How the regions of the world are compared to the visions of human sense, and that the more divinity immerses itself into the multitude, the more its rays are covered and hidden from human sense.*

Just as three visions are observed to exist in man—one of which is corporeal, and is occupied with bodily objects, in which the exterior sense is most often deceived by judging as true those things which are in reality feigned and false images, so that this is the most uncertain of all human visions; the second is in the imagination or <term>phantasy</term> <note>The "phantastic" spirit was considered a bridge between the physical senses and the rational mind.</note>, which is the first grade of spiritual vision, in which the likenesses and, as it were, shadows of bodies are perceived (for sometimes bodily objects appear to the phantastic spirit no differently than an image in a mirror); and this vision, inasmuch as it is a medium between the external sense and the intellect, sometimes sees false things and is deceived, but truly looking toward the intellect it can by no means be deceived, wherefore this species of human vision is more certain than the corporeal one; the third and final species of vision is the intellectual, which is accustomed to gaze upon things which are neither corporeal nor have the forms of bodies, and the objects of this kind of human vision are the mind itself, GOD, justice, wisdom, and every good affection of the soul—in a similar way does the matter stand in the inspection of the efficient cause of <term>meteors</term> <note>In the 17th century, "meteors" (meteororum) referred to all atmospheric phenomena, including rain, wind, and lightning, not just falling stars.</note> among men. 

For those to whom it is given by the vision of the intellect to look into and gaze upon the very marrow of meteors, they see indeed that God himself, the supreme mind, the word or divine Wisdom, is the sole and infallible agent in their production; and that vision is truly intellectual. There is also another vision, which is phantastic, by which men see and gaze upon the cause of meteors: and by this vision a man discerns that the Angels or <term>daemons</term> <note>The author uses "dæmones" in the classical sense of guiding spirits or intermediaries, rather than purely evil beings.</note> themselves are the causes of meteors, and in this kind of inspection a man sometimes errs, namely by having respect for the created nature or the human spirit (which has the closest proximity to corporeal things). For in attributing the efficient cause of a meteor to a created thing he errs, and seems to fall into the crime of Idolatry; but truly if he looks to the internal Angel, which is the light or divine emanation which it received immediately from the source of the <term>Ensoph</term> <note>original: "Ensoph" — from the Hebrew "Ein Sof," meaning the Infinite or the divine origin before manifestation.</note>, to that extent he is not deceived in his vision, inasmuch as it is intellectual. Finally, if we look back at the celestial bodies through the corporeal vision of the first order with the Astrologers, or look at the bodies of the elements and things composed of elements of the first degree with the <term>Peripatetic Philosophers</term> <note>Followers of Aristotle.</note>, it is necessary that we fall into great error, and immerse ourselves in the deep sea of Idolatry...

namely, by attributing that wondrous work to coarse and, to the senses, visible creatures—which are in truth dead in themselves and of no importance—specifically to the sun, the remaining stars, the elements of fire and air, the heat of the earth, the cold of the middle region of the air, exhalations, vapors, and so on. These angels, in respect to their proximity and nearness, are with the Divinity insofar as they immediately receive the impressions of light or divine emanations, which they then later, led by divine command, desire to impart to creatures, whether they are perfectly or imperfectly mixed.

Allow me to present a most fitting comparison for your consideration. A certain man wounds another with a sword: it is now asked, "Which of these men committed the wounding?" One will answer (in the **Peripatetic** <note>original: "more Peripatetico"; referring to the followers of Aristotle</note> manner, like those who attribute the efficient cause of a meteor to fire or air) that "the sword did this." Another (following the example of the **Astrologers**, who attribute the acting cause to the meteors or stars) will say that "the hand of the striker is the effecter of that deed." A third, again approaching the matter more closely (along with the **Magi** <note>Wise men or practitioners of natural magic</note> who say the authors of meteors are demons), will say it is the "spirit within the man" who did it. Finally, one skilled in **theographic** <note>Writing or study concerning God's direct action</note> mysteries, looking with eyes somewhat sharper into the very center of each thing, will say that "God did both this and that." By this example, the error of the world is clearly explained. We, however, in this place, will make mention of the winds only in the common manner, under which name we nonetheless understand the **Angels of GOD**, who are accustomed to animate them. But since in this booklet of the third member we intend to act in a physical manner and deal with the elements, we will therefore treat the winds in this place according to the manner of common philosophers.

## CAP. II.

-> On the correct division of the winds, and that they are the efficient causes (speaking in <-
